(1.) In some foreign proper names and in a very few Latin words the quantity of a vowel varied. Vergil has ⟦b:Sȳchaeus⟧ and ⟦b:Sychaeus⟧ within six verses; also ⟦b:Āsia⟧ and ⟦b:Asia⟧, ⟦b:Lavīnium⟧ and ⟦b:Lāvīnius⟧; so also ⟦b:glōmus⟧ (Lucr.), ⟦b:glomus⟧ (Hor.); ⟦b:cōturnīx⟧ (Plaut., Lucr.), ⟦b:coturnīx⟧ (Ov.).
(2.) Sometimes such variations in vowel quantity are only apparent: thus, the occasional long final ⟦b:-ē⟧ of the active infinitive (⟦b:darē⟧, ⟦b:prōmerē⟧) has probably a different origin from the usual ⟦b:-ĕ⟧. For metrical lengthening, see ⟦r2505:2505⟧.

title: Quantitative Vowel Gradation
text:
⟦#135⟧
The same stem often shows a long vowel in some of its forms and a short vowel in others. In most cases these variations of quantity were not developed on Latin soil but inherited from a much earlier period. Such old inherited differences in vowel quantity are called ⟦i:quantitative vowel gradation⟧.
(1.) Instances of this are ⟦b:prō⟧ for ⟦b:*prōd⟧ (⟦r149:149⟧; cf. ⟦b:prōdesse⟧) and ⟦b:pro-⟧ (Greek πρό); ⟦b:nē⟧ and ⟦b:ne-⟧ in ⟦b:nescius⟧; the couples ⟦b:regō⟧, ⟦i:I rule⟧, and ⟦b:rēxī⟧; ⟦b:vehō⟧, ⟦i:I draw⟧, ⟦b:vēxī⟧; ⟦b:veniō⟧, ⟦i:I come⟧, ⟦b:vēnī⟧, where the long vowel is characteristic of the perfect stem (⟦r862:862⟧); ⟦b:vocō⟧, ⟦i:I call⟧, and ⟦b:vōx⟧, ⟦i:voice⟧; ⟦b:regō⟧, ⟦i:I rule⟧, and ⟦b:rēx⟧, ⟦i:ruler⟧; ⟦b:legō⟧, ⟦i:I read⟧, and ⟦b:lēx⟧, ⟦i:bill⟧; ⟦b:sedeō⟧, ⟦i:I sit⟧, and ⟦b:sēdēs⟧, ⟦i:seat⟧; ⟦b:fidēs⟧, ⟦i:confidence⟧, and ⟦b:fīdō⟧, ⟦i:I trust⟧; ⟦b:dux⟧ (cf. ⟦b:ducis⟧), ⟦i:leader⟧, and ⟦b:dūcō⟧, ⟦i:I lead⟧, where verb and noun are differentiated by the quantity of the root vowel; and many others.
(2.) Sometimes the reduction of the vowel in certain forms amounts to complete loss, as in the adverbial ending ⟦b:-is-⟧ in ⟦b:magis⟧ (⟦r346:346⟧, ⟦r363:363⟧) compared with the comparative suffix ⟦b:-ios⟧, ⟦b:-iōs⟧ (Nom. ⟦b:-ior⟧, Genit. ⟦b:-iōris⟧); in the oblique cases of the stem ⟦b:carōn-⟧ (nomin. sg. ⟦b:carō⟧, ⟦r497:497⟧), where the suffix becomes ⟦b:-n-⟧ (⟦r545:545⟧), genitive ⟦b:car-n-is⟧; in the suffix ⟦b:-ter⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-tr-⟧ in all cases but the nom. sg. (⟦b:pater⟧, ⟦b:patris⟧, etc., ⟦r470:470⟧, ⟦r487:487⟧); in the feminine ⟦b:-tr-ī-c-⟧ to the suffix ⟦b:-tor-⟧; but the nom. sing. ⟦b:Caecīlis⟧ (⟦r465:465⟧) for ⟦b:Caecīlios⟧ is probably due to syncope.

title: Qualitative Vowel Changes
text:
⟦#136⟧
(1.) ⟦b:i⟧ before an ⟦b:r⟧ which goes back to an earlier voiced ⟦b:s⟧ (⟦r154:154⟧) was changed to ⟦b:e⟧: as, ⟦b:cineris⟧, ⟦i:of ashes⟧, for ⟦b:*cinisis⟧, from the stem ⟦b:cinis⟧ (⟦r491:491⟧); ⟦b:Faleriī⟧, for ⟦b:*Falisiī⟧, cf. ⟦b:Falis-cus⟧; (formed like ⟦b:Etrūria⟧, for ⟦b:*Etrūsia⟧, cf. ⟦b:Etrūs-cī⟧).
(2.) In the nominative singular of compounds like ⟦b:iūdex⟧, ⟦i:judge⟧ (from ⟦b:iūs⟧ and ⟦b:dīcere⟧), ⟦b:comes⟧, ⟦i:companion⟧ (from ⟦b:com⟧, ⟦i:with⟧, and ⟦b:īre⟧, ⟦i:go⟧), the ⟦b:i⟧ of the second member of the compounds is changed to ⟦b:e⟧ (⟦r470:470⟧) after the analogy of words like ⟦b:artifex⟧, ⟦i:artisan⟧, etc. (107, ⟦i:d⟧).
⟦#137⟧
⟦b:e⟧ before ⟦b:-gn-⟧ became ⟦b:i⟧: as, ⟦b:īlignus⟧, from the stem ⟦b:īlec-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:īlex⟧).
⟦#138⟧
⟦b:e⟧ before the guttural nasal (⟦r62:62⟧) followed by a guttural mute was changed to ⟦b:i⟧: as, ⟦b:septingentī⟧, from ⟦b:septem⟧; ⟦b:singulī⟧, from the stem ⟦b:sem-⟧ in ⟦b:semel⟧ (for the assimilation of ⟦b:m⟧ see ⟦r164:164⟧, 3); ⟦b:obtingō⟧ (⟦r925:925⟧), ⟦i:I attain⟧, for ⟦b:*óbtengō⟧ (104, ⟦i:c⟧) from ⟦b:*ob-tangō⟧ (104, ⟦i:e⟧).
⟦#139⟧
A similar change took place in the group ⟦b:-enl-⟧ which became first ⟦b:-inl-⟧ and then ⟦b:-ill-⟧: as, ⟦b:*signilum⟧, diminutive of ⟦b:sīgnum⟧ (for ⟦b:ī⟧, see ⟦r122:122⟧, ⟦i:c⟧), first changed by syncope (⟦r111:111⟧) from ⟦b:*signilum⟧ to ⟦b:*sign̥lum⟧, then to ⟦b:*sigenlum⟧ (⟦r172:172, 3⟧), then to ⟦b:*siginlum⟧, and finally to ⟦b:sigillum⟧.
⟦#140⟧
⟦b:o⟧ before ⟦b:nc⟧ became ⟦b:u⟧: as, ⟦b:homunculus⟧, ⟦i:manikin⟧ for ⟦b:*homonculus⟧, from the stem ⟦b:homon-⟧ (⟦r485:485⟧); ⟦b:nūncupāre⟧, ⟦i:name⟧, for ⟦b:*nōn-cupāre⟧ (⟦b:nōn-⟧ for ⟦b:nōm-⟧ (⟦r164:164, 3⟧) = syncopated ⟦b:nōmen⟧); ⟦b:hunc⟧, ⟦i:him⟧, for ⟦b:*honc⟧, from ⟦b:hom-ce⟧ (⟦r662:662⟧).
⟦#141⟧
⟦b:o⟧ before ⟦b:l⟧ followed by any consonant save ⟦b:l⟧ was changed to ⟦b:u⟧: as, ⟦b:cultus⟧, ⟦i:tilled⟧, for ⟦b:*coltus⟧, from ⟦b:colere⟧; ⟦b:multa⟧, ⟦i:fine⟧, for old Latin ⟦b:molta⟧. But ⟦b:o⟧ before ⟦b:ll⟧ is retained: as, ⟦b:collis⟧, ⟦i:hill⟧.
⟦#142⟧
⟦b:e⟧ before guttural ⟦b:l⟧ (⟦r60:60⟧) was changed to ⟦b:o⟧: as, ⟦b:solvō⟧, ⟦i:I undo⟧, from ⟦b:*seluō⟧ (⟦b:se-⟧, as in ⟦b:se-cordia⟧, ⟦b:luō⟧ = Greek λύω); ⟦b:culmen⟧, ⟦i:top⟧, for ⟦b:*celmen⟧, from ⟦b:*cellō⟧ in ⟦b:ex-cellō⟧; ⟦b:volō⟧, ⟦i:I wish⟧, for ⟦b:*velō⟧; but ⟦b:e⟧ is preserved before dental ⟦b:l⟧ (⟦r60:60⟧): as in ⟦b:velle⟧, ⟦b:velim⟧ (⟦r773:773⟧). Before ⟦b:l⟧ followed by any consonant save ⟦b:l⟧ this ⟦b:o⟧ changes to ⟦b:u⟧ (⟦r141:141⟧): as, ⟦b:vult⟧.
⟦#143⟧
In a number of words, notably in ⟦b:voster⟧, ⟦i:your⟧, ⟦b:vorsus⟧, ⟦i:turned⟧, ⟦b:vortex⟧, ⟦i:eddy⟧, and ⟦b:votāre⟧, ⟦i:forbid⟧, the forms with ⟦b:o⟧ were replaced, about the second century B.C. by forms with ⟦b:e⟧: as, ⟦b:vester⟧, ⟦b:versus⟧, ⟦b:vertex⟧, ⟦b:vetāre⟧ (Quint. 1, 7, 25).

title: Vowel Change: Assimilation
text:
⟦#144⟧
In a few cases a vowel is influenced by the vowel of a neighbouring syllable: as,
⟦b:nisi⟧, ⟦i:unless⟧, for ⟦b:*nesi⟧; ⟦b:iīs⟧, for ⟦b:eīs⟧, ⟦i:to them⟧ (⟦r671:671⟧, ⟦r674:674⟧); ⟦b:diī⟧, ⟦b:diīs⟧, ⟦i:gods⟧, for ⟦b:deī⟧, ⟦b:deīs⟧ (⟦r450:450⟧); ⟦b:nihil⟧, ⟦i:nothing⟧, for ⟦b:*nehil⟧; ⟦b:homō⟧, ⟦i:man⟧, for ⟦b:*hemō⟧ (cf. ⟦b:nēmō⟧, from ⟦b:ne-hemō⟧, ⟦r118:118⟧); see also 104, ⟦i:d⟧; 105, ⟦i:i⟧.

title: Qualitative Vowel Gradation
text:
⟦#145⟧
The same stem often shows different vowels in different forms. In most of these cases this difference was inherited from a very early period and continued in the Latin. Such old inherited variation of the quality of the stem-vowel is called ⟦i:qualitative vowel gradation⟧. The qualitative variations may be accompanied by quantitative changes (⟦r135:135⟧).
Often the verb and the noun are thus distinguished by different vowels: as, ⟦b:tegō⟧, ⟦i:I cover⟧, and ⟦b:toga⟧, ⟦i:a garment⟧, ⟦i:toga⟧; ⟦b:precor⟧, ⟦i:I beg⟧, and ⟦b:procus⟧, ⟦i:suitor⟧, cf. English ⟦i:to sing⟧ and ⟦i:a song⟧, ⟦i:to bind⟧, and ⟦i:a bond⟧. The different tenses of some verbs show a like gradation: as, ⟦b:capiō⟧, ⟦i:I take⟧, ⟦b:cēpī⟧; ⟦b:faciō⟧, ⟦i:I make⟧, ⟦b:fēcī⟧, cf. English ⟦i:I sing⟧, ⟦i:I sang⟧; ⟦i:I bring⟧, ⟦i:I brought⟧. The same occurs in derivation: as ⟦b:doceō⟧, ⟦i:I teach⟧, by the side of ⟦b:decet⟧; ⟦b:noceō⟧, ⟦i:I harm⟧, by the side of ⟦b:nex⟧ (⟦b:nec-s⟧). The two vowels which occur most frequently in such gradation are ⟦b:e⟧ and ⟦b:o⟧: as in stems in ⟦b:-o-⟧, ⟦b:domine⟧, ⟦b:dominus⟧ (for ⟦b:dominos⟧); as variable vowel (⟦r824:824⟧); ⟦b:genos⟧ (⟦b:genus⟧, 107, ⟦i:c⟧) in the nom. sg. by the side of ⟦b:*genes-⟧ in the oblique cases (gen. ⟦b:generis⟧ for ⟦b:*genesis⟧, ⟦r154:154⟧); ⟦b:honōs⟧ by the side of ⟦b:hones-⟧ in ⟦b:hones-tus⟧; ⟦b:modus⟧, ⟦i:measure⟧, for ⟦b:*modos⟧ (originally a neuter ⟦b:-s-⟧ stem like ⟦b:genus⟧ (⟦r487:487⟧, ⟦r491:491⟧), but transferred later to the ⟦b:-o-⟧ declension), by the side of ⟦b:modes-⟧ in ⟦b:modes-tus⟧, ⟦i:seemly⟧. See ⟦r187:187⟧.

title: Consonant Change
text:
⟦#146⟧
In a number of words which belong more or less clearly to the stem of the pronoun ⟦b:quo-⟧ (⟦r681:681⟧), ⟦b:cu-⟧ (⟦r157:157⟧), the initial ⟦b:c⟧ has disappeared before ⟦b:u⟧: as,
⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦i:which of the two⟧, ⟦b:ubĭ⟧, ⟦i:where⟧, ⟦b:unde⟧, ⟦i:whence⟧ (⟦r711:711⟧). For the conjunction ⟦b:ut⟧, ⟦b:utī⟧, ⟦i:that⟧, connection with this pronominal stem is much more doubtful. The ⟦b:c-⟧ appears in the compounds with ⟦b:sī⟧ and ⟦b:nē̆⟧: as, ⟦b:sī-cubī⟧ (cf. ⟦b:sī-quidem⟧, ⟦b:sī-quandō⟧), ⟦b:sī-cunde⟧, ⟦b:nē-cubi⟧, ⟦b:ne-cunde⟧, ⟦b:ne-cuter⟧.
⟦#147⟧
⟦b:d⟧ varies in a few words with ⟦b:l⟧: as old Latin ⟦b:dacruma⟧, ⟦i:tear⟧, for later ⟦b:lacrima⟧; ⟦b:dingua⟧, ⟦i:tongue⟧, for later ⟦b:lingua⟧; ⟦b:odor⟧, ⟦i:smell⟧, by the side of ⟦b:oleō⟧, ⟦i:I smell⟧.
⟦#148⟧
Very rarely, before labials, final ⟦b:d⟧ of the preposition ⟦b:ad⟧ varies with ⟦b:r⟧: as, old Latin ⟦b:arfuērunt⟧, ⟦i:they were present⟧, for later ⟦b:adfuērunt⟧ (⟦r2257:2257⟧); ⟦b:arvorsum⟧, ⟦i:against⟧, for ⟦b:advorsum⟧. The only instances of this in classical Latin are ⟦b:arbiter⟧, ⟦i:umpire⟧, and ⟦b:arcēssō⟧ (⟦r970:970⟧), ⟦i:I summon⟧, which shows ⟦b:r⟧ before a guttural.
⟦#149⟧
(1.) Final d after a long vowel disappeared in classical Latin: thus, in the ablative singular of ⟦b:-ā-⟧ and ⟦b:-o-⟧ stems (⟦r426:426⟧), and in the ablative-accusative forms ⟦b:mēd⟧, ⟦b:tēd⟧, ⟦b:sēd⟧ (⟦r648:648⟧). The prepositions ⟦b:prō⟧ and ⟦b:sē⟧ (⟦r1417:1417⟧) originally ended in ⟦b:-d⟧ which is still seen in ⟦b:prōdesse⟧, ⟦i:be of advantage⟧, ⟦b:prōd-īre⟧, ⟦i:go forth⟧; ⟦b:sēd-itiō⟧, ⟦i:a going-apart⟧, ⟦i:sedition⟧. According to the grammarians, the negative ⟦b:haud⟧ preserved its ⟦b:d⟧ before vowels, but lost it before consonants (⟦r1450:1450⟧).
(2.) Late inscriptions confuse final ⟦b:-d⟧ and ⟦b:-t⟧: as FECID (⟦r729:729⟧), ALIVT for ⟦b:aliud⟧. But in very old Latin ⟦b:-d⟧ in the third person singular seems to be the remnant of a secondary ending (cf. the Greek distinction of primary -ται and secondary -το).
⟦#150⟧
In a number of words ⟦b:f⟧ varies dialectically with ⟦b:h⟧. In some of these ⟦b:f⟧ appears to have been original, in others ⟦b:h⟧: as, old Latin ⟦b:fordeum⟧, ⟦i:barley⟧, for classical ⟦b:hordeum⟧; old Latin ⟦b:haba⟧, ⟦i:bean⟧, for classical ⟦b:faba⟧. The word ⟦b:fīlum⟧, ⟦i:thread⟧, appears as ⟦b:*hīlum⟧ in ⟦b:nihil⟧, ⟦i:nothing⟧, for ⟦b:*ne-hīlum⟧.
⟦#151⟧
⟦b:h⟧ being a weak sound (⟦r58:58⟧) was often lost between two like vowels, especially in rapid utterance: as, ⟦b:nīl⟧, ⟦i:nothing⟧, ⟦b:prēndere⟧, ⟦i:take⟧, ⟦b:vēmēns⟧, ⟦i:rapid⟧, by the side of ⟦b:nihil⟧, ⟦b:prehendere⟧, ⟦b:vehemēns⟧; and always ⟦b:nēmō⟧, ⟦i:nobody⟧, for ⟦b:*ne-hemō⟧, ⟦i:no man⟧.
⟦#152⟧
In some words ⟦b:h⟧ between two vowels is not original, but goes back to a guttural aspirate ⟦i:gh⟧. Before consonants this guttural appears: as, ⟦b:vehō⟧, ⟦i:I draw⟧, ⟦b:vectus⟧ (⟦r953:953⟧) from a stem ⟦b:vegh-⟧, ⟦b:trahō⟧, ⟦i:I drag⟧, ⟦b:tractus⟧ (⟦r953:953⟧) from a stem ⟦b:tragh-⟧.
⟦#153⟧
(1.) ⟦b:v⟧ not infrequently disappeared between two like vowels: as, ⟦b:dītior⟧, ⟦i:richer⟧, for ⟦b:dīvitior⟧; ⟦b:sīs⟧ (Cic. ⟦i:O.⟧ 154), for ⟦b:sī vīs⟧ (⟦r774:774⟧); ⟦b:lātrīna⟧, for ⟦b:lavatrīna⟧; ⟦b:fīnīsse⟧, for ⟦b:fīnīvisse⟧; ⟦b:dēlēram⟧, for ⟦b:dēlēveram⟧; and later also in perfect forms in which the preceding and following vowel differed: as, ⟦b:amāsse⟧, for ⟦b:amāvisse⟧. The abbreviated forms of the perfects in ⟦b:-vī⟧ (⟦r890:890⟧) were common in Cicero’s (⟦i:O.⟧ 157) and Quintilian’s (1, 6, 17) time. ⟦b:v⟧ also disappeared before ⟦b:o⟧ in ⟦b:deorsum⟧, ⟦b:seorsum⟧.
(2.) Old and original unsyllabic ⟦b:i⟧ (⟦r82:82⟧; ⟦r83:83⟧) disappeared everywhere between vowels. Wherever unsyllabic ⟦b:i⟧ appears between vowels it represents double ⟦b:i̭i̭⟧, and is the result of the assimilation of ⟦b:g⟧ to ⟦b:i̭⟧ (⟦r166:166, 9⟧), or ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:i̭⟧ (⟦r166:166, 9⟧), or of the combination of two ⟦b:i̭⟧’s: as in ⟦b:ei-i̭us⟧, ⟦b:quoi̭-i̭us⟧ (⟦b:eius⟧, ⟦b:quoius⟧ = ⟦b:cuius⟧, ⟦r688:688⟧). See ⟦r23:23⟧; 166, 9. In all these cases the first ⟦b:i̭⟧ joined to the preceding vowel (⟦r83:83⟧) formed with it a diphthong, and the syllable is thus long (⟦r133:133, 2⟧).
(3.) The combinations of unsyllabic (⟦r83:83⟧) ⟦b:ṷ⟧ with the vowel ⟦b:u⟧ and of unsyllabic ⟦b:i̭⟧ with the vowel ⟦b:i⟧ were avoided in classical Latin; see ⟦r52:52⟧.
(4.) In composition, unsyllabic (⟦r82:82⟧) ⟦b:i̭⟧ after a consonant became syllabic in ⟦b:quoniam⟧, ⟦i:since⟧, for ⟦b:quomi̭am⟧ (⟦r164:164, 5⟧), and ⟦b:etiam⟧, ⟦i:also⟧, for ⟦b:eti̭am⟧ (both compounds with ⟦b:iam⟧).
⟦#154⟧
In early Latin ⟦b:s⟧ between two vowels was voiced (⟦r75:75⟧), and in the fourth century B.C. this voiced ⟦b:s⟧ changed into ⟦b:r⟧. According to Cicero (⟦i:Fam.⟧ 9, 21, 2) L. Papīrius Crassus, consul in 336 B.C., changed his family name ⟦b:Papīsius⟧ to ⟦b:Papīrius⟧. Old inscriptions show frequently ⟦b:s⟧ for ⟦b:r⟧: as, ASA, ⟦i:altar⟧, AVSELII. This change of intervocalic ⟦b:s⟧ to ⟦b:r⟧ plays an important part in declension, conjugation, and derivation: as,
Nominative ⟦b:iūs⟧, ⟦i:right⟧, genitive ⟦b:iūris⟧; ⟦b:spērō⟧, ⟦i:I hope⟧, derived from ⟦b:spēs⟧; ⟦b:nefārius⟧, ⟦i:wicked⟧, from ⟦b:nefās⟧; ⟦b:gerō⟧, ⟦i:I carry⟧, from a stem ⟦b:ges-⟧ which appears in ⟦b:ges-sī⟧, ⟦b:ges-tus⟧ (⟦r953:953⟧); ⟦b:erō⟧, ⟦i:I shall be⟧, from the stem ⟦b:es-⟧ in ⟦b:esse⟧; the subjunctive ending ⟦b:-sem⟧ in ⟦b:es-sem⟧ appears as ⟦b:-rem⟧ after vowels: as, ⟦b:stārem⟧; the infinitive ending (⟦r894:894⟧, ⟦r895:895⟧) ⟦b:-se⟧ in ⟦b:es-se⟧ appears as ⟦b:-re⟧ after vowels: as, ⟦b:legere⟧, for ⟦b:*legese⟧, ⟦i:to read⟧, ⟦b:stāre⟧, for ⟦b:*stāse⟧, ⟦i:to stand⟧. Where all oblique cases show ⟦b:-r-⟧ and only the nominative singular ⟦b:-s⟧, the latter is sometimes changed to ⟦b:-r⟧ by analogy: as, ⟦b:arbor⟧, ⟦i:tree⟧, ⟦b:honor⟧, ⟦i:honour⟧, for original ⟦b:arbōs⟧, ⟦b:honōs⟧, by analogy to the oblique cases ⟦b:arboris⟧, ⟦b:arborī⟧, ⟦b:honōris⟧, ⟦b:honōrī⟧, etc. (⟦r487:487⟧, ⟦r488:488⟧). The final ⟦b:-s⟧ of the prefix ⟦b:dis-⟧ follows this rule: as, ⟦b:dir-imō⟧, ⟦i:I take apart⟧, for ⟦b:*dis-emō⟧; but an initial ⟦b:s-⟧ of the second member of a compound remains unchanged: as, ⟦b:dē-sinō⟧, ⟦i:I stop⟧.
⟦#155⟧
Wherever intervocalic ⟦b:s⟧ is found in classical Latin it is not original, but the result (⟦i:a.⟧) of earlier ⟦b:-ns-⟧: as, ⟦b:formōsus⟧, ⟦i:handsome⟧, for ⟦b:formōnsus⟧ (⟦r63:63⟧); (⟦i:b.⟧) of earlier ⟦b:-ss-⟧ (⟦r170:170, 7⟧): as, ⟦b:ūsus⟧ for ⟦b:*ūssus⟧, ⟦i:use⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧); ⟦b:causa⟧, ⟦i:thing⟧, for ⟦b:caussa⟧ (Quint. 1, 7, 20); or (⟦i:c.⟧) it occurs in borrowed words like ⟦b:asinus⟧, ⟦i:ass⟧. (⟦i:d.⟧) There are a few words in which an ⟦b:r⟧ in a neighbouring syllable seems to have prevented the change: as ⟦b:miser⟧, ⟦i:miserable⟧ (⟦r173:173⟧).
⟦#156⟧
Before the ⟦b:o⟧ described in ⟦r142:142⟧ ⟦b:qu⟧ changed to ⟦b:c⟧: as, ⟦b:incola⟧, ⟦i:inhabitant⟧, for ⟦b:*inquola⟧, from ⟦b:*inquela⟧; the stem ⟦b:quel-⟧ appears in ⟦b:in-quil-īnus⟧, ⟦i:lodger⟧.
⟦#157⟧
As ⟦b:v⟧ before ⟦b:u⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧), so ⟦b:qu⟧ was not tolerated before ⟦b:u⟧, but changed to ⟦b:c⟧.
Hence when, about the beginning of our era, the ⟦b:o⟧ of ⟦b:quom⟧, ⟦i:when⟧, ⟦b:sequontur⟧, ⟦i:they followed⟧, changed to ⟦b:u⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧), they became ⟦b:cum⟧, ⟦b:secuntur⟧; thus ⟦b:equos⟧ but ⟦b:ecus⟧, ⟦i:horse⟧ (⟦r452:452⟧); ⟦b:reliquom⟧ but RELICVM, ⟦i:the rest⟧; ⟦b:loquor⟧, ⟦i:I speak⟧, but ⟦b:locūtus⟧ (⟦r978:978⟧). Much later, in the second century of our era, the grammarians restored the ⟦b:qu⟧ before ⟦b:u⟧ by analogy to those forms in the paradigm in which ⟦b:qu⟧ came before other vowels: as, ⟦b:sequuntur⟧ for ⟦b:secuntur⟧ by analogy to ⟦b:sequor⟧, ⟦b:sequeris⟧, ⟦b:sequitur⟧, ⟦b:sequimur⟧, ⟦b:sequimini⟧, etc.; ⟦b:equus⟧, ⟦b:equum⟧, for ⟦b:ecus⟧, ⟦b:ecum⟧, by analogy to ⟦b:equī⟧, ⟦b:equō⟧, ⟦b:eque⟧, ⟦b:equōrum⟧, ⟦b:equīs⟧, ⟦b:equōs⟧.
⟦#158⟧
⟦b:qu⟧ before consonants or when final changed to ⟦b:c⟧: as, ⟦b:relictus⟧ from the stem ⟦b:liqu-⟧, ⟦i:leave⟧ (present, ⟦b:linquō⟧, ⟦r938:938⟧); ⟦b:ac⟧, ⟦i:and⟧, for ⟦b:*atc⟧, by apocope from ⟦b:atque⟧; ⟦b:nec⟧, ⟦i:nor⟧, by apocope from ⟦b:neque⟧. See also ⟦b:*torctus⟧ (⟦r170:170, 3⟧), ⟦b:quīnctus⟧ (⟦r170:170, 4⟧).
⟦#159⟧
When in the process of early word formation a ⟦b:t⟧ was followed by another ⟦b:t⟧, the combination ⟦b:tt⟧, unless followed by ⟦b:r⟧, changed to ⟦b:ss⟧: as, ⟦b:obsessus⟧, ⟦i:besieged⟧, ⟦i:sat upon⟧, for ⟦b:*obsettus⟧, from ⟦b:*obsed-tus⟧ (cf. ⟦b:sedeō⟧). After long vowels, nasals, and liquids this double ⟦b:ss⟧ was simplified to ⟦b:s⟧ (⟦r170:170, 7⟧): as, ⟦b:ūsus⟧ from ⟦b:*ūt-tus⟧, ⟦i:used⟧ (cf. ⟦b:ūtor⟧); ⟦b:scānsus⟧, ⟦i:climbed⟧, from ⟦b:*scant-tus⟧ for ⟦b:*scandtus⟧ (cf. ⟦b:scandō⟧).
In this way arose a suffix ⟦b:-sus⟧ (⟦r906:906⟧, ⟦r912:912⟧) for the past participle of verbs ending in a dental, and this spread to other verbs (⟦r912:912⟧): as ⟦b:mānsus⟧, ⟦i:stayed⟧, from ⟦b:maneō⟧ (⟦r1000:1000⟧), ⟦b:pulsus⟧, ⟦i:pushed⟧, from ⟦b:pellō⟧ (⟦r932:932⟧). The regular participles of these two verbs still appear in the derivative verbs ⟦b:mantāre⟧ and ⟦b:pultāre⟧, which presuppose the past participles ⟦b:*mantus⟧ and ⟦b:*pultus⟧ (⟦r371:371⟧). If the double ⟦b:tt⟧ was followed by ⟦b:r⟧ it changed to ⟦b:st⟧: as, ⟦b:assestrīx⟧ from ⟦b:*assettrīx⟧, while ⟦b:*assettor⟧ changed to ⟦b:assessor⟧.
⟦#160⟧
But wherever the combination ⟦b:tt⟧ arose in historical times it remained unchanged: as, ⟦b:attineō⟧; ⟦b:cette⟧, syncopated for ⟦b:cé-d(i)te⟧, i.e. the particle ⟦b:ce⟧ (⟦r93:93, 3⟧) which is here proclitic, and the imperative ⟦b:date⟧, ⟦i:give⟧.
⟦#161⟧
Initial ⟦b:dv⟧ (⟦i:dṷ⟧) changed to ⟦b:b⟧, unless the ⟦b:v⟧ (⟦i:ṷ⟧) was converted into the corresponding vowel: as, ⟦b:bis⟧, ⟦i:twice⟧, for ⟦b:*dṷis⟧ (cf. ⟦b:duo⟧); ⟦b:bidēns⟧ for ⟦b:*dṷidens⟧, by the side of old Latin ⟦b:duidēns⟧ with vocalic ⟦b:u⟧; ⟦b:bonus⟧, ⟦i:good⟧, for ⟦b:dṷonus⟧, by the side of trisyllabic ⟦b:duonus⟧; ⟦b:bellum⟧, ⟦i:war⟧, for ⟦b:*dṷellum⟧, by the side of ⟦b:duellum⟧ with vocalic ⟦b:u⟧; ⟦b:bēs⟧, ⟦i:two thirds⟧, for ⟦b:*dṷēs⟧ (⟦r2427:2427⟧). Cicero (⟦i:O.⟧ 153) notes that the change of ⟦b:duellum⟧ to ⟦b:bellum⟧ affected even the proper name ⟦b:Duellius⟧ (name of the admiral who won the naval victory over the Carthaginians in 260 B.C.) which was changed to ⟦b:Bellius⟧. Plautus always scans ⟦b:dṷellum⟧ disyllabic with synizesis (⟦r2503:2503⟧).

title: Changes of Consonant Groups
text:
⟦#162⟧
Many groups of consonants undergo changes in order to facilitate their pronunciation in rapid speech. These changes involve (⟦i:a.⟧) Assimilation of consonants; (⟦i:b.⟧) the development of consonantal glides; (⟦i:c.⟧) the loss of one member of the group; and (⟦i:d.⟧) the development of a vowel between the consonants.

title: Consonant Change: Assimilation
text:
⟦#163⟧
Of two successive consonants belonging to different syllables (⟦r175:175⟧), the first is, as a rule, assimilated to the second (⟦i:regressive assimilation⟧), rarely the second to the first (⟦i:progressive assimilation⟧). A consonant may be assimilated, either entirely or partially, to another consonant.
Assimilation is very common in prepositions prefixed to a verb.
⟦#164⟧
Partial assimilation. (1.) A voiced mute before an unvoiced consonant became unvoiced: as, ⟦b:rēx⟧, ⟦i:king⟧, for ⟦b:*rēgs⟧ (cf. ⟦b:rēgis⟧); ⟦b:rēxī⟧, ⟦i:I guided⟧, for ⟦b:*rēgsī⟧ (cf. ⟦b:regō⟧); ⟦b:rēctus⟧, ⟦i:guided⟧, for ⟦b:*rēgtus⟧; ⟦b:scrīpsī⟧, ⟦i:I wrote⟧, for ⟦b:*scrībsī⟧ (cf. ⟦b:scribō⟧); ⟦b:scrīptus⟧, ⟦i:written⟧, for ⟦b:*scribtus⟧; ⟦b:trāxī⟧, ⟦i:I dragged⟧, for ⟦b:*trāghsī⟧; ⟦b:tractus⟧, ⟦i:dragged⟧, for ⟦b:*traghtus⟧ (⟦r152:152⟧). The spelling did not always conform to this pronunciation: as, ⟦b:urbs⟧, ⟦i:city⟧, pronounced ⟦b:urps⟧ (⟦r54:54⟧) but spelled with ⟦b:b⟧ by analogy to the oblique cases ⟦b:urbis⟧, ⟦b:urbem⟧, etc.; ⟦b:obtineō⟧, ⟦i:I get⟧, pronounced ⟦b:optineō⟧.
(2.) An unvoiced mute before a voiced consonant became voiced. The prepositions ⟦b:ob⟧, ⟦b:ab⟧, ⟦b:sub⟧, for ⟦b:*op⟧, ⟦b:*ap⟧, ⟦b:*sup⟧, owe their final ⟦b:b⟧ to their frequent position before voiced mutes: as, ⟦b:obdūcō⟧, ⟦b:abdīcō⟧, ⟦b:sub dīvō⟧. The forms ⟦b:*op⟧ (still preserved in ⟦b:op-eriō⟧, ⟦i:I close⟧, ⟦r1019:1019⟧) ⟦b:*ap⟧ (preserved in ⟦b:ap-erio⟧, ⟦i:I open⟧, ⟦r1019:1019⟧; cf. Greek ἀπό) and ⟦b:*sup⟧ (preserved in the adjective ⟦b:supīnus⟧, ⟦i:supine⟧) were then crowded out by ⟦b:ob⟧, ⟦b:ab⟧, and ⟦b:sub⟧.
(3.) Nasals changed their place of articulation to that of the following consonant. Thus, dental ⟦b:n⟧ before the labials ⟦b:p⟧ and ⟦b:b⟧ became labial ⟦b:m⟧: as, ⟦b:imbibō⟧, ⟦i:I drink in⟧, ⟦b:impendeō⟧, ⟦i:I hang over⟧. Labial ⟦b:m⟧ before the gutturals ⟦b:c⟧ and ⟦b:g⟧ became guttural ⟦b:n⟧ (⟦r62:62⟧): as, ⟦b:prīnceps⟧, ⟦i:leader⟧, ⟦b:singulī⟧, ⟦i:severally⟧ (the original labials appear in ⟦b:prīmus⟧, ⟦b:semel⟧ (⟦r138:138⟧)); ⟦b:hunc⟧ for ⟦b:*homce⟧ (⟦r662:662⟧). Labial ⟦b:m⟧ before the dentals ⟦b:t⟧, ⟦b:d⟧, ⟦b:s⟧ became dental ⟦b:n⟧: as, ⟦b:cōnsecrō⟧, ⟦i:I consecrate⟧, from ⟦b:com⟧ (⟦b:cum⟧) and ⟦b:sacrō⟧; ⟦b:tantus⟧, ⟦i:so great⟧, from ⟦b:tam⟧; ⟦b:quondam⟧, ⟦i:once⟧, from ⟦b:quom⟧; ⟦b:tandem⟧, ⟦i:at length⟧, from ⟦b:tam⟧. But sometimes the etymological spelling was retained: as, ⟦b:quamdiū⟧, ⟦i:as long as⟧. But ⟦b:m⟧ does not change to ⟦b:n⟧ before ⟦b:t⟧ or ⟦b:s⟧ in the inflection of verbs and nouns, where ⟦b:mt⟧, ⟦b:ms⟧ develop into ⟦b:mpt⟧, ⟦b:mps⟧ (⟦r167:167⟧): as, ⟦b:sūmptus⟧, ⟦b:sūmpsī⟧, from ⟦b:sūmō⟧.
(4.) ⟦b:p⟧ and ⟦b:b⟧ before ⟦b:n⟧ changed to ⟦b:m⟧: as, ⟦b:somnus⟧, ⟦i:sleep⟧, for ⟦b:*sop-nus⟧ (cf. ⟦b:sopor⟧); ⟦b:omnis⟧, ⟦i:all⟧, for ⟦b:*op-nis⟧ (cf. ⟦b:opēs⟧); ⟦b:Samnium⟧, for ⟦b:*Sabnium⟧ (cf. ⟦b:Sabīnī⟧).
(5.) ⟦b:m⟧ before unsyllabic ⟦b:i⟧ (⟦b:i̭⟧) became ⟦b:n⟧: as, ⟦b:quoniam⟧ (with vocalic ⟦b:i⟧; 153, 4), ⟦i:since⟧, for ⟦b:*quoni̭am⟧ from ⟦b:quom iam⟧ (⟦r1882:1882⟧); ⟦b:coniungō⟧, ⟦i:I join together⟧, for ⟦b:*comiungō⟧.
(6.) ⟦b:c⟧ between ⟦b:n⟧ and ⟦b:l⟧, and before ⟦b:m⟧, changed to ⟦b:g⟧: as, ⟦b:angulus⟧, ⟦i:corner⟧, with anaptyctical (⟦r172:172⟧) vowel ⟦b:u⟧ for ⟦b:*anglus⟧, from ⟦b:*anclus⟧ (cf. ⟦b:ancus⟧); ⟦b:segmentum⟧, ⟦i:section⟧, from the stem ⟦b:sec-⟧ in ⟦b:secāre⟧.
⟦#165⟧
It appears that at a very early period the neighbourhood of a nasal changed an unvoiced mute into a voiced one: as, ⟦b:ē-mungō⟧, ⟦i:I clean out⟧, by the side of ⟦b:mūcus⟧; ⟦b:pangō⟧, ⟦i:I fix⟧, by the side of ⟦b:pāc-⟧ in ⟦b:pāx⟧, ⟦i:peace⟧ (gen. ⟦b:pāc-is⟧).
⟦#166⟧
Entire assimilation. (1.) One mute is assimilated to another: thus ⟦b:p⟧ or ⟦b:b⟧ to ⟦b:c⟧: as, ⟦b:suc-currō⟧, ⟦i:I assist⟧; ⟦b:t⟧ or ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:c⟧: as, ⟦b:sic-cus⟧, ⟦i:dry⟧ (cf. ⟦b:sit-is⟧, ⟦i:thirst⟧), ⟦b:accipiō⟧, ⟦i:I accept⟧; ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:g⟧: as, ⟦b:agglūtinō⟧, ⟦i:I glue on⟧; ⟦b:t⟧ or ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:qu⟧: as, ⟦b:quicquam⟧, ⟦i:anything⟧; ⟦b:t⟧ or ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:p⟧: as, ⟦b:appellō⟧, ⟦i:I call⟧; ⟦b:quippe⟧, ⟦i:why?⟧ (⟦r1690:1690⟧).
(2.) A mute is assimilated to a spirant: thus, ⟦b:p⟧ to ⟦b:f⟧ in ⟦b:officīna⟧, ⟦i:workshop⟧, for ⟦b:*opficīna⟧, syncopated form of ⟦b:*opificīna⟧; ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:f⟧: as, ⟦b:afferō⟧, ⟦i:I bring hither⟧; when ⟦b:t⟧ is thus assimilated to ⟦b:s⟧ the result is ⟦b:ss⟧ after a short vowel, and ⟦b:s⟧ after a long vowel (⟦r170:170, 7⟧) or when final (⟦r171:171⟧); as, in the ⟦b:-s-⟧ perfects, ⟦b:concussī⟧, ⟦i:I shook⟧, for ⟦b:*concutsī⟧ (⟦b:concutiō⟧, ⟦r961:961⟧); ⟦b:messuī⟧, ⟦i:I mowed⟧, for ⟦b:*metsuī⟧ (⟦b:metō⟧, ⟦r835:835⟧); ⟦b:suāsī⟧, ⟦i:I advised⟧, for ⟦b:*suātsī⟧ (⟦b:suādeō⟧, ⟦r1000:1000⟧); ⟦b:clausī⟧, ⟦i:I shut⟧, for ⟦b:*clautsī⟧ (⟦b:claudō⟧, ⟦r958:958⟧); ⟦b:haesī⟧, ⟦i:I stuck⟧, for ⟦b:haes-sī⟧ (⟦r868:868⟧) from ⟦b:haerēre⟧, stem ⟦b:haes-⟧ (⟦r154:154⟧); in the same way ⟦b:possum⟧, ⟦i:I can⟧, for ⟦b:*potsum⟧ (cf. ⟦b:pot-est⟧, ⟦r752:752⟧); ⟦b:prōsum⟧, ⟦i:I am of advantage⟧, for ⟦b:*prōtsum⟧ (cf. ⟦b:prōd-esse⟧); ⟦b:legēns⟧, ⟦i:reading⟧, for ⟦b:*legents⟧ (from the stem ⟦b:legent-⟧, cf. genitive ⟦b:legent-is⟧). An ⟦b:s⟧ is never assimilated to a following ⟦b:t⟧: as, ⟦b:haustus⟧, ⟦i:drained⟧ (⟦r1014:1014⟧), from the stem ⟦b:haus-⟧, present ⟦b:hauriō⟧ (⟦r154:154⟧). Forms like the rare ⟦b:hausūrus⟧ (Verg.) are made after the analogy of dental stems.
(3.) One spirant, ⟦b:s⟧, is assimilated to another, ⟦b:f⟧: as, ⟦b:difficilis⟧, ⟦i:difficult⟧, ⟦b:differō⟧, ⟦i:I am unlike⟧, from ⟦b:dis⟧ and ⟦b:facilis⟧, ⟦b:ferō⟧.
(4.) A mute is assimilated to a nasal: thus ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:m⟧ in ⟦b:mamma⟧, ⟦i:woman’s breast⟧, from the stem ⟦b:mad-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:madeō⟧, ⟦r1006:1006⟧); ⟦b:rāmus⟧, ⟦i:branch⟧, ⟦b:rāmentum⟧, ⟦i:splinter⟧, from the stem ⟦b:rād-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:rādō⟧, ⟦r958:958⟧) with simplification of the double ⟦b:m⟧ after the long vowel. ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:n⟧ in ⟦b:mercēnārius⟧, ⟦i:hireling⟧, from the stem ⟦b:mercēd-⟧, ⟦i:reward⟧, (for ⟦b:mercennarius⟧, see ⟦r133:133⟧, 1); ⟦b:p⟧ to ⟦b:m⟧ in ⟦b:summus⟧, ⟦i:highest⟧, from the stem ⟦b:sup-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:super⟧). A progressive assimilation of ⟦b:nd⟧ to ⟦b:nn⟧ belongs to the Oscan dialect, and occurs only very rarely in Latin: as, ⟦b:tennitur⟧ (Ter.), ⟦b:distennite⟧ (Plaut.) See ⟦r924:924⟧; ⟦r950:950⟧.
(5.) One nasal, ⟦b:n⟧, is assimilated to another, ⟦b:m⟧: as ⟦b:immōtus⟧, ⟦i:unmoved⟧. But an ⟦b:m⟧ before ⟦b:n⟧ is never assimilated: as, ⟦b:amnis⟧, ⟦i:river⟧.
(6.) Mutes or nasals are assimilated to liquids; thus ⟦b:n⟧ to ⟦b:l⟧: as, ⟦b:homullus⟧, ⟦i:manikin⟧, for ⟦b:*homon-lus⟧ (cf. ⟦b:homun-culus⟧); ⟦b:ūllus⟧ (⟦r274:274⟧); ⟦b:d⟧ to ⟦b:l⟧: as, ⟦b:sella⟧, ⟦i:seat⟧, for ⟦b:*sed-la⟧ from the stem ⟦b:sed-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:sedeō⟧); ⟦b:caelum⟧, ⟦i:chisel⟧, from the stem ⟦b:caed-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:caedō⟧) with simplification of the double ⟦b:l⟧ after the diphthong (⟦r170:170, 7⟧); ⟦b:n⟧ to ⟦b:r⟧: as, ⟦b:irruō⟧, ⟦i:I rush in⟧; and with progressive assimilation ⟦b:n⟧ to a preceding ⟦b:l⟧: as, ⟦b:tollō⟧, ⟦i:I lift⟧, for ⟦b:*tolnō⟧ (⟦r833:833⟧); ⟦b:fallō⟧, ⟦i:I cheat⟧ (⟦r932:932⟧); ⟦b:pellō⟧, ⟦i:I push⟧ (⟦r932:932⟧). But no assimilation is to be assumed for ⟦b:parricīda⟧, which does not stand for ⟦b:patricīda⟧ (⟦r133:133, 1⟧).
(7.) One liquid, ⟦b:r⟧, is assimilated to another, ⟦b:l⟧: as, ⟦b:pelliciō⟧, ⟦i:I lead astray⟧ (⟦r956:956⟧), for ⟦b:*per-liciō⟧; ⟦b:agellus⟧, ⟦i:small field⟧, for ⟦b:*agerlos⟧; ⟦b:pūllus⟧, ⟦i:clean⟧, from ⟦b:*pūrlos⟧ (cf. ⟦b:pūrus⟧, ⟦i:clean⟧).
(8.) A spirant, ⟦b:s⟧, is assimilated to a preceding liquid in ⟦b:velle⟧, ⟦i:wish⟧, for ⟦b:*velse⟧, ⟦b:ferre⟧, ⟦i:carry⟧, for ⟦b:*ferse⟧ (the infinitive ending ⟦b:-se⟧ appears in ⟦b:es-se⟧, ⟦r895:895⟧); ⟦b:facillimus⟧, ⟦i:easiest⟧, for ⟦b:*facilsimus⟧ (⟦r345:345⟧); ⟦b:sacerrimus⟧, ⟦i:holiest⟧, for ⟦b:*sacersimus⟧ (⟦r344:344⟧). But where ⟦b:ls⟧ and ⟦b:rs⟧ are not original but the result of lightening (170, 3; ⟦r10:10⟧) they remain unchanged: as, ⟦b:arsī⟧, ⟦i:I burnt⟧, for ⟦b:*artsī⟧ from the stem ⟦b:ard-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:ardeō⟧, ⟦r1000:1000⟧); ⟦b:alsī⟧, ⟦i:I felt cold⟧, for ⟦b:*alcsī⟧ from the stem ⟦b:alg-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:algeō⟧, ⟦r1000:1000⟧).
(9.) ⟦b:g⟧ and ⟦b:d⟧ were assimilated to a following unsyllabic ⟦b:i⟧ (⟦b:i̭⟧) the result being (⟦r153:153, 2⟧) ⟦b:ii⟧ (⟦b:i̭i̭⟧); thus ⟦b:peiior⟧, ⟦i:worse⟧, for ⟦b:*ped-i̭or⟧, from the stem ⟦b:ped-⟧ (⟦r532:532⟧), whence also the superlative ⟦b:pessimus⟧ for ⟦b:*petsimus⟧ (⟦r166:166, 2⟧); ⟦b:maiior⟧, ⟦i:greater⟧, for ⟦b:*mag-i̭or⟧ (the stem ⟦b:mag-⟧ appears in ⟦b:magis⟧); ⟦b:aiiō⟧, ⟦i:I say⟧, for ⟦b:*ag-i̭ō⟧ (the stem ⟦b:ag-⟧ appears in ⟦b:ad-ag-ium⟧, ⟦b:prōd-ig-ium⟧, ⟦r219:219⟧). These forms were pronounced by Cicero with doubled ⟦b:i̭⟧ (⟦r23:23⟧), and traces of the spelling with double ⟦b:ii⟧ are still found (⟦r23:23⟧), though in common practice only one ⟦b:i⟧ is written (⟦r153:153, 2⟧). On the confusion of syllabic quantity with vowel quantity in these words, see ⟦r133:133⟧, 2.

title: Consonantal Glides
text:
⟦#167⟧
Pronunciation of two successive consonants is sometimes facilitated by the insertion of a consonant which serves as a glide. Such insertion is not frequent.
In inflection a ⟦b:p⟧ was thus developed between ⟦b:m⟧ and ⟦b:s⟧, between ⟦b:m⟧ and ⟦b:l⟧, and between ⟦b:m⟧ and ⟦b:t⟧ (elsewhere ⟦b:mt⟧ changed to ⟦b:nt⟧, see ⟦r164:164⟧, 3): as, ⟦b:sūmpsī⟧, ⟦i:I took⟧, ⟦b:sūmptus⟧, ⟦i:taken⟧, from ⟦b:sūmere⟧ for ⟦b:*sūmsī⟧, ⟦b:*sūmtus⟧; and in the corresponding forms of ⟦b:cōmō⟧, ⟦b:dēmō⟧, ⟦b:prōmō⟧ (⟦r953:953⟧); ⟦b:exemplum⟧, ⟦i:pattern⟧, for ⟦b:*exemlum⟧ from the stem ⟦b:em-⟧, ⟦i:take⟧ (cf. ⟦b:eximere⟧, ⟦r103:103, ⟧⟦r103:⟦b:a⟧⟧).

title: Disappearance
text:
⟦#168⟧
A word may be lightened by the disappearance of an initial, a medial, or a final consonant.
Disappearance of an initial consonant is sometimes called ⟦i:Aphaeresis⟧, of a medial, ⟦i:Syncope⟧, of a final, ⟦i:Apocope⟧.
⟦#169⟧
Initial disappearance. (1.) Initial ⟦b:tl⟧ changed to ⟦b:l⟧: as, ⟦b:lātus⟧, ⟦i:borne⟧, for ⟦b:*tlātus⟧ from ⟦b:tollō⟧ (⟦r187:187⟧, ⟦r917:917⟧).
(2.) Initial ⟦b:gn⟧ changed to ⟦b:n⟧: as, ⟦b:nātus⟧, ⟦i:born⟧, for earlier GNATVS from the stem ⟦b:gen-⟧, ⟦b:gnā⟧ (⟦r187:187⟧); ⟦b:nōscō⟧, ⟦i:I find out⟧, for ⟦b:gnōscō⟧, GNOSCIER (⟦r897:897⟧); ⟦b:nārus⟧, ⟦i:knowing⟧, for the more frequent ⟦b:gnārus⟧, ⟦b:nāvus⟧, ⟦i:active⟧, for ⟦b:gnāvus⟧. Cf. the compounds ⟦b:cō-gnātus⟧, ⟦b:cō-gnōscō⟧, ⟦b:ī-gnārus⟧, ⟦b:ī-gnāvus⟧ (⟦r170:170, 6⟧) which preserve the ⟦b:g⟧. But ⟦b:Gnaeus⟧ retained its ⟦b:G⟧.
(3.) Initial ⟦b:d⟧ when followed by consonant ⟦b:i⟧ (⟦i:i̭⟧), disappeared: as, ⟦b:Iovis⟧, ⟦b:Iūpiter⟧, for ⟦b:*Di̭ovis⟧, ⟦b:*Di̭ūpiter⟧. Where the ⟦b:i⟧ was vocalic, ⟦b:d⟧ was retained: as, ⟦b:dīus⟧.
(4.) Initial ⟦b:stl-⟧ first changed to ⟦b:sl⟧ and then to ⟦b:l⟧: as, Old Latin ⟦b:stlocus⟧, ⟦i:place⟧, ⟦b:stlīs⟧, ⟦i:law-suit⟧ (Quint. 1, 4, 16), STLOC, SLIS, classical ⟦b:locus⟧, ⟦b:līs⟧; also ⟦b:lātus⟧, ⟦i:wide⟧, for ⟦b:*stlātus⟧. That a form ⟦b:*slocus⟧ existed is proved by ⟦b:īlicō⟧ (⟦r698:698⟧, ⟦r703:703⟧) from ⟦b:*in-slocō⟧, ⟦i:on the spot⟧ (⟦r170:170, 2⟧).
⟦#170⟧
Medial Disappearance. (1.) ⟦b:c⟧, ⟦b:g⟧, ⟦b:p⟧, and ⟦b:b⟧ disappear before ⟦b:s⟧ followed by an unvoiced consonant: as, ⟦b:sescentī⟧, ⟦i:six hundred⟧, for ⟦b:*sexcentī⟧ from ⟦b:sex⟧; ⟦b:illūstris⟧, ⟦i:resplendent⟧, for ⟦b:*illūcstris⟧ from ⟦b:lūceō⟧; ⟦b:discō⟧, ⟦i:I learn⟧, from ⟦b:*dicscō⟧ for ⟦b:*di-tc-scō⟧ (⟦r834:834⟧), a reduplicated present from the root ⟦b:dec-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:decet⟧) like ⟦b:gignō⟧ (from the root ⟦b:gen-⟧), and ⟦b:sīdō⟧ (for ⟦b:*si-sd-ō⟧, 170, 2, from the root ⟦b:sed-⟧, ⟦r829:829⟧). Sometimes prepositions follow this rule: as, ⟦b:asportō⟧, ⟦i:I carry off⟧, for ⟦b:*absportō⟧, ⟦b:suscipiō⟧, ⟦i:I undertake⟧, for ⟦b:*subscipiō⟧ (⟦b:subs⟧ formed from ⟦b:sub⟧ like ⟦b:abs⟧ from ⟦b:ab⟧; ⟦b:sub-cipiō⟧ gives ⟦b:succipiō⟧); occasionally also ⟦b:ecferō⟧, for ⟦b:exferō⟧, ⟦i:I carry out⟧. But more frequently prepositional compounds remain unchanged: as, ⟦b:obscūrus⟧, ⟦i:dark⟧; ⟦b:abscēdō⟧, ⟦i:I withdraw⟧. In some words the lost consonant has been restored by analogy: as, ⟦b:sextus⟧, ⟦i:sixth⟧, for ⟦b:*sestus⟧ (cf. ⟦b:Sēstius⟧) after ⟦b:sex⟧; ⟦b:textor⟧, ⟦i:weaver⟧, for ⟦b:*testor⟧ after ⟦b:texō⟧.
(2.) ⟦b:s⟧ before voiced consonants was voiced (⟦r75:75⟧) and is dropped. If a consonant precedes the ⟦b:s⟧ this is dropped also. In either case the preceding vowel is lengthened. Voiced ⟦b:s⟧ alone is dropped: as, ⟦b:prīmus⟧, ⟦i:first⟧, for ⟦b:*prīs-mus⟧ (cf. ⟦b:prīs-cus⟧); ⟦b:cānus⟧, ⟦i:gray⟧, for ⟦b:*casnus⟧ (cf. ⟦b:cas-cus⟧); adverb ⟦b:pōne⟧, ⟦i:behind⟧, for ⟦b:*posne⟧ (cf. ⟦b:pos⟧, ⟦r1410:1410⟧); ⟦b:dīlābī⟧, ⟦i:glide apart⟧, for ⟦b:*dislābi⟧; ⟦b:īdem⟧, ⟦i:the same⟧, for ISDEM (⟦r678:678⟧); ⟦b:iūdex⟧, ⟦i:judge⟧, for ⟦b:iūsdex⟧; ⟦b:trēdecim⟧, ⟦i:thirteen⟧, for ⟦b:*trēsdecim⟧. And with subsequent shortening of the final syllable (⟦r130:130, 3⟧) ⟦b:abin⟧, ⟦i:goest thou?⟧ for ⟦b:abisn(e)⟧; ⟦b:viden⟧, ⟦i:seest thou?⟧ for ⟦b:vidēsn(e)⟧. Voiced ⟦b:s⟧ with the preceding consonant is dropped: as, ⟦b:trādūcō⟧, ⟦i:I lead across⟧, ⟦b:trānō⟧, ⟦i:I swim across⟧, for ⟦b:trānsdūcō⟧, ⟦b:trānsnō⟧; but in these prepositional compounds the ⟦b:-ns⟧ was often retained: as, ⟦b:trānsmittō⟧, ⟦i:I send across⟧; ⟦b:sēnī⟧, ⟦i:six each⟧, for ⟦b:*secsnī⟧; ⟦b:sēmēnstris⟧, ⟦i:every six months⟧, for ⟦b:secsmēnstris⟧; ⟦b:sēvirī⟧, ⟦i:the Board of Six⟧, for ⟦b:secsvirī⟧; ⟦b:āla⟧, ⟦i:wing⟧, for ⟦b:*acsla⟧ (cf. ⟦b:ax-illa⟧, Cic. ⟦i:O.⟧ 153); ⟦b:māvolō⟧ (⟦r779:779⟧) for ⟦b:magsvolō⟧ from ⟦b:magisvolō⟧, ⟦r396:396⟧; ⟦b:tōles⟧ (plural), ⟦i:goiter⟧, for ⟦b:*tōnsles⟧ (cf. ⟦b:tōnsillae⟧, ⟦i:tonsils⟧); ⟦b:pīlum⟧, ⟦i:pestle⟧, for ⟦b:*pīnslum⟧ from ⟦b:pīnsere⟧, ⟦i:crush⟧; two consonants and voiced ⟦b:s⟧ are dropped in ⟦b:scāla⟧, ⟦i:stair⟧, for ⟦b:*scand-sla⟧ (cf. ⟦b:scandō⟧).
(3.) ⟦b:c⟧ falls away when it stands between a liquid and ⟦b:t⟧, ⟦b:s⟧, ⟦b:m⟧, or ⟦b:n⟧: as, ⟦b:ultus⟧, ⟦i:avenged⟧, for ⟦b:*ulctus⟧ from ⟦b:ulc-iscor⟧ (⟦r980:980⟧); ⟦b:mulsī⟧ for ⟦b:*mulcsī⟧ from both ⟦b:mulgeō⟧, ⟦i:I milk⟧, and ⟦b:mulceō⟧, ⟦i:I stroke⟧; similarly other stems in ⟦b:-c⟧ and ⟦b:-g⟧ (⟦r1000:1000⟧, ⟦r1014:1014⟧); ⟦b:quernus⟧, ⟦i:oaken⟧, for ⟦b:*quercnus⟧ from ⟦b:quercus⟧; ⟦b:tortus⟧, ⟦i:turned⟧, for ⟦b:*torctus⟧ from ⟦b:torqueō⟧ (for the change of ⟦b:qu⟧ to ⟦b:c⟧, see ⟦r158:158⟧); for ⟦b:fortis⟧, ⟦i:brave⟧, ⟦b:forctis⟧ is found in old Latin.
(4.) ⟦b:c⟧ drops out when it stands between ⟦b:n⟧ and ⟦b:t⟧: as, ⟦b:quīntus⟧, ⟦i:fifth⟧, for older ⟦b:quīnctus⟧ (⟦r2412:2412⟧), from ⟦b:quīnque⟧ (for the change of ⟦b:qu⟧ to ⟦b:c⟧, see ⟦r158:158⟧; for the long ⟦b:ī⟧ in ⟦b:quīnque⟧, see ⟦r122:122⟧, ⟦i:b⟧). But verbs having stems in ⟦b:-nc⟧ or ⟦b:-ng⟧ retain the ⟦b:c⟧ in their past participles: as, ⟦b:vīnctus⟧, ⟦i:bound⟧, from ⟦b:vincīre⟧ (⟦r1014:1014⟧); ⟦b:iūnctus⟧, ⟦i:joined⟧, from ⟦b:iungere⟧ (⟦r954:954⟧). In ⟦b:pāstus⟧ (⟦r965:965⟧) ⟦b:c⟧ has dropped out between ⟦b:s⟧ and ⟦b:t⟧.
(5.) The group ⟦b:-ncn-⟧ was simplified to simple ⟦b:-n-⟧, and the preceding vowel was lengthened: as, ⟦b:quīnī⟧, ⟦i:five each⟧, for ⟦b:*quīnc-nī⟧ (⟦r317:317⟧); ⟦b:cō-nīveō⟧, ⟦i:wink and blink⟧, for ⟦b:con-cnīveō⟧.
(6.) ⟦b:n⟧ before ⟦b:gn⟧ was dropped and the preceding vowel lengthened: as, ⟦b:ī-gnōscō⟧, ⟦i:I forgive⟧, for ⟦b:*in-gnōscō⟧, ⟦b:cō-gnōscō⟧, ⟦i:I know⟧, for ⟦b:*con-gnōscō⟧. In this manner (170, 5; 6) arises a form ⟦b:cō-⟧ by the side of ⟦b:con-⟧ (122, ⟦i:e⟧): as, ⟦b:cō-nectō⟧, ⟦b:cō-nubium⟧, ⟦b:cō-ligātus⟧ (Gell. 2, 17, 8).
(7.) In the imperial age, ⟦b:ss⟧ after long vowels and diphthongs was regularly changed to ⟦b:s⟧: as, ⟦b:clausī⟧, ⟦i:I closed⟧; ⟦b:ūsus⟧, ⟦i:used⟧ (⟦r166:166, 2⟧); but always ⟦b:ēsse⟧, ⟦i:to eat⟧ (⟦r769:769⟧); ⟦b:ll⟧ changed to ⟦b:l⟧ after diphthongs: as, ⟦b:caelum⟧, ⟦i:chisel⟧ (⟦r166:166, 6⟧); also when preceded by ⟦b:ī⟧ and followed by ⟦b:i⟧: as, ⟦b:vīlla⟧, ⟦i:country-place⟧, but ⟦b:vīlicus⟧ (adject.); ⟦b:mille⟧, ⟦i:thousand⟧, but ⟦b:mīlia⟧ (⟦r642:642⟧). Elsewhere ⟦b:ll⟧ was retained after long vowels: as, ⟦b:pūllus⟧ (⟦r166:166, 7⟧), ⟦i:clean⟧; ⟦b:rāllum⟧, ⟦i:ploughshare⟧, from ⟦b:rādō⟧ with suffix ⟦b:-lo-⟧ (⟦r209:209⟧). In Cicero’s time (Quint. 1, 7, 20) the spelling was still ⟦b:caussa⟧ (155, ⟦i:b⟧), ⟦i:matter⟧; ⟦b:cāssus⟧ (⟦r930:930⟧), ⟦i:fallen⟧; ⟦b:divīssiō⟧ (cf. ⟦r912:912⟧), ⟦i:division⟧. Vergil also, according to Quintilian, retained the doubled consonants, and the best manuscripts of both Vergil and Plautus frequently show ⟦b:ll⟧ and ⟦b:ss⟧ for later ⟦b:l⟧ and ⟦b:s⟧, as do inscriptions: as, PROMEISSERIT, ⟦i:he might have promised⟧ (49 B.C.); ACCVSSASSE, ⟦i:to have accused⟧.
(8.) After a long vowel ⟦b:d⟧ was dropped before consonant ⟦b:u⟧ (⟦b:v⟧): as, ⟦b:svāvis⟧, ⟦i:sweet⟧, for ⟦b:*svādvis⟧ from ⟦b:svād-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:svādeō⟧).
(9.) ⟦b:r⟧ before ⟦b:st⟧ was dropped: as, ⟦b:tostus⟧, ⟦i:roasted⟧ (⟦r1004:1004⟧) for ⟦b:*torstus⟧ from the stem ⟦b:tors-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:torreo⟧ with assimilated ⟦b:-rs-⟧, 166, 8).
(10.) ⟦b:-rts-⟧ changed to ⟦b:-rs⟧: as, ⟦b:arsī⟧, ⟦i:I burnt⟧, for ⟦b:*artsī⟧ (⟦r1000:1000⟧). ⟦b:-rcsc-⟧ changed to ⟦b:-sc-⟧: as, ⟦b:poscō⟧, ⟦i:I demand⟧, for ⟦b:*porcscō⟧ (⟦r834:834⟧).
(11.) In ⟦b:ipse⟧, ⟦i:self⟧, for ⟦b:*is-pse⟧, an ⟦b:s⟧ has disappeared before ⟦b:-ps-⟧
(12.) (12.) ⟦b:d⟧ (⟦b:t⟧) disappears between ⟦b:r⟧ and ⟦b:c⟧: as, ⟦b:cor-culum⟧ for ⟦b:cord(i)-culum⟧ (⟦r275:275⟧).
⟦#171⟧
Final Disappearance. (1.) A word never ends in a doubled consonant: as, ⟦b:es⟧ for ⟦b:*es-s⟧, ⟦i:thou art⟧, which Plautus and Terence still scan as a long syllable; and the following cases of assimilation: ⟦b:ter⟧ for ⟦b:*terr⟧ from ⟦b:*ters⟧ (cf. ⟦b:terr-uncius⟧, ⟦i:a quarter of an⟧ ⟦b:ās⟧, ⟦i:a farthing⟧, ⟦r1272:1272⟧, for ⟦b:*ters-uncius⟧, 166, 8); ⟦b:fār⟧, ⟦i:spelt⟧, for ⟦b:*farr⟧, from ⟦b:*fars⟧ (⟦r489:489⟧); ⟦b:fel⟧, ⟦i:gall⟧, for ⟦b:*fell⟧, from ⟦b:*fels⟧ (⟦r482:482⟧); in ⟦b:mīles⟧, ⟦i:soldier⟧, for ⟦b:*mīless⟧ from ⟦b:*mīlets⟧ (cf. Gen. ⟦b:mīlitis⟧, ⟦r477:477⟧) the final syllable is still long in Plautus. ⟦b:hoc⟧, ⟦i:this⟧, for ⟦b:*hocc⟧ from ⟦b:*hod-c(e)⟧(the neuter ⟦b:*hod⟧ from the stem ⟦b:ho-⟧, as ⟦b:istud⟧, ⟦b:illud⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧) from ⟦b:isto-⟧, ⟦b:illo-⟧) counts as a long syllable even in classical poetry.
(2.) No Latin word can end in two explosives: thus, final ⟦b:t⟧ is dropped in ⟦b:lac⟧, ⟦i:milk⟧ (⟦r478:478⟧); final ⟦b:d⟧ in ⟦b:cor⟧, ⟦i:heart⟧ (⟦r476:476⟧).
(3.) When final ⟦b:s⟧ was preceded by ⟦b:r⟧ or ⟦b:l⟧, it was assimilated to these liquids, and final ⟦b:rr⟧ and ⟦b:ll⟧ were then simplified to ⟦b:r⟧ and ⟦b:l⟧. See the examples under (1). Wherever final ⟦b:-rs⟧ and ⟦b:-ls⟧ appear they are not original but the result of the disappearance of an intervening consonant: as, ⟦b:puls⟧, ⟦i:pottage⟧, for ⟦b:*pults⟧ (⟦r533:533⟧); ⟦b:pars⟧, ⟦i:part⟧, for ⟦b:*parts⟧ (⟦r533:533⟧); all with syncope (⟦r111:111⟧) of the vowel ⟦b:i⟧ in the nominative ⟦b:sg⟧.
(4.) Original final ⟦b:ns⟧ was changed to ⟦b:s⟧ and the preceding vowel was lengthened: as, ⟦b:sanguīs⟧, ⟦i:blood⟧ (⟦r2452:2452⟧), for ⟦b:*sanguins⟧ from the stem ⟦b:sanguin-⟧ (⟦r486:486⟧). Wherever final ⟦b:-ns⟧ appears it is not original but the result of the disappearance of an intervening consonant: as, ⟦b:ferēns⟧, ⟦i:carrying⟧, for ⟦b:*ferents⟧, from the stem ⟦b:ferent-⟧; ⟦b:frōns⟧, ⟦i:foliage⟧, for ⟦b:*fronds⟧, from the stem ⟦b:frond-⟧.
(5.) A dental mute before final ⟦b:s⟧ is dropped: as, ⟦b:hērēs⟧, ⟦i:heir⟧, for ⟦b:*hērēds⟧ (⟦r475:475⟧); ⟦b:virtūs⟧, ⟦i:virtue⟧, for ⟦b:*virtūts⟧ (⟦r477:477⟧); ⟦b:nox⟧, ⟦i:night⟧, for ⟦b:*nocts⟧ (⟦r533:533⟧); a labial or guttural mute is retained: as, ⟦b:fornāx⟧ (⟦b:x⟧ = ⟦b:cs⟧), ⟦i:furnace⟧, from the stem ⟦b:fornāc-⟧ (⟦r531:531⟧); ⟦b:lēx⟧, ⟦i:law⟧, from the stem ⟦b:leg-⟧ (⟦r472:472⟧); ⟦b:urbs⟧, ⟦i:city⟧, from the stem ⟦b:urb-⟧ (⟦r480:480⟧); ⟦b:ops⟧ from the stem ⟦b:op-⟧, ⟦i:help⟧ (⟦r480:480⟧).

title: Development of an Anaptyctical Vowel
text:
⟦#172⟧
Certain consonant groups, notably those containing a liquid, are sometimes eased by the insertion of a vowel which develops between the consonants. This is called ⟦i:Anaptyxis⟧ (Greek ἀναπτύσσειν, ⟦i:unfold⟧). It is the opposite of syncope of vowels (⟦r110:110⟧, ⟦r111:111⟧).
(1.) The suffix ⟦b:-clo-⟧ (⟦r242:242⟧), changed to ⟦b:-culo-⟧, being thus no longer distinguishable from the diminutive suffix ⟦b:-culo-⟧ (⟦r267:267⟧): as, ⟦b:pōculum⟧, ⟦i:cup⟧, for ⟦b:pōclum⟧ (Plaut.); ⟦b:vehiculum⟧, ⟦i:carriage⟧, for ⟦b:vehiclum⟧ (Plaut.). But ⟦b:-clo-⟧ is more common in Plautus than ⟦b:-culo-⟧, especially after long vowels. The suffixes ⟦b:-blo-⟧ (⟦r245:245⟧), and ⟦b:-bli-⟧ (⟦r294:294⟧) always show the anaptyctical vowel. Its colour depends on the nature of the ⟦b:l⟧ (⟦r60:60⟧): as, ⟦b:stabulum⟧, ⟦i:resting-place⟧; ⟦b:stabilis⟧, ⟦i:steady⟧. The group ⟦b:-ngl-⟧ also changes to ⟦b:-ngul-⟧: as, ⟦b:angulus⟧ (⟦r164:164, 6⟧).
(2.) In words borrowed from the Greek an unfamiliar sequence of consonants was so lightened; as, ⟦b:mina⟧, ⟦i:mina⟧, for ⟦b:*mna⟧ (μνᾶ); and in Old Latin ⟦b:drachuma⟧ (Plaut.) for later ⟦b:drachma⟧, ⟦i:drachma⟧ (δραχμή); ⟦b:techina⟧, ⟦i:trick⟧, from Greek τέχνη; ⟦b:Tecumēssa⟧ for ⟦b:Tecmēssa⟧ (Τέκμησσα).
(3.) Before syllabic (⟦r83:83⟧) ⟦b:l⟧ and ⟦b:r⟧ a vowel is developed (111, ⟦i:b⟧): as, ⟦b:íncertus⟧, ⟦i:uncertain⟧, for ⟦b:*íncr̥tus⟧; ⟦b:fácultās⟧, ⟦i:capability⟧, for ⟦b:fácl̥tās⟧. Likewise before syllabic ⟦b:n⟧ (⟦r139:139⟧).

title: Dissimilation
text:
⟦#173⟧
(1.) To avoid the repetition of the same liquid in successive syllables ⟦b:l⟧ is sometimes changed to ⟦b:r⟧: as, ⟦b:caeruleus⟧, ⟦i:sky-blue⟧, for ⟦b:*caeluleus⟧, from ⟦b:caelum⟧; ⟦b:Parīlia⟧, by the side of ⟦b:Palīlia⟧, from ⟦b:Palēs⟧; the suffix ⟦b:-clo-⟧ appears as ⟦b:-cro-⟧ after an ⟦b:l⟧: as, ⟦b:lavācrum⟧, ⟦i:bath⟧, ⟦b:simulācrum⟧, ⟦i:image⟧ (⟦r241:241⟧); the suffix ⟦b:-āli-⟧ under like conditions changes to ⟦b:-āri-⟧; as, ⟦b:molāre⟧, ⟦i:of a mill⟧ (⟦r313:313⟧), but ⟦b:augurāle⟧, ⟦i:of an augur⟧.
(2.) In a few cases repetition is avoided by dropping the sound once: as, ⟦b:praestīgiae⟧, ⟦i:jugglery⟧, for ⟦b:praestrīgiae⟧. This also applies to the spirant ⟦b:s⟧ followed by a consonant, a combination which is not tolerated in successive syllables: as in the reduplicated perfects ⟦b:stetī⟧, for ⟦b:*stestī⟧; ⟦b:spopondī⟧, for ⟦b:*spospondī⟧ (⟦r859:859⟧), where the second syllable, and in ⟦b:quisquiliae⟧, ⟦i:sweepings⟧, for ⟦b:*squisquiliae⟧, where the first syllable was lightened.

title: Changes Within Compounds
text:
⟦#174⟧
The final syllable of the first member of compounds (⟦r181:181⟧) sometimes undergoes certain changes by analogy to other compounds:
(1.) The final ⟦b:-ā⟧ of ⟦b:ā-⟧stems, by analogy to the more frequent ⟦b:-o-⟧stems, usually changed to ⟦b:-o⟧, which in atonic syllables became ⟦b:-i⟧ (⟦r105:105⟧): as, ⟦b:āli-ger⟧, ⟦i:winged⟧, for ⟦b:*ālo-ger⟧ from ⟦b:ālā-⟧.
(2.) Stems in ⟦b:-on-⟧ substitute ⟦b:-o-⟧ for ⟦b:-on-⟧ by analogy to the ⟦b:-o-⟧stems: as, ⟦b:homi-cída⟧, ⟦i:murderer⟧, for ⟦b:*homo-cīda⟧ (⟦r105:105⟧) from ⟦b:homon-⟧ (Nom. ⟦b:homō⟧).
(3.) Some stems in ⟦b:-s⟧ substitute ⟦b:-o-⟧ by analogy to the ⟦b:-o-⟧stems: as, ⟦b:foedi-fragus⟧, ⟦i:treaty-breaking⟧, for ⟦b:*foedo-fragus⟧ from the stem ⟦b:foedos-⟧ (Nom. ⟦b:foedus⟧, Gen. ⟦b:foederis⟧; 154).

title: Syllables
text:
⟦#175⟧
A word has as many syllables as it has separate vowels or diphthongs. The last syllable is called the ⟦i:Ultima⟧; the last syllable but one is called the ⟦i:Penult⟧; the last syllable but two is called the ⟦i:Antepenult⟧.
⟦#176⟧
The quantity of single sounds (e.g. the quantity of a vowel) must be carefully distinguished from the quantity of the group of sounds or the syllable of which the single sound forms a part.

title: Length of Syllables
text:
⟦#177⟧
A syllable is long if its vowel is long, or if its vowel is followed by two consonants or by ⟦b:x⟧ or ⟦b:z⟧: as,
⟦b:dūcēbās⟧; ⟦b:volvunt⟧. In ⟦b:dūcēbās⟧ both the vowels and the syllables are long; in ⟦b:volvunt⟧ the vowels are short, but the syllables are long; in cases like the last the syllables (not the vowels) are said to be ⟦i:long by position⟧. ⟦b:h⟧ does not count as a consonant (⟦r58:58⟧) and ⟦b:qu⟧ (or ⟦b:qv⟧, ⟦r27:27⟧) has the value of a single consonant only: thus, in ⟦b:adhūc⟧ and ⟦b:aqua⟧ the first syllable is short.
⟦#178⟧
In prose or old dramatic verse a syllable with a short vowel before a mute or ⟦b:f⟧ followed by ⟦b:l⟧ or ⟦b:r⟧ is not long: as ⟦b:tenebrae⟧. In other verse, however, such syllables are sometimes regarded as long. In compounds such syllables are long in any verse: as ⟦b:obruit⟧.

title: Loss of Syllables
text:
⟦#179⟧
The first of two successive syllables which begin with the same sound is sometimes lost. This is called ⟦i:Haplology⟧.
Thus, ⟦b:sēmodius⟧ for ⟦b:sēmimodius⟧, ⟦i:half a bushel⟧; ⟦b:calamitōsus⟧ for ⟦b:*calamitātōsus⟧, from the stem ⟦b:calamitāt-⟧ (⟦r262:262⟧) and suffix ⟦b:-oso-⟧ (⟦r336:336⟧); ⟦b:voluntārius⟧, for ⟦b:voluntātārius⟧ (⟦r262:262⟧, ⟦r309:309⟧); ⟦b:cōnsuētūdō⟧, for ⟦b:cōnsuētitūdō⟧ (⟦r264:264⟧). See also ⟦r255:255⟧; ⟦r379:379⟧.

title: Formation
text:
⟦#180⟧
Formation is the process by which stems are formed from roots or from other stems.
⟦#181⟧
A word containing a single stem is called a ⟦i:Simple⟧ word: as, ⟦b:magnus⟧, ⟦i:great⟧, stem ⟦b:magno-⟧; ⟦b:animus⟧, ⟦i:soul⟧, stem ⟦b:animo-⟧. A word containing two or more stems is called a ⟦i:Compound⟧ word: as, ⟦b:magnanimus⟧, ⟦i:great-souled⟧, stem ⟦b:magnanimo-⟧.
⟦#182⟧
Most inflected words consist of two parts: a stem, which is usually a modified root (⟦r195:195⟧), and an inflection ending: thus, in ⟦b:ductōrī⟧, ⟦i:for a leader⟧, the root is ⟦b:⟦i:duc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:lead⟧, the stem is ⟦b:ductōr-⟧, ⟦i:leader⟧, and ⟦b:-ī⟧ is the inflection ending, meaning ⟦i:for⟧.

title: Roots
text:
⟦#183⟧
A Root is a monosyllable which gives the fundamental meaning to a word or group of words.
⟦#184⟧
A root is not a real word; it is neither a noun, naming something, nor a verb, denoting action. Thus ⟦b:⟦i:iug-⟧⟧, ⟦i:yoke⟧, does not mean ⟦i:a yoke⟧ nor ⟦i:I yoke⟧; it merely ⟦i:suggests⟧ something about yoking. The root becomes a real word only when an inflection ending is added, or, more commonly, both a formative suffix and an inflection ending: as, ⟦b:iug-u-m⟧, ⟦i:a yoke⟧.
⟦#185⟧
Roots are common to Latin and its cognate languages, such as the Sanskrit and the Greek. When a root is named in this book, the specific Latin form of the root is meant. This often differs somewhat from the form of the root which is assumed as applicable to all the cognate languages.
⟦#186⟧
Almost all roots are noun and verb roots; that is, roots with a meaning which may be embodied either in a noun or in a verb, or in both. Besides these there is a small class, less than a dozen in number, of pronoun roots. There are many words which cannot be traced back to their roots.
⟦#187⟧
A root sometimes has two or more forms: as, ⟦b:⟦i:fīd-⟧⟧ (for ⟦b:⟦i:feid-⟧⟧), ⟦b:⟦i:foed-⟧⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:fid-⟧⟧, ⟦i:trust⟧; ⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:gn-⟧⟧, ⟦i:sire⟧; ⟦b:⟦i:tol⟧⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:tl⟧⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧; see ⟦r135:135⟧, ⟦r145:145⟧.
Thus, ⟦b:⟦i:fīd-⟧⟧ is found in ⟦b:fīd-us⟧, ⟦i:trusty⟧, ⟦b:fīd-ūcia⟧, ⟦i:confidence⟧, ⟦b:fīd-ūciō⟧, ⟦i:I pledge⟧, ⟦b:fīd-ūciārius⟧, ⟦i:in trust⟧, ⟦b:fīd-ere⟧, ⟦i:put trust in⟧, ⟦b:fīd-ēns⟧, ⟦i:courageous⟧, ⟦b:fīd-entia⟧, ⟦i:courage⟧; ⟦b:foed-⟧ in ⟦b:foed-us⟧, ⟦i:pledge of faith⟧, ⟦b:foed-erātus⟧, ⟦i:bound by a pledge of faith⟧; ⟦b:⟦i:fid-⟧⟧ in ⟦b:fid-ēs⟧, ⟦i:faith⟧, ⟦b:fid-ēlis⟧, ⟦i:faithful⟧, ⟦b:fid-ēliter⟧, ⟦i:faithfully⟧, ⟦b:fid-ēlitās⟧, ⟦i:faithfulness⟧, ⟦b:per-fid-us⟧, ⟦i:faithless⟧, ⟦b:per-fid-ia⟧, ⟦i:faithlessness⟧, ⟦b:per-fid-iōsus⟧, ⟦i:full of faithlessness⟧, per-fid-iōsē, faithlessly. ⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧ in ⟦b:gen-itor⟧, ⟦i:sire⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:gn-⟧⟧ in ⟦b:gi-gn-ere⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:gn⟧⟧⟦b:-ā-⟧ in ⟦b:gnā-tus⟧, ⟦i:son⟧.
⟦#188⟧
A root ending in a vowel is called a ⟦i:Vowel Root⟧: as, ⟦b:⟦i:da-⟧⟧, ⟦i:give⟧; a root ending in a consonant is called a ⟦i:Consonant Root⟧: as, ⟦b:⟦i:rup-⟧⟧, ⟦i:break⟧. Roots are conveniently indicated by the sign √: as, √⟦b:⟦i:teg-⟧⟧, to be read ‘root ⟦b:⟦i:teg-⟧⟧.’
⟦#189⟧
A root or a part of a root is sometimes doubled in forming a word; this is called ⟦i:Reduplication⟧: as, ⟦b:mur-mur⟧, ⟦i:murmur⟧; ⟦b:tur-tur⟧, ⟦i:turtle-dove⟧; ⟦b:po-pul-us⟧, ⟦i:people⟧; ⟦b:ul-ul-āre⟧, ⟦i:yell⟧.

title: Present Stems As Roots
text:
⟦#190⟧
Many nouns are formed from the present stems of verbs, which take the place of roots. Stems thus used are mostly those of verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ and ⟦b:-īre⟧.
Thus, from ⟦b:ōrā-⟧, stem of ⟦b:ōrāre⟧, ⟦i:speak⟧, are formed ⟦b:ōrā-tor⟧, ⟦i:speaker⟧, and ⟦b:ōrā-tiō⟧, ⟦i:speech⟧; from ⟦b:audī-⟧, stem of ⟦b:audīre⟧, ⟦i:hear⟧, are formed ⟦b:audī-tor⟧, ⟦i:hearer⟧, and ⟦b:audī-tiō⟧, ⟦i:hearing⟧.
⟦#191⟧
Verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧, and those in ⟦b:-āre⟧ and ⟦b:-īre⟧ in which the ⟦b:ā⟧ or ⟦b:ī⟧ is confined to the present system (⟦r868:868⟧, ⟦r874:874⟧) usually have parallel nouns formed directly from a root: as,
⟦b:doc-tor⟧, ⟦i:teacher⟧, ⟦b:doc-umentum⟧, ⟦i:lesson⟧, ⟦b:doc-ilis⟧, ⟦i:teachable⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:doc-⟧⟧, ⟦b:docēre⟧); ⟦b:sec-tor⟧, ⟦i:cutter⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sec-⟧⟧, ⟦b:secāre⟧); ⟦b:dom-itor⟧, ⟦i:tamer⟧, ⟦b:dom-inus⟧, ⟦i:master⟧, ⟦b:dom-itus⟧, ⟦i:tamed⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:dom-⟧⟧, ⟦b:domāre⟧); ⟦b:sarc-ina⟧, ⟦i:package⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sarc-⟧⟧, ⟦b:sarcīre⟧).
⟦#192⟧
But a noun is sometimes exceptionally formed from the present stem of a verb in ⟦b:-ēre⟧: as, ⟦b:monē-ta⟧, ⟦i:mint⟧ (⟦b:monēre⟧); ⟦b:acē-tum⟧, ⟦i:vinegar⟧ (⟦b:acēre⟧); ⟦b:virē-tum⟧, ⟦i:a green⟧ (⟦b:virēre⟧); ⟦b:suādē-la⟧, ⟦i:persuasion⟧ (⟦b:suādēre⟧); ⟦b:habē-na⟧, ⟦i:rein⟧ (⟦b:habēre⟧); ⟦b:egē-nus⟧, ⟦i:needy⟧ (⟦b:egēre⟧); ⟦b:verē-cundus⟧, ⟦i:shamefast⟧ (⟦b:verērī⟧); ⟦b:valē-tūdō⟧, ⟦i:health⟧ (⟦b:valēre⟧).
⟦#193⟧
Verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, and particularly such as have a present in ⟦b:-nō⟧, ⟦b:-scō⟧, ⟦b:-tō⟧ or ⟦b:-iō⟧ (⟦r832:832⟧), usually have their parallel nouns formed directly from a root: as,
⟦b:vic-tor⟧, ⟦i:conqueror⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:vic-⟧⟧, ⟦b:vincere⟧); ⟦b:incrē-mentum⟧, ⟦i:growth⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:crē-⟧⟧, ⟦b:crēscere⟧); ⟦b:pul-sus⟧, ⟦i:a push⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pol-⟧⟧, ⟦b:pellere⟧).
⟦#194⟧
Sometimes, however, nouns are formed from such verb stems, and not from roots: as, ⟦b:lecti-stern-ium⟧, ⟦i:a couch-spreading⟧ (⟦b:sternere⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:ster-⟧⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:strā-⟧⟧); ⟦b:vinc-ibilis⟧, ⟦i:conquerable⟧ (⟦b:vincere⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:vīc-⟧⟧); ⟦b:pāsc-uum⟧, ⟦i:pasture⟧ (⟦b:pāscere⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:pā-⟧⟧); ⟦b:pect-en⟧, ⟦i:comb⟧ (⟦b:pectere⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:pec-⟧⟧); ⟦b:fall-āx⟧, ⟦i:deceitful⟧ (⟦b:fallere⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:fal-⟧⟧).

title: Stems
text:
⟦#195⟧
A Stem is that part of a word which contains its meaning, and is either a root alone or more commonly a root with an addition called a ⟦i:Formative Suffix⟧.
Thus, in the word ⟦b:ducis⟧, ⟦i:leader’s⟧, the stem, which is identical with the root ⟦b:⟦i:duc-⟧⟧, means ⟦i:leader⟧; a root thus serving as a stem is called a ⟦i:Root Stem⟧; in ⟦b:ductōris⟧, ⟦i:leader’s⟧, the stem is formed by the formative suffix ⟦b:-tōr-⟧, denoting the agent, attached to the √⟦b:⟦i:duc-⟧⟧.
⟦#196⟧
New stems are formed by adding a suffix to a stem. Thus, from ⟦b:ōrātōr-⟧, ⟦i:speaker⟧, is formed by the addition of the suffix ⟦b:-io-⟧, a new stem ⟦b:ōrātōr-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:ōrātōrius⟧, ⟦i:speaker’s⟧.
⟦#197⟧
The noun has usually only one form of the stem. The verb has different stems to indicate mood and tense; these stems are all based on two principal tense stems, the present and the perfect active.

title: Primitives and Denominatives
text:
⟦#198⟧
I. A stem or word formed directly from a root or a verb stem is called a ⟦i:Primitive⟧. II. A stem or word formed from a noun stem is called a ⟦i:Denominative⟧.
(⟦i:a.⟧) Primitives: from √⟦b:⟦i:rēg-⟧⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:reg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧: ⟦b:rēx⟧, stem ⟦b:rēg-⟧, ⟦i:king⟧; ⟦b:rēgnum⟧, stem ⟦b:rēg-no-⟧, ⟦i:kingdom⟧; ⟦b:rēctus⟧, stem ⟦b:rēc-to-⟧, ⟦i:guided⟧; ⟦b:regere⟧, stem ⟦b:reg-e-⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧. From ⟦b:ōrā-⟧, stem of ⟦b:ōrāre⟧, ⟦i:speak⟧: ⟦b:ōrātor⟧, stem ⟦b:ōrā-tōr-⟧, ⟦i:speaker⟧; ⟦b:ōrātiō⟧, stem ⟦b:ōrā-tiōn-⟧, ⟦i:speech⟧.
(⟦i:b.⟧) Denominatives: from noun stem ⟦b:rēg-⟧, ⟦i:king⟧: ⟦b:rēgīna⟧, stem ⟦b:rēg-īnā⟧, ⟦i:queen⟧; ⟦b:rēgius⟧, stem ⟦b:rēg-io-⟧, ⟦b:rēgālis⟧, stem ⟦b:rēg-āli-⟧, ⟦i:royal⟧. From ⟦b:ōrātiōn-⟧, ⟦i:speech⟧: ⟦b:ōrātiūncula⟧, stem ⟦b:ōrātiūn-culā-⟧, ⟦i:little speech⟧. From ⟦b:rēg-no-⟧, ⟦i:kingdom⟧: ⟦b:rēgnāre⟧, stem ⟦b:rēgnā-⟧, ⟦i:to rule⟧. From ⟦b:iūs⟧, ⟦i:law⟧: ⟦b:iūrāre⟧, ⟦i:swear⟧, stem ⟦b:iūrā⟧ (⟦r154:154⟧).

title: Formation of the Noun: Without a Formative Suffix
text:
⟦#199⟧
Some roots are used as noun stems: as, ⟦b:duc-⟧, N. ⟦b:dux⟧, ⟦i:leader⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:duc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:lead⟧); ⟦b:rēg-⟧, N. ⟦b:rēx⟧, ⟦i:king⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:rēg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧); particularly at the end of a compound: as, ⟦b:con-iug-⟧, N. ⟦b:coniūnx⟧, ⟦i:yoke-fellow⟧, ⟦i:spouse⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:jug-⟧⟧, ⟦i:yoke⟧); ⟦b:tubi-cin-⟧, N. ⟦b:tubicen⟧, ⟦i:trumpeter⟧ (⟦b:tubā-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:can-⟧⟧, ⟦i:play⟧).

title: Formation of the Noun: With a Formative Suffix
text:
⟦#200⟧
Simple formative suffixes are vowels: as, ⟦b:-ā-⟧, ⟦b:-o-⟧, ⟦b:-i-⟧, ⟦b:-u-⟧; also ⟦b:-io-⟧, ⟦b:-uo-⟧, (⟦b:-vo-⟧); or such little syllables as ⟦b:-mo-⟧, ⟦b:-min-⟧; ⟦b:-ro-⟧, ⟦b:-lo-⟧; ⟦b:-ōn-⟧; ⟦b:-no-⟧, ⟦b:-ni-⟧, ⟦b:-nu-⟧; ⟦b:-to-⟧, ⟦b:-ti-⟧, ⟦b:-tu-⟧; ⟦b:-ter-⟧, ⟦b:-tōr-⟧; ⟦b:-unt-⟧ (⟦b:-nt-⟧); ⟦b:-es-⟧ (⟦b:-er-⟧), ⟦b:-ōr-⟧; these syllables sometimes have slight modifications of form. Compound suffixes consist of one or more simple suffixes attached to a simple suffix: as, ⟦b:-tōr-io-⟧, ⟦b:-ti-mo-⟧, &c., &c.
⟦#201⟧
The following are examples of noun stems formed from roots or verb stems by simple suffixes added:
⟦b:fug-ā-⟧  ⟦b:fuga⟧, ⟦i:flight⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:fug-⟧⟧, ⟦i:fly⟧
⟦b:fīd-o-⟧  ⟦b:fīdus⟧, ⟦i:trusty⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:fīd-⟧⟧, ⟦i:trust⟧
⟦b:ac-u-⟧  ⟦b:acus⟧, ⟦i:pin⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:ac-⟧⟧, ⟦i:point⟧
⟦b:od-io-⟧  ⟦b:odium⟧, ⟦i:hate⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:od-⟧⟧, ⟦i:hate⟧
⟦b:pluv-iā-⟧  ⟦b:pluvia⟧, ⟦i:rain⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:plov-⟧⟧, ⟦i:wet⟧
⟦b:ar-vo-⟧  ⟦b:arvom⟧, ⟦i:tilth⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:ar-⟧⟧, ⟦i:till⟧
⟦b:al-vo-⟧  ⟦b:alvos⟧, ⟦i:belly⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:al-⟧⟧, ⟦i:nurture⟧
⟦b:sal-vo-⟧  ⟦b:salvos⟧, ⟦i:safe⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:sal-⟧⟧, ⟦i:safe⟧
⟦b:fā-mā-⟧  ⟦b:fāma⟧, ⟦i:tale⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:fā-⟧⟧, ⟦i:tell⟧
⟦b:teg-min-⟧  ⟦b:tegmen⟧, ⟦i:cover⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:teg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:cover⟧
⟦b:sel-lā-⟧  ⟦b:sella⟧, ⟦i:seat⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:sed-⟧⟧, ⟦i:sit⟧
⟦b:err-ōn-⟧  ⟦b:errō⟧, ⟦i:stroller⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:errā-⟧⟧, ⟦i:stroll⟧
⟦b:som-no-⟧  ⟦b:somnus⟧, ⟦i:sleep⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:sop-⟧⟧, ⟦i:sleep⟧
⟦b:plē-no-⟧  ⟦b:plēnus⟧, ⟦i:full⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:plē-⟧⟧, ⟦i:fill⟧
⟦b:rēg-no-⟧  ⟦b:rēgnum⟧, ⟦i:realm⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:rēg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧
⟦b:da-to-⟧  ⟦b:datus⟧, ⟦i:given⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:da-⟧⟧, ⟦i:give⟧
⟦b:lec-to-⟧  ⟦b:lectus⟧, ⟦i:bed⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:leg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:lie⟧
⟦b:gen-ti-⟧  ⟦b:gēns⟧, ⟦i:race⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧
⟦b:sta-tu-⟧  ⟦b:status⟧, ⟦i:stand⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:sta-⟧⟧, ⟦i:stand⟧
⟦b:rēc-tōr-⟧  ⟦b:rēctor⟧, ⟦i:ruler⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:rēg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧
⟦b:e-unt-⟧,  ⟦b:iēns⟧, ⟦i:going⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:i-⟧⟧, ⟦i:go⟧
⟦b:rege-nt-⟧  ⟦b:regēns⟧, ⟦i:guiding⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:rege-⟧⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧
⟦b:gen-er-⟧  ⟦b:genus⟧, ⟦i:race⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧
⟦b:fur-ōr-⟧  ⟦b:furor⟧, ⟦i:madness⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:fur-⟧⟧, ⟦i:rave⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.
⟦#202⟧
Formative suffixes are often preceded by a vowel, which in many instances is a stem vowel, real or presumed; in others, the vowel has come to be regarded as a part of the suffix itself.
Thus, ⟦b:-lo-⟧: ⟦b:fīlio-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:fīlio-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:little son⟧ (⟦b:fīlio-⟧); ⟦b:hortu-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:little garden⟧ (⟦b:horto-⟧, 105, ⟦i:h⟧); but ⟦b:-ulo-⟧: ⟦b:rēg-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:petty king⟧ (⟦b:rēg-⟧); ⟦b:ger-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:porter⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ges-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧), ⟦b:-ci-⟧: ⟦b:pugnā-ci-⟧, N. ⟦b:pugnā-x⟧, ⟦i:full of fight⟧ (⟦b:pugnā-re⟧); but ⟦b:-āci-⟧: ⟦b:fer-āx⟧, ⟦i:productive⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fer-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧), ⟦b:-to-⟧: ⟦b:laudā-to-⟧, N. ⟦b:laudā-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:praised⟧ (⟦b:laudā-re⟧); but ⟦b:-āto-⟧: ⟦b:dent-ātus⟧, ⟦i:toothed⟧ (⟦b:denti-⟧). ⟦b:-tu-⟧: ⟦b:equitā-tu-⟧, N. ⟦b:equitā-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:cavalry⟧ (⟦b:equitā-re⟧); but ⟦b:-ātu-⟧: ⟦b:sen-ātu-s⟧, ⟦i:senate⟧ (⟦b:sen-⟧). ⟦b:-lā-⟧: ⟦b:suādē-lā-⟧, N. ⟦b:suādē-la⟧, ⟦i:persuasion⟧ (⟦b:suādē-re⟧, ⟦r192:192⟧); but ⟦b:-ēlā-⟧: ⟦b:loqu-ēla⟧, ⟦i:talk⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:loqu-⟧⟧, ⟦i:speak⟧). ⟦b:-tāt-⟧: ⟦b:cīvi-tāt-⟧, N. ⟦b:cīvi-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:citizenship⟧ (⟦b:cīvi-⟧); but ⟦b:-itāt-⟧: ⟦b:auctōr-itā-s⟧, ⟦i:authority⟧ (⟦b:auctōr-⟧). ⟦b:-cio-⟧: ⟦b:aedīli-cio-⟧, N. ⟦b:aedīli-ciu-s⟧, ⟦i:of an aedile⟧ (⟦b:aedīli-⟧); but ⟦b:-icio-⟧: ⟦b:patr-iciu-s⟧, ⟦i:patrician⟧ (⟦b:patr-⟧). ⟦b:-timo-⟧: ⟦b:fīni-timo-⟧, N. ⟦b:fīni-timu-s⟧, ⟦i:bordering⟧ (⟦b:fīni-⟧); but ⟦b:-itimo-⟧: ⟦b:lēg-itimu-s⟧, ⟦i:of the law⟧ (⟦b:lēg-⟧).
⟦#203⟧
There are many formative suffixes of nouns. The commonest only can be named, and these may be conveniently grouped as below, by their meanings. Compound suffixes are arranged with reference to the last element of the suffix: thus, under the adjective suffix ⟦b:-io-⟧ (⟦r304:304⟧) will be found ⟦b:-c-io-⟧, ⟦b:-īc-io-⟧, ⟦b:-tōr-io-⟧, and ⟦b:-ār-io-⟧. In many instances it is difficult to distinguish between simple and compound suffixes.

title: The Agent
text:
⟦#204⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-tōr-⟧, ⟦b:-o-⟧, ⟦b:-ā-⟧, ⟦b:-lo-⟧, and ⟦b:-ōn-⟧, are used to denote the ⟦i:Agent⟧: as,
⟦b:lēc-tōr-⟧  ⟦b:lēctor⟧, ⟦i:reader⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:lēg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:read⟧
⟦b:scrīb-ā-⟧  ⟦b:scrība⟧, ⟦i:writer⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:scrīb-⟧⟧, ⟦i:write⟧
⟦b:fig-ulo-⟧  ⟦b:figulus⟧, ⟦i:potter⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:fig-⟧⟧, ⟦i:mould⟧
⟦b:err-ōn-⟧  ⟦b:errō⟧, ⟦i:stroller⟧  ⟦b:errā-re⟧, ⟦i:stroll⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.

title: -tōr- (N. -tor)
text:
⟦#205⟧
⟦b:-tōr-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tor⟧, or ⟦b:-sōr-⟧, N. ⟦b:-sor⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧, ⟦r202:202⟧), is the commonest suffix of the agent; the feminine is ⟦b:-trī-ci-⟧, N. ⟦b:-trī-x⟧. ⟦b:-tōr-⟧ is sometimes used in a present sense, of action repeated or occurring at any time, and sometimes in a past sense.
⟦#206⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) ⟦b:-tōr-⟧ (⟦b:-sōr-⟧), in the present sense, often denotes one who makes a regular business of the action of the root or verb.
⟦b:ōrā-tōr-⟧, N. ⟦b:ōrā-tor⟧, ⟦i:spokesman⟧, ⟦i:speaker⟧ (⟦b:ōrā-re⟧); ⟦b:lēc-tor⟧, ⟦i:reader⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:leg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:read⟧). Workmen and tradesmen: ⟦b:arā-tor⟧, ⟦i:ploughman⟧, ⟦b:pās-tor⟧, ⟦i:shepherd⟧, ⟦b:pīc-tor⟧, ⟦i:painter⟧, ⟦b:sū-tor⟧, ⟦i:shoemaker⟧. Semi-professional: ⟦b:captā-tor⟧, ⟦i:legacy-hunter⟧, ⟦b:dēlā-tor⟧, ⟦i:professional informer⟧. Government officials: ⟦b:cēn-sor⟧, ⟦i:appraiser⟧, ⟦i:censor⟧, ⟦b:imperā-tor⟧, ⟦i:commander⟧, ⟦b:prae-tor⟧, (⟦i:leader⟧), ⟦i:praetor⟧, ⟦b:dictā-tor⟧, ⟦b:līc-tor⟧. Of the law: ⟦b:āc-tor⟧, ⟦i:manager⟧, ⟦b:accūsā-tor⟧, ⟦i:accuser⟧, ⟦b:spōn-sor⟧, ⟦i:bondsman⟧, ⟦b:tū-tor⟧, ⟦i:guardian⟧. From presumed verb stems (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:sen-ātor⟧, ⟦i:senator⟧ (⟦b:sen-⟧); ⟦b:viā-tor⟧, ⟦i:wayfarer⟧ (⟦b:viā-⟧); ⟦b:fundi-tor⟧, ⟦i:slinger⟧ (⟦b:fundā-⟧). ⟦b:-tro-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ter⟧, has the meaning of ⟦b:-tōr-⟧: as, ⟦b:aus-tro-⟧, N. ⟦b:aus-ter⟧ (⟦i:scorcher⟧), ⟦i:south-wester⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:aus-⟧⟧, ⟦i:burn⟧).
⟦#207⟧
In the present sense ⟦b:-tōr-⟧ (⟦b:-sōr-⟧) is also used to indicate permanent character, quality, capability, tendency, likelihood: as, ⟦b:bellā-tor⟧, ⟦i:a man of war⟧, ⟦i:warlike⟧; ⟦b:dēlīberā-tor⟧, ⟦i:a man of caution⟧; ⟦b:cessā-tor⟧, ⟦i:a loiterer⟧; ⟦b:dērī-sor⟧, ⟦i:a mocker⟧, ⟦i:ironical⟧; ⟦b:cōnsūmp-tor⟧, ⟦i:apt to destroy⟧, ⟦i:destructive⟧; ⟦b:aedificā-tor⟧, ⟦i:building-mad⟧.
⟦#208⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) ⟦b:-tōr-⟧ (⟦b:-sōr-⟧), in a perfect sense, is used particularly in old Latin, or to denote an agent who has acquired a permanent name by a single conspicuous action. In this sense it usually has a genitive of the object, or a possessive pronoun: thus,
⟦b:castīgā-tor meus⟧, ⟦i:my mentor⟧, or ⟦i:the man who has upbraided me⟧; ⟦b:olīvae inven-tor⟧, ⟦i:the deviser of the olive⟧ (Aristaeus); ⟦b:reper-tor vītis⟧, ⟦i:the author of the vine⟧ (Bacchus); ⟦b:patriae līberā-tōrēs⟧, ⟦i:the emancipators of the nation⟧.

title: -o- (N. -u-s), -ā- (N. -a); -lo- (N. -lu-s); -ōn- (N. -ō)
text:
⟦#209⟧
⟦b:-o-⟧ and ⟦b:-ā-⟧ stems may denote vocation or class; many are compounds. ⟦b:-o-⟧, N. ⟦b:-u-s⟧: ⟦b:coqu-o-⟧, N. ⟦b:coqu-o-s⟧ or ⟦b:coc-u-s⟧, ⟦i:cook⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:coqu-⟧⟧, ⟦i:cook⟧); ⟦b:causidic-u-s⟧, ⟦i:pleader⟧ (⟦b:causā-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:dic-⟧⟧, ⟦i:speak⟧). ⟦b:-ā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-a⟧: ⟦b:scrīb-ā-⟧, N. ⟦b:scrīb-a⟧, ⟦i:clerk⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:scrīb-⟧⟧, ⟦i:write⟧); ⟦b:agricol-a⟧, ⟦i:husbandman⟧ (⟦b:agro-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:col-⟧⟧, ⟦i:till⟧).
⟦#210⟧
⟦b:-u-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-u-lu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:ger-ulo-⟧, N. ⟦b:ger-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:bearer⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ges-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧); ⟦b:fig-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:potter⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fig-⟧⟧, ⟦i:shape⟧, ⟦i:mould⟧).
⟦#211⟧
⟦b:-ōn-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ō-⟧: ⟦b:err-ōn-⟧, N. ⟦b:err-ō⟧, ⟦i:stroller⟧ (⟦b:errā-re⟧); especially in compounds: ⟦b:praed-ō⟧, ⟦i:robber⟧ (⟦b:praedā-rī⟧); ⟦b:praec-ō⟧ for ⟦b:*praevocō⟧, ⟦i:herald⟧ (⟦b:prae-vocā-re⟧); ⟦b:combib-ō⟧, ⟦i:fellow-drinker⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:bib-⟧⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧).

title: The Action
text:
⟦#212⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-ā-⟧, ⟦b:-io-⟧, ⟦b:-iā-⟧; ⟦b:-min-⟧; ⟦b:-i-ōn-⟧, ⟦b:-ti-ōn-⟧; ⟦b:-lā-⟧; ⟦b:-mā-⟧, ⟦b:-nā-⟧; ⟦b:-tā-⟧, ⟦b:-tu-⟧; ⟦b:-er-⟧, ⟦b:-or-⟧, ⟦b:-ōr-⟧, are used to denote the ⟦i:Action⟧: as,
⟦b:od-io-⟧  ⟦b:odium⟧, ⟦i:hate⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:od-⟧⟧, ⟦i:hate⟧
⟦b:āc-tiōn-⟧  ⟦b:āctiō⟧, ⟦i:action⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:āg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:do⟧
⟦b:ques-tu-⟧  ⟦b:questus⟧, ⟦i:complaint⟧  √⟦b:q⟧⟦b:⟦i:ues-⟧⟧, ⟦i:complain⟧
⟦b:fur-ōr-⟧  ⟦b:furor⟧, ⟦i:rage⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:fur-⟧⟧, ⟦i:rave⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.
⟦#213⟧
Words denoting action (⟦r1470:1470⟧) in a substantive form have a wide range of meaning; they may denote, according to the connection, action intransitive, transitive, or passive, complete or incomplete; if the verb denotes condition or state, the word of action often comes very near to denominatives of quality; furthermore the idea of action is often lost, and passes over to result, concrete effect, means or instrument, or place.

title: -ā- (N. -a); -io- (N. -iu-m); -iā- (N. -ia), -iē- (N. -iē-s)
text:
⟦#214⟧
⟦b:-ā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-a⟧, is rare in words of action: ⟦b:fug-ā-⟧, N. ⟦b:fug-a⟧, ⟦i:flight⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fug-⟧⟧, ⟦i:fly⟧); most words are concrete: ⟦b:mol-a⟧, ⟦i:mill⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:mol-⟧⟧, ⟦i:grind⟧); ⟦b:tog-a⟧, ⟦i:covering⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:teg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:cover⟧).
⟦#215⟧
⟦b:-ūr-ā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ūr-a⟧, is rare: ⟦b:fig-ūrā-⟧, N. ⟦b:fig-ūra⟧, ⟦i:shape⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fig-⟧⟧, ⟦i:shape⟧).
⟦#216⟧
⟦b:-tūr-ā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tūr-a⟧, or ⟦b:-sūr-ā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-sūr-a⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧, ⟦r202:202⟧), akin to the agent in ⟦b:-tōr-⟧ (⟦b:-sōr-⟧): ⟦b:armā-tūrā-⟧, N. ⟦b:armā-tūra⟧, ⟦i:equipment⟧ (⟦b:armā-re⟧); ⟦b:pīc-tūra⟧, ⟦i:painting⟧, i.e., ⟦i:act of painting⟧ or ⟦i:picture⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pig-⟧⟧, ⟦i:paint⟧). Words parallel with official personal names (⟦r206:206⟧) denote office: ⟦b:cēn-sūra⟧, ⟦i:taxing⟧, ⟦i:censor’s office⟧ (cf. ⟦b:cēnsōr-⟧); ⟦b:prae-tūra⟧, ⟦i:praetorship⟧ (cf. ⟦b:praetōr-⟧).
⟦#217⟧
⟦b:-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-iu-m⟧, sometimes denotes the effect or the object. The line cannot always be drawn very sharply between these stems in ⟦b:-io-⟧ (many of which may be formed through a presumed noun stem), and denominatives in ⟦b:-io-⟧ (⟦r249:249⟧).
⟦#218⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) ⟦b:-io-⟧ is rarely suffixed to simple roots or verb stems: ⟦b:od-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:od-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:hate⟧, ⟦i:hateful thing⟧, ⟦i:hateful conduct⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:od-⟧⟧, ⟦i:hate⟧); some words become concrete: ⟦b:lab-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:lip⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:lab-⟧⟧, ⟦i:lick⟧).
⟦#219⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) Most primitives in ⟦b:-io-⟧ are compounds: as, ⟦b:adag-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:proverb⟧ (⟦b:ad⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:ag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:speak⟧); ⟦b:ingen-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:disposition⟧ (in, √⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧); ⟦b:dīscid-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:separation⟧, ⟦b:exscid-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:destruction⟧ (⟦b:dī-⟧, ⟦b:ex⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:scid-⟧⟧, ⟦i:cleave⟧); ⟦b:incend-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:conflagration⟧ (in, √⟦b:⟦i:cand-⟧⟧, ⟦i:light⟧); ⟦b:obsequ-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:compliance⟧ (⟦b:ob-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:sequ-⟧⟧, ⟦i:follow⟧); ⟦b:conloqu-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:parley⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:loqu-⟧⟧, ⟦i:talk⟧); ⟦b:obsid-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:siege⟧ (⟦b:ob⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:sed-⟧⟧, ⟦i:sit⟧).
⟦#220⟧
⟦b:-t-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-t-iu-m⟧: ⟦b:spa-tio-⟧, N. ⟦b:spa-tiu-m⟧, ⟦i:stretch⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:spa-⟧⟧, ⟦i:span⟧, ⟦i:stretch⟧); ⟦b:sōlsti-tiu-m⟧, ⟦i:sun-stand⟧, ⟦i:solstice⟧ (⟦b:sōl-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:sta-⟧⟧, ⟦i:stand⟧); ⟦b:ini-tiu-m⟧, ⟦i:a beginning⟧ (⟦b:in⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:i-⟧⟧, ⟦i:go⟧).
⟦#221⟧
⟦b:-iā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ia⟧: ⟦b:fur-iā-⟧, N. ⟦b:fur-iae⟧, plural, ⟦i:ravings⟧, ⟦i:madness⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fur-⟧⟧, ⟦i:rave⟧); ⟦b:pluvia⟧, ⟦i:rain⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pluv-⟧⟧, ⟦i:rain⟧). Most stems in ⟦b:-iā-⟧ are compounds, used in the plural only, often with concrete or passive meaning: ⟦i:dēlic-iae⟧, ⟦i:allurements⟧, ⟦i:pet⟧ (⟦b:dē⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:lac-⟧⟧, ⟦i:allure⟧); ⟦b:excub-iae⟧, ⟦i:patrol⟧ (⟦b:ex⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:cub-⟧⟧, ⟦i:lie⟧).
⟦#222⟧
⟦b:-iē-⟧, N. ⟦b:-iē-s⟧, a variation of ⟦b:-iā-⟧, usually denotes result (⟦r604:604⟧): ⟦b:ser-iē-⟧, N. ⟦b:ser-iē-s⟧, ⟦i:row⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ser-⟧⟧, ⟦i:string⟧); ⟦b:spec-iē-s⟧, ⟦i:sight⟧, ⟦i:looks⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:spec-⟧⟧, ⟦i:spy⟧, ⟦i:see⟧); ⟦b:pernic-iē-s⟧, ⟦i:destruction⟧ (⟦b:per⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:nec-⟧⟧, ⟦i:murder⟧).
⟦#223⟧
⟦b:-t-iē-⟧, N. ⟦b:-t-iē-s⟧: ⟦b:permi-tiē-⟧, N. ⟦b:permi-tiē-s⟧, ⟦i:wasting away⟧ (⟦b:per⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:mi-⟧⟧, ⟦i:less⟧).

title: -min- (103) (N. -men); -din-, -gin- (105, g) (N. -dō, -gō)
text:
⟦#224⟧
⟦b:-min-⟧, N. ⟦b:-men⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), usually active, occasionally passive, is very common; it sometimes denotes the means, instrument, or effect.
⟦b:certā-min-⟧, N. ⟦b:certā-men⟧, ⟦i:contest⟧ (⟦b:certā-re⟧); ⟦b:crī-men⟧, ⟦i:charge⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:cer-⟧⟧, ⟦b:crī-⟧, ⟦i:sift⟧); ⟦b:spec-imen⟧, ⟦i:what is inspected⟧, ⟦i:sample⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:spec-⟧⟧, ⟦i:spy⟧, ⟦i:see⟧); ⟦b:lū-men⟧, ⟦i:light⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:lūc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:light⟧); ⟦b:flū-men⟧, ⟦i:flood⟧, ⟦i:stream⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:flugṷ-⟧⟧, ⟦i:flow⟧); ⟦b:ag-men⟧, ⟦i:what is led⟧, ⟦i:train⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:lead⟧). Words in ⟦b:-min-⟧ often mean nearly the same as those in ⟦b:-mento-⟧ (⟦r239:239⟧): as, ⟦b:levā-men⟧, ⟦b:levā-mentu-m⟧, ⟦i:lightening⟧; ⟦b:teg-umen⟧, ⟦b:teg-umentu-m⟧, ⟦i:covering⟧.
⟦#225⟧
⟦b:ē-din-⟧, ⟦b:-ī-din-⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:-ē-din-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ē-dō⟧: ⟦b:grav-ēdin-⟧, N. ⟦b:grav-ēdō⟧, (⟦i:heaviness⟧), ⟦i:catarrh⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:grav-⟧⟧, ⟦i:heavy⟧), ⟦b:-ī-din-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ī-dō⟧: ⟦b:cup-īdin-⟧, N. ⟦b:cup-īdō⟧, ⟦i:desire⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:cup-⟧⟧, ⟦i:desire⟧); ⟦b:lib-idō⟧, ⟦i:whim⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:lib-⟧⟧, ⟦i:yearn⟧).
⟦#226⟧
⟦b:-ā-gin-⟧, ⟦b:-ī-gin-⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:-ā-gin-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ā-gō⟧: ⟦b:vorā-gin-⟧, N. ⟦b:vorā-gō⟧, ⟦i:gulf⟧ (⟦b:vorā-re⟧); ⟦b:imā-gō⟧, ⟦i:representation⟧ (⟦b:*imā-⟧, cf. ⟦b:imitārī⟧). ⟦b:-ī-gin-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ī-gō⟧: ⟦b:orī-gin-⟧, N. ⟦b:orī-gō⟧, ⟦i:source⟧ (⟦b:orī-rī⟧); ⟦b:cāl-īgō⟧, ⟦i:darkness⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:cāl-⟧⟧, ⟦i:hide⟧). A few denominatives have ⟦b:-ū-gin-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ū-gō⟧: ⟦b:aer-ūgin-⟧, N. ⟦b:aer-ūgō⟧, ⟦i:copper rust⟧ (⟦b:aer-⟧).

title: -i-ōn- (N. -i-ō); -ti-ōn- or -si-ōn- (N. -ti-ō or -si-ō)
text:
⟦#227⟧
⟦b:-i-ōn-⟧, N. ⟦b:-i-ō⟧: ⟦b:opīn-iōn-⟧, N. ⟦b:opīn-iō⟧, ⟦i:notion⟧ (⟦b:opīnā-rī⟧); ⟦b:condic-iō⟧, ⟦i:agreement⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:dic-⟧⟧, ⟦i:say⟧); ⟦b:contāg-iō⟧, ⟦i:touch⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:tag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:touch⟧). Some words are concrete: ⟦b:leg-iō⟧, ⟦i:pick⟧, ⟦i:legion⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:leg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:pick⟧). A few are denominatives: ⟦b:commūn-iō⟧, ⟦i:mutual participation⟧ (⟦b:commūni-⟧).
⟦#228⟧
⟦b:-ti-ōn-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ti-ō⟧, or ⟦b:-si-ōn-⟧, N. ⟦b:-si-ō⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧, ⟦r202:202⟧), is very common, and may denote action either intransitive, transitive, or passive, or the manner or possibility of action.
⟦b:cōgitā-tiōn-⟧, N. ⟦b:cōgitā-tiō⟧, ⟦i:a thinking⟧, ⟦i:a thought⟧ (⟦i:cōgitā-re⟧); ⟦b:exīstimā-tiō⟧, ⟦i:judging⟧, ⟦i:reputation⟧ (⟦b:exīstimā-re⟧); ⟦b:coven-tiō⟧, commonly ⟦b:cōn-tiō⟧, ⟦i:meeting⟧, ⟦i:speech⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:ven-⟧⟧, ⟦i:come⟧); ⟦b:dēpul-siō⟧, ⟦i:warding off⟧ (⟦b:dē-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:pol-⟧⟧, ⟦i:push⟧); ⟦b:oppugnā-tiō⟧, ⟦i:besieging⟧, ⟦i:method of besieging⟧ (⟦b:oppugnā-re⟧); ⟦b:occultā-tiō⟧, ⟦i:hiding⟧, ⟦i:chance to hide⟧, ⟦i:possibility of hiding⟧ (⟦b:occultā-re⟧). Some words denote the place where: ⟦b:sta-tiō⟧, ⟦i:a stand⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sta-⟧⟧, ⟦i:stand⟧); some become collectives or concretes: ⟦b:salūtā-tiō⟧, ⟦i:greeting⟧, ⟦i:levee⟧, ⟦i:guests at a levee⟧ (⟦b:salūtā-re⟧); ⟦b:mūnī-tiō⟧, ⟦i:fortification⟧, i.e., ⟦i:act of fortifying or works⟧ (⟦b:mūnī-re⟧).

title: -ē-lā- (N. -ē-la), -tē-lā- (N. -tē-la)
text:
⟦#229⟧
⟦b:-ē-lā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ē-la⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:suādē-lā-⟧, N. ⟦b:suādē-la⟧, ⟦i:persuasion⟧ (⟦b:suādē-rē⟧): ⟦b:loqu-ēla⟧, ⟦i:talk⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:loqu-⟧⟧, ⟦i:talk⟧); ⟦b:quer-ēla⟧ or ⟦b:quer-ēlla⟧, ⟦i:complaint⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ques-⟧⟧, ⟦i:complain⟧). Some words are concrete: ⟦b:candē-la⟧, ⟦i:candle⟧ (⟦b:candē-re⟧).
⟦#230⟧
⟦b:-tē-lā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tē-la-⟧: ⟦b:conrup-tēlā-⟧, N. ⟦b:conrup-tēla⟧, ⟦i:a seduction⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:rup-⟧⟧, ⟦i:spoil⟧, ⟦i:ruin⟧); ⟦b:tū-tēla⟧, ⟦i:protection⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:tū-⟧⟧, ⟦i:watch⟧, ⟦i:protect⟧).

title: -mā- (N. -ma), -nā- (N. -na); -trī-nā- (N. -trī-na)
text:
⟦#231⟧
⟦b:-mā-⟧ and ⟦b:-nā-⟧ are rare, and denote result or something concrete. ⟦b:-mā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ma⟧: ⟦b:fā-mā-⟧, N. ⟦b:fā-ma⟧, ⟦i:tale⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fā-⟧⟧, ⟦i:tell⟧); ⟦b:-nā⟧, N. ⟦b:-na⟧: ⟦b:ur-na⟧, ⟦i:pitcher⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:urc-⟧⟧ in ⟦b:urc-eus⟧, ⟦i:pitcher⟧, 170, 3); with original suffix ⟦b:-sna⟧ (⟦r170:170, 2⟧): ⟦b:lū-na⟧, ⟦i:moon⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:lūc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:light⟧); ⟦b:scāla⟧, ⟦i:stairs⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:scand-⟧⟧, ⟦i:mount⟧).
⟦#232⟧
⟦b:-inā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ina⟧: ⟦b:ang-inā-⟧, N. ⟦b:ang-ina⟧, ⟦i:choking⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ang-⟧⟧, ⟦i:choke⟧); ⟦b:pāg-ina⟧, ⟦i:page⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pāg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:fasten⟧); ⟦b:sarc-ina⟧, ⟦i:package⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sarc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:patch⟧). ⟦b:-īnā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-īna⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:ru-īnā-⟧, N. ⟦b:ru-īna⟧, ⟦i:downfall⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ru-⟧⟧, ⟦i:tumble⟧); ⟦b:-īnā-⟧ is very common in denominatives: ⟦b:pisc-īna⟧, ⟦i:fish-pond⟧ (⟦b:pisci-⟧).
⟦#233⟧
⟦b:-trī-nā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-trī-na⟧, akin to the agent in ⟦b:-tōr-⟧: ⟦b:doc-trīnā-⟧, N. ⟦b:doc-trīna⟧, ⟦i:teaching⟧, either ⟦i:the act of teaching⟧ or ⟦i:what is taught⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:doc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:teach⟧); ⟦b:sū-trīna⟧, ⟦i:shoemaking⟧, ⟦i:shoemaker’s trade⟧, ⟦i:shoemaker’s shop⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sū-⟧⟧, ⟦i:sew⟧).

title: -tā- or -sā- (N. -ta or -sa); -tu- or -su- (N. -tu-s or -su-s)
text:
⟦#234⟧
⟦b:-tā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ta⟧, or ⟦b:-sā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-sa⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧), is rare, and sometimes denotes result, or something concrete: as, ⟦b:no-tā-⟧, N. ⟦b:no-ta⟧, ⟦i:mark⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:gno-⟧⟧, ⟦i:know⟧); ⟦b:por-ta⟧ (⟦i:passage⟧), ⟦i:gate⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:por-⟧⟧, ⟦i:fare⟧); ⟦b:fos-sa⟧, ⟦i:ditch⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fod-⟧⟧, ⟦i:dig⟧); ⟦b:repul-sa⟧, ⟦i:repulse⟧ (⟦b:re-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:pol-⟧⟧, ⟦i:push⟧); ⟦b:offēn-sa⟧, ⟦i:offence⟧ (⟦b:ob⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:fend-⟧⟧, ⟦i:strike⟧).
⟦#235⟧
⟦b:-tu-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tu-s⟧, or ⟦b:-su-⟧, N. ⟦b:-su-s⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧, ⟦r202:202⟧), denotes the action and its results: ⟦b:ques-tu-⟧, N. ⟦b:ques-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:complaint⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ques-⟧⟧, ⟦i:complain⟧); ⟦b:gem-itus⟧, ⟦i:groan⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:gem-⟧⟧, ⟦i:groan⟧). Stems in ⟦b:-ā-tu-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ā-tu-s⟧, sometimes denote office or officials: ⟦b:cōnsul-ātu-⟧, N. ⟦b:cōnsul-ātu-s⟧, ⟦i:being consul⟧, ⟦i:consulship⟧ (⟦b:cōnsul-⟧); ⟦b:sen-ātu-s⟧, ⟦i:senate⟧ (⟦b:sen-⟧). ⟦b:-tu-⟧ is seldom passive: ⟦b:vī-su-s⟧, active, ⟦i:sight⟧, passive, ⟦i:looks⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:vīd-⟧⟧, ⟦i:see⟧); ⟦b:apparā-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:preparation⟧, either ⟦i:a getting ready⟧, or ⟦i:what is got ready⟧ (⟦b:apparā-re⟧). The supine (⟦r2269:2269⟧) is the accusative or ablative of substantives in ⟦b:-tu-⟧ (⟦b:-su-⟧). Most words in ⟦b:-tu-⟧ (⟦b:-su-⟧) are defective in case, and are chiefly used in the ablative (⟦r430:430⟧).

title: -er- for -es- (N. -us); -ōr- (N. -or)
text:
⟦#236⟧
Neuter stems in ⟦b:-er-⟧ (for ⟦b:-es-⟧), or in ⟦b:-or-⟧ (for ⟦b:-os-⟧), N. ⟦b:-us⟧, denote result, or have a concrete meaning: ⟦b:gen-er-⟧, N. ⟦b:gen-us⟧, ⟦i:birth⟧, ⟦i:race⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧); ⟦b:op-er-⟧, N. ⟦b:op-us⟧, ⟦i:work⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:op-⟧⟧, ⟦i:work⟧); ⟦b:frīg-or-⟧, N. ⟦b:frīg-us⟧, ⟦i:cold⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:frīg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:cold⟧). ⟦b:-ēs⟧ with lengthened ⟦b:ē⟧ is sometimes used in the nominative of gender words: as, ⟦b:nūb-ēs⟧, ⟦i:cloud⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:nūb-⟧⟧, ⟦i:veil⟧); ⟦b:sēd-ēs⟧, ⟦i:seat⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sēd-⟧⟧); ⟦b:vāt-ēs⟧, ⟦i:bard⟧. ⟦b:-n-er-⟧, ⟦b:-n-or-⟧, N. ⟦b:-n-us⟧: ⟦b:vol-ner-⟧, N. ⟦b:vol-nus⟧, ⟦i:wound⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:vol-⟧⟧, ⟦i:tear⟧); ⟦b:fac-inor-⟧, N. ⟦b:fac-inus⟧, ⟦i:deed⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fac-⟧⟧, ⟦i:do⟧, ⟦r202:202⟧).
⟦#237⟧
⟦b:-ōr-⟧ (for an older form ⟦b:-ōs-⟧, ⟦r154:154⟧), N. ⟦b:-ōs⟧, commonly ⟦b:-or⟧, masculine, denotes a state. Many substantives in ⟦b:-ōr-⟧ have a parallel verb, usually in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ (⟦r368:368⟧), and an adjective in ⟦b:-ido-⟧ (⟦r287:287⟧).
⟦b:od-ōr-⟧, N. ⟦b:od-ōs⟧ or ⟦b:od-or⟧, ⟦i:smell⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:od-⟧⟧, ⟦i:smell⟧, cf. ⟦b:olē-re⟧); ⟦b:pall-or⟧, ⟦i:paleness⟧ (cf. ⟦b:pallē-re⟧); ⟦b:cal-or⟧, ⟦i:warmth⟧ (cf. ⟦b:calē-re⟧); ⟦b:ūm-or⟧, ⟦i:moisture⟧ (cf. ⟦b:ūmē-re⟧); ⟦b:am-or⟧, ⟦i:love⟧ (cf. ⟦b:amā-re⟧); ⟦b:ang-or⟧, ⟦i:choking⟧, ⟦i:anguish⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ang-⟧⟧, ⟦i:choke⟧).

title: The Instrument or Means
text:
⟦#238⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-men-to-⟧, ⟦b:-tro-⟧, ⟦b:-cro-⟧ or ⟦b:-culo-⟧, ⟦b:-lo-⟧, ⟦b:-bro-⟧ or ⟦b:-bulo-⟧, are used to denote the ⟦i:Instrument⟧ or ⟦i:Means⟧: as,
⟦b:ōrnā-mento-⟧  ⟦b:ōrnāmentum⟧, ⟦i:embellishment⟧  ⟦b:ōrnā-re⟧, ⟦i:embellish⟧
⟦b:arā-tro-⟧  ⟦b:arātrum⟧, ⟦i:plough⟧  ⟦b:arā-re⟧, ⟦i:plough⟧
⟦b:pō-culo-⟧  ⟦b:pōculum⟧, ⟦i:drinking-cup⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:pō-⟧⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧
⟦b:pā-bulo-⟧  ⟦b:pābulum⟧, ⟦i:fodder⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:pā-⟧⟧, ⟦i:feed⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.
⟦#239⟧
⟦b:-men-to-⟧, N. ⟦b:-men-tu-m⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), is one of the commonest suffixes; it sometimes denotes result of action, rarely action itself.
⟦b:pig-mento-⟧, N. ⟦b:pig-mentu-m⟧, ⟦i:paint⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pīg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:paint⟧); ⟦b:experī-mentu-m⟧, ⟦i:test⟧ (⟦b:experī-rī⟧); ⟦b:ōrnā-mentu-m⟧, ⟦i:ornament⟧ (⟦b:ōrnā-re⟧); ⟦b:frag-mentu-m⟧, ⟦i:fragment⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:frag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:break⟧); ⟦b:cae-mentu-m⟧, ⟦i:quarried stone⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:caed-⟧⟧, ⟦i:cut⟧); ⟦b:incrē-mentu-m⟧, ⟦i:growth⟧ (⟦b:in⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:crē-⟧⟧, ⟦i:grow⟧); ⟦b:al-imentu-m⟧, ⟦i:nourishment⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:al-⟧⟧, ⟦i:nurture⟧); ⟦b:doc-umentu-m⟧, ⟦i:lesson⟧ (√⟦b:doc-⟧, ⟦i:teach⟧). See also ⟦b:-min-⟧ (⟦r224:224⟧). ⟦b:-men-tā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-men-ta⟧, F., is rare: ⟦b:ful-menta⟧, ⟦i:prop⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fulc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:prop⟧); ⟦b:rā-menta⟧, ⟦i:scraping⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:rād-⟧⟧, ⟦i:scrape⟧).
⟦#240⟧
⟦b:-tro-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tru-m⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:arā-tro-⟧, N. ⟦b:arā-tru-m⟧, ⟦i:plough⟧ (⟦b:arā-re⟧); ⟦b:fer-etru-m⟧, ⟦i:bier⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fer-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧); ⟦b:rōs-tru-m⟧, ⟦i:beak⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:rōd-⟧⟧, ⟦i:peck⟧). Sometimes ⟦b:-stro-⟧: ⟦b:mōn-stru-m⟧, ⟦i:warning⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:mon-⟧⟧, ⟦i:mind⟧); ⟦b:lu-stra⟧, plural, ⟦i:fen⟧, ⟦i:jungle⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:lu-⟧⟧, ⟦i:wash⟧); ⟦b:lū-stru-m⟧, ⟦i:purification⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:lou-⟧⟧, ⟦i:wash⟧). ⟦b:-trā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tra⟧, F.: ⟦b:mulc-trā-⟧, N. ⟦b:mulc-tra⟧ (also ⟦b:mulc-tru-m⟧, Ne.), ⟦i:milking-pail⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:mulg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:milk⟧). ⟦b:-es-trā-⟧: ⟦b:fen-estra⟧, ⟦i:window⟧.
⟦#241⟧
⟦b:-cro-⟧, N. ⟦b:-cru-m⟧, used when an ⟦b:l⟧ precedes: ⟦b:ful-cro-⟧, N. ⟦b:ful-cru-m⟧, ⟦i:couch-leg⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fulc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:prop⟧). ⟦b:-cro-⟧ sometimes denotes the place where: ⟦b:ambulā-cru-m⟧, ⟦i:promenade⟧ (⟦b:ambulā-re⟧); sometimes the effect: ⟦b:simulā-cru-m⟧, ⟦i:likeness⟧ (⟦b:simulā-re⟧).
⟦#242⟧
⟦b:-culo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-culu-m⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:pō-culo-⟧, N. ⟦b:pō-culu-m⟧, ⟦i:cup⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pō-⟧⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧); ⟦b:fer-culu-m⟧, ⟦i:tray⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fer-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧). ⟦b:-culo-⟧ sometimes denotes the place where: ⟦b:cub-iculu-m⟧, ⟦i:sleeping-room⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:cub-⟧⟧, ⟦i:lie⟧); ⟦b:cēnā-culu-m⟧, originally ⟦i:dining-room⟧, usually ⟦i:garret⟧ (⟦b:cēnā-re⟧).
⟦#243⟧
⟦b:-u-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-u-lu-m-⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): chiefly after ⟦b:c⟧ or ⟦b:g⟧: ⟦b:vinc-ulo-⟧, N. ⟦b:vinc-ulu-m⟧, ⟦i:bond⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:vinc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bind⟧); ⟦b:cing-ulu-m⟧, ⟦i:girdle⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:cing-⟧⟧, ⟦i:gird⟧). ⟦b:-u-lā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-u-la⟧, F., ⟦b:rēg-ula⟧, ⟦i:rule⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:rēg-⟧⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧).
⟦#244⟧
⟦b:-bro-⟧, N. ⟦b:-bru-m⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:crī-bro-⟧, N. ⟦b:crī-bru-m⟧, ⟦i:sieve⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:cer-⟧⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:crī-⟧⟧, ⟦i:sift⟧); ⟦b:lā-bru-m⟧, ⟦i:wash-basin⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:lav-⟧⟧, ⟦i:wash⟧). ⟦b:-brā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-bra⟧, F.: ⟦b:dolā-bra⟧, ⟦i:chisel⟧, ⟦i:mattock⟧ (⟦b:dolā-re⟧); ⟦b:late-bra⟧, ⟦i:hiding-place⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:lat-⟧⟧, ⟦i:hide⟧).
⟦#245⟧
⟦b:-bulo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-bulu-m⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:pā-bulo-⟧, N. ⟦b:pā-bulu-m⟧, ⟦i:fodder⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pā-⟧⟧, ⟦i:keep⟧); ⟦b:vēnā-bulu-m⟧, ⟦i:hunting-spear⟧ (⟦b:vēnā-rī⟧); ⟦b:pat-ibulu-m⟧, ⟦i:pillory⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pat-⟧⟧, ⟦i:stretch⟧). ⟦b:-bulo-⟧ sometimes denotes the place where: ⟦b:sta-bulu-m⟧, ⟦i:standing-place⟧, ⟦i:stall⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sta-⟧⟧, ⟦i:stand⟧). ⟦b:-bulā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-bula⟧, F., rare: ⟦b:sū-bula⟧, ⟦i:awl⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:su-⟧⟧, ⟦i:sew⟧); ⟦b:ta-bula⟧, ⟦i:board⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ta-⟧⟧, ⟦i:stretch⟧); ⟦b:fā-bula⟧, ⟦i:talk⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fā-⟧⟧, ⟦i:talk⟧).

title: The Quality
text:
⟦#246⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-io-⟧, ⟦b:-iā-⟧; ⟦b:-tā-⟧, ⟦b:-tāt-⟧, ⟦b:-tūt-⟧, ⟦b:-tū-din-⟧, are used to denote the ⟦i:Quality⟧: as,
⟦b:conlēg-io-⟧  ⟦b:conlēgium⟧, ⟦i:colleagueship⟧  ⟦b:conlēgā-⟧, N. ⟦b:conlēga⟧, ⟦i:colleague⟧
⟦b:audāc-iā-⟧  ⟦b:audācia⟧, ⟦i:boldness⟧  ⟦b:audāci-⟧, N. ⟦b:audāx⟧, ⟦i:bold⟧
⟦b:cīvi-tāt-⟧  ⟦b:cīvitās⟧, ⟦i:citizenship⟧  ⟦b:cīvi-⟧, N. ⟦b:cīvis⟧, ⟦i:citizen⟧
⟦b:magni-tūdin-⟧  ⟦b:magnitūdō⟧, ⟦i:greatness⟧  ⟦b:magno-⟧, N. ⟦b:magnus⟧, ⟦i:great⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.
⟦#247⟧
These abstracts are feminine, and come chiefly from adjectives or participles, except those in ⟦b:-io-⟧, which are neuters, and come mostly from substantives. Sometimes the same stem takes two or more of these suffixes: as, ⟦b:clāri-tāt-⟧ or ⟦b:clāri-tūdin-⟧, ⟦i:brightness⟧ (⟦b:clāro-⟧); ⟦b:iuven-tūt-⟧, in poetry ⟦b:iuven-tāt-⟧ or ⟦b:iuven-tā-⟧, ⟦i:youth⟧ (⟦b:iuven-⟧).

title: -io- (N. -iu-m), -iā- (N. -ia), -iē- (N. -iēs)
text:
⟦#248⟧
⟦b:-iē-⟧ sometimes occurs as collateral form to ⟦b:-iā-⟧ (⟦r604:604⟧); ⟦b:-io-⟧ or ⟦b:-iā-⟧ is sometimes attached to other suffixes: thus, ⟦b:-t-io-⟧, ⟦b:-t-iā-⟧ (⟦b:-t-iē-⟧); ⟦b:-mōn-io-⟧, ⟦b:-mōn-iā-⟧; ⟦b:-cin-io-⟧.
⟦#249⟧
⟦b:-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-iu-m⟧, chiefly used in compounds, denotes ⟦i:belonging to⟧, with a very wide range of meaning; many of these words are clearly neuter adjectives in ⟦b:-io-⟧ (⟦r305:305⟧). Suffixed to personal names ⟦b:-io-⟧ often denotes the condition, action, or employment, which gives rise to the name; this meaning sometimes passes over to that of result, relation of persons, collection of persons, or place.
⟦#250⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) From simple noun stems: ⟦b:sen-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:sen-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:feeble old age⟧ (⟦b:sen-⟧); ⟦b:somn-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:dream⟧ (⟦b:somno-⟧); ⟦b:sāv-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:love-kiss⟧ (⟦b:suāvi-⟧); ⟦b:silent-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:silence⟧ (⟦b:silenti-⟧); ⟦b:crepund-ia⟧, plural, ⟦i:rattle⟧ (⟦b:*crepundo-⟧); ⟦b:mendāc-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:lie⟧ (⟦b:mendāci-⟧); ⟦b:sōlāc-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:comfort⟧ (⟦b:*sōlāci-⟧, ⟦i:comforting⟧).
⟦#251⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) Direct compounds (⟦r377:377⟧): ⟦b:aequinoct-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:equinox⟧ (⟦b:aequo-⟧, ⟦b:nocti-⟧); ⟦b:contubern-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:companionship⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, ⟦b:tabernā-⟧); ⟦b:prīvilēg-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:special enactment⟧ (⟦b:prīvo-⟧, ⟦b:lēg-⟧).
⟦#252⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) Indirect compounds (⟦r377:377⟧), chiefly from personal names: ⟦b:cōnsil-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:deliberating together⟧, ⟦i:faculty of deliberation⟧, ⟦i:conclusion⟧, ⟦i:advice⟧, ⟦i:deliberative body⟧ (⟦b:cōnsul-⟧); ⟦b:auspic-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:taking auspices⟧, ⟦i:auspices taken⟧ (⟦b:auspic-⟧); ⟦b:rēmig-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:rowing⟧, ⟦i:oars⟧, ⟦i:oarsmen⟧ (⟦b:rēmig-⟧); ⟦b:conlēg-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:colleagueship⟧, ⟦i:corporation⟧ (⟦b:conlēgā-⟧); ⟦b:aedific-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:building⟧ (⟦b:*aedific-⟧, ⟦i:builder⟧); ⟦b:perfug-iu-m⟧, ⟦i:asylum⟧ (⟦b:perfugā-⟧).
⟦#253⟧
⟦b:-t-io-⟧ N. ⟦b:-t-iu-m⟧, rare: ⟦b:servi-tio-⟧, N. ⟦b:servi-tiu-m⟧, ⟦i:slavery⟧, ⟦i:slaves⟧ (⟦b:servo-⟧); ⟦b:calvi-tiu-m⟧, ⟦i:baldness⟧ (⟦b:calvo-⟧).
⟦#254⟧
⟦b:-mōn-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-mōn-iu-m⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:testi-mōnio-⟧, N. ⟦b:testi-mōniu-m⟧, ⟦i:evidence⟧ (⟦b:testi-⟧); ⟦b:mātr-imōniu-m⟧, ⟦i:marriage⟧ (⟦b:mātr-⟧); ⟦b:patr-imōniu-m⟧, ⟦i:patrimony⟧ (⟦b:patr-⟧).
⟦#255⟧
⟦b:-cin-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-cin-iu-m⟧, rare: ⟦b:latrō-cinio-⟧, N. ⟦b:latrō-ciniu-m⟧, ⟦i:robbery⟧ (⟦b:latrōn-⟧); ⟦b:patrō-ciniu-m⟧, ⟦i:protection⟧ (⟦b:patrōno-⟧).
⟦#256⟧
⟦b:-iā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ia⟧, is very common indeed, forming abstracts from nouns, mostly adjectives or present participles.
⟦b:audāc-iā-⟧, N. ⟦b:audāc-ia⟧, ⟦i:boldness⟧ (⟦b:audāci-⟧); ⟦b:miser-ia⟧, ⟦i:wretchedness⟧ (⟦b:misero-⟧); ⟦b:abundant-ia⟧, ⟦i:plenty⟧ (⟦b:abundanti-⟧); ⟦b:scient-ia⟧, ⟦i:knowledge⟧ (⟦b:scienti-⟧); ⟦b:mīlit-ia⟧, ⟦i:warfare⟧ (⟦b:mīlit-⟧); ⟦b:victōr-ia⟧, ⟦i:victory⟧ (⟦b:victōr-⟧); ⟦b:māter-ia⟧, ⟦i:timber⟧ (⟦b:māter-⟧); ⟦b:custōd-ia⟧, ⟦i:guard⟧ (⟦b:custōd-⟧).
⟦#257⟧
⟦b:-iē-⟧, N. ⟦b:-iē-s⟧: ⟦b:pauper-iē-⟧, N. ⟦b:pauper-iē-s⟧, ⟦i:moderate means⟧ (⟦b:pauper-⟧). Most stems in ⟦b:-iē-⟧ are primitive (⟦r222:222⟧).
⟦#258⟧
⟦b:-t-iā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-t-ia⟧, is suffixed to a few adjective stems, chiefly in ⟦b:-o-⟧: ⟦b:iūsti-tiā-⟧, N. ⟦b:iūsti-tia⟧, ⟦i:justice⟧ (⟦b:iūsto-⟧); ⟦b:mali-tia⟧, ⟦i:wickedness⟧ (⟦b:malo-⟧); ⟦b:pudīci-tia⟧, ⟦i:shamefastness⟧ (⟦b:pudīco-⟧); ⟦b:trīsti-tia⟧, ⟦i:sadness⟧ (⟦b:trīsti-⟧).
⟦#259⟧
⟦b:-t-iē-⟧, N. ⟦b:-t-iē-s⟧, particularly as a collateral form of ⟦b:-t-iā-⟧ in the N., Ac., and Ab. singular (⟦r604:604⟧): ⟦b:molli-tiē-⟧, N. ⟦b:molli-tiē-s⟧, ⟦i:softness⟧ (⟦b:molli-⟧).
⟦#260⟧
⟦b:-mōn-iā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-mōn-ia⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:ācri-mōniā-⟧, N. ⟦b:ācri-mōnia⟧, ⟦i:sharpness⟧ (⟦b:ācri-⟧); ⟦b:parsi-mōnia⟧, ⟦i:economy⟧ (⟦b:parso-⟧). Analogously from roots, ⟦b:quer-imōnia⟧, ⟦i:complaint⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:ques-⟧⟧, ⟦i:complain⟧); ⟦b:al-imōnia⟧, ⟦i:nurture⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:al-⟧⟧, ⟦i:nurture⟧).

title: -tā- (N. -ta), -tāt- (N. -tā-s), -tūt- (N. -tū-s), -tū-din- (N. -tū-dō)
text:
⟦#261⟧
⟦b:-tā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ta⟧: chiefly poetic: ⟦b:iuven-tā-⟧, N. ⟦b:iuven-ta⟧, ⟦i:youth⟧ (⟦b:iuven-⟧); ⟦b:senec-ta⟧, ⟦i:age⟧ (⟦b:sen-ec-⟧).
⟦#262⟧
⟦b:-tāt-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tā-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), is one of the very commonest suffixes.
⟦b:pie-tāt-⟧, N. ⟦b:pie-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:dutifulness⟧ (⟦b:pio-⟧, ⟦r105:105⟧); ⟦b:fēlīci-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:happiness⟧ (⟦b:fēlīci-⟧); ⟦b:cīvi-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:citizenship⟧, ⟦i:the community⟧ (⟦b:cīvi-⟧); ⟦b:facili-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:easiness⟧, ⟦b:facul-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:ability⟧ (⟦b:facili-⟧); ⟦b:cāri-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:dearness⟧ (⟦b:cāro-⟧); ⟦b:auctōr-itā-s⟧, ⟦i:authority⟧ (⟦b:auctōr-⟧); ⟦b:līber-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:freedom⟧ (⟦b:lībro-⟧, 111, ⟦i:b⟧); ⟦b:maies-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:grandeur⟧ (⟦b:maiōs-⟧); ⟦b:volun-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:wish⟧ (⟦b:*volunti-⟧, ⟦r179:179⟧); ⟦b:venus-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:grace⟧ (⟦b:venusto-⟧, ⟦r179:179⟧); ⟦b:ae-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:age⟧ (⟦b:aevo-⟧, 111, ⟦i:a⟧); ⟦b:tempes-tā-s⟧, ⟦i:kind of time⟧, ⟦i:weather⟧ (⟦b:tempes-⟧).
⟦#263⟧
⟦b:-tūt-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tū-s⟧, only in ⟦b:iuven-tūt-⟧, N. ⟦b:iuven-tū-s⟧, ⟦i:youth⟧ (⟦b:iuven-⟧), ⟦b:senec-tū-s⟧, ⟦i:age⟧ (⟦b:senec-⟧), ⟦b:servi-tū-s⟧, ⟦i:slavery⟧ (⟦b:servo-⟧), and ⟦b:vir-tū-s⟧, ⟦i:manhood⟧ (⟦b:viro-⟧, ⟦r111:111⟧).
⟦#264⟧
⟦b:-tū-din-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tū-dō⟧, suffixed to adjective stems: ⟦b:magni-tūdin-⟧, N. ⟦b:magni-tūdō⟧, ⟦i:greatness⟧ (⟦b:magno-⟧); ⟦b:forti-túdō⟧, ⟦i:courage⟧ (⟦b:forti-⟧); and to a few participles: ⟦b:cōnsuē-tūdō⟧, ⟦i:custom⟧ (⟦b:cōnsuēto-⟧, ⟦r179:179⟧); ⟦b:sollici-tūdō⟧, ⟦i:anxiety⟧ (⟦b:sollicito-⟧); analogously ⟦b:valē-tūdō⟧, ⟦i:health⟧ (⟦b:*valēto-⟧, ⟦b:valēre⟧).

title: The Person Concerned
text:
⟦#265⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-ārio-⟧, ⟦b:-ōn-⟧, ⟦b:-iōn-⟧, ⟦b:-li-⟧, ⟦b:-no-⟧, and some others, are used to denote the ⟦i:Person concerned⟧ or ⟦i:occupied⟧ with a thing: as,
⟦b:sīc-ārio-⟧  ⟦b:sīcārius⟧, ⟦i:assassin⟧  ⟦b:sīcā-⟧, N. ⟦b:sīca⟧, ⟦i:dagger⟧
⟦b:āle-ōn-⟧  ⟦b:āleō⟧, ⟦i:gambler⟧  ⟦b:āleā-⟧, N. ⟦b:ālea⟧, ⟦i:die⟧
⟦b:lūd-iōn-⟧  ⟦b:lūdiō⟧, ⟦i:player⟧  ⟦b:lūdo-⟧, N. ⟦b:lūdus⟧, ⟦i:play⟧
⟦b:aedī-li-⟧  ⟦b:aedīlis⟧, ⟦i:aedile⟧  ⟦b:aedi-⟧, N. ⟦b:aedis⟧, ⟦i:house⟧
⟦b:tribū-no-⟧  ⟦b:tribūnus⟧, ⟦i:tribune⟧  ⟦b:tribu-⟧, N ⟦b:tribus⟧, ⟦i:tribe⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.

title: The Place
text:
⟦#266⟧
Neuters with the suffixes ⟦b:-tōrio-⟧, ⟦b:-ārio-⟧, ⟦b:-īli-⟧, ⟦b:-to-⟧, or ⟦b:-ēto-⟧ are often used to denote the ⟦i:Place⟧: as,
⟦b:audī-tōrio-⟧  ⟦b:audī-tōrium⟧, ⟦i:lecture-room⟧  ⟦b:audītōr-⟧, N. ⟦b:audītor⟧, ⟦i:hearer⟧
⟦b:aer-ārio-⟧  ⟦b:aerārium⟧, ⟦i:treasury⟧  ⟦b:aer-⟧, N. ⟦b:aes⟧, ⟦i:money⟧
