⟦b:ov-īli-⟧  ⟦b:ovīle⟧, ⟦i:sheepfold⟧  ⟦b:ovi-⟧, N. ⟦b:ovis⟧, ⟦i:sheep⟧
⟦b:murt-ēto-⟧  ⟦b:murtēta⟧, ⟦i:myrtlegroves⟧  ⟦b:murto-⟧, N. ⟦b:murtus⟧, ⟦i:myrtle⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.

title: The Substantive: Diminutives
text:
⟦#267⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-lo-⟧, ⟦b:-lā-⟧, or ⟦b:-cu-lo-⟧, ⟦b:-cu-lā-⟧, are used to form substantives with a ⟦i:Diminutive⟧ meaning. Diminutives may denote:
⟦#268⟧
(1.) Actual smallness: as, ⟦b:secūricula⟧, ⟦i:a little hatchet⟧; ⟦b:ventulus⟧, ⟦i:a bit of wind⟧; ⟦b:spēcula⟧, ⟦i:a ray of hope⟧.
⟦#269⟧
(2.) Imputed smallness: implying, (⟦i:a.⟧) admiration, affection, or compassion; (⟦i:b.⟧) contempt or irony. This diminutive, which usually serves to add point to sentences themselves of a playful, patronizing, or slurring character, is very hard to translate; ⟦i:little⟧ and ⟦i:small⟧ are often inadequate; ⟦i:old⟧ or ⟦i:poor⟧ will sometimes do; but usually recourse must be had to free translations adapted to the particular context: as,
⟦b:ōrātiuncula⟧, ⟦i:a gem of a speech⟧, ⟦i:an attempt at a speech⟧; ⟦b:mātercula⟧, ⟦i:an anxious mother⟧, ⟦i:poor mamma⟧, ⟦i:dear mamma⟧; ⟦b:lectulus⟧, ⟦i:one’s own little bed⟧; ⟦b:ānellus aureolus⟧, ⟦i:a gay gold ring⟧; ⟦b:Graeculī⟧, ⟦i:our Greek cousins⟧, ⟦i:the good people in Greece⟧; ⟦b:Graeculus⟧, ⟦i:a regular Greek⟧, ⟦i:your gentleman from Greece⟧; ⟦b:muliercula⟧, ⟦i:a pretty girl⟧, ⟦i:a lady gay⟧, ⟦i:one of the gentler sex⟧, ⟦i:a mere woman⟧, ⟦i:an unprotected female⟧, ⟦i:a maiden all forlorn⟧; ⟦b:lacrimula⟧, ⟦i:a wee tear⟧, ⟦i:a crocodile tear⟧; ⟦b:volpēcula⟧, ⟦i:Master Reynard⟧, ⟦i:dan Russel⟧; ⟦b:tōnstrīcula⟧, ⟦i:a common barber girl⟧; ⟦b:popellus⟧, ⟦i:rabble⟧; ⟦b:nummulī⟧, ⟦i:filthy lucre⟧; ⟦b:mercēdula⟧, ⟦i:an apology for pay⟧; ⟦b:ratiuncula⟧, ⟦i:a first rate reason⟧; ⟦b:caupōnula⟧, ⟦i:a low tavern⟧.
⟦#270⟧
Some diminutives have entirely lost the diminutive meaning: as, ⟦b:puella⟧, ⟦i:girl⟧, not necessarily ⟦i:little girl⟧; others have changed their original meaning: as, ⟦b:avunculus⟧, ⟦i:uncle⟧, originally ⟦i:grandpapa⟧; ⟦b:anguīlla⟧, ⟦i:eel⟧, originally ⟦i:little snake⟧. Some words are only found in the diminutive form: as, ⟦b:stēlla⟧, ⟦i:star⟧ (⟦b:*ster-⟧). Diminutives usually have the gender of their primitives; exceptions are rare: as, ⟦b:rāna⟧, ⟦i:frog⟧, ⟦b:F.⟧, ⟦b:rānunculus⟧, ⟦i:tadpole⟧, ⟦b:M.⟧

title: -lo- (N., M. -lu-s, Ne. -lu-m), -lā- (N. -la)
text:
⟦#271⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-o-⟧, ⟦b:-ā-⟧, or a mute (⟦b:-g-⟧, ⟦b:-c-⟧, ⟦b:-d-⟧, or ⟦b:-t-⟧), take ⟦b:-lo-⟧ or ⟦b:-lā-⟧, which is usually preceded by ⟦b:-u-⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧).
⟦b:hortu-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:hortu-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:little garden⟧ (⟦b:horto-⟧); ⟦b:oppidu-lu-m⟧, ⟦i:hamlet⟧ (⟦b:oppido-⟧); ⟦b:serru-lā-⟧, N. ⟦b:serru-la⟧, ⟦i:little saw⟧ (⟦b:serrā-⟧); ⟦b:rēg-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:chieftain⟧ (⟦b:rēg-⟧); ⟦b:vōc-ula⟧, ⟦i:a bit of a voice⟧ (⟦b:vōc-⟧); ⟦b:calc-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:pebble⟧ (⟦b:calci-⟧); ⟦b:nepōt-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:a grandson dear⟧ (⟦b:nepōt-⟧); ⟦b:aetāt-ula⟧, ⟦i:tender age⟧ (⟦b:aetāt-⟧).
⟦#272⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-eo-⟧, ⟦b:-io-⟧, or ⟦b:-vo-⟧, retain ⟦b:-o-⟧ before ⟦b:-lo-⟧; stems in ⟦b:-eā-⟧, ⟦b:-iā-⟧, or ⟦b:-vā-⟧, also have ⟦b:-o-⟧ before ⟦b:-lā-⟧.
⟦b:alveo-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:alveo-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:little tray⟧ (⟦b:alveo-⟧); ⟦b:gladio-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:little sword⟧ (⟦b:gladio-⟧); ⟦b:servo-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:little slave⟧ (⟦b:servo-⟧); ⟦b:nauseo-lā-⟧, N. ⟦b:nauseo-la⟧, ⟦i:a slight squeamishness⟧ (⟦b:nauseā-⟧); ⟦b:bēstio-la⟧, ⟦i:little animal⟧ (⟦b:bēstiā-⟧); ⟦b:fīlio-la⟧, ⟦i:little daughter⟧ (⟦b:fīliā-⟧).
⟦#273⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-lo-⟧, ⟦b:-ro-⟧, ⟦b:-no-⟧, and ⟦b:-lā-⟧, ⟦b:-rā-⟧, ⟦b:-nā-⟧, commonly drop the stem vowel and assimilate ⟦b:-r-⟧ or ⟦b:-n-⟧ to ⟦b:-l-⟧: thus: ⟦b:-el-lo-⟧, ⟦b:-el-lā-⟧ (111, ⟦i:b⟧; 166, 6, 7).
⟦b:catel-lo-⟧, for ⟦b:*catululo-⟧, N. ⟦b:catel-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:puppy⟧ (⟦b:catulo-⟧); ⟦b:agel-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:little field⟧ (⟦b:agro-⟧); ⟦b:asel-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:donkey⟧ (⟦b:asino-⟧); ⟦b:fābel-lā-⟧, N. ⟦b:fābel-la⟧, ⟦i:short story⟧ (⟦b:fābulā-⟧); ⟦b:umbel-la⟧, ⟦i:sunshade⟧ (⟦b:umbrā-⟧); ⟦b:pāgel-la⟧, ⟦i:short page⟧ (⟦b:pāginā-⟧). A few words are not thus changed: ⟦b:pueru-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:pueru-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:poor boy⟧ (⟦b:puero-⟧), as well as ⟦b:puel-lu-s⟧.
⟦#274⟧
Another vowel than ⟦b:e⟧ (⟦r172:172⟧, ⟦r3:3⟧) appears in: ⟦b:Hispāl-lu-s⟧ (⟦b:Hispāno-⟧), ⟦b:Messāl-la⟧ (⟦b:Messānā-⟧), proper names; ⟦b:corōl-la⟧, ⟦i:chaplet⟧ (⟦b:corōnā-⟧); ⟦b:ūl-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:the least one⟧, ⟦i:any at all⟧ (⟦b:ūno-⟧); ⟦b:Sūl-la⟧ (⟦b:Sūrā-⟧), proper name; ⟦b:lapil-lu-s⟧, for ⟦b:*lapid-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:pebble⟧ (⟦b:lapid-⟧). Also ⟦b:homul-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:son of the dust⟧ (⟦b:homon-⟧).

title: -cu-lo- (N., M. -cu-lu-s, Ne. -cu-lu-m), -cu-lā- (N. -cu-la)
text:
⟦#275⟧
Stems in a continuous sound (⟦b:-l-⟧, ⟦b:-n-⟧, ⟦b:-r-⟧, or ⟦b:-s-⟧), or in ⟦b:-i-⟧, ⟦b:-u-⟧, or ⟦b:-ē-⟧, usually take ⟦b:-cu-lo-⟧ or ⟦b:-cu-lā-⟧.
⟦b:sermūn-culo-⟧, N. ⟦b:sermūn-culu-s⟧, ⟦i:small-talk⟧ (⟦b:sermōn-⟧); ⟦b:virgun-culā-⟧, N. ⟦b:virgun-cula⟧, ⟦i:little maid⟧ (⟦b:virgon-⟧); ⟦b:homun-culu-s⟧, ⟦i:son of earth⟧ (⟦b:homon-⟧); ⟦b:arbus-cula⟧, ⟦i:tiny tree⟧ (⟦b:arbos-⟧); ⟦b:cor-culu-m⟧, ⟦i:heart of hearts⟧ (⟦b:cord-⟧, 170, 12); ⟦b:igni-culu-s⟧, ⟦i:spark⟧ (⟦b:igni-⟧); ⟦b:ani-cula⟧, ⟦i:grandam⟧ (⟦b:anu-⟧); ⟦b:diē-cula⟧, ⟦i:brief day⟧ (⟦b:diē-⟧); analogously, ⟦b:volpē-cula⟧ (⟦i:vixen⟧), ⟦i:little fox⟧ (⟦b:*volpē-⟧). Rarely with ⟦b:ī⟧: ⟦b:canī-cula⟧, ⟦i:little dog⟧ (⟦b:can-⟧).
⟦#276⟧
⟦b:-un-culo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-un-culu-s⟧: ⟦b:av-unculo-⟧, N. ⟦b:av-unculu-s⟧, ⟦i:uncle⟧ (⟦b:avo-⟧); ⟦b:rān-unculu-s⟧, ⟦i:tadpole⟧ (⟦b:rānā-⟧). ⟦b:-un-culā-⟧, N. ⟦b:-un-cula⟧: ⟦b:dom-unculā-⟧, N. ⟦b:dom-uncula⟧, ⟦i:little house⟧ (⟦b:domo-⟧).
⟦#277⟧
Diminutives are sometimes formed from other diminutives: ⟦b:cistel-lu-la⟧, ⟦i:casket⟧ (⟦b:cistel-la⟧, ⟦b:cistu-la⟧, ⟦b:cistā-⟧).
⟦#278⟧
A few other suffixes have a diminutive meaning: as, ⟦b:-ciōn-⟧, ⟦b:-leo-⟧, ⟦b:-astro-⟧, ⟦b:-ttā-⟧: ⟦b:homun-ciō⟧, ⟦i:manikin⟧, ⟦i:child of dust⟧ (⟦b:homon-⟧); ⟦b:acu-leu-s⟧, ⟦i:sting⟧ (⟦b:acu-⟧); ⟦b:Antōni-aster⟧, ⟦i:regular little Antony⟧; ⟦b:pīn-aster⟧, ⟦i:bastard pine⟧; ⟦b:Iūli-tta⟧, ⟦i:Juliet⟧ (⟦b:Iūliā-⟧); ⟦b:Pōlli-tta⟧, ⟦i:little Polla⟧ (⟦b:Pōllā-⟧).

title: Patronymics
text:
⟦#279⟧
Patronymics, or proper names which denote descent from a father or ancestor, have stems in ⟦b:-dā-⟧ (N. ⟦b:-dē-s⟧), F. ⟦b:-d-⟧ (N. ⟦b:-s⟧). These are chiefly Greek names used in poetry.
⟦b:Prīami-dā-⟧, N. ⟦b:Prīami-dē-s⟧, ⟦i:scion of Priam’s house⟧; ⟦b:Tantali-d-⟧, N. ⟦b:Tantali-s⟧, ⟦i:daughter of Tantalus⟧. ⟦b:Pēlī-dē-s⟧ (⟦b:Pēleu-s⟧); ⟦b:Aenea-dē-s⟧ (⟦b:Aenēā-⟧); ⟦b:Thestia-dē-s⟧ (⟦b:Thestio-⟧); ⟦b:Lāertia-dē-s⟧ (⟦b:Lāertā-⟧); ⟦b:Scīpia-dā-s⟧ (⟦b:Scīpiōn-⟧). ⟦b:F.⟧ sometimes ⟦b:-īnē⟧ or ⟦b:-ōnē⟧: ⟦b:Neptūnīnē⟧ (⟦b:Neptūno-⟧); ⟦b:Acrisiōnē⟧ (⟦b:Acrisio-⟧).

title: Primitives
text:
⟦#280⟧
Primitive adjectives may usually be divided into active and passive; but the same suffix often has either an active or a passive meaning. Under primitive adjectives belong the participles; but these will be mentioned in connection with the verb.

title: The Adjective: With an Active Meaning
text:
⟦#281⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-o-⟧, ⟦b:-uo-⟧, ⟦b:-ci-⟧, ⟦b:-lo-⟧, and ⟦b:-do-⟧, are used to form adjectives with an ⟦i:Active⟧ meaning: as,
⟦b:vag-o-⟧  ⟦b:vagus⟧, ⟦i:wandering⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:vag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:wander⟧
⟦b:contig-uo-⟧  ⟦b:contiguus⟧, ⟦i:touching⟧  ⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:tag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:touch⟧
⟦b:minā-ci-⟧  ⟦b:mināx⟧, ⟦i:threatening⟧  ⟦b:minā-rī⟧, ⟦i:threaten⟧
⟦b:cali-do-⟧  ⟦b:calidus⟧, ⟦i:warm⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:cal-⟧⟧, ⟦i:warm⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.

title: -o- (N. -u-s); -uo- (N. -uu-s)
text:
⟦#282⟧
⟦b:-o-⟧ (N. ⟦b:-u-s⟧): such words express nature or capacity: ⟦b:vag-o-⟧, N. ⟦b:vag-u-s⟧, ⟦i:roaming⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:vag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:roam⟧); ⟦b:vīv-u-s⟧, ⟦i:living⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:vīv-⟧⟧, ⟦i:live⟧); many are compounds: as, ⟦b:male-dic-u-s⟧, ⟦i:abusive⟧ (⟦b:male⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:dic-⟧⟧, ⟦i:say⟧); ⟦b:pro-fug-u-s⟧, ⟦i:flying on⟧ (⟦b:prō-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:fug-⟧⟧, ⟦i:fly⟧). Passive: ⟦b:fīd-u-s⟧, ⟦i:trustworthy⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fīd-⟧⟧, ⟦i:trust⟧).
⟦#283⟧
⟦b:-uo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-uu-s⟧: ⟦b:adsid-uo-⟧, N. ⟦b:adsid-uu-s⟧, ⟦i:unremitting⟧ (⟦b:ad⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:sed-⟧⟧, ⟦i:sit⟧); ⟦b:contig-uu-s⟧, ⟦i:touching⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:tag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:touch⟧); ⟦b:perpet-uu-s⟧, ⟦i:uninterrupted⟧ (⟦b:per⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:pet-⟧⟧, ⟦i:go⟧). Some words are passive: as, ⟦b:sal-vu-s⟧, ⟦i:safe⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sal-⟧⟧, ⟦i:save⟧); ⟦b:vac-uu-s⟧, ⟦i:empty⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:vac-⟧⟧, ⟦i:empty⟧); ⟦b:relic-uo-s⟧, ⟦i:left behind⟧ (⟦b:re-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:liqu-⟧⟧, ⟦i:leave⟧), later ⟦b:reliquos⟧, ⟦b:relicus⟧, ⟦b:reliquus⟧ (⟦r157:157⟧).

title: -ci- (N. -x); -lo- (N. -lu-s); -do- (N. -du-s)
text:
⟦#284⟧
⟦b:-ā-ci-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ā-x⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), denotes capacity, habit, or inclination, often implying censure: ⟦b:pugnā-ci-⟧, N. ⟦b:pugnā-x⟧, ⟦i:full of fight⟧ (⟦b:pugnā-re⟧); ⟦b:minā-x⟧, ⟦i:threatening⟧ (⟦b:minā-ri⟧); ⟦b:fer-āx⟧, ⟦i:productive⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fer-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧); ⟦b:dic-āx⟧, ⟦i:full of mother-wit⟧, ⟦i:quick at a joke⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:dic-⟧⟧, ⟦i:say⟧); ⟦b:rap-āx⟧, ⟦i:apt to snatch⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:rap-⟧⟧, ⟦i:snatch⟧).
⟦#285⟧
⟦b:-u-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-u-lu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), denotes simple action: as, ⟦b:pat-ulo-⟧, N. ⟦b:pat-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:spreading⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:pat-⟧⟧, ⟦i:spread⟧); or inclination: as, ⟦b:bib-ulu-s⟧, ⟦i:apt to drink⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:bib-⟧⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧).
⟦#286⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-undo-⟧ (⟦b:-endo-⟧), ⟦b:-bundo-⟧, and ⟦b:-cundo-⟧ form a group and are possibly related to the suffix in ⟦b:-do-⟧.
⟦#287⟧
⟦b:-do-⟧, N. ⟦b:-du-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), denotes a state, and usually has a parallel verb in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ (⟦r368:368⟧): ⟦b:cali-do-⟧, N. ⟦b:cali-du-s⟧ ⟦i:warm⟧ (cf. ⟦b:calē-re⟧); ⟦b:calli-du-s⟧, ⟦i:knowing⟧ (cf. ⟦b:callē-re⟧); ⟦b:niti-du-s⟧, ⟦i:shining⟧ (cf. ⟦b:nitē-re⟧); rarely in ⟦b:-ere⟧: ⟦b:cup-idu-s⟧, ⟦i:desirous⟧ (cf. ⟦b:cupe-re⟧); ⟦b:flui-du-s⟧, ⟦i:liquid⟧ (cf. ⟦b:flue-re⟧); ⟦b:rapi-du-s⟧, ⟦i:hurried⟧ (cf. ⟦b:rape-re⟧). ⟦b:-i-do-⟧ becomes ⟦b:-i-di-⟧ in ⟦b:viri-di-s⟧, ⟦i:green⟧ (cf. ⟦b:virē-re⟧). ⟦b:-do-⟧ sometimes occurs in denominatives: ⟦b:herbi-du-s⟧, ⟦i:grassy⟧ (⟦b:herbā-⟧).
⟦#288⟧
⟦b:-undo-⟧ (⟦b:-endo-⟧), N. ⟦b:-undu-s⟧, (⟦b:-endu-s⟧) is the suffix of the gerundive, which was originally neither active nor passive (⟦r2238:2238⟧). In a few words from reflexives, which have become adjectives, it has a reflexive or active meaning: ⟦b:lāb-undo-⟧, N. ⟦b:lāb-undu-s⟧, ⟦i:gliding⟧, ⟦i:slipping⟧ (⟦b:lābī⟧); ⟦b:ori-undu-s⟧, ⟦i:arising⟧ (⟦b:orīrī⟧); ⟦b:sec-undu-s⟧, ⟦i:following⟧ (⟦b:sequī⟧); ⟦b:volv-endu-s⟧, ⟦i:rolling⟧ (⟦i:volvī⟧). See ⟦r899:899⟧.
⟦#289⟧
⟦b:-bundo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-bundu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), has the meaning of an exaggerated present participle: ⟦b:freme-bundo-⟧, N. ⟦b:freme-bundu-s⟧, ⟦i:muttering away⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:frem-⟧⟧, ⟦i:roar⟧); ⟦b:treme-bundu-s⟧, ⟦i:all in a flutter⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:trem-⟧⟧, ⟦i:quiver⟧); ⟦b:fur-ibundu-s⟧, ⟦i:hot with rage⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fur-⟧⟧, ⟦i:rave⟧); ⟦b:cōntiōnā-bundu-s⟧, ⟦i:speaking a speech⟧ (⟦b:cōntiōnā-rī⟧); ⟦b:minitā-bundu-s⟧, ⟦i:breathing out threatenings⟧ (⟦b:minitā-rī⟧); ⟦b:vītā-bundu-s⟧, ⟦i:forever dodging⟧ (⟦b:vītā-re⟧).
⟦#290⟧
⟦b:-cundo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-cundu-s⟧, denotes permanent quality: ⟦b:fā-cundo-⟧, N. ⟦b:fā-cundu-s⟧, ⟦i:eloquent⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fā-⟧⟧, ⟦i:speak⟧); ⟦b:īrā-cundu-s⟧, ⟦i:choleric⟧ (⟦b:īrā-scī⟧); ⟦b:iū-cundu-s⟧, ⟦i:pleasant⟧, ⟦i:interesting⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:iuv-⟧⟧, ⟦i:help⟧).

title: The Adjective: With a Passive Meaning
text:
⟦#291⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-li-⟧, ⟦b:-ti-li-⟧, ⟦b:-bili-⟧, ⟦b:-tīvo-⟧, ⟦b:-no-⟧, and ⟦b:-mino-⟧, are used to form adjectives with a ⟦i:Passive⟧ meaning: as,
⟦b:fac-ili-⟧  ⟦b:facilis⟧, ⟦i:easy to do⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:fac-⟧⟧, ⟦i:do⟧
⟦b:duc-tili-⟧  ⟦b:ductilis⟧, ⟦i:ductile⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:duc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:draw⟧
⟦b:amā-bili-⟧  ⟦b:amābilis⟧, ⟦i:lovable⟧  ⟦b:amā-re⟧, ⟦i:love⟧
⟦b:mag-no-⟧  ⟦b:magnus⟧, ⟦i:great⟧  √⟦b:⟦i:mag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:increase⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.

title: -li-, (N. -li-s); -ti-li-, -bili- (N. -ti-li-s, -bili-s)
text:
⟦#292⟧
⟦b:-i-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:-i-li-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), denotes passive capability: ⟦b:fac-ili-⟧, N. ⟦b:fac-ili-s⟧, ⟦i:easy to do⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fac-⟧⟧, ⟦i:do⟧); ⟦b:frag-ili-s⟧, ⟦i:breakable⟧, ⟦i:frail⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:frag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:break⟧); ⟦b:hab-ili-s⟧, ⟦i:manageable⟧, ⟦i:handy⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:hab-⟧⟧, ⟦i:hold⟧); ⟦b:nūb-ili-s⟧, ⟦i:marriageable⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:nūb-⟧⟧, ⟦i:veil⟧).
⟦#293⟧
⟦b:-ti-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ti-li-s⟧, or ⟦b:-si-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:-si-li-s⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧), denotes capability or quality: as, ⟦b:duc-tili⟧, N. ⟦b:duc-tili-s⟧, ⟦i:capable of being drawn out⟧, ⟦i:ductile⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:duc-⟧⟧, ⟦i:draw⟧); ⟦b:fis-sili-s⟧, ⟦i:cleavable⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fid-⟧⟧, ⟦i:split⟧); ⟦b:rā-sili-s⟧, ⟦i:scraped⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:rād-⟧⟧, ⟦i:scrape⟧). Rarely active: as, ⟦b:fer-tili-s⟧, ⟦i:productive⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:fer-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧).
⟦#294⟧
⟦b:-bili-⟧, N. ⟦b:-bili-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), denotes passive capability like ⟦b:-i-li-⟧, but is far more common: ⟦b:horr-ibili-s⟧, ⟦i:exciting a shudder⟧ (cf. ⟦b:horrē-re⟧); ⟦b:amā-bili-s⟧, ⟦i:lovable⟧ (⟦b:amā-re⟧); ⟦b:flē-bili-s⟧, ⟦i:lamentable⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:flē-⟧⟧, ⟦i:weep⟧). Rarely active: as, ⟦b:sta-bili-s⟧, ⟦i:that can stand⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sta-⟧⟧, ⟦i:stand⟧); ⟦b:penetrā-bili-s⟧, ⟦i:piercing⟧ (⟦b:penetrā-re⟧). ⟦b:-ti-bili-⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧), passive, rare: ⟦b:flexibili-s⟧, ⟦i:flexible⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:flec-⟧⟧, ⟦i:bend⟧, ⟦r960:960⟧).
⟦#295⟧
⟦b:-tīvo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tīvu-s⟧, denotes the way a thing originated: as, ⟦b:cap-tīvu-s⟧, ⟦i:captive⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:cap-⟧⟧, ⟦i:take⟧); ⟦b:sta-tīvu-s⟧, ⟦i:set⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:sta-⟧⟧, ⟦i:set⟧).

title: -no- (N. -nu-s); -mino- (N. -minu-s)
text:
⟦#296⟧
⟦b:-no-⟧, N. ⟦b:-nu-s⟧, an old passive participle suffix, denotes result: ⟦b:mag-nu-s⟧ (⟦i:enlarged⟧), ⟦i:great⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:mag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:great⟧); ⟦b:plē-nus⟧, ⟦i:full⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:plē-⟧⟧, ⟦i:fill⟧). Neuter as substantive: ⟦b:dō-nu-m⟧, ⟦i:gift⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:dō-⟧⟧, ⟦i:give⟧). Sometimes active: ⟦b:egē-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:needy⟧ (⟦b:egē-re⟧, ⟦r192:192⟧).
⟦#297⟧
The suffix ⟦b:-mino-⟧ (for ⟦b:-meno-⟧, 103, ⟦i:a⟧) in its weakest form (⟦r135:135, 2⟧) is found in a few substantives: as, ⟦b:alu-mnu-s⟧, ⟦i:nursling⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:al-⟧⟧, ⟦i:nurse⟧). The endings ⟦b:-minī⟧ (⟦r730:730⟧) and ⟦b:-minō⟧ (⟦r731:731⟧) are apparently case forms of the same suffix. ⟦b:-minō⟧ would seem to be an ablative; ⟦b:-minī⟧ may be a nominative plural.

title: The Adjective: Denominatives
text:
⟦#298⟧
Denominative adjectives may be divided into such as denote: I. ⟦i:Material⟧ or ⟦i:Resemblance⟧. II. ⟦i:Appurtenance⟧: implying sometimes ⟦i:possession⟧, often ⟦i:fitness⟧, ⟦i:conformity⟧, ⟦i:character⟧, or ⟦i:origin⟧. III. ⟦i:Supply.⟧ IV. Diminutives. V. Comparatives and Superlatives; a few of these are primitive.

title: Material or Resemblance
text:
⟦#299⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-eo-⟧ and ⟦b:-n-eo-⟧ are used to form adjectives denoting ⟦i:Material⟧ or ⟦i:Resemblance⟧: as,
⟦b:aur-eo-⟧  ⟦b:aureus⟧, ⟦i:golden⟧  ⟦b:auro-⟧, N. ⟦b:aurum⟧, ⟦i:gold⟧
⟦b:ahē-neo-⟧  ⟦b:ahēneus⟧, ⟦i:bronze⟧ (⟦r58:58⟧)  ⟦b:aes-⟧, N. ⟦b:aes⟧, ⟦i:bronze⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.
⟦#300⟧
⟦b:-eo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-eu-s⟧: ⟦b:aur-eo-⟧, N. ⟦b:aur-eu-s⟧, ⟦i:golden⟧, ⟦i:all gold⟧, ⟦i:as good as gold⟧ (⟦b:auro-⟧); ⟦b:ferr-eu-s⟧, ⟦i:iron⟧ (⟦b:ferro-⟧); ⟦b:pulver-eu-s⟧, ⟦i:all dust⟧ (⟦b:pulver-⟧); ⟦b:virgin-eu-s⟧, ⟦i:girlish⟧ (⟦b:virgin-⟧).
⟦#301⟧
⟦b:-n-eo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-n-eu-s⟧: ⟦b:ahē-neu-s⟧, ⟦i:bronze⟧ (⟦b:ahē-⟧, ⟦r58:58⟧; ⟦b:aes-⟧); ⟦b:quer-neu-s⟧, ⟦i:oaken⟧ (⟦b:quercu-⟧). ⟦b:-no-⟧ is usually poetical: as, ⟦b:ebur-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:ivory⟧ (⟦b:ebur-⟧); ⟦b:quer-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:oaken⟧ (⟦b:quercu-⟧). ⟦b:-ā-neo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ā-neu-s⟧: ⟦b:miscell-āneu-s⟧, ⟦i:mixed⟧ (⟦b:miscello-⟧).

title: Appurtenance
text:
⟦#302⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-o-⟧, ⟦b:-io-⟧, ⟦b:-vo-⟧; ⟦b:-timo-⟧, ⟦b:-li-⟧, ⟦b:-no-⟧; ⟦b:-bri-⟧, ⟦b:-cri-⟧, ⟦b:-tri-⟧; ⟦b:-co-⟧, ⟦b:-ti-⟧, ⟦b:-si-⟧, are used to form adjectives denoting ⟦i:Belonging to⟧: as,
⟦b:rēg-io-⟧  ⟦b:rēgius⟧, ⟦i:kingly⟧  ⟦b:rēg-⟧, N. ⟦b:rēx⟧, ⟦i:king⟧
⟦b:mari-timo-⟧  ⟦b:maritimus⟧, ⟦i:of the sea⟧  ⟦b:mari-⟧, N. ⟦b:mare⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧
⟦b:rēg-āli-⟧  ⟦b:rēgālis⟧, ⟦i:of a king⟧  ⟦b:rēg-⟧, N. ⟦b:rēx⟧, ⟦i:king⟧
⟦b:can-īno-⟧  ⟦b:canīnus⟧, ⟦i:of a dog⟧  ⟦b:can-⟧, N. ⟦b:canis⟧, ⟦i:dog⟧
⟦b:mulie-bri-⟧  ⟦b:muliebris⟧, ⟦i:womanly⟧  ⟦b:mulier-⟧, N. ⟦b:mulier⟧, ⟦i:woman⟧
⟦b:cīvi-co-⟧  ⟦b:cīvicus⟧, ⟦i:citizen’s⟧  ⟦b:cīvi-⟧, N. ⟦b:cīvis⟧, ⟦i:citizen⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.

title: -o- (N. -u-s), -io- (N. -iu-s), -vo- (N. -vu-s)
text:
⟦#303⟧
⟦b:-o-⟧, N. ⟦b:-u-s⟧: ⟦b:decōr-o-⟧, N. ⟦b:decōr-u-s⟧, ⟦i:becoming⟧ (⟦b:decōr-⟧); ⟦b:canōr-u-s⟧, ⟦i:melodious⟧ (⟦b:canōr-⟧); ⟦b:pervius⟧, ⟦i:passable⟧ (⟦b:via-⟧).
⟦#304⟧
⟦b:-io-⟧ is one of the commonest suffixes, and is often added to other suffixes; thus: ⟦b:-c-io-⟧, ⟦b:-īc-io-⟧; ⟦b:-tōr-io-⟧ (⟦b:-sōr-io-⟧); ⟦b:-ār-io-⟧.
⟦#305⟧
⟦b:-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-iu-s⟧: ⟦b:rēg-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:rēg-iu-s⟧, ⟦i:of⟧ or ⟦i:like a king⟧ (⟦b:rēg-⟧); ⟦b:patr-iu-s⟧, ⟦i:of a father⟧ (⟦b:patr-⟧). Here belong many gentile names: as, ⟦b:Sēst-iu-s⟧ (⟦b:Sexto-⟧). These are used with substantives as adjectives: as, ⟦b:lēx Cornēl-ia⟧, ⟦b:lēx Iūl-ia⟧. Furthermore patrial adjectives: as, ⟦b:Corinth-iu-s⟧, ⟦i:Corinthian⟧ (⟦b:Corintho-⟧). In some, consonant ⟦b:-io-⟧ is used: ⟦b:plēbē-iu-s⟧, ⟦i:of the commons⟧ (⟦b:plēbē-⟧). ⟦b:-io-⟧ is rare in primitives: ⟦b:exim-iu-s⟧, ⟦i:select⟧ (⟦b:ex⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:em-⟧⟧, ⟦i:take⟧).
⟦#306⟧
⟦b:-c-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-c-iu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:aedīli-cio⟧, N. ⟦b:aedīli-ciu-s⟧, ⟦i:of an aedile⟧ (⟦b:aedīli-⟧); ⟦b:patr-iciu-s⟧, ⟦i:of the fathers⟧ (⟦b:patr-⟧); ⟦b:later-iciu-s⟧, ⟦i:of brick⟧ (⟦b:later-⟧).
⟦#307⟧
⟦b:-īc-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-īc-iu-s⟧: ⟦b:nov-īcio-⟧, N. ⟦b:nov-īciu-s⟧, ⟦i:new⟧, ⟦i:new-comer⟧ (⟦b:novo-⟧); ⟦b:nātāl-īciu-s⟧, ⟦i:birthday’s⟧ (⟦b:nātāli-⟧); ⟦b:caement-īciu-s⟧, ⟦i:rubble⟧ (⟦b:caemento-⟧). Usually suffixed to perfect participles to denote the quality derived from the past act: ⟦b:conduct-īciu-s⟧, ⟦i:hired⟧ (⟦b:conducto-⟧); ⟦b:trālāt-īciu-s⟧, ⟦i:transferred⟧ (⟦b:trālāto-⟧).
⟦#308⟧
⟦b:-tōr-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tōr-iu-s⟧, or ⟦b:-sōr-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-sōr-iu-s⟧, from the agent (⟦r205:205⟧) in ⟦b:-tōr-⟧ (⟦b:-sōr-⟧), is the commonest ending with ⟦b:-io-⟧: ⟦b:imperā-tōrio-⟧, N. ⟦b:imperā-tōriu-s⟧, ⟦i:of a commander⟧ (⟦b:imperātōr-⟧). The neuter, as substantive, denotes the place where (⟦r266:266⟧): ⟦b:audī-tōriu-m⟧, ⟦i:lecture-room⟧ (⟦b:audītōr-⟧); ⟦b:dēvor-sōriu-m⟧, ⟦i:inn⟧ (⟦b:dēvorsōr-⟧).
⟦#309⟧
⟦b:-ār-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ār-iu-s⟧, very common, is chiefly added to substantives: as, ⟦b:agr-ārio-⟧, N. ⟦b:agr-āriu-s⟧, ⟦i:of land⟧ (⟦b:agro-⟧). Often as substantive: ⟦b:not-āriu-s⟧ (⟦r265:265⟧), ⟦i:stenographer⟧ (⟦b:notā-⟧); ⟦b:aer-āriu-m⟧ (⟦r266:266⟧), ⟦i:treastury⟧ (⟦b:aer-⟧); ⟦b:sēmin-āriu-m⟧, ⟦i:nursery⟧ (⟦b:sēmin-⟧); ⟦b:bell-āria⟧, plural, ⟦i:goodies⟧, ⟦i:bonbons⟧ (⟦b:bello-⟧).
⟦#310⟧
⟦b:-ī-vo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ī-vu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:tempest-īvu-s⟧, ⟦i:seasonable⟧ (⟦b:tempestāt-⟧, ⟦r126:126⟧); ⟦b:aest-īvu-s⟧, ⟦i:summer’s⟧ (⟦b:aestāt-⟧). See ⟦r179:179⟧.

title: -timo- (N. -timu-s); -li- (N. -li-s); -no- (N. -nu-s)
text:
⟦#311⟧
⟦b:-timo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-timu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), for an older ⟦b:-tumo-⟧ (⟦r28:28⟧): ⟦b:mari-timo-⟧, N. ⟦b:mari-timu-s⟧, ⟦i:of the sea⟧ (⟦b:mari-⟧); ⟦b:fīni-timu-s⟧, ⟦i:of the border⟧ (⟦b:fīni-⟧); ⟦b:lēg-itimu-s⟧, ⟦i:lawful⟧ (⟦b:lēg-⟧).
⟦#312⟧
⟦b:-li-⟧ N. ⟦b:-li-s⟧: ⟦b:humi-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:humi-li-s⟧, ⟦i:lowly⟧ (⟦b:humo-⟧); but almost always in denominatives ⟦b:-li-⟧ is preceded by a long vowel (⟦r202:202⟧), usually ⟦b:-ā-⟧ or ⟦b:-ī-⟧, thus: ⟦b:-ā-li-⟧ (⟦b:-ā-ri-⟧), ⟦b:-ī-li⟧; ⟦b:-ē-li-⟧, ⟦b:-ū-li-⟧.
⟦#313⟧
⟦b:-ā-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ā-li-s⟧: ⟦b:rēg-āli-⟧, N. ⟦b:rēg-āli-s⟧, ⟦i:kingly⟧ (⟦b:rēg-⟧); ⟦b:decemvir-āli-s⟧, ⟦i:of a decemvir⟧ (⟦b:decemviro-⟧); ⟦b:fāt-āli-s⟧, ⟦i:fated⟧ (⟦b:fāto-⟧); ⟦b:t-āli-s⟧, ⟦i:such⟧ (stem ⟦b:to-⟧, ⟦i:that⟧); ⟦b:qu-āli-s⟧, ⟦i:as⟧ (⟦b:quo-⟧), ⟦b:-ā-ri-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ā-ri-s⟧, is used for ⟦b:-āli-⟧ if an ⟦b:l⟧ precedes (⟦r173:173⟧): as, ⟦b:mol-āri-⟧, N. ⟦b:mol-āri-s⟧, ⟦i:of a mill⟧ (⟦b:molā-⟧); ⟦b:mīlit-āri-s⟧, ⟦i:of a soldier⟧ (⟦b:mīlit-⟧). Neuters in ⟦b:-āli-⟧ and ⟦b:-āri-⟧ often become substantives (⟦r600:600⟧): ⟦b:fōc-āle⟧, ⟦i:neckcloth⟧ (⟦b:fauci-⟧); ⟦b:anim-al⟧, ⟦i:breathing thing⟧ (⟦b:animā-⟧); ⟦b:calc-ar⟧, ⟦i:spur⟧ (⟦b:calci-⟧).
⟦#314⟧
⟦b:-ī-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ī-li-s⟧: ⟦b:cīv-īli-⟧, N. ⟦b:cīv-īli-s⟧, ⟦i:of a citizen⟧ (⟦b:cīvi-⟧); ⟦b:puer-ili-s⟧, ⟦i:boyish⟧ (⟦b:puero-⟧). The neuter, as substantive, sometimes denotes the place where (⟦r266:266⟧): ⟦b:ov-īle⟧, ⟦i:sheepfold⟧ (⟦b:ovi-⟧).
⟦#315⟧
⟦b:-ē-li⟧, N. ⟦b:-ē-li-s⟧: ⟦b:fidē-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:fidē-li-s⟧, ⟦i:faithful⟧ (⟦b:fidē-⟧); ⟦b:crūd-ēli-s⟧, ⟦i:cruel⟧ (⟦b:crūdo-⟧); ⟦b:patru-ēli-s⟧, ⟦i:cousin⟧ (⟦b:patruo-⟧). ⟦b:-ū-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ū-li-s⟧: ⟦b:tribū-li-⟧, N. ⟦b:tribū-li-s⟧, ⟦i:tribesman⟧ (⟦b:tribu-⟧).
⟦#316⟧
The old participle suffix ⟦b:-no-⟧ (⟦r296:296⟧) is sometimes added at once to noun stems, sometimes to other suffixes: thus, ⟦b:-ā-no-⟧, ⟦b:-ī-no-⟧; ⟦b:-ti-no-⟧, ⟦b:-tī-no-⟧; ⟦b:-er-no-⟧, ⟦b:-ur-no-⟧.
⟦#317⟧
⟦b:-no-⟧, N. ⟦b:-nu-s⟧, is added to stems formed with the comparative suffix ⟦b:-ero-⟧ or ⟦b:-tero-⟧ (⟦r347:347⟧), denoting place: ⟦b:super-no-⟧, N. ⟦b:super-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:above⟧; ⟦b:inter-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:internal⟧ (⟦b:inter⟧); ⟦b:exter-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:outside⟧; so, also, ⟦b:alter-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:every other⟧ (⟦b:altero-⟧); and to a very few substantives: as, ⟦b:pater-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:fatherly⟧ (⟦b:patr-⟧); ⟦b:frāter-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:brotherly⟧ (⟦b:frātr-⟧); ⟦b:vēr-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:of spring⟧ (⟦b:vēr-⟧). Also to cardinals, making distributives: as, ⟦b:bī-nī⟧, ⟦i:two by two⟧ (for ⟦b:*dṷīnī⟧, ⟦b:duo-⟧, ⟦r161:161⟧).
⟦#318⟧
⟦b:-ā-no-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ā-nu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:arcā-no-⟧, N. ⟦b:arc-ānu-s⟧, ⟦i:secret⟧ (⟦b:arcā-⟧); ⟦b:Rōma-nu-s⟧, ⟦i:of Rome⟧ (⟦b:Rōmā-⟧); ⟦b:mont-ānu-s⟧, ⟦i:of a mountain⟧ (⟦b:monti-⟧); ⟦b:oppid-ānu-s⟧, ⟦i:of a town⟧ (⟦b:oppido-⟧). ⟦b:-i-āno-⟧: ⟦b:Cicerōn-iāno-⟧, N. ⟦b:Cicerōn-iānu-s⟧, ⟦i:Cicero’s⟧. Rarely ⟦b:-ā-neo-⟧: ⟦b:mediterrā-neu-s⟧, ⟦i:midland⟧ (⟦b:medio-⟧, ⟦b:terrā-⟧).
⟦#319⟧
⟦b:-ī-no-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ī-nu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:mar-īno-⟧, N. ⟦b:mar-īnu-s⟧, ⟦i:of the sea⟧; ⟦b:repent-īnu-s⟧, ⟦i:sudden⟧ (⟦b:repenti-⟧); oftenest added to names of living beings: as, ⟦b:can-īnu-s⟧, ⟦i:of a dog⟧ (⟦b:can-⟧); ⟦b:dīv-īnu-s⟧, ⟦i:of a god⟧ (⟦b:dīvo-⟧); ⟦b:-ē-no-⟧: ⟦b:lani-ēnu-s⟧, ⟦b:ali-ēnu-s⟧. Also to proper names: as, ⟦b:Plaut-īno-⟧, N. ⟦b:Plaut-īnu-s⟧, ⟦i:of Plautus⟧ (⟦b:Plauto-⟧); ⟦b:Alp-īnu-s⟧, ⟦i:Alpine⟧ (⟦b:Alpi-⟧).
⟦#320⟧
⟦b:-ti-no-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ti-nu-s⟧, is used in some adjectives of time: ⟦b:crās-tinu-s⟧, ⟦i:to-morrow’s⟧ (⟦b:crās-⟧); ⟦b:diū-tinu-s⟧, ⟦i:lasting⟧ (⟦b:diū⟧); ⟦b:prīs-tinu-s⟧, ⟦i:of aforetime⟧ (⟦b:prī-⟧, ⟦b:prae⟧).
⟦#321⟧
⟦b:-tī-no-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tī-nu-s⟧, is used in a few words of place and time: ⟦b:intes-tīno-⟧, N. ⟦b:intes-tinu-s⟧, ⟦i:inward⟧ (⟦b:intus⟧); ⟦b:vesper-tīnu-s⟧, ⟦i:at eventide⟧ (⟦b:vespero-⟧).
⟦#322⟧
From words like ⟦b:frāter-nus⟧ (from ⟦b:*fratr(i)-nus⟧, 111, ⟦i:b⟧), ⟦b:pater-nus⟧, ⟦b:exter-nus⟧, ⟦b:inter-nus⟧, arose a new suffix ⟦b:-terno-⟧: as, ⟦b:hes-ternus⟧, from the stem ⟦b:hes-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:her-ī⟧, ⟦r154:154⟧), and ⟦b:-erno-⟧ in ⟦b:hodiernus⟧. From the adverb ⟦b:*noctur⟧ (νυκτωρ) was derived ⟦b:noctur-nus⟧, by analogy to which ⟦b:diurnus⟧ was formed. Elsewhere the ⟦b:-ur⟧ of ⟦b:-urnus⟧ and the ⟦b:-tur-⟧ of ⟦b:-turnus⟧ belong to the stem: as, ⟦b:ebur-nus⟧; ⟦b:tacitur-nus⟧, from the agent ⟦b:*taci-tor⟧ (⟦r205:205⟧).

title: -bri-, -cri-, -tri- (N. -ber or -bri-s, &c.)
text:
⟦#323⟧
⟦b:-bri-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ber⟧ or ⟦b:-bri-s⟧: ⟦b:salū-bri-⟧, N. ⟦b:salū-ber⟧, ⟦i:healthy⟧ (⟦b:salūt-⟧); ⟦b:mulie-bri-s⟧, ⟦i:womanly⟧ (⟦b:mulier-⟧).
⟦#324⟧
⟦b:-cri-⟧, N. ⟦b:-cer⟧ or ⟦b:-cri-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:volu-cri-⟧, N. ⟦b:volu-cer⟧, ⟦i:winged⟧ (⟦b:*volo-⟧, ⟦i:flying⟧); ⟦b:medio-cri-s⟧, ⟦i:middling⟧ (⟦b:medio-⟧).
⟦#325⟧
⟦b:-tri-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ter⟧ or ⟦b:-tri-s⟧: ⟦b:eques-tri-⟧, N. ⟦b:eques-ter⟧, ⟦i:of horsemen⟧ (⟦b:equit-⟧, ⟦r152:152⟧); ⟦b:sēmēs-tri-s⟧, ⟦i:of six months⟧ (⟦b:sex⟧, ⟦b:mēns-⟧). ⟦b:-es-tri-⟧ is used in a few words: ⟦b:camp-ester⟧, ⟦i:of fields⟧ (⟦b:campo-⟧); ⟦b:silv-estri-s⟧, ⟦i:of woods⟧ (⟦b:silvā-⟧).

title: -co- (N. -cu-s); -ti-, -si- (N. -s, -si-s)
text:
⟦#326⟧
⟦b:-co-⟧ is often suffixed to ⟦b:-ti-⟧, sometimes to ⟦b:-es-ti-⟧; thus: ⟦b:-ti-co-⟧, ⟦b:-es-ti-co-⟧.
⟦#327⟧
⟦b:-co-⟧, N. ⟦b:-cu-s⟧: ⟦b:cīvi-co-⟧, N. ⟦b:cīvi-cu-s⟧, ⟦i:of a citizen⟧ (⟦b:cīvi-⟧); ⟦b:belli-cu-s⟧, ⟦i:of war⟧ (⟦b:bello-⟧); ⟦b:vīli-cu-s⟧, ⟦i:bailiff⟧ (⟦b:vīllā-⟧). ⟦b:-ā-co-⟧, ⟦b:-ī-co-⟧, ⟦b:-ū-co-⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:merā-cu-s⟧, ⟦b:amī-cu-s⟧, ⟦b:antī-cu-s⟧, ⟦b:aprī-cu-s⟧, ⟦b:postī-cu-s⟧, ⟦b:pudī-cu-s⟧, ⟦b:cadū-cu-s⟧. ⟦b:-ti-co-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ti-cu-s⟧: ⟦b:rūs-tico-⟧, N. ⟦b:rūs-ticu-s⟧, ⟦i:of the country⟧ (⟦b:rūs-⟧). ⟦b:-es-ti-co-⟧, N. ⟦b:-es-ti-cu-s⟧: ⟦b:dom-esticu-s⟧, ⟦i:of a house⟧ (⟦b:domo-⟧, ⟦b:domu-⟧).
⟦#328⟧
⟦b:-ti-⟧ or ⟦b:-si-⟧ denotes belonging to a place; usually ⟦b:-ā-ti-⟧, ⟦b:-ī-ti-⟧, ⟦b:-es-ti-⟧, ⟦b:-en-ti-⟧; ⟦b:-ēn-si-⟧, or ⟦b:-i-ēn-si-⟧.
⟦#329⟧
⟦b:-ti-⟧, N. ⟦b:-s⟧: ⟦b:Tībur-ti-⟧, N. ⟦b:Tībur-s⟧, ⟦i:Tiburtine⟧ (⟦b:Tībur-⟧). ⟦b:-ā-ti-⟧: ⟦b:quoi-āti-⟧, N. ⟦b:quoi-ā-s⟧, ⟦i:what countryman?⟧ (⟦b:quoio-⟧); ⟦b:Anti-ā-s⟧, ⟦i:of Antium⟧ (⟦b:Antio-⟧); ⟦b:optim-ātēs⟧, ⟦i:good men and true⟧ (⟦b:optimo-⟧). ⟦b:-ī-ti-⟧: ⟦b:Samn-īti-⟧, N. ⟦b:Samn-ī-s⟧, ⟦i:Samnian⟧ (⟦b:Samnio-⟧). ⟦b:-en-ti-⟧: ⟦b:Vēi-enti-⟧, N. ⟦b:Vēi-ēn-s⟧, ⟦i:of Vei⟧ (⟦b:Vēio-⟧). ⟦b:-es-ti-⟧, N. ⟦b:-es-ti-s⟧: ⟦b:agr-esti-⟧, N. ⟦b:agr-esti-s⟧, ⟦i:of the fields⟧ (⟦b:agro-⟧); ⟦b:cael-esti-s⟧, ⟦i:heavenly⟧ (⟦b:caelo-⟧).
⟦#330⟧
⟦b:-ēn-si-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ēn-si-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), from appellatives of place or proper names of place: ⟦b:castr-ēnsi-⟧, N. ⟦b:castr-ēnsi-s⟧, ⟦i:of a camp⟧ (⟦b:castro-⟧); ⟦b:circ-ēnsi-s⟧, ⟦i:of the circus⟧ (⟦b:circo-⟧); ⟦b:Hispāni-ēnsi-s⟧ (⟦i:temporarily) of Spain⟧. ⟦b:-i-ēnsi-⟧: ⟦b:Karthāgin-iēnsi-s⟧, ⟦i:of Carthage⟧ (⟦b:Karthāgin-⟧).

title: Supply
text:
⟦#331⟧
The suffixes ⟦b:-to-⟧ or ⟦b:-ōso-⟧ are used to form adjectives denoting ⟦i:Supplied⟧ or ⟦i:Furnished with⟧: as,
⟦b:barbā-to-⟧  ⟦b:barbātus⟧, ⟦i:bearded⟧  ⟦b:barbā-⟧, N. ⟦b:barba⟧, ⟦i:beard⟧
⟦b:ann-ōso-⟧  ⟦b:annōsus⟧, ⟦i:full of years⟧  ⟦b:anno-⟧, N. ⟦b:annus⟧, ⟦i:year⟧
⟦/⟧
Stem. Nominative. From.

title: -to- (N. -tu-s); -len-to- (N. -len-tu-s)
text:
⟦#332⟧
⟦b:-to-⟧, the perfect participle suffix, is sometimes added at once to a noun stem, sometimes to other suffixes, thus: ⟦b:-āto-⟧, ⟦b:-īto-⟧, ⟦b:-ēto-⟧, ⟦b:-ūto-⟧, ⟦b:-ento-⟧, ⟦b:-lento-⟧.
⟦#333⟧
⟦b:-to-⟧, N. ⟦b:-tu-s⟧: ⟦b:onus-to-⟧, N. ⟦b:onus-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:loaded⟧ (⟦b:onus-⟧); ⟦b:vetus-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:full of years⟧ (⟦b:*vetus-⟧, ⟦i:year⟧); ⟦b:iūs-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:just⟧ (⟦b:iūs-⟧); ⟦b:hones-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:honourable⟧ (⟦b:*hones-⟧); ⟦b:fūnes-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:deadly⟧ (⟦b:fūnes-⟧). ⟦b:-ā-to-⟧: ⟦b:barbā-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:bearded⟧ (⟦b:barbā-⟧); ⟦b:dent-ātu-s⟧, ⟦i:toothed⟧ (⟦b:denti-⟧); ⟦b:-ī-to-⟧: ⟦b:aurī-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:long-eared⟧ (⟦b:auri-⟧); ⟦b:-ū-to-⟧: ⟦b:cornū-tu-s⟧, ⟦i:horned⟧ (⟦b:cornu-⟧). ⟦b:-en-to-⟧, N. ⟦b:-en-tu-s⟧: ⟦b:cru-ento-⟧, N. ⟦b:cru-entu-s⟧, ⟦i:all gore⟧ (⟦b:*cruenti-⟧, ⟦b:*cruēre⟧). As substantive, ⟦b:arg-entu-m⟧ (⟦i:white metal⟧), ⟦i:silver⟧; ⟦b:flu-enta⟧, plural, ⟦i:streams⟧ (⟦b:fluenti-⟧).
⟦#334⟧
The neuter of stems in ⟦b:-to-⟧, as a substantive, denotes the place where something, generally a plant, is found (⟦r266:266⟧): ⟦b:arbus-tu-m⟧, ⟦i:vineyard⟧ (⟦b:arbos-⟧); commonly preceded by ⟦b:-ē-⟧, forming ⟦b:-ē-to-⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧), usually plural: ⟦b:dūm-ēta⟧, ⟦i:thorn-thickets⟧ (⟦b:dūmo-⟧); ⟦b:murt-ēta⟧, ⟦i:myrtle-groves⟧ (⟦b:murto-⟧).
⟦#335⟧
⟦b:-len-to-⟧, N. ⟦b:-len-tu-s⟧ (⟦r202:202⟧): ⟦b:vīno-lento-⟧, N. ⟦b:vīno-lentu-s⟧, ⟦i:drunken⟧ (⟦b:vīno-⟧); ⟦b:sanguin-olentu-s⟧, ⟦i:all blood⟧ (⟦b:sanguin-⟧); ⟦b:lūcu-lentu-s⟧, ⟦i:bright⟧ (⟦b:lūci-⟧, ⟦r28:28⟧); ⟦b:pulver-ulentu-s⟧, ⟦i:dusty⟧ (⟦b:pulver-⟧). A shorter form ⟦b:-lenti-⟧ is rare: ⟦b:vi-olenti-⟧, N. ⟦b:vi-olēn-s⟧, ⟦i:violent⟧ (⟦b:vi-⟧); ⟦b:op-ulēn-s⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧ (⟦b:op-⟧).

title: -ōso- (N. -ōsu-s)
text:
⟦#336⟧
⟦b:-ōso-⟧ (sometimes ⟦b:-ōnso-⟧, ⟦b:-ōsso-⟧), N. ⟦b:-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:full of⟧, is very common indeed, ⟦b:-ōso-⟧ is sometimes attached to other suffixes, thus: ⟦b:-c-ōso-⟧, ⟦b:-ul-ōso-⟧, ⟦b:-ūc-ul-ōso-⟧.
⟦#337⟧
⟦b:-ōso-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ōsu-s⟧: ⟦b:ann-ōso-⟧, N. ⟦b:ann-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:full of years⟧; ⟦b:fōrm-ōnsu-s⟧, ⟦b:fōrm-ōssu-s⟧ or ⟦b:fōrm-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:shapely⟧ (⟦b:fōrmā-⟧); ⟦b:perīcul-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:with danger fraught⟧ (⟦b:perīculo-⟧); ⟦b:mōr-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:priggish⟧, ⟦i:cross⟧ (⟦b:mōr-⟧); ⟦b:calamit-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:full of damage⟧ (⟦b:calamitāt-⟧, ⟦r179:179⟧); ⟦b:superstiti-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:superstitious⟧ (⟦b:superstitiōn-⟧, ⟦r179:179⟧); ⟦b:frūctu-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:fruitful⟧ (⟦b:frūctu-⟧, 116, ⟦i:c⟧); ⟦b:mont-uōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:full of mountains⟧ (⟦b:monti-⟧, ⟦r202:202⟧); ⟦b:cūri-ōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:full of care⟧ (⟦b:cūrā-⟧); ⟦b:labōr-iōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:toilsome⟧ (⟦b:labōr-⟧, ⟦r202:202⟧).
⟦#338⟧
⟦b:-c-ōso-⟧, N. ⟦b:-c-ōsu-s⟧: ⟦b:belli-cōso-⟧, N. ⟦b:belli-cōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:warlike⟧ (⟦b:bello-⟧, ⟦b:bellico-⟧). ⟦b:-ul-ōso-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ul-ōsu-s⟧: ⟦b:formīd-ulōso-⟧, N. ⟦b:formid-ulōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:terrible⟧ (⟦b:formīdin-⟧, ⟦r179:179⟧). ⟦b:-ūc-ul-ōso-⟧, N. ⟦b:-ūc-ul-ōsu-s⟧: ⟦b:met-ū-culoso-⟧, N. ⟦b:met-ū-culōsu-s⟧, ⟦i:skittish⟧ (⟦b:metu-⟧).

title: The Adjective: Diminutives
text:
⟦#339⟧
Diminutives are formed from adjectives, as from substantives (⟦r267:267⟧).
⟦b:-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-lu-s⟧: ⟦b:aureo-lo-⟧, N. ⟦b:aureo-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:all gold⟧, ⟦i:of precious gold⟧, ⟦i:of red red gold⟧, ⟦i:good as gold⟧ (⟦b:aureo-⟧); ⟦b:ebrio-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:tipsy⟧ (⟦b:ebrio-⟧); ⟦b:parvo-lu-s⟧, or ⟦b:parvu-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:smallish⟧ (⟦b:parvo-⟧); ⟦b:frīgidu-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:chilly⟧ (⟦b:frigido-⟧); ⟦b:vet-ulus⟧, ⟦i:little old⟧ (⟦b:vet-⟧); ⟦b:tenellu-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:soft and sweet⟧ (⟦b:tenello-⟧, ⟦b:tenero-⟧); ⟦b:pulchel-lus⟧, ⟦i:sweet pretty⟧ (⟦b:pulchro-⟧); ⟦b:bel-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:bonny⟧ (⟦b:bono-⟧); ⟦b:novel-lu-s⟧, ⟦i:newborn⟧ (⟦b:*novolo-⟧, ⟦b:novo-⟧). ⟦b:-culo-⟧, N. ⟦b:-culu-s⟧: ⟦b:pauper-culo-⟧, N. ⟦b:pauper-culu-s⟧, ⟦i:poorish⟧ (⟦b:pauper-⟧); ⟦b:levi-culu-s⟧, ⟦i:somewhat vain⟧ (⟦b:levi-⟧).
⟦#340⟧
A peculiar class of diminutives is formed by adding ⟦b:-culo-⟧ to the comparative stem ⟦b:-ius-⟧ (⟦r346:346⟧): as, ⟦b:nitidius-culo-⟧, N. ⟦b:nitidius-culu-s⟧, ⟦i:a trifle sleeker⟧ (⟦b:nitidius-⟧); ⟦b:longius-culu-s⟧, ⟦i:a bit longer⟧ (⟦b:longius-⟧).
⟦#341⟧
Adverbs sometimes have a diminutive form: as, ⟦b:bellē⟧, ⟦i:charmingly⟧; ⟦b:paullulum⟧, ⟦i:a little bit⟧; ⟦b:meliusculē⟧, ⟦i:a bit better⟧ (⟦r340:340⟧).

title: Comparatives and Superlatives
text:
⟦#342⟧
Comparatives and superlatives are usually formed from the stem of the positive: as, ⟦b:dignior⟧, ⟦i:worthier⟧, ⟦b:dignissimus⟧, ⟦i:worthiest⟧, from ⟦b:digno-⟧, stem of ⟦b:dignus⟧. A few are formed directly from roots: thus, ⟦b:maior⟧, ⟦i:greater⟧, and ⟦b:maximus⟧, ⟦i:greatest⟧, are formed from the √⟦b:⟦i:mag-⟧⟧, and not from ⟦b:magno-⟧, stem of ⟦b:magnus⟧.

title: Comparative -ior, Superlative -issimus
text:
⟦#343⟧
The nominative of comparative adjectives ends usually in ⟦b:-ior⟧, and that of superlatives in ⟦b:-issimus⟧: thus,
Masc.  Fem.  Neut.  Masc.  Fem.  Neut.
⟦b:-ior⟧  ⟦b:-ior⟧  ⟦b:-ius⟧  ⟦b:-issimus⟧  ⟦b:-issima⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:altus⟧, ⟦i:high⟧,  ⟦b:altior⟧, ⟦i:higher⟧,  ⟦b:altissimus⟧, ⟦i:highest⟧.
⟦b:trīstis⟧, ⟦i:sad⟧,  ⟦b:trīstior⟧, ⟦i:sadder⟧,
⟦/⟧
⟦#344⟧
⟦b:pauper⟧, ⟦i:poor⟧,  ⟦b:pauperior⟧, ⟦i:poorer⟧,  ⟦b:pauperrimus⟧, ⟦i:poorest⟧.
⟦b:ācer⟧, ⟦i:sharp⟧,  ⟦b:ācrior⟧, ⟦i:sharper⟧,  ⟦b:ācerrimus⟧, ⟦i:sharpest⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦b:mātūrrimus⟧ occurs once (Tac.), for ⟦b:mātūrissimus⟧, positive ⟦b:mātūrus⟧, ⟦i:ripe⟧.

title: Superlative -limus
text:
⟦#345⟧
⟦b:humilis⟧, ⟦b:difficilis⟧, and ⟦b:facilis⟧,
⟦b:similis⟧, ⟦b:dissimilis⟧, and ⟦b:gracilis⟧,
have the nominative of the superlative in ⟦b:-limus⟧, following ⟦b:l⟧ of the stem (⟦r350:350⟧): as,
⟦b:humilis⟧, ⟦i:lowly⟧,  ⟦b:humilior⟧, ⟦i:lowlier⟧,  ⟦b:humillimus⟧, ⟦i:lowliest⟧.
⟦/⟧
Positive. Comparative. Superlative.

title: The Comparative Suffix
text:
⟦#346⟧
The comparative suffix is ⟦b:-iōs-⟧, which becomes in the singular, nominative masculine and feminine, ⟦b:-ior⟧ (⟦r154:154⟧; ⟦r132:132⟧), neuter nominative and accusative, ⟦b:-ius⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧); in all other cases ⟦b:-iōr-⟧ (⟦r154:154⟧).
⟦#347⟧
Other comparative suffixes are ⟦b:-ro-⟧ or ⟦b:-ero-⟧, and ⟦b:-tro-⟧ or ⟦b:-tero-⟧, used in a few words, principally designating place: as, ⟦b:sup-erī⟧, ⟦i:the upper ones⟧, ⟦b:īnferī⟧, ⟦i:the nether ones⟧; ⟦b:ex-terī⟧, ⟦i:outsiders⟧, ⟦b:posterī⟧, ⟦i:after-generations⟧; ⟦b:alter⟧, ⟦i:the other⟧; ⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦i:whether? which of the two?⟧ (for ⟦b:*quo-ter⟧, ⟦r146:146⟧); ⟦b:dexter⟧, ⟦i:right⟧.
⟦#348⟧
Some words designating place have a doubled comparative suffix, ⟦b:-er-iōr-⟧, or ⟦b:-ter-iōr-⟧: as, ⟦b:sup-er-ior⟧, ⟦i:upper⟧, ⟦b:īnferior⟧, ⟦i:lower⟧. ⟦b:ci-ter-ior⟧, ⟦i:hither⟧, ⟦b:dēterior⟧ (⟦i:lower⟧), ⟦i:worse⟧, ⟦b:exterior⟧, ⟦i:outer⟧, ⟦b:interior⟧, ⟦i:inner⟧, ⟦b:posterior⟧, ⟦i:hinder⟧, ⟦i:after⟧, ⟦b:ulterior⟧, ⟦i:further⟧, ⟦b:dexterior⟧, ⟦i:more to the right⟧, ⟦b:-is-tro-⟧ is used in two words which have become substantives: ⟦b:min-is-ter⟧ (⟦i:inferior⟧), ⟦i:servant⟧, and ⟦b:magister⟧ (⟦i:superior⟧), ⟦i:master⟧.

title: The Superlative Suffix
text:
⟦#349⟧
The common superlative suffix is ⟦b:-issimo-⟧, nominative ⟦b:-issimus⟧, with older ⟦b:-issumo-⟧, nominative ⟦b:-issumus⟧ (⟦r28:28⟧).
⟦#350⟧
Stems which end in ⟦b:-ro-⟧, ⟦b:-ri-⟧, or ⟦b:-li-⟧ (⟦r344:344⟧, ⟦r345:345⟧) take the suffix ⟦b:-issimo-⟧ (cf. ⟦b:-simo-⟧, ⟦r351:351⟧) with syncope of its initial ⟦b:i⟧ (⟦r111:111⟧) and assimilation of the final ⟦b:l⟧ or ⟦b:r⟧ (⟦r166:166, 8⟧).
⟦#351⟧
The suffix ⟦b:-timo-⟧ is further used in a few root superlatives: ⟦b:ci-timus⟧, ⟦b:dextimus⟧, ⟦b:extimus⟧, ⟦b:intimus⟧, ⟦b:optimus⟧, ⟦b:postumus⟧, and ⟦b:ultimus⟧; and ⟦b:-simo-⟧ in ⟦b:maximus⟧, ⟦b:pessimus⟧, and ⟦b:proximus⟧.
⟦#352⟧
The suffix ⟦b:-mo-⟧ or ⟦b:-imo-⟧ is used in ⟦b:sum-mo-⟧, N. ⟦b:summus⟧, ⟦i:highest⟧ (⟦b:sub⟧); ⟦b:min-imo-⟧, N. ⟦b:minimus⟧, ⟦i:least⟧; ⟦b:prīmus⟧, ⟦i:first⟧, ⟦b:septimus⟧, ⟦i:seventh⟧, ⟦b:decimus⟧, ⟦i:tenth⟧. ⟦b:-mo-⟧ or ⟦b:-imo-⟧ is attached to ⟦b:-is-⟧ (⟦r135:135, 2⟧) in ⟦b:plūrimus⟧ for ⟦b:*plō-is-imo-s⟧ (⟦i:fullest⟧), ⟦i:most⟧ (⟦r99:99⟧); and to ⟦b:-rē-⟧ or ⟦b:-trē-⟧, possibly an adverbial form (⟦r705:705⟧), in ⟦b:suprēmus⟧, ⟦b:extrēmus⟧, and ⟦b:postrēmus⟧.

title: Peculiarities of Comparison
text:
⟦#353⟧
Some positives have a comparative or superlative, or both, from a different form of the stem: such are,
⟦b:frūgī⟧, ⟦i:thrifty⟧,  ⟦b:frūgālior⟧,  ⟦b:frūgālissimus⟧.
⟦b:nēquam⟧, ⟦i:naughty⟧,  ⟦b:nēquior⟧,  ⟦b:nēquissimus⟧.
⟦b:iuvenis⟧, ⟦i:young⟧,  ⟦b:iūnior⟧,  (⟦b:nātū minimus⟧).
⟦b:senex⟧, ⟦i:old⟧,  ⟦b:senior⟧,  (⟦b:nātū maximus⟧).
⟦b:magnus⟧, ⟦i:great⟧,  ⟦b:maior⟧,  ⟦b:maximus⟧ (⟦r351:351⟧).
⟦b:beneficus⟧, ⟦i:kindly⟧,  ⟦b:beneficentior⟧,  ⟦b:beneficentissimus⟧.
⟦b:honōrificus⟧, ⟦i:complimentary⟧,  ⟦b:honōrificentior⟧,  ⟦b:honōrificentissimus⟧.
⟦b:magnificus⟧, ⟦i:grand⟧,  ⟦b:magnificentior⟧,  ⟦b:magnificentissimus⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#354⟧
⟦b:iuvenior⟧, ⟦i:younger⟧, is late (Sen., Plin., Tac.). ⟦b:benevolēns⟧, ⟦i:kindly⟧, ⟦b:benevolentior⟧, ⟦b:benevolentissimus⟧, and ⟦b:maledīcēns⟧, ⟦i:abusive⟧, ⟦b:maledīcentior⟧ (once each, Plaut.), ⟦b:maledīcentissimus⟧, have usually as positive ⟦b:benevolus⟧ and ⟦b:maledicus⟧ respectively.
⟦#355⟧
Some positives have a comparative or superlative, or both, from a wholly different stem: such are,
⟦b:bonus⟧, ⟦i:good⟧,  ⟦b:melior⟧,  ⟦b:optimus⟧ (⟦r351:351⟧).
⟦b:malus⟧, ⟦i:bad⟧,  ⟦b:peior⟧,  ⟦b:pessimus⟧ (⟦r351:351⟧).
⟦b:multus⟧, ⟦i:much⟧,  ⟦b:plūs⟧ (sing. Ne. only),  ⟦b:plūrimus⟧ (⟦r352:352⟧).
⟦b:parvus⟧, ⟦i:little⟧,  ⟦b:minor⟧,  ⟦b:minimus⟧ (⟦r352:352⟧).
⟦/⟧
⟦b:parvus⟧ has rarely ⟦b:parvissimus⟧.
⟦#356⟧
Four comparatives in ⟦b:-erior⟧ or ⟦b:-terior⟧, denoting place (⟦r348:348⟧), have two forms of the superlative; the nominative masculine singular of the positive is not in common use:
⟦b:exterior⟧,  ⟦b:extimus⟧ (⟦r351:351⟧), or ⟦b:extrēmus⟧ (⟦r352:352⟧), ⟦i:outermost⟧.
⟦b:īnferior⟧,  ⟦b:īnfimus⟧, or ⟦b:īmus⟧, ⟦i:lowest⟧.
⟦b:posterior⟧,  ⟦b:postumus⟧ (⟦r351:351⟧), ⟦i:lastborn⟧, or ⟦b:postrēmus⟧ (⟦r352:352⟧), ⟦i:last⟧.
⟦b:superior⟧,  ⟦b:summus⟧ (⟦r352:352⟧), or ⟦b:suprēmus⟧ (⟦r352:352⟧), ⟦i:highest⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#357⟧
Six, denoting place, have the positive only as an adverb or preposition:
⟦b:cis⟧, ⟦i:this side⟧,  ⟦b:citerior⟧ (⟦r348:348⟧),  ⟦b:citimus⟧ (⟦r351:351⟧), ⟦i:hitherest⟧.
⟦b:dē⟧, ⟦i:down⟧,  ⟦b:dēterior⟧ (⟦r348:348⟧),  ⟦b:dēterrimus⟧, ⟦i:lowest⟧, ⟦i:worst⟧.
⟦b:in⟧, ⟦i:in⟧,  ⟦b:interior⟧ (⟦r348:348⟧),  ⟦b:intimus⟧, ⟦i:inmost⟧.
⟦b:prae⟧, ⟦i:before⟧,  ⟦b:prior⟧,  ⟦b:prīmus⟧ (⟦r352:352⟧), ⟦i:first⟧.
⟦b:prope⟧, ⟦i:near⟧,  ⟦b:propior⟧,  ⟦b:proximus⟧ (⟦r351:351⟧), ⟦i:nearest⟧.
⟦b:uls⟧, ⟦i:beyond⟧,  ⟦b:ulterior⟧ (⟦r348:348⟧),  ⟦b:ultimus⟧ (⟦r351:351⟧), ⟦i:furthest⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦b:ōcior⟧, ⟦i:swifter⟧, ⟦b:ōcissimus⟧, has no positive.
⟦#358⟧
These have a superlative, but no comparative: ⟦b:bellus⟧, ⟦i:pretty⟧, ⟦b:falsus⟧, ⟦i:false⟧, ⟦b:inclutus⟧, ⟦i:famed⟧, ⟦b:invictus⟧, ⟦i:unconquered⟧, ⟦b:invītus⟧, ⟦i:unwilling⟧, ⟦b:meritus⟧, ⟦i:deserving⟧, ⟦b:novus⟧, ⟦i:new⟧; ⟦b:vetus⟧, ⟦b:veterrimus⟧, ⟦i:old⟧, ⟦b:sacer⟧, ⟦b:sacerrimus⟧, ⟦i:sacred⟧, ⟦b:vafer⟧, ⟦b:vaferrimus⟧, ⟦i:sly⟧; ⟦b:malevolus⟧, ⟦b:malevolentissimus⟧ (twice, Cic.), ⟦i:spiteful⟧; ⟦b:maleficus⟧, ⟦b:maleficentissimus⟧ (once, Suet.), ⟦i:wicked⟧, ⟦b:mūnificus⟧, ⟦b:mūnificentissimus⟧ (inscrr.; Cic. once), ⟦i:generous⟧, ⟦b:mīrificus⟧, ⟦b:mīrificissimus⟧ (twice, Acc., Ter.), ⟦i:strange⟧. Plautus has ⟦b:ipsissumus⟧, ⟦i:his very self⟧.
⟦#359⟧
Most primitives in ⟦b:-ilis⟧ and ⟦b:-bilis⟧ (⟦r292:292⟧, ⟦r294:294⟧), have a comparative, but no superlative; but these have a superlative: ⟦b:facilis⟧ and ⟦b:difficilis⟧ (⟦r345:345⟧), ⟦i:easy⟧ and ⟦i:hard⟧, ⟦b:ūtilis⟧, ⟦i:useful⟧; also ⟦b:fertilis⟧, ⟦i:productive⟧, ⟦b:amābilis⟧, ⟦i:lovable⟧, ⟦b:mōbilis⟧, ⟦i:movable⟧, ⟦b:nōbilis⟧, ⟦i:well known⟧.
⟦#360⟧
Many adjectives have no suffixes of comparison, and supply the place of these by ⟦b:magis⟧, ⟦i:more⟧, and ⟦b:maximē⟧, ⟦i:most⟧: as, ⟦b:mīrus⟧, ⟦i:strange⟧, ⟦b:magis mīrus⟧, ⟦b:maximē mīrus⟧. Many adjectives, from their meaning, do not admit of comparison.

title: Comparative and Superlative Adverbs
text:
⟦#361⟧
Adverbs derived from adjectives have as their comparative the accusative singular neuter of the comparative adjective; the superlative is formed like that of the adjective, but ends in ⟦b:-ē⟧: as,
⟦b:altē⟧, ⟦i:on high⟧,  ⟦b:altius⟧,  ⟦b:altissimē⟧.
⟦b:ācriter⟧, ⟦i:sharply⟧,  ⟦b:ācrius⟧,  ⟦b:ācerrimē⟧.
⟦b:facile⟧, ⟦i:easily⟧,  ⟦b:facilius⟧,  ⟦b:facillimē⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#362⟧
An older superlative ending, ⟦b:-ēd⟧ for ⟦b:-ē⟧, occurs in an inscription of 186 B.C.: FACILVMED, i.e. ⟦b:facillimē⟧. A few adverbs have superlatives in ⟦b:-ō⟧ or ⟦b:-um⟧: as, ⟦b:meritissimō⟧, ⟦i:most deservedly⟧; ⟦b:prīmō⟧, ⟦i:at first⟧, ⟦b:prīmum⟧, ⟦i:first⟧; ⟦b:postrēmō⟧, ⟦i:at last⟧, ⟦b:postrēmum⟧, ⟦i:for the last time⟧.
⟦#363⟧
If the comparison of the adjective has peculiarities, they are retained in the adverb likewise: as, ⟦b:bene⟧, ⟦i:well⟧, ⟦b:melius⟧, ⟦b:optimē⟧; ⟦b:male⟧, ⟦i:ill⟧, ⟦b:peius⟧, ⟦b:pessimē⟧; ⟦b:multum⟧, ⟦i:much⟧, ⟦b:plūs⟧, ⟦b:plūrimum⟧; ⟦b:mātūrē⟧, ⟦i:betimes⟧, ⟦b:mātūrius⟧, ⟦b:mātūrissimē⟧ (Cic., Plin.), or ⟦b:mātūrrimē⟧ (Cic., Caes., Sall., Tac.). ⟦b:ōcius⟧, ⟦i:swifter⟧, no positive, ⟦b:ōcissimē⟧. ⟦b:minus⟧, ⟦i:less⟧, is formed by the nominal suffix ⟦b:-es-⟧ (⟦r236:236⟧), from √⟦b:⟦i:min-⟧⟧ (⟦b:minuō⟧); for ⟦b:magis⟧, ⟦i:more⟧, see 135, 2. In poetry ⟦b:magis⟧ sometimes becomes ⟦b:mage⟧, as if neuter of an adjective in ⟦b:-i-⟧.
⟦#364⟧
A few adverbs not derived from adjectives are compared: as, ⟦b:diū⟧, ⟦i:long⟧, ⟦b:diūtius⟧, ⟦b:diūtissimē⟧; ⟦b:saepe⟧, ⟦i:often⟧, ⟦b:saepius⟧, ⟦b:saepissimē⟧; ⟦b:nūper⟧, ⟦i:lately⟧, no comparative, ⟦b:nūperrimē⟧; ⟦b:secus⟧, ⟦i:otherwise⟧, ⟦b:sētius⟧, ⟦i:the less⟧; ⟦b:temperī⟧, ⟦i:betimes⟧, ⟦b:temperius⟧, ⟦i:earlier⟧, no superlative.

title: Formation of Denominative Verbs
text:
⟦#365⟧
Denominative verb stems have present infinitives in ⟦b:-āre⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, or ⟦b:-īre⟧ (⟦b:-ārī⟧, ⟦b:-ērī⟧, or ⟦b:-īrī⟧), and are formed from noun stems of all endings: as,
⟦b:fugā-re⟧, ⟦i:rout⟧  ⟦b:fugā-⟧, N. ⟦b:fuga⟧
⟦b:locā-re⟧, ⟦i:place⟧  ⟦b:loco-⟧, N. ⟦b:locus⟧
⟦b:nōminā-re⟧, ⟦i:name⟧  ⟦b:nōmin-⟧, N. ⟦b:nōmen⟧
⟦b:levā-re⟧, ⟦i:lighten⟧  ⟦b:levi-⟧, N. ⟦b:levis⟧
⟦b:sinuā-re⟧, ⟦i:bend⟧  ⟦b:sinu-⟧, N. ⟦b:sinus⟧
⟦b:albē-re⟧, ⟦i:be white⟧  ⟦b:albo-⟧, N. ⟦b:albus⟧
⟦b:miserē-rī⟧, ⟦i:pity⟧  ⟦b:misero-⟧, N. ⟦b:miser⟧
⟦b:flōrē-re⟧, ⟦i:blossom⟧  ⟦b:flōr-⟧, N. ⟦b:flōs⟧
⟦b:sordē-re⟧, ⟦i:be dirty⟧  ⟦b:sordi-⟧, N. ⟦b:sordēs⟧
⟦b:pūnī-re⟧, ⟦i:punish⟧  ⟦b:poenā-⟧, N. ⟦b:poena⟧
⟦b:condī-re⟧, ⟦i:season⟧  ⟦b:condo-⟧, N. ⟦b:condus⟧
⟦b:custōdī-re⟧, ⟦i:guard⟧  ⟦b:custōd-⟧, N. ⟦b:custōs⟧
⟦b:vestī-re⟧, ⟦i:dress⟧  ⟦b:vesti-⟧, N. ⟦i:vestis⟧
⟦b:gestī-re⟧, ⟦i:flutter⟧  ⟦b:gestu-⟧, N. ⟦i:gestus⟧
⟦/⟧
Verb. From Noun.
⟦#366⟧
These present verb stems are formed by adding the suffix ⟦b:-i̭o-⟧, ⟦b:-i̭e-⟧ to the noun stem: as ⟦b:*fugā-i̭ō⟧, ⟦i:I flee⟧; the ⟦b:i̭⟧ between two vowels was dropped (⟦r153:153, 2⟧) and the final vowel of noun stem was often contracted with the ending (⟦r118:118, 3⟧). The noun stem ending is often slightly modified.
⟦#367⟧
In a half a dozen denominatives from stems in ⟦b:-u-⟧ the ⟦b:u⟧ of the noun stem remains without modification, and is not contracted with the variable vowel (116, ⟦i:c⟧): these are, ⟦b:acuere⟧, ⟦i:sharpen⟧ (⟦b:acu-⟧), ⟦b:metuere⟧, ⟦i:fear⟧, ⟦b:statuere⟧, ⟦i:set⟧, ⟦b:tribuere⟧, ⟦i:assign⟧; ⟦b:arguere⟧, ⟦i:make clear⟧, ⟦b:bātuere⟧, ⟦i:beat⟧.
⟦#368⟧
Verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ are by far the most numerous class of denominatives; they are usually transitive; but deponents often express condition, sometimes occupation: as, ⟦b:dominārī⟧, ⟦i:lord it⟧, ⟦i:play the lord⟧; ⟦b:aquārī⟧, ⟦i:get oneself water⟧. Most verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧ also are transitive; those in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ usually denote a state: as, ⟦b:calēre⟧, ⟦i:be warm⟧; but some are causative: as, ⟦b:monēre⟧, ⟦i:remind⟧.
⟦#369⟧
Many denominative verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ contain a noun suffix which is not actually found in the noun itself; such suffixes are: ⟦b:-co-⟧, ⟦b:-cin-⟧, ⟦b:-lo-⟧, ⟦b:-er-⟧, ⟦b:-ro-⟧, ⟦b:-to-⟧, &c.: as,
⟦b:-co-⟧: ⟦b:albi-cāre⟧, ⟦i:be white⟧ (⟦b:*albi-co-⟧); ⟦b:velli-cāre⟧, ⟦i:pluck⟧ (⟦b:*velli-co-⟧, ⟦i:plucker⟧). ⟦b:-cin-⟧: ⟦b:latrō-cinārī⟧, ⟦i:be a robber⟧ (⟦b:latrōn-⟧); ⟦b:sermō-cinārī⟧, ⟦i:discourse⟧ (⟦b:sermōn-⟧). ⟦b:-lo-⟧: ⟦b:grātu-lārī⟧, ⟦i:give one joy⟧ (⟦b:*grātu-lo-⟧); ⟦b:vi-olāre⟧, ⟦i:harm⟧ (⟦b:*vi-olo-⟧); ⟦b:heiu-lāri⟧, ⟦i:cry⟧ ‘⟦b:heia⟧’ (⟦b:*heiu-lo-⟧). ⟦b:-er-⟧: ⟦b:mod-erārī⟧, ⟦i:check⟧ (⟦b:*mod-es-⟧, ⟦r236:236⟧). ⟦b:-ro-⟧: ⟦b:tole-rāre⟧, ⟦i:endure⟧ (⟦b:*tole-ro-⟧); ⟦b:flag-rāre⟧, ⟦i:blaze⟧ (⟦b:*flag-ro-⟧). ⟦b:-to-⟧: ⟦b:dēbili-tāre⟧, ⟦i:lame⟧ (⟦b:*dēbili-to-⟧); ⟦b:dubi-tāre⟧, ⟦i:doubt⟧ (⟦b:*dubi-to-⟧).
⟦#370⟧
Many denominatives in ⟦b:-āre⟧ are indirect compounds (⟦r377:377⟧), often from compound noun stems which are not actually found. So, particularly, when the first part is a preposition, or the second is from the root ⟦b:⟦i:fac-⟧⟧, ⟦i:make⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:ag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:drive⟧, ⟦i:do⟧, or ⟦b:⟦i:cap-⟧⟧, ⟦i:take⟧: as,
⟦b:opi-tul-ārī⟧, ⟦i:bear help⟧ (⟦b:opitulo-⟧); ⟦b:suf-fōc-āre⟧, ⟦i:suffocate⟧ (⟦b:*suf-fōc-o-⟧, ⟦b:fauci-⟧); ⟦b:aedi-fic-āre⟧ (⟦i:housebuild⟧), ⟦i:build⟧ (⟦b:*aedific-⟧ or ⟦b:*aedifico-⟧, ⟦i:housebuilder⟧); ⟦b:sīgni-fic-āre⟧, ⟦i:give token⟧ (⟦b:*sīgnifico-⟧); ⟦b:fūm-ig-āre⟧, ⟦i:make smoke⟧ (⟦b:*fūmigo-⟧, ⟦i:smoker⟧, ⟦b:fūmo-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:ag-⟧⟧); ⟦b:nāv-ig-āre⟧, ⟦i:sail⟧, and ⟦b:rēm-ig-āre⟧, ⟦i:row⟧ (⟦b:nāvi-⟧, ⟦i:ship⟧, and ⟦b:rēmo-⟧, ⟦i:oar⟧); ⟦b:mīt-ig-āre⟧, ⟦i:make mild⟧ (⟦b:mīti-⟧); ⟦b:iūr-ig-āre⟧, commonly ⟦b:iūr-g-āre⟧, ⟦i:quarrel⟧ (⟦b:iūr-⟧); ⟦b:pūr-ig-āre⟧, commonly ⟦b:pūr-g-āre⟧, ⟦i:clean⟧ (⟦b:pūro-⟧); ⟦b:gnār-ig-āre⟧, ⟦i:tell⟧ (⟦b:gnāro-⟧, ⟦b:narrāre⟧, 169, 2; ⟦r133:133, 1⟧); ⟦b:anti-cip-āre⟧, ⟦i:take beforehand⟧ (⟦b:*anticipo-⟧, ⟦b:ante⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:cap-⟧⟧); ⟦b:oc-cup-āre⟧, ⟦i:seize⟧ (⟦b:*occupo-⟧); ⟦b:re-cup-er-āre⟧, ⟦i:get back⟧ (⟦b:*recupero-⟧).
⟦#371⟧
Many verbs in ⟦b:-tāre⟧ (⟦b:-sāre⟧), or ⟦b:-tārī⟧ (⟦b:-sārī⟧), express frequent, intense, or sometimes attempted action. These are called ⟦i:Frequentatives⟧ or ⟦i:Intensives⟧; they are formed from perfect participle stems; but stems in ⟦b:-ā-to-⟧ become ⟦b:-i-to-⟧: as,
⟦b:cant-āre⟧, ⟦i:sing⟧ (⟦b:canto-⟧); ⟦b:cess-āre⟧, ⟦i:loiter⟧ (⟦b:cesso-⟧); ⟦b:amplex-ārī⟧, ⟦i:embrace⟧ (⟦b:amplexo-⟧); ⟦b:habit-āre⟧, ⟦i:live⟧ (⟦b:habito-⟧); ⟦b:pollicit-āri⟧, ⟦i:make overtures⟧ (⟦b:pollicito-⟧); ⟦b:dormīt-āre⟧, ⟦i:be sleepy⟧ (⟦b:dormīto-⟧); ⟦b:neg-itāre⟧, ⟦i:keep denying⟧ (for ⟦b:*negā-tāre⟧, with suffix ⟦b:-i-tāre⟧, ⟦r910:910⟧).
⟦#372⟧
Some frequentatives in ⟦b:-tāre⟧ are formed from the present stem of a verb in ⟦b:-ere⟧; the formative vowel before ⟦b:-tāre⟧ becomes ⟦b:i⟧: as,
⟦b:agi-tāre⟧, ⟦i:shake⟧ (⟦b:age-re⟧); ⟦b:flui-tāre⟧, ⟦i:float⟧ (⟦b:flue-re⟧); ⟦b:nōsci-tāre⟧, ⟦i:recognize⟧ (⟦b:nōsce-re⟧); ⟦b:quaeri-tāre⟧, ⟦i:keep seeking⟧ (⟦b:quaere-re⟧); ⟦b:scīsci-tārī⟧, ⟦i:enquire⟧ (⟦b:scīsce-re⟧); ⟦b:vēndi-tāre⟧, ⟦i:try to sell⟧ (⟦b:vēnde-re⟧).
⟦#373⟧
A few frequentatives add ⟦b:-tā-⟧ to the perfect participle stem: as,
⟦b:ācti-tāre⟧, ⟦i:act often⟧ (⟦b:ācto-⟧); ⟦b:facti-tāre⟧, ⟦i:do repeatedly⟧ (⟦b:facto-⟧); ⟦b:lēcti-tāre⟧, ⟦i:read again and again⟧ (⟦b:lēcto-⟧); ⟦b:ūncti-tāre⟧, ⟦i:anoint often⟧ (⟦b:ūncto-⟧). From a frequentative another frequentative is sometimes derived: as, ⟦b:dict-āre⟧, ⟦i:dictate⟧, ⟦b:dicti-tāre⟧, ⟦i:keep asserting⟧ (⟦b:dicto-⟧).
⟦#374⟧
Some verbs are found only as frequentatives: as, ⟦b:gust-āre⟧, ⟦i:taste⟧ (⟦b:*gusto-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:gus-⟧⟧, ⟦i:taste⟧); ⟦b:put-āre⟧, ⟦i:think⟧ (⟦b:puto-⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:pu-⟧⟧, ⟦i:clean⟧); ⟦b:aegrōt-āre⟧, ⟦i:be ill⟧ (⟦b:aegrōto-⟧).
⟦#375⟧
A few verbs in ⟦b:-uriō⟧, ⟦b:-urīre⟧, express desire; such are called ⟦i:Desideratives⟧: as, ⟦b:ēss-urīre⟧ or ⟦b:ēs-urīre⟧, ⟦i:want to eat⟧ (⟦b:edere⟧, ⟦b:ēsse⟧). A few in ⟦b:-ssō⟧, ⟦b:-ssere⟧, express earnest action; such are called ⟦i:Meditatives⟧: as, ⟦b:lacē-ssō⟧, ⟦b:lacē-ssere⟧, ⟦i:provoke⟧.

title: Composition
text:
⟦#376⟧
In compounds, the fundamental word is usually the second, which has its meaning qualified by the first.
⟦#377⟧
A Direct Compound is one formed directly from two parts: as, ⟦b:con-iug-⟧, N. ⟦b:coniūnx⟧, ⟦i:yoke-fellow⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, ⟦i:together⟧, √⟦b:⟦i:iug-⟧⟧, ⟦i:yoke⟧); ⟦b:con-iungere⟧, ⟦i:join together⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, ⟦b:iungere⟧); an Indirect Compound is one formed by the addition of a suffix to a direct compound: as, ⟦b:iūdic-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:iūudicium⟧, ⟦i:trial⟧ (⟦b:iūdic-⟧): ⟦b:iūdicā-re⟧, ⟦i:judge⟧ (⟦b:iūdic-⟧).
⟦#378⟧
A Real Compound is a word whose stem is formed from two stems, or an inseparable prefix and a stem, fused into one stem; an Apparent Compound is formed by the juxtaposition of an inflected word with another inflected word, a preposition, or an adverb.

title: Form of Compounds
text:
⟦#379⟧
If the first part is a noun, its stem is taken: as, ⟦b:Ahēno-barbus⟧, ⟦i:Redbeard⟧, ⟦i:Barbarossa⟧; usually with weakening of a stem vowel (⟦r103:103-105⟧): as, ⟦b:aurifex⟧, ⟦i:jeweller⟧ (⟦b:auro-⟧). On other changes of the final vowel in the first member of compounds, see ⟦r174:174⟧. Sometimes with disappearance of a syllable (⟦r179:179⟧); as, ⟦b:*venēni-ficus⟧, ⟦b:venē-ficus⟧, ⟦i:poisoner⟧ (⟦b:venēno-⟧); or of a vowel (⟦r111:111⟧): as, ⟦b:man-ceps⟧, ⟦i:contractor⟧ (⟦b:manu-⟧); particularly before a vowel (⟦r119:119⟧): as, ⟦b:magn-animus⟧, ⟦i:great-souled⟧ (⟦b:magno-⟧). Consonant stems are often extended by ⟦b:i⟧ before a consonant: as, ⟦b:mōri-gerus⟧, ⟦i:complaisant⟧ (⟦b:mōr-⟧).
⟦#380⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-s-⟧, including those in ⟦b:-er-⟧, ⟦b:-or-⟧ and ⟦b:-ōr-⟧ (⟦r236:236⟧), are sometimes compounded as above (⟦r379:379⟧): as, ⟦b:nemori-vagus⟧, ⟦i:woodranger⟧; ⟦b:honōri-ficus⟧, ⟦i:complimentary⟧; but usually they drop the suffix and take ⟦b:i⟧: as, ⟦b:opi-fex⟧, ⟦i:work-man⟧ (⟦b:oper-⟧); ⟦b:foedi-fragus⟧, ⟦i:truce-breaker⟧ (⟦b:foeder-⟧); ⟦b:volni-ficus⟧, ⟦i:wounding⟧ (⟦b:volner-⟧); ⟦b:mūni-ficus⟧, ⟦i:generous⟧ (⟦b:mūner-⟧); ⟦b:terri-ficus⟧, ⟦i:awe-inspiring⟧ (⟦b:terrōr-⟧); ⟦b:horri-fer⟧, ⟦i:dreadful⟧, ⟦b:horri-sonus⟧, ⟦i:awful-sounding⟧ (⟦b:horrōr-⟧).
⟦#381⟧
The second part, which often has weakening of the vowel (⟦r102:102⟧), is sometimes a bare root used as a stem (⟦r199:199⟧), oftener a root with a formative suffix; or a noun stem, sometimes with its stem ending modified: as, ⟦b:iū-dic-⟧, N. ⟦b:iūdex⟧, ⟦i:juror⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:dic-⟧⟧, ⟦i:declare⟧); ⟦b:causi-dic-o-⟧, N. ⟦b:causidicus⟧, ⟦i:pleader⟧ (⟦r209:209⟧); ⟦b:in-gen-io-⟧, N. ⟦b:ingenium⟧, ⟦i:disposition⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧, ⟦r219:219⟧); ⟦b:con-tāg-iōn-⟧, N. ⟦b:contāgiō⟧, ⟦i:touching together⟧ (√⟦b:⟦i:tag-⟧⟧, ⟦i:touch⟧, ⟦r227:227⟧); ⟦b:im-berb-i-⟧, N. ⟦b:imberbis⟧, ⟦i:beardless⟧ (⟦b:barbā-⟧).

title: Meaning of Compounds
text:
⟦#382⟧
Determinatives are compounds in which the second part keeps its original meaning, though determined or modified by the first part. The meaning of a determinative may often be best expressed by two words.
⟦#383⟧
(1.) The first part of a determinative may be an adjective, an adverb, a preposition, or an inseparable prefix; the second part is a noun: as,
⟦b:lāti-fundium⟧, i.e. ⟦b:lātī fundī⟧, ⟦i:broad acres⟧; ⟦b:prīvi-lēgium⟧, i.e. ⟦b:prīva lēx⟧, ⟦i:special act⟧; ⟦b:alti-sonāns⟧, i.e. ⟦b:altē sonāns⟧, ⟦i:high-sounding⟧; ⟦b:con-discipulus⟧, i.e. ⟦b:cum alterō discipulus⟧, ⟦i:fellow-pupil⟧; ⟦b:per-magnus⟧, i.e. ⟦b:valdē magnus⟧, ⟦i:very great⟧; ⟦b:in-dignus⟧, i.e. ⟦b:nōn dignus⟧, ⟦i:unworthy⟧.
⟦#384⟧
(2.) The first part of a determinative may represent the oblique case of a noun, generally a substantive; the second part is a noun or verb stem. These compounds are called ⟦i:Objectives⟧: as,
Accusative of direct object (⟦r1132:1132⟧), ⟦b:armi-ger⟧, i.e. ⟦b:quī arma gerit⟧, ⟦i:armour-bearer⟧; dative of indirect object (⟦r1208:1208⟧), ⟦b:man-tēle⟧, i.e. ⟦b:manibus tēla⟧, ⟦i:handkerchief⟧, ⟦i:napkin⟧; genitive (⟦r1227:1227⟧), ⟦b:sōl-stitium⟧, i.e. ⟦b:sōlis statiō⟧, ⟦i:solstice⟧; ablative instrumental (⟦r1300:1300⟧), ⟦b:tubi-cen⟧, i.e. ⟦b:quī tubā canit⟧, ⟦i:trumpeter⟧; locative (⟦r1331:1331⟧), ⟦b:Troiu-gena⟧, i.e. ⟦b:Troiae nātus⟧, ⟦i:Troy-born⟧; ablative locative (⟦r1350:1350⟧), ⟦b:nocti-vagus⟧, ⟦i:night-wandering⟧; ⟦b:monti-vagus⟧, ⟦i:mountain-ranging⟧.
⟦#385⟧
Possessives are adjective compounds in which the meaning of the second part is changed. The second part of a possessive is always formed from a substantive, qualified by the noun, adverb, or inseparable prefix of the first part, and the whole expresses an attribute which something ⟦i:has⟧: as,
⟦b:longi-manus⟧, ⟦i:longarms⟧, ⟦i:long-armed⟧; ⟦b:miseri-cors⟧, ⟦i:tender-hearted⟧; ⟦b:bi-linguis⟧, ⟦i:two-tongued⟧; ⟦b:magn-animus⟧, ⟦i:greatheart⟧, ⟦i:great-hearted⟧; ⟦b:im-berbis⟧, ⟦i:beardless⟧.

title: Composition of Nouns: Apparent Compounds
text:
⟦#386⟧
Apparent Compounds are formed:
⟦#387⟧
(1.) By two nouns combined, one with an unchanging case ending, the other with full inflections: as, ⟦b:aquae-ductus⟧, ⟦i:aqueduct⟧; ⟦b:senātūs-cōnsultum⟧, ⟦i:decree of the senate⟧; ⟦b:pater-familiās⟧, ⟦i:father of a family⟧; ⟦b:vērī-similis⟧, ⟦i:like the truth⟧; in these words, ⟦b:aquae⟧, ⟦b:senātūs⟧, ⟦b:familiās⟧, and ⟦b:vērī⟧ are genitives, and remain genitives, while the other part of the compound is declinable.
⟦#388⟧
(2.) By a substantive with an adjective habitually agreeing with it, both parts being declined: as, ⟦b:rēs pūblica⟧, ⟦i:the common-weal⟧; ⟦b:rēs gestae⟧, ⟦i:exploits⟧; ⟦b:iūs iūrandum⟧, ⟦i:oath⟧; ⟦b:pecūniae repetundae⟧, ⟦i:money claim⟧.
⟦#389⟧
(3.) By nouns, chiefly substantives, in the same case placed loosely side by side and making one idea. The two words may be used: (⟦i:a.⟧) Copulatively: as, ⟦b:ūsus-frūctus⟧, ⟦i:use and enjoyment⟧; ⟦b:pactum-conventum⟧, ⟦i:bargain and covenant⟧; ⟦b:duo-decim⟧, ⟦i:two and ten⟧, ⟦i:twelve⟧; or (⟦i:b.⟧) Appositively: one word explaining the other (⟦r1045:1045⟧): as, ⟦b:Iuppiter⟧, ⟦i:Jove the Father⟧ (⟦r94:94⟧; ⟦r133:133⟧); ⟦b:Mārspiter⟧, ⟦i:Mars the Father⟧, for ⟦b:Mārs pater⟧.
⟦#390⟧
(4.) From an original combination of an oblique case with a preposition: as, ⟦b:prōcōnsul⟧, ⟦i:proconsul⟧, from ⟦b:prō cōnsule⟧, ⟦i:for a consul⟧; ⟦b:ēgregius⟧, ⟦i:select⟧, from ⟦b:ē grege⟧, ⟦i:out of the herd⟧; ⟦b:dēlīrus⟧, ⟦i:astray⟧, ⟦i:mad⟧, from ⟦b:dē līrā⟧, ⟦i:out of the furrow⟧.

title: Real Compounds
text:
⟦#391⟧
Real Compounds are direct compounds of a verb with a preposition; the root vowel or diphthong of the verb is often weakened (⟦r102:102⟧): as,
⟦b:per-agere⟧, ⟦i:put through⟧, ⟦i:accomplish⟧; ⟦b:ab-igere⟧, ⟦i:drive away⟧; ⟦b:ex-quīrere⟧, ⟦i:seek out⟧. The prefix, which was originally a separate adverb modifying the verb, is in poetry sometimes separated from the verb by another word; the disyllabic prepositions in particular often remain as juxtaposed adverbs (⟦r396:396⟧).
⟦#392⟧
Some prepositions are inseparable, that is, used only in composition: ⟦b:ambi-⟧, ⟦i:round⟧, ⟦b:an-⟧, ⟦i:up⟧, ⟦b:dis-⟧, ⟦i:in two⟧, ⟦i:apart⟧, ⟦b:por-⟧, ⟦i:towards⟧, ⟦b:red-⟧, ⟦b:re-⟧, ⟦i:back⟧, ⟦b:sēd-⟧, ⟦b:sē-⟧, ⟦i:by oneself⟧, ⟦i:away⟧: as, ⟦b:amb-īre⟧, ⟦i:go round to⟧; ⟦b:an-hēlāre⟧, ⟦i:breathe up⟧; ⟦b:dis-pellere⟧, ⟦i:drive apart⟧; ⟦b:por-rigere⟧, ⟦i:stretch forth⟧; ⟦b:red-dere⟧, ⟦i:give back⟧; ⟦b:sē-iungere⟧, ⟦i:separate⟧.

title: Composition of Verbs: Apparent Compounds
text:
⟦#393⟧
Apparent Compounds are formed by the juxtaposition of:
⟦#394⟧
(1.) A verb with a verb: ⟦b:faciō⟧ and ⟦b:fīō⟧ are added to present stems, mostly of intransitive verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧; the ⟦b:-e-⟧ of the first verb is sometimes long, and sometimes short (⟦r130:130, 5⟧): as, ⟦b:calē̆-facere⟧, ⟦i:make warm⟧ (⟦b:calēre⟧); ⟦b:excandē̆-facere⟧, ⟦i:make blaze⟧ (⟦b:candēre⟧); ⟦b:madē̆-facere⟧, ⟦i:make wet⟧ (⟦b:madēre⟧). In these apparent compounds, the accent of ⟦b:faciō⟧ remains the same as in the simple verb: as, ⟦b:calē̆fácis⟧.
⟦#395⟧
(2.) A substantive with a verb: as, ⟦b:anim-advertere⟧, ⟦i:pay heed to⟧, ⟦b:animum advertere⟧; ⟦b:vēnum-dare⟧, or ⟦b:vēndere⟧, ⟦i:sell⟧, ⟦b:vēnum dare⟧; ⟦b:vēn-īre⟧, ⟦i:be sold⟧, ⟦b:vēnum īre⟧; ⟦b:lucrī-facere⟧, ⟦i:make gain⟧, ⟦b:lucrī facere⟧; ⟦b:manū-mittere⟧, ⟦i:set free⟧.
⟦#396⟧
(3.) An adverb with a verb: as, ⟦b:circum-dare⟧, ⟦i:put round⟧; ⟦b:satis-facere⟧, ⟦b:satis-dare⟧, ⟦i:give satisfaction⟧; ⟦b:intro-īre⟧, ⟦i:go inside⟧; ⟦b:mālle⟧, ⟦i:prefer⟧, for ⟦b:magis velle⟧ (⟦r170:170, 2⟧); ⟦b:nōlō⟧, ⟦i:be unwilling⟧, for ⟦b:ne volō⟧; ⟦b:ne-scīre⟧, ⟦b:hau-scīre⟧, ⟦i:not know⟧.

title: Inflection
text:
⟦#397⟧
Inflection is the change which nouns, pronouns, and verbs undergo, to indicate their relation in a sentence.
The inflection of a noun or pronoun is often called ⟦i:Declension⟧, and that of a verb, ⟦i:Conjugation⟧.

title: Inflection of the Noun
text:
⟦#398⟧
The noun or pronoun is inflected by attaching case endings to the stem.
The endings, which are called case endings for brevity, indicate number as well as case, and serve also to distinguish gender words from neuters in the nominative and accusative singular of some stems, and of all plurals. These endings are nearly the same for stems of all kinds.

title: Inflection of the Noun: The Stem
text:
⟦#399⟧
The stem contains the meaning of the noun. Noun stems are arranged in the following order: (1.) stems in ⟦b:-ā-⟧, in ⟦b:-o-⟧, in a consonant, or in ⟦b:-i-⟧; these are substantive, including proper names, or adjective; (2.) stems in ⟦b:-u-⟧ or ⟦b:-ē-⟧; these are substantive only, and include no proper names.
⟦#400⟧
In some instances, a final stem vowel is retained before a case ending which begins with a vowel: as, ⟦b:urbi-um⟧, ⟦b:ācri-a⟧, ⟦b:cornu-a⟧, ⟦b:portu-ī⟧, ⟦b:portu-um⟧ (116, ⟦i:c⟧); in others the stem vowel blends inseparably with the vowel of the case ending: as, ⟦b:mēnsīs⟧, ⟦b:dominīs⟧ (108, ⟦i:a⟧).
⟦#401⟧
Some nouns have more than one form of the stem: as,
⟦b:sēdēs⟧ (⟦r476:476⟧); ⟦b:femur⟧, ⟦b:iecur⟧ (⟦r489:489⟧); ⟦b:vās⟧, ⟦b:mēnsis⟧ (⟦r492:492⟧); ⟦b:vīrus⟧, ⟦b:volgus⟧ (⟦r493:493⟧); ⟦b:iter⟧, ⟦b:nix⟧, ⟦b:senex⟧, &c. (⟦r500:500⟧); ⟦b:vīs⟧ (⟦r518:518⟧); ⟦b:caedēs⟧ (⟦r523:523⟧); ⟦b:famēs⟧, ⟦b:plēbēs⟧ (⟦r524:524⟧); ⟦b:domus⟧ (⟦r594:594⟧); ⟦b:angiportus⟧, &c. (⟦r595:595⟧). Many nouns have a consonant stem in the singular, and an ⟦b:-i-⟧ stem in the plural: see ⟦r516:516⟧; most substantives in ⟦b:-iē-⟧ or ⟦b:-tiē-⟧ have a collateral form in ⟦b:-iā-⟧ or ⟦b:-tiā-⟧ (⟦r604:604⟧). Some adjectives have two different stems: as, ⟦b:hilarus⟧, ⟦b:hilara⟧, ⟦b:hilarum⟧, and ⟦b:hilaris⟧, ⟦b:hilare⟧; ⟦b:exanimus⟧ and ⟦b:exanimis⟧.

title: Gender
text:
⟦#402⟧
There are two genders, ⟦i:Masculine⟧ and ⟦i:Feminine⟧. Masculine and feminine nouns are called ⟦i:Gender nouns⟧. Nouns without gender are called ⟦i:Neuter⟧.
⟦#403⟧
Gender is, properly speaking, the distinction of sex. In Latin, a great many things without life have gender in grammar, and are masculine or feminine.
⟦#404⟧
Some classes of substantives may be brought under general heads of signification, as below, like the names of rivers and winds (⟦r405:405⟧), which are usually of the masculine gender, or of plants (⟦r407:407⟧), which are usually of the feminine. When the gender cannot be determined thus, it must be learned from the special rules for the several stems and their nominatives.

title: Masculines
text:
⟦#405⟧
Names of male beings, rivers, winds, and mountains, are masculine: as,
⟦b:Caesar⟧, ⟦b:Gāius⟧, ⟦b:Sūlla⟧, men’s names; ⟦b:pater⟧, ⟦i:father⟧; ⟦b:erus⟧, ⟦i:master⟧; ⟦b:scrība⟧, ⟦i:scrivener⟧; ⟦b:Tiberis⟧, ⟦i:the Tiber⟧; ⟦b:Aquilō⟧, ⟦i:a Norther⟧; ⟦b:Lūcrētilis⟧, ⟦i:Mt. Lucretilis⟧.
⟦#406⟧
The river names: ⟦b:Allia⟧, ⟦b:Dūria⟧, ⟦b:Sagra⟧, ⟦b:Lēthē⟧, and ⟦b:Styx⟧ are feminine. Also the mountain names ⟦b:Alpēs⟧, plural, ⟦i:the Alps⟧, and some Greek names of mountains in ⟦b:-a⟧ or ⟦b:-ē⟧: as, ⟦b:Aetna⟧, ⟦i:Mt. Etna⟧; ⟦b:Rhodopē⟧, a Thracian range. A few are neuter, as ⟦b:Sōracte⟧.

title: Feminines
text:
⟦#407⟧
Names of female beings, plants, flowers, shrubs, and trees, are feminine: as,
⟦b:Gāia⟧, ⟦b:Glycerium⟧, women’s names; ⟦b:mālus⟧, ⟦i:apple-tree⟧; ⟦b:quercus⟧, ⟦i:oak⟧; ⟦b:īlex⟧, ⟦i:holm-oak⟧; ⟦b:abiēs⟧, ⟦i:fir⟧.
⟦#408⟧
Masculine are: ⟦b:bōlētus⟧, ⟦i:mushroom⟧, ⟦b:carduus⟧, ⟦i:thistle⟧, ⟦b:dūmī⟧, plural, ⟦i:brambles⟧, ⟦b:intibus⟧, ⟦i:endive⟧, ⟦b:iuncus⟧, ⟦i:rush⟧, ⟦b:oleaster⟧, ⟦i:bastard olive⟧, ⟦b:rubus⟧, ⟦i:bramble⟧, ⟦b:rumex⟧, ⟦i:sorrel⟧, ⟦b:scirpus⟧, ⟦i:bulrush⟧, and rarely ⟦b:fīcus⟧, ⟦i:fig⟧. Also some of Greek origin: as, ⟦b:acanthus⟧, ⟦b:amāracus⟧, ⟦b:asparagus⟧, and ⟦b:crocus⟧. Neuter are: ⟦b:apium⟧, ⟦i:parsley⟧, ⟦b:balsamum⟧, ⟦i:balsam-tree⟧, ⟦b:rōbur⟧, ⟦i:heart of oak⟧, and some names with stems in ⟦b:-er-⟧ (⟦r573:573⟧).

title: Mobile, Common, and Epicene Nouns
text:
⟦#409⟧
Mobile Nouns have different forms to distinguish sex: as, ⟦b:Iūlius⟧, a man, ⟦i:Julius⟧, ⟦b:Iūlia⟧, a woman, ⟦i:Julia⟧; ⟦b:cervus⟧, ⟦i:stag⟧, ⟦b:cerva⟧, ⟦i:hind⟧; ⟦b:socer⟧, ⟦i:father-in-law⟧, ⟦b:socrus⟧, ⟦i:mother-in-law⟧; ⟦b:victor⟧, ⟦i:conqueror⟧, ⟦b:victrīx⟧, ⟦i:conqueress⟧. Adjectives ‘of three endings’ (⟦r611:611⟧), belong to this class.
⟦#410⟧
Some nouns have one ending, but are applicable to either sex. Such are said, to be of ⟦i:Common Gender⟧: as, ⟦b:adulēscēns⟧, ⟦i:young man⟧ or ⟦i:young woman⟧; ⟦b:dux⟧, ⟦i:leader⟧; ⟦b:īnfāns⟧, ⟦i:baby⟧, ⟦i:child⟧; and many other consonant stems or stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧, denoting persons. Adjectives ‘of two endings’ or ‘of one ending’ (⟦r611:611⟧), belong to this class.
⟦#411⟧
Epicenes have one ending and one grammatical gender, though applicable to animals of either sex. Thus, ⟦b:aquila⟧, ⟦i:eagle⟧, is feminine, though it may denote a ⟦i:he-eagle⟧ as well as a ⟦i:she-eagle⟧; ⟦b:anatēs⟧, ⟦i:ducks⟧, feminine, includes ⟦i:drakes⟧.

title: Neuters
text:
⟦#412⟧
Infinitives, words and expressions quoted or explained, and letters of the alphabet, are neuter: as,
⟦b:vīvere ipsum⟧, ⟦i:mere living⟧; ⟦b:istūc ‘taceō,’⟧ ⟦i:your ‘I won’t mention;’⟧ ⟦b:longum vale⟧, ⟦i:a long goodbye⟧; ⟦b:o Graecum⟧, ⟦i:Greek O⟧. But the letters have sometimes a feminine adjective, agreeing with ⟦b:littera⟧ understood.

title: Variable Gender
text:
⟦#413⟧
Some substantives have different genders in the two numbers; the different gender is sometimes indicated by a difference of stem: as, ⟦b:epulum⟧, neuter, ⟦b:epulae⟧, feminine, ⟦i:feast⟧. See ⟦b:balneum⟧, ⟦b:frēnum⟧, ⟦b:jocus⟧, ⟦b:locus⟧, ⟦b:margarīta⟧, ⟦b:ostrea⟧, ⟦b:rāstrum⟧, in the dictionary.

title: Number
text:
⟦#414⟧
There are two numbers, the ⟦i:Singular⟧ used of one, the ⟦i:Plural⟧ of more than one.
⟦#415⟧
⟦b:ambō⟧, ⟦i:both⟧, and ⟦b:duo⟧, ⟦i:two⟧, nominative and accusative masculine and neuter, are the only remnants of an old ⟦i:Dual⟧ number, denoting two.
⟦#416⟧
Some substantives, from their meaning, have no plural.
Such are: proper names: as, ⟦b:Cicerō⟧, ⟦i:Cicero⟧; ⟦b:Rōma⟧, ⟦i:Rome⟧; material and abstract substantives: as, ⟦b:oleum⟧, ⟦i:oil⟧, ⟦b:vīnum⟧, ⟦i:wine⟧, ⟦b:iūstitia⟧, ⟦i:justice⟧; and gerunds: as, ⟦b:regendī⟧, ⟦i:of guiding⟧. For the occasional use of the plural, ⟦r1105:1105-1110⟧.
⟦#417⟧
Some substantives, from their meaning, have no singular.
Such are: names of persons of a class: as, ⟦b:maiōrēs⟧, ⟦i:ancestors⟧; ⟦b:superī⟧, ⟦i:the beings above⟧; ⟦b:mānēs⟧, ⟦i:ghosts⟧; of feasts, sacrifices, days: as, ⟦b:Sāturnālia⟧, ⟦i:festival of Saturn⟧; ⟦b:kalendae⟧, ⟦i:first of the month⟧; of things made of parts or consisting of a series of acts: as, ⟦b:arma⟧, ⟦i:arms⟧; ⟦b:artūs⟧, ⟦i:joints⟧; ⟦b:quadrīgae⟧, ⟦i:four-in-hand⟧; ⟦b:exsequiae⟧, ⟦i:funeral rites⟧; of some places: as, ⟦b:Faleriī⟧; ⟦b:Vēī⟧; ⟦b:Pompēī⟧; ⟦b:Athēnae⟧, ⟦i:Athens⟧; ⟦b:Alpēs⟧, ⟦i:the Alps⟧.
⟦#418⟧
Some substantives have different meanings in the two numbers: as,
⟦b:aedis⟧, ⟦i:temple⟧, ⟦b:aedēs⟧, ⟦i:house⟧; ⟦b:auxilium⟧, ⟦i:aid⟧, ⟦b:auxilia⟧, ⟦i:auxiliaries⟧; ⟦b:carcer⟧, ⟦i:jail⟧, ⟦b:carcerēs⟧, ⟦i:race-barriers⟧; ⟦b:Castrum⟧, ⟦i:Castle⟧, ⟦b:castra⟧, ⟦i:camp⟧; ⟦b:comitium⟧, ⟦i:meeting-place⟧, ⟦b:comitia⟧, ⟦i:election⟧; ⟦b:cōpia⟧, ⟦i:abundance⟧, ⟦b:cōpiae⟧, ⟦i:troops⟧; ⟦b:facultās⟧, ⟦i:ability⟧, ⟦b:facultātēs⟧, ⟦i:wealth⟧; ⟦b:fīnis⟧, ⟦i:end⟧, ⟦b:fīnēs⟧, ⟦i:boundaries⟧; ⟦b:grātia⟧, ⟦i:favour⟧, ⟦b:grātiae⟧, ⟦i:thanks⟧; ⟦b:impedīmentum⟧, ⟦i:hindrance⟧, ⟦b:impedīmenta⟧, ⟦i:baggage⟧; ⟦b:littera⟧, ⟦i:letter (of the alphabet)⟧, ⟦b:litterae⟧, ⟦i:epistle⟧; ⟦b:rōstrum⟧, ⟦i:beak⟧, ⟦b:rōstra⟧, ⟦i:speakers stand⟧. See also ⟦b:aqua⟧, ⟦b:bonum⟧, ⟦b:fortūna⟧, ⟦b:lūdus⟧, ⟦b:opera⟧, ⟦b:pars⟧, in the dictionary.

title: Inflection of the Noun: Case
text:
⟦#419⟧
Nouns have five cases, the ⟦i:Nominative⟧, ⟦i:Genitive⟧, ⟦i:Dative⟧, ⟦i:Accusative⟧, and ⟦i:Ablative⟧.
The nominative represents a noun as subject, the accusative as object; the genitive denotes the relation of ⟦i:of⟧, the dative of ⟦i:to⟧ or ⟦i:for⟧, and the ablative of ⟦i:from⟧, ⟦i:with⟧, ⟦i:in⟧, or ⟦i:by⟧. But the meanings of the cases are best learnt from reading. All cases but the nominative and vocative (⟦r420:420⟧) are called ⟦i:Oblique Cases⟧.
⟦#420⟧
Town names and a few appellatives have also a case denoting the place where, called the ⟦i:Locative⟧. Masculine stems in ⟦b:-o-⟧ and some Greek stems with other endings have still another form used in addressing a person or thing, called the ⟦i:Vocative⟧.
⟦#421⟧
The stem of a noun is best seen in the genitive; in the genitive plural it is preserved without change, except that ⟦b:o⟧ of ⟦b:-o-⟧ stems is lengthened (⟦r123:123⟧). In dictionaries the stem ending is indicated by the genitive singular, thus: ⟦b:-ae⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦b:-is⟧, ⟦b:-ūs⟧ (⟦b:-ĕī⟧), indicate respectively stems in ⟦b:-ā-⟧, ⟦b:-o-⟧, a consonant or ⟦b:-i-⟧, ⟦b:-u-⟧, and ⟦b:-ē-⟧, as follows:
⟦b:-ae⟧, ⟦b:mēnsae⟧, ⟦i:table⟧  ⟦b:-ārum⟧, ⟦b:mēnsā-rum⟧  ⟦b:-ā-⟧, ⟦b:mēnsā-⟧, N. ⟦b:mēnsa⟧
⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦b:dominī⟧, ⟦i:master⟧  ⟦b:-ōrum⟧, ⟦b:dominō-rum⟧  ⟦b:-o-⟧, ⟦b:domino-⟧, N. ⟦b:dominus⟧
⟦b:-is⟧, ⟦b:rēgis⟧, ⟦i:king⟧  -cons. ⟦b:um⟧, ⟦b:rēg-um⟧  -consonant, ⟦b:rēg-⟧, N. ⟦b:rēx⟧
⟦b:-is⟧, ⟦b:cīvis⟧, ⟦i:citizen⟧  ⟦b:-ium⟧, ⟦b:cīvi-um⟧  ⟦b:-i-⟧, ⟦b:cīvi-⟧, N. ⟦b:cīvis⟧
⟦b:-ūs⟧, ⟦b:portus⟧, ⟦i:port⟧  ⟦b:-uum⟧, ⟦b:portu-um⟧  ⟦b:-u-⟧, ⟦b:portu-⟧, N. ⟦b:portus⟧
(⟦b:ĕ̄ī⟧, ⟦b:rĕ̄ī⟧), ⟦i:thing⟧  (⟦b:-ērum⟧, ⟦b:rē-rum⟧)  ⟦b:-ē⟧, ⟦b:rē-⟧, N. ⟦b:rēs⟧
⟦/⟧
Genitive Singular. Genitive Plural. Stems in.
⟦#422⟧
Gender nominatives usually add ⟦b:-s⟧ to the stem: as, ⟦b:servo-s⟧ or ⟦b:servu-s⟧, ⟦i:slave⟧, ⟦b:rēx⟧ (⟦r164:164, 1⟧), ⟦b:cīvi-s⟧, ⟦b:portu-s⟧, ⟦b:rē-s⟧. But stems in ⟦b:-ā-⟧ or in a continuous consonant (⟦b:-l-⟧, ⟦b:-n-⟧, ⟦b:-r-⟧, or ⟦b:-s-⟧) have no ⟦b:-s⟧: as, ⟦b:mēnsa⟧, ⟦b:cōnsul⟧, ⟦i:consul⟧, ⟦b:flāmen⟧, ⟦i:special priest⟧, ⟦b:pater⟧, ⟦i:father⟧, ⟦b:flōs⟧, ⟦i:flower⟧.
⟦#423⟧
Neuters have the nominative and accusative alike; in the singular the stem is used: as ⟦b:nōmen⟧, ⟦i:name⟧; or a shortened stem: as, ⟦b:exemplar⟧, ⟦i:pattern⟧; but stems in ⟦b:-o-⟧ take ⟦b:-m⟧: as, ⟦b:aevo-m⟧ or ⟦b:aevu-m⟧, ⟦i:age⟧. In the plural ⟦b:-a⟧ is always used: as, ⟦b:rēgna⟧, ⟦i:kingdoms⟧, ⟦b:nōmina⟧, ⟦b:cornua⟧, ⟦i:horns⟧. For ⟦b:-s⟧ in adjectives ‘of one ending,’ see ⟦r612:612⟧.
⟦#424⟧
Gender accusatives singular add ⟦b:-m⟧ to the stem: as, ⟦b:mēnsa-m⟧, ⟦b:servo-m⟧ or ⟦b:servu-m⟧, ⟦b:nāvi-m⟧, ⟦i:ship⟧, ⟦b:portu-m⟧, ⟦b:die-m⟧. The consonant stems have the ending ⟦b:-em⟧: as, ⟦b:rēg-em⟧; most substantive stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ and all adjectives also drop ⟦b:-i-⟧ and take ⟦b:-em⟧: as, nāv-em, ⟦b:trīst-em⟧, ⟦i:sad⟧. In the plural, gender stems add ⟦b:-s⟧ before which the vowel is long: as, ⟦b:mēnsā-s⟧, ⟦b:servō-s⟧, ⟦b:rēgē-s⟧, ⟦b:nāvī-s⟧ or ⟦b:nāvē-s⟧, ⟦b:portū-s⟧, ⟦b:rē-s⟧.
⟦#425⟧
The ablative singular usually ends in the long vowel of the stem: as, ⟦b:mēnsā⟧, ⟦b:dominō⟧, ⟦b:nāvī⟧, ⟦b:portū⟧, ⟦b:rē⟧. The ablative of consonant stems usually has ⟦b:-e⟧ (rarely ⟦b:-ī-⟧, see ⟦r502:502⟧): as, ⟦b:patre⟧, ⟦i:father⟧; and that of substantive ⟦b:-i-⟧ stems has ⟦b:-e⟧ more commonly than ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:nāve⟧.
⟦#426⟧
The ablative singular of ⟦b:-ā-⟧ and ⟦b:-o-⟧ stems ended anciently in ⟦b:-ād⟧ and ⟦b:-ōd⟧ respectively: as, PRAIDAD, PREIVATOD; that of consonant stems in ⟦b:-īd⟧: as, AIRID, COVENTIONID. But ⟦b:-d⟧ is almost entirely confined to inscriptions and disappeared early (⟦r149:149⟧).
⟦#427⟧
The genitive plural adds ⟦b:-rum⟧ to ⟦b:-ā-⟧, ⟦b:-o-⟧, and ⟦b:-ē-⟧ stems: as, ⟦b:mēnsā-rum⟧, ⟦b:dominō-rum⟧, ⟦b:rē-rum⟧; and ⟦b:-um⟧ to consonant stems, ⟦b:-i-⟧ stems, and ⟦b:-u-⟧ stems: as, ⟦b:rēg-um⟧, ⟦b:cīvi-um⟧, ⟦b:portu-um⟧.
⟦#428⟧
The dative and ablative plural are always alike: stems in ⟦b:-ā-⟧ and ⟦b:-o-⟧ take ⟦b:-is⟧, which blends with the stem vowel (⟦r400:400⟧): as, ⟦b:mēnsīs⟧, ⟦b:dominīs⟧; other stems have ⟦b:-bus⟧, before which consonant stems are extended by ⟦b:i⟧: as, ⟦b:rēgi-bus⟧, ⟦b:nāvi-bus⟧, ⟦b:portu-bus⟧ or ⟦b:porti-bus⟧, ⟦b:rē-bus⟧.
⟦#429⟧
Some pronouns and a few adjectives have some peculiar case endings; see ⟦r618:618-694⟧.
⟦#430⟧
Many nouns are defective in case.
Thus, many monosyllables have no genitive plural: as, ⟦b:aes⟧, ⟦i:copper⟧, ⟦b:cor⟧, ⟦i:heart⟧, ⟦b:cōs⟧, ⟦i:whetstone⟧, ⟦b:dōs⟧, ⟦i:dowry⟧, ⟦b:ōs⟧, ⟦i:face⟧, ⟦b:pāx⟧, ⟦i:peace⟧, ⟦b:pix⟧, ⟦i:pitch⟧, ⟦b:rōs⟧, ⟦i:dew⟧, ⟦b:sāl⟧, ⟦i:salt⟧, ⟦b:lūx⟧, ⟦i:light⟧; many words have no genitive, dative, or ablative plural: as, ⟦b:hiemps⟧, ⟦i:winter⟧; especially neuters: as, ⟦b:fār⟧, ⟦i:spelt⟧, ⟦b:fel⟧, ⟦i:gall⟧, ⟦b:mel⟧, ⟦i:honey⟧, ⟦b:pūs⟧, ⟦i:matter⟧, ⟦b:rūs⟧, ⟦i:country⟧, ⟦b:tūs⟧, ⟦i:frankincense⟧. Many words in ⟦b:-tu-⟧ (⟦b:-su-⟧) have only the ablative (⟦r235:235⟧). For ⟦b:-ē-⟧ stems, see ⟦r600:600⟧. Other words more or less defective are ⟦b:exlēx⟧, ⟦b:exspēs⟧, ⟦b:fās⟧ and ⟦b:nefās⟧, ⟦b:īnfitiās⟧, ⟦b:inquiēs⟧, ⟦b:īnstar⟧, ⟦b:luēs⟧, ⟦b:nēmō⟧, ⟦b:opis⟧ and ⟦b:vicis⟧ genitives, ⟦b:pondō⟧ and ⟦b:sponte⟧ ablatives, ⟦b:secus⟧, ⟦b:vīs⟧. Many adjectives ‘of one ending’ want the nominative and accusative neuter plural and genitive plural.
⟦#431⟧
Some adjectives are altogether indeclinable: as, ⟦b:frūgī⟧, ⟦i:thrifty⟧, an old dative; ⟦b:nēquam⟧, ⟦i:naughty⟧, an old accusative; ⟦b:quot⟧, ⟦i:how many⟧; ⟦b:tot⟧, ⟦i:so many⟧; and most numerals (⟦r637:637⟧). These adjectives are attached to any case of a substantive without varying their own forms.

title: Stems in -ā-
text:
⟦=⟧⟦i:The First Declension.⟧
⟦=⟧Genitive singular ⟦b:-ae⟧, genitive plural ⟦b:-ā-rum⟧.
⟦#432⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-ā-⟧ include substantives and adjectives; both substantives and adjectives are feminine.
⟦#433⟧
Names of males are masculine (⟦r405:405⟧): as, ⟦b:scrība⟧, ⟦i:writer⟧; also ⟦b:Hadria⟧, ⟦i:the Adriatic⟧, and rarely ⟦b:damma⟧, ⟦i:deer⟧, and ⟦b:talpa⟧, ⟦i:mole⟧.
⟦#434⟧
The nominative of stems in ⟦b:-ā-⟧ ends in the shortened stem vowel ⟦b:-a⟧.
⟦#435⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-ā-⟧ are declined as follows:

title: Stems in -ā-: Singular Cases
text:
⟦#436⟧
⟦b:-ā-⟧ of the stem was shortened in the nominative and accusative singular at an early period (⟦r130:130⟧, ⟦r132:132⟧). A few apparent examples of the nominative in ⟦b:-ā⟧, found in the oldest writers, seem due to metrical causes: as, ⟦b:aquilā́⟧ (Enn.). But ⟦b:-ā⟧ occurs in Greek proper names (⟦r445:445⟧). A couple of old masculine nominatives in ⟦b:-ās⟧ are quoted (⟦r422:422⟧): ⟦b:pāricīdās⟧, ⟦i:murderer⟧, and ⟦b:hosticapās⟧, ⟦i:taker of enemies⟧. In the accusative singular ⟦b:-ām⟧ occurs once: ⟦b:inimīcitiā́m⟧ (Enn.).
⟦#437⟧
The genitive sometimes ends (1.) in ⟦b:-āī⟧ in poetry: as, ⟦b:aulāī⟧, ⟦i:of the hall⟧; ⟦b:pīctāī⟧, ⟦i:embroidered⟧; (2.) in ⟦b:-ās⟧: as, ⟦b:molās⟧, ⟦i:of a mill⟧. This genitive is rare, but was always kept up in the word ⟦b:familiās⟧ with ⟦b:pater⟧ or ⟦b:māter⟧, sometimes with ⟦b:fīlius⟧ or ⟦b:fīlia⟧: ⟦b:pater familiās⟧, ⟦i:the goodman⟧, ⟦b:māter familiās⟧, ⟦i:the housewife⟧. But ⟦b:pater familiae⟧, or in the plural ⟦b:patrēs familiārum⟧, is equally common.
⟦#438⟧
Town names and a few appellatives have a locative case in ⟦b:-ae⟧: as, ⟦b:Rōmae⟧, ⟦i:at Rome⟧, ⟦i:in Rome⟧; ⟦b:mīlitiae⟧, ⟦i:in war⟧, ⟦i:in the field⟧, ⟦i:in the army⟧.

title: Stems in -ā-: Plural Cases
text:
⟦#439⟧
Compounds ending with ⟦b:-cola⟧, ⟦i:inhabiting⟧, and ⟦b:-gena⟧, ⟦i:born⟧, and patronymics, sometimes have the genitive plural in ⟦b:-ū̆m⟧ in poetry: as, ⟦b:caelicolū̆m⟧, ⟦i:of occupants of heaven⟧; ⟦b:Graiugenū̆m⟧, ⟦i:of Greek-born men⟧; ⟦b:Aeneadū̆m⟧, ⟦i:of Aeneas’s sons⟧; also names of peoples: as, ⟦b:Lapithū̆m⟧, ⟦i:of the Lapithae⟧. With these last ⟦b:-ū̆m⟧ occurs even in prose: as, ⟦b:Crotōniātū̆m⟧, ⟦i:of the Crotona people⟧. Others in ⟦b:-ŭm⟧ are ⟦b:drachmŭm⟧, ⟦b:amphorū̆m⟧.
⟦#440⟧
In the dative and ablative plural, ⟦b:-eis⟧ sometimes occurs (⟦r443:443⟧): as, ⟦b:tueis ingrātieis⟧, ⟦i:against your will⟧ (Plaut.). Nouns in ⟦b:-ia⟧ have rarely a single ⟦b:ī⟧: as, ⟦b:pecūnīs⟧, ⟦i:by moneys⟧ (Cic.); ⟦b:taenīs⟧, ⟦i:with fillets⟧ (Verg.); ⟦b:nōnīs Iūnīs⟧, ⟦i:on the fifth of June⟧ (Cic.). See ⟦r24:24⟧.
⟦#441⟧
In the dative and ablative plural, words in ⟦b:-āia⟧, or plural ⟦b:-āiae⟧, have ⟦b:-āīs⟧, and those in ⟦b:-ēia⟧ have ⟦b:-ēīs⟧ (⟦r127:127, 7⟧): as KAL. MAIS, ⟦i:on the calends of May⟧ (inscr.); ⟦b:Bāīs⟧, ⟦i:at Bajae⟧ (Hor.); ⟦b:plēbēīs⟧, ⟦i:plebeian⟧.
⟦#442⟧
The dative and ablative plural sometimes end in ⟦b:-ābus⟧, particularly in ⟦b:deābus⟧, ⟦i:goddesses⟧, and ⟦b:fīliābus⟧, ⟦i:daughters⟧, to distinguish them from ⟦b:deīs⟧, ⟦i:gods⟧, and ⟦b:fīliīs⟧, ⟦i:sons⟧. ⟦b:ambae⟧, ⟦i:both⟧, and ⟦b:duae⟧, ⟦i:two⟧, regularly have ⟦b:ambābus⟧ and ⟦b:duābus⟧.
⟦#443⟧
Other case forms are found in inscriptions, as follows:
G. ⟦b:-ai⟧, which may be monosyllabic or disyllabic in pronunciation: PVLCHRAI; LAVERNAI; ⟦b:-āēs⟧, after 80 B.C., chiefly in proper names, mostly Greek: HERAES; rarely in appellatives: DOMINAES; ⟦b:-ēs⟧: MINERVES; ⟦b:-ā⟧, VESTA; COIRA, i.e. ⟦b:Cūrae⟧. D. ⟦b:-ai⟧, in all periods (⟦r96:96⟧): FILIAI; ⟦b:-ā⟧: FORTVNA; ⟦b:-ē⟧ (⟦r96:96⟧): FORTVNE. Ac. ⟦b:-a⟧ (⟦r61:61⟧): TAVRASIA; MAGNA SAPIENTIA. Ab. ⟦b:-ād⟧ (⟦r426:426⟧): PRAIDAD. Loc. ⟦b:-ai⟧: ROMAI. Plural: N. ⟦b:-ai⟧ (⟦r96:96⟧): TABELAI DATAI; ⟦b:-ā⟧, rare: MATRONA; ⟦b:-ē⟧, rare and provincial (⟦r96:96⟧): MVSTE, i.e. ⟦b:mystae⟧. D. and Ab. ⟦b:-eis⟧, very often (⟦r98:98⟧): SCRIBEIS; D. ⟦b:-ās⟧, once: DEVAS CORNISCAS, i.e. ⟦b:dīvīs Cornīscīs⟧. Ab. ⟦b:-ēs⟧ once (⟦r98:98⟧): NVGES, i.e. ⟦b:nūgīs⟧.

title: Stems in -ā-: Greek Nouns
text:
⟦#444⟧
Greek appellatives always take a Latin form in the dative singular and in the plural, and usually throughout: thus, ⟦b:poēta⟧, M., ⟦i:poet⟧, and ⟦b:aula⟧, F., ⟦i:court⟧, are declined like ⟦b:mēnsa⟧. Masculines have sometimes a nominative ⟦b:-ēs⟧ and accusative ⟦b:-ēn⟧: as, ⟦b:anagnōstēs⟧, ⟦i:reader⟧, ⟦b:anagnōstēn⟧; rarely an ablative ⟦b:-ē⟧: as, ⟦b:sophistē⟧, ⟦i:sophist⟧. Greek feminines in ⟦b:-ē⟧ sometimes have Greek forms in late writers: as, N. ⟦b:grammaticē⟧, ⟦i:philology⟧, G. ⟦b:grammaticēs⟧, Ac. ⟦b:grammaticēn⟧, Ab. ⟦b:grammaticē⟧ (Quintil.).
⟦#445⟧
Greek proper names sometimes have the following forms. Nominative masculine ⟦b:-ās⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧: as, ⟦b:Prūsiās⟧, ⟦b:Atrīdēs⟧; feminine ⟦b:-ā⟧: as, ⟦b:Gelā⟧, ⟦b:Phaedrā⟧; ⟦b:-ē⟧: as, ⟦b:Circē⟧. Genitive feminine ⟦b:-ēs⟧: as, ⟦b:Circēs⟧. Accusative masculine ⟦b:-ān⟧, ⟦b:-dēn⟧: as, ⟦b:Aenēān⟧, ⟦b:Pēlīdēn⟧; feminine ⟦b:-ēn⟧: as, ⟦b:Circēn⟧. Ablative feminine ⟦b:-ē⟧: as, ⟦b:Tīsiphonē⟧. Vocative ⟦b:-ā⟧ or ⟦b:-a⟧: as, ⟦b:Atrīdā⟧, ⟦b:Atrīda⟧, ⟦b:Thyesta⟧; ⟦b:-tē⟧: as, ⟦b:Boōtē⟧; ⟦b:-dē⟧: as, ⟦b:Aeacidē⟧.

title: Stems in -o-
text:
⟦=⟧⟦i:The Second Declension.⟧
⟦=⟧Genitive singular ⟦b:-ī⟧, genitive plural ⟦b:-ō-rum⟧.
⟦#446⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-o-⟧ include substantives and adjectives, masculine or neuter.
⟦#447⟧
Most names of plants in ⟦b:-us⟧ are feminine (⟦r407:407⟧); also the following: ⟦b:alvos⟧ or ⟦b:alvus⟧, ⟦i:belly⟧, ⟦b:colus⟧, ⟦i:distaff⟧, ⟦b:domus⟧, ⟦i:house⟧, ⟦b:humus⟧, ⟦i:ground⟧, ⟦b:vannus⟧, ⟦i:fan⟧.
⟦#448⟧
The nominative of masculines ends, including the stem vowel, in ⟦b:-o-s⟧, or usually ⟦b:-u-s⟧; some end in ⟦b:-r⟧; neuters end in ⟦b:-o-m⟧, or usually ⟦b:-u-m⟧.

⟦#450⟧
⟦b:deus⟧, ⟦i:god⟧, is declined as follows: N. ⟦b:deus⟧, G. ⟦b:deī⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:deō⟧, Ac. ⟦b:deum⟧. Plural: N. ⟦b:deī⟧, ⟦b:di͡i⟧, commonly ⟦b:dī⟧, G. ⟦b:deōrum⟧ or ⟦b:deŭm⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:deīs⟧, ⟦b:di͡is⟧, commonly ⟦b:dīs⟧, Ac. ⟦b:deōs⟧.
⟦#451⟧
