title: Stems in -o-: Singular Cases
text:
⟦#452⟧
⟦b:-us⟧ and ⟦b:-um⟧ were originally ⟦b:-os⟧ and ⟦b:-om⟧. But ⟦b:-us⟧ was used in the earliest times, ⟦b:-um⟧ somewhat later, and both became prevalent between 218 and 55 B.C. (107, ⟦i:c⟧). After ⟦b:u⟧ or ⟦b:v⟧, however, the ⟦b:-os⟧ and ⟦b:-om⟧ were retained till toward 50 A.D. (107, ⟦i:c⟧); also after ⟦b:qu⟧; but ⟦b:-cus⟧ and ⟦b:-cum⟧ often displaced ⟦b:-quos⟧ and ⟦b:-quom⟧ (⟦r157:157⟧): as, ⟦b:equos⟧, ⟦b:equom⟧, or ⟦b:ecus⟧, ⟦b:ecum⟧, ⟦i:horse⟧; ⟦b:antīquos⟧, ⟦b:antīquom⟧, or ⟦b:antīcus⟧, ⟦b:antīcum⟧, ⟦i:ancient⟧. In the vocative ⟦b:-e⟧ was always used, and is retained by Plautus in ⟦b:puere⟧, ⟦i:thou boy⟧.
⟦#453⟧
Words in ⟦b:-rus⟧ with a long penult, as, ⟦b:sevērus⟧, ⟦i:stern⟧, and the following substantives with a short penult are declined like ⟦b:domimus⟧ (⟦r449:449⟧):
⟦b:erus⟧, ⟦i:master⟧
⟦b:iūniperus⟧, ⟦i:juniper⟧
⟦b:numerus⟧, ⟦i:number⟧
⟦b:umerus⟧, ⟦i:shoulder⟧
⟦b:uterus⟧, ⟦i:womb⟧
For adjective stems in ⟦b:-ro-⟧ with nominative ⟦b:-rus⟧, see ⟦r615:615⟧.
⟦#454⟧
Masculine stems in ⟦b:-ro-⟧ preceded by a short vowel or a mute, except those above (⟦r453:453⟧), drop ⟦b:-os⟧ in the nominative, and have no vocative: as, stem ⟦b:puero-⟧, N. ⟦b:puer⟧, ⟦i:boy⟧ (111, ⟦i:b⟧). Most masculines in ⟦b:-ro-⟧ have a vowel before ⟦b:r⟧ only in the nominative ⟦b:-er⟧ (111, ⟦i:b⟧): as ⟦b:agro-⟧, N. ⟦b:ager⟧. But in compounds ending in ⟦b:-fer⟧ and ⟦b:-ger⟧, ⟦i:carrying⟧, ⟦i:having⟧, and the following, the vowel before ⟦b:-r⟧ is a part of the stem, and is found in all the cases:
⟦b:adulter⟧, ⟦b:Līber⟧, ⟦i:paramour⟧, ⟦i:Liber⟧
⟦b:gener⟧, ⟦b:socer⟧, ⟦i:son-in-law⟧, ⟦i:father-in-law⟧
⟦b:puer⟧, ⟦b:vir⟧, ⟦i:boy⟧, ⟦i:man⟧
⟦b:līberī⟧, ⟦b:vesper⟧, ⟦i:children⟧, ⟦i:evening⟧
For ⟦b:Mulciber⟧, ⟦b:Hibēr⟧, and ⟦b:Celtibē̆r⟧, see the dictionary; for adjective stems in ⟦b:-ro-⟧ with nominative ⟦b:-r⟧, see ⟦r616:616⟧. Once ⟦b:socerus⟧ (Pl.).
⟦#455⟧
⟦b:nihilum⟧, ⟦i:nothing⟧, usually drops ⟦b:-um⟧ in the nominative and accusative, becoming ⟦b:nihil⟧ or ⟦b:nīl⟧, and similarly ⟦b:nōn⟧, ⟦i:not⟧, may be for ⟦b:noenum⟧, ⟦i:naught⟧ (⟦r99:99⟧). ⟦b:famul⟧ is used for ⟦b:famulus⟧, ⟦i:slave⟧, by Ennius and Lucretius, once each (111, ⟦i:b⟧).
⟦#456⟧
Substantives ending in ⟦b:-ius⟧ or ⟦b:-ium⟧ (but never adjectives), have commonly a single ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the genitive singular: as,
⟦b:Vergilius⟧, G. ⟦b:Vergílī⟧ (⟦r87:87⟧); ⟦b:fīlius⟧, ⟦i:son⟧, G. ⟦b:fīlī⟧; ⟦b:cōnūbium⟧, ⟦i:marriage⟧, G. ⟦b:cōnūbī⟧.
⟦#457⟧
Vergil has once a genitive ⟦b:-iī⟧, ⟦b:fluviī⟧, ⟦i:river’s⟧. Propertius has ⟦b:-iī⟧ two or three times; with Ovid, Seneca, and later writers, ⟦b:-iī⟧ is common: as, ⟦b:gladiī⟧, ⟦i:of a sword⟧; even in proper names, which were the last to take ⟦b:-iī⟧: as, ⟦b:Tarquiniī⟧; but family names almost always retain a single ⟦b:-ī⟧. Locatives have ⟦b:-iī⟧: as, ⟦b:Iconiī⟧ (Cic.).
⟦#458⟧
Proper names ending in ⟦b:-āius⟧, ⟦b:-ēius⟧, or ⟦b:-ōius⟧ have ⟦b:-āī⟧, ⟦b:-ēī⟧, or ⟦b:-ōī⟧ in the genitive and vocative singular and nominative plural, and ⟦b:-āīs⟧, ⟦b:-ēīs⟧, or ⟦b:-ōīs⟧ in the dative and ablative plural (⟦r127:127, 7⟧): as,
⟦b:Gāius⟧, G., V., and N. Pl. ⟦b:Gāī⟧, D. and Ab. Pl. ⟦b:Gāīs⟧; ⟦b:Pompēī⟧, ⟦b:Pompēīs⟧; ⟦b:Bōī⟧, ⟦b:Bōīs⟧. In verse ⟦b:-ēī⟧ of the vocative is sometimes made one syllable (⟦r120:120⟧): as, ⟦b:Pompe͡i⟧; ⟦b:Volte͡i⟧ (Hor.).
⟦#459⟧
Latin proper names in ⟦b:-ius⟧ have the vocative in ⟦b:-ī⟧ only: as,
⟦b:Vergilius⟧, V. ⟦b:Vergílī⟧; ⟦b:Mercurius⟧, V. ⟦b:Mercúrī⟧ (⟦r87:87⟧). So, also, ⟦b:fīlius⟧, ⟦b:fīlī⟧, ⟦i:son⟧; ⟦b:genius⟧, ⟦b:genī⟧, ⟦i:good angel⟧; ⟦b:volturius⟧, ⟦b:volturī⟧, ⟦i:vulture⟧; ⟦b:meus⟧, ⟦b:mī⟧, ⟦i:my⟧.
⟦#460⟧
Town names and a few appellatives have a locative case in ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:Ephesī⟧, ⟦i:in Ephesus⟧; ⟦b:humī⟧, ⟦i:on the ground⟧; ⟦b:bellī⟧, ⟦i:in war⟧.

title: Stems in -o-: Plural Cases
text:
⟦#461⟧
In the nominative plural masculine, ⟦b:-ei⟧ sometimes occurs (⟦r465:465⟧): as, ⟦b:nātei geminei⟧, ⟦i:twins born⟧ (Plaut.); ⟦b:-eis⟧ or ⟦b:-īs⟧ is rare (⟦r465:465⟧): as, ⟦b:Sardeis⟧, ⟦i:Sardians⟧; ⟦b:oculīs⟧, ⟦i:eyes⟧; not infrequently ⟦b:hīsce⟧, ⟦i:these here⟧ (Plaut.); masculine stems in ⟦b:-io-⟧ have rarely a single ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:fīlī⟧, ⟦i:sons⟧. For ⟦b:-āī⟧, ⟦b:-ēī⟧, or ⟦b:-ōī⟧, see ⟦r458:458⟧. The nominative and accusative plural of neuters ended anciently in ⟦b:-ā⟧ (⟦r130:130, 2⟧). But ⟦b:-ā⟧ was shortened at an early period.
⟦#462⟧
In the common genitive plural ⟦b:-ōrum⟧, the ⟦b:-o-⟧ of the stem is lengthened (⟦r123:123⟧). A genitive plural in ⟦b:-ū̆m⟧ (or, after ⟦b:v⟧, in ⟦b:-ŏ̄m⟧) is common from ⟦b:dīvos⟧, ⟦b:dīvus⟧, and ⟦b:deus⟧, ⟦i:god⟧; from ⟦b:dēnārius⟧, ⟦i:denar⟧, ⟦b:modius⟧, ⟦i:peck⟧, ⟦b:nummus⟧, ⟦i:money⟧, ⟦b:sēstertius⟧, ⟦i:sesterce⟧, and ⟦b:talentum⟧, ⟦i:talent⟧, with numerals; and from cardinals and distributives (⟦r641:641⟧): as, ⟦b:dīvŏ̄m⟧, ⟦b:divū̆m⟧, ⟦b:deū̆m⟧; ⟦b:mīlle sēstertiŭm⟧; ⟦b:ducentū̆m⟧; ⟦b:bīnŭm⟧. The ⟦b:u⟧ was originally long (⟦r132:132⟧); but it was shortened before 100 A.D.
⟦#463⟧
Other masculine substantives have occasionally this genitive: as, ⟦b:līberū̆m⟧, ⟦i:of children⟧; particularly in set phrases and in verse: as, ⟦b:centuria fabrū̆m⟧, ⟦i:century of mechanics⟧; ⟦b:Graiū̆m⟧, ⟦i:of Greeks⟧. With neuter substantives, as ⟦b:oppidū̆m⟧, for ⟦b:oppidōrum⟧, ⟦i:of towns⟧, and with adjectives it is rare.
⟦#464⟧
In the dative and ablative plural, ⟦b:-eis⟧ is rare (⟦r98:98⟧): as, ⟦b:Epidamnieis⟧ (Plaut.). Stems in ⟦b:-io-⟧ have rarely a single ⟦b:ī⟧: as, ⟦b:fīlīs⟧, ⟦i:for sons⟧. For ⟦b:-āīs⟧, ⟦b:-ēīs⟧, or ⟦b:-ōīs⟧, see ⟦r458:458⟧. ⟦b:ambō⟧, ⟦i:both⟧, and ⟦b:duo⟧, ⟦i:two⟧, have ⟦b:ambōbus⟧ and ⟦b:duōbus⟧ (⟦r640:640⟧).
⟦#465⟧
Other case forms are found in inscriptions as follows:
N. ⟦b:-os⟧, ⟦b:-om⟧, with ⟦b:o⟧ retained (107, ⟦i:c⟧): FILIOS, TRIBVNOS; POCOLOM; in proper names ⟦b:-o⟧ (⟦r66:66⟧): CORNELIO; ⟦b:-u⟧, rare: LECTV; ⟦b:-is⟧, or ⟦b:-i⟧, for ⟦b:-ius⟧ (⟦r135:135, 2⟧): CAECILIS; CLAVDI; neuter ⟦b:-o⟧ (⟦r61:61⟧): POCOLO. G. oldest form ⟦b:-ī⟧: VRBANI; ⟦b:-ei⟧, from 146 B.C. to Augustus: POPVLEI; CONLEGEI; ⟦b:-iī⟧ from stems in ⟦b:-io-⟧ not before Tiberius: COLLEGII. Ac. ⟦b:-om⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧): VOLCANOM; ⟦b:-o⟧ (⟦r61:61⟧): OPTVMO VIRO; ⟦b:-u⟧: GREMIV. Ab. ⟦b:-od⟧, not after 186 B.C. (⟦r426:426⟧): POPLICOD, PREIVATOD. Plural: N. ⟦b:-ei⟧, always common (⟦r98:98⟧): VIREI; FILEI; -ēs, ⟦b:-eis⟧, ⟦b:-īs⟧ (⟦r461:461⟧): ATILIES; COQVES; LEIBEREIS, i.e. ⟦b:līnerī⟧; MAGISTREIS; MAGISTRIS; ⟦b:-ē⟧, rare: PLOIRVME, i.e. ⟦b:plūrumī⟧. G. ⟦b:-ōm⟧ or ⟦b:-ō⟧ (⟦r61:61⟧) ROMANOM; ROMANO; ⟦b:-ōro⟧ (⟦r61:61⟧): DVONORO. D. and Ab. ⟦b:-eis⟧, the only form down to about 130 B.C. (⟦r98:98⟧): ANTIQVEIS; PROXSVMEIS; ⟦b:-ēs⟧, twice: CAVATVRINES.

title: Stems in -o-: Greek Nouns
text:
⟦#466⟧
Greek stems in ⟦b:-o-⟧ are generally declined like Latin nouns, but in the singular sometimes have ⟦b:-os⟧ in the nominative, ⟦b:-on⟧ in the nominative or accusative neuter, rarely ⟦b:-ū⟧ in the genitive, or ⟦b:-ō⟧ in the feminine ablative. Plural, nominative sometimes ⟦b:-oe⟧, masculine or feminine, and genitive, chiefly in book-titles, ⟦b:-ōn⟧: as,
Nominative ⟦b:Īlios⟧; ⟦b:Īlion⟧ or ⟦b:Īlium⟧. Genitive ⟦b:Menandrū⟧, ⟦i:of Menander⟧. Ablative feminine adjective ⟦b:lectīcā octōphorō⟧, ⟦i:in a sedan with eight bearers⟧. Plural: nominative ⟦b:Adelphoe⟧, ⟦i:the Brothers⟧; ⟦b:canēphoroe⟧, ⟦i:basket-bearers⟧, feminine. Genitive ⟦b:Geōrgicōn liber⟧, ⟦i:book of Husbandry⟧. For ⟦b:Androgeōs⟧, ⟦b:Athŏ̄s⟧ and ⟦b:Panthūs⟧, see the dictionary.

title: Consonant Stems
text:
⟦=⟧⟦i:The Third Declension.⟧
⟦=⟧Genitive singular ⟦b:-is⟧, genitive plural ⟦b:-um⟧.
⟦#467⟧
Consonant stems are mostly substantive, and include both gender words and neuters.
Comparatives and a few other words are adjective. For the gender of substantives, see ⟦r570:570⟧.
⟦#468⟧
The nominative of consonant stems ends in ⟦b:-s⟧ (or ⟦b:-x⟧); or in ⟦b:-n⟧ (⟦b:-ō⟧), ⟦b:-l⟧, ⟦b:-r⟧, or ⟦b:-s⟧ of the stem, rarely in ⟦b:-c⟧ or ⟦b:-t⟧.
⟦#469⟧
Most consonant stems have one syllable less in the nominative than in the genitive.
Such words are called ⟦i:Imparisyllabic⟧ words or ⟦i:Imparisyllables⟧: as, nominative ⟦b:rēx⟧, ⟦i:king⟧, one syllable; genitive ⟦b:rēgis⟧, ⟦i:of a king⟧, two syllables.
⟦#470⟧
Many consonant stems have a double form: one form used in the nominative singular (neuters have this form in the accusative also), another form in the other cases: as,
⟦b:iūdex⟧, ⟦i:juror⟧, stem of nominative ⟦b:iūdec-⟧ (⟦r136:136, 2⟧), of other cases ⟦b:iūdic-⟧; ⟦b:flāmen⟧ (103, ⟦i:a⟧), ⟦i:special priest⟧, ⟦b:flāmin-⟧ (103, ⟦i:a⟧); ⟦b:virgō⟧, ⟦i:maid⟧, ⟦b:virgin-⟧ (105, ⟦i:g⟧); ⟦b:auceps⟧ (107, ⟦i:d⟧), ⟦i:fowler⟧, ⟦b:aucup-⟧ (104, ⟦i:c⟧); ⟦b:ebur⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧), ⟦i:ivory⟧, ⟦b:ebor-⟧; ⟦b:genus⟧, ⟦i:race⟧, ⟦b:gener-⟧ (⟦r145:145⟧; 107, ⟦i:c⟧); ⟦b:trīstius⟧ (⟦r346:346⟧), ⟦i:sadder⟧, ⟦b:trīstiōr-⟧ (⟦r346:346⟧); ⟦b:corpus⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧), ⟦i:body⟧, ⟦b:corpor-⟧ (105, ⟦i:i⟧); ⟦b:pater⟧ (⟦r135:135, 2⟧), ⟦i:father⟧, ⟦b:patr-⟧. In such instances the stem of the oblique cases is taken for brevity to represent both forms of the stem.

title: Mute Stems
text:
⟦#471⟧
(1.) Stems in a guttural mute, ⟦b:-g-⟧ or ⟦b:-c-⟧, are declined as follows:
Examples
Stems ⟦b:rēx⟧, ⟦i:king⟧,

Singular

⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:rēgis⟧, ⟦i:a king’s⟧, ⟦i:of a king⟧  ⟦b:ducis⟧  ⟦b:iūdicis⟧  ⟦b:-is⟧

endings
In the nominative and accusative, neuters have no case ending in the singular, and ⟦b:-a⟧ in the plural. In the other cases they have the same case endings as gender stems.
⟦#472⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-g-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-x⟧, genitive ⟦b:-gis⟧, are:
⟦b:-ex⟧, ⟦b:-egis⟧  ⟦b:grex⟧, M., (F.), ⟦i:herd⟧; ⟦b:aquilex⟧, M., ⟦i:spring-hunter⟧, ⟦i:hydraulic engineer⟧.
⟦b:-ēx⟧, ⟦b:-ēgis⟧  ⟦b:rēx⟧, M., ⟦i:king⟧; ⟦b:interrēx⟧, ⟦i:regent⟧; ⟦b:lēx⟧, F., ⟦i:law⟧; and N. and Ac. ⟦b:exlēx⟧, ⟦b:exlēgem⟧, ⟦i:beyond the law⟧, adjective.
⟦b:-ex⟧, ⟦b:-igis⟧  ⟦b:rēmex⟧, M., ⟦i:oarsman⟧.
⟦b:-ī̆x⟧, ⟦b:-ī̆gis⟧  ⟦b:strī̆x⟧, F., ⟦i:screech-owl⟧.
⟦b:-ūnx⟧, ⟦b:-ūgis⟧  ⟦b:coniūnx⟧ (122, ⟦i:e⟧) or ⟦b:coniux⟧, M., F., ⟦i:spouse⟧.
⟦b:-ūx⟧, ⟦b:-ūgis⟧  ⟦b:frūx⟧, F., ⟦i:fruit⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#473⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-c-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-x⟧, genitive ⟦b:-cis⟧, are:
⟦b:-ax⟧, ⟦b:-acis⟧  ⟦b:fax⟧, F., ⟦i:torch⟧, no G. Pl. in good writers (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-āx⟧, ⟦b:-ācis⟧  ⟦b:pāx⟧, F., ⟦i:peace⟧, Pl. only N. and Ac. ⟦b:pācēs⟧; ⟦b:līmāx⟧, F., ⟦i:snail⟧.
⟦b:-ex⟧, ⟦b:-ecis⟧  ⟦b:faenisex⟧, M., ⟦i:haycutter⟧; ⟦b:nex⟧, F., ⟦i:murder⟧; ⟦b:precī⟧, D., F., ⟦i:prayer⟧, no N., usually plural.
⟦b:-ēx⟧, ⟦b:-ēcis⟧  ⟦b:vervēx⟧, M., ⟦i:wether⟧; ⟦b:allēx⟧, F., ⟦i:fish-pickle⟧, also ⟦b:allēc⟧, Ne.
⟦b:-ex⟧, ⟦b:-icis⟧  Masculines mostly: ⟦b:apex⟧, ⟦i:point⟧; ⟦b:cārex⟧, F., ⟦i:rush⟧; ⟦b:caudex⟧ or ⟦b:cōdex⟧, ⟦i:block⟧, ⟦i:book⟧; ⟦b:cīmex⟧, ⟦i:bug⟧; ⟦b:cortex⟧, M., F., ⟦i:bark⟧; ⟦b:culex⟧, ⟦i:gnat⟧; ⟦b:forfex⟧, M., F., ⟦i:shears⟧; ⟦b:frutex⟧, ⟦i:shrub⟧; ⟦b:īlex⟧, F., ⟦i:holm-oak⟧; ⟦b:illex⟧, M., F., ⟦i:seducer⟧; ⟦b:imbrex⟧, ⟦i:tile⟧; ⟦b:latex⟧, ⟦i:fluid⟧; ⟦b:mūrex⟧, ⟦i:purple-shell⟧; ⟦b:obice⟧, Ab., M., F., ⟦i:bar⟧, no N.; ⟦b:paelex⟧, F., ⟦i:concubine⟧, ⟦b:pollex⟧, ⟦i:thumb⟧; ⟦b:pūlex⟧, ⟦i:flea⟧; ⟦b:pūmex⟧, ⟦i:pumice-slone⟧; ⟦b:rāmex⟧, ⟦i:blood-vessel⟧; ⟦b:rumex⟧, ⟦i:sorrel⟧; ⟦b:silex⟧, M., F., ⟦i:flint⟧; ⟦b:sōrex⟧, ⟦i:shrew-mouse⟧; ⟦b:vortex⟧ or ⟦b:vertex⟧, ⟦i:whirl⟧; ⟦b:vītex⟧, F., ⟦i:a shrub⟧. Also some compounds: as, ⟦b:iūdex⟧, ⟦i:juror⟧; ⟦b:artifex⟧, ⟦i:artisan⟧; ⟦b:auspex⟧, ⟦i:bird-viewer⟧.

Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧); ⟦b:salix⟧, ⟦i:willow⟧; ⟦b:vārix⟧, ⟦i:swollen vein⟧; ⟦b:vicis⟧, G., ⟦i:change⟧, no N., D., or G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-īx⟧, ⟦b:-īcis⟧  Feminines: ⟦b:cervīx⟧, ⟦i:neck⟧; ⟦b:cicātrīx⟧, ⟦i:scar⟧; ⟦b:cornīx⟧, ⟦i:crow⟧; ⟦b:cŏ̄turnīx⟧ (⟦r62:62⟧), ⟦i:quail⟧; ⟦b:lōdīx⟧, ⟦i:blanket⟧; ⟦b:rādīx⟧, ⟦i:root⟧; ⟦b:struīx⟧, ⟦i:heap⟧. Also ⟦b:coxendīx⟧, ⟦i:hip⟧, later ⟦b:coxendix⟧, ⟦b:coxendicis⟧.
⟦b:-ōx⟧, ⟦b:-ōcis⟧  ⟦b:vōx⟧, F., ⟦i:voice⟧.
⟦b:-ux⟧, ⟦b:-ucis⟧  ⟦b:crux⟧, F., ⟦i:cross⟧; ⟦b:dux⟧, M., F., ⟦i:leader⟧; ⟦b:nux⟧, F., ⟦i:nut-tree⟧, ⟦i:nut⟧; ⟦b:trādux⟧, M., ⟦i:vinelayer⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#474⟧
(2.) Stems in a dental mute, ⟦b:-d-⟧ or ⟦b:-t-⟧, are declined as follows:
Examples  ⟦b:custōs⟧, ⟦i:keeper⟧, ⟦b:custōd-⟧, M.  ⟦b:aetās⟧, ⟦i:age⟧, ⟦b:aetāt-⟧, F.  ⟦b:virtūs⟧, ⟦i:virtue⟧, ⟦b:virtūt-⟧, F.  ⟦b:mīles⟧, ⟦i:soldier⟧, ⟦b:mīlit-⟧, M.

⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:custōdem⟧  ⟦b:aetātem⟧  ⟦b:virtūtem⟧  ⟦b:mīlitem⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:custōde⟧  ⟦b:aetāte⟧  ⟦b:virtūte⟧  ⟦b:mīlite⟧
Plural
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:custōdēs⟧  ⟦b:aetātēs⟧  ⟦b:virtūtēs⟧  ⟦b:mīlitēs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:custōdum⟧  ⟦b:aetātum⟧  ⟦b:virtūtum⟧  ⟦b:mīlitum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:custōdibus⟧  ⟦b:aetātibus⟧  ⟦b:virtūtibus⟧  ⟦b:mīlitibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:custōdēs⟧  ⟦b:aetātēs⟧  ⟦b:virtūtēs⟧  ⟦b:mīlitēs⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:custōdibus⟧  ⟦b:aetātibus⟧  ⟦b:virtūtibus⟧  ⟦b:mīlitibus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#475⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-d-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-s⟧, genitive ⟦b:-dis⟧, are:
⟦b:-as⟧, ⟦b:-adis⟧  ⟦b:vas⟧, M., F., ⟦i:personal surety⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-aes⟧, ⟦b:-aedis⟧  ⟦b:praes⟧, M., ⟦i:bondsman⟧.
⟦b:-es⟧, ⟦b:-idis⟧  ⟦b:obses⟧, M., F., ⟦i:hostage⟧; ⟦b:praeses⟧, M., F., ⟦i:overseer⟧. ⟦b:*dēses⟧, ⟦i:slothful⟧, adjective.
⟦b:-ēs⟧, ⟦b:-edis⟧  ⟦b:pēs⟧, M., ⟦i:foot⟧.
⟦b:-ēs⟧, ⟦b:-ēdis⟧  ⟦b:hērēs⟧, M., F., ⟦i:heir⟧; ⟦b:exhērēs⟧, ⟦i:disinherited⟧, adjective; ⟦b:mercēs⟧, F., ⟦i:reward⟧.
⟦b:-is⟧, ⟦b:-idis⟧  Feminines: ⟦b:capis⟧, ⟦i:cup⟧; ⟦b:cassis⟧, ⟦i:helmet⟧; ⟦b:cuspis⟧, ⟦i:spear-point⟧; ⟦b:prōmulsis⟧, ⟦i:appetizer⟧; ⟦b:lapis⟧, M., ⟦i:stone⟧.
⟦b:-ōs⟧, ⟦b:-ōdis⟧  ⟦b:custōs⟧, M., F., ⟦i:guard⟧.
⟦b:-aus⟧, ⟦b:-audis⟧  ⟦b:laus⟧, F., ⟦i:praise⟧.
⟦b:-us⟧, ⟦b:-udis⟧  ⟦b:pecus⟧, F., ⟦i:beast⟧, ⟦i:head of cattle⟧.
⟦b:-ūs⟧, ⟦b:-ūdis⟧  Feminines: ⟦b:incūs⟧, ⟦i:anvil⟧; ⟦b:palūs⟧, ⟦i:swamp⟧, nominative once in Horace ⟦b:palus⟧, as from an ⟦b:-o-⟧ stem; ⟦b:subscūs⟧, ⟦i:dovetail⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#476⟧
⟦b:sēdēs⟧, F., ⟦i:seat⟧, has an ⟦b:-s-⟧ stem, namely ⟦b:-ēs⟧ (⟦r236:236⟧), in the nominative, and ⟦b:sēd-⟧ in the other cases (⟦r401:401⟧); G. Pl. ⟦b:sēdum⟧, once ⟦b:sēdium⟧ (Vell. Pat.). The only example of a neuter stem in ⟦b:-d-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-r⟧, genitive ⟦b:-dis⟧, is ⟦b:cor⟧ (⟦r171:171, 2⟧), ⟦i:heart⟧, ⟦b:cordis⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦#477⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-t-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-s⟧, genitive ⟦b:-tis⟧, are:
⟦b:-as⟧, ⟦b:-atis⟧  ⟦b:anas⟧, F., ⟦i:duck⟧; G. Pl. also ⟦b:anitum⟧ (Cic.), and Ac. Pl. ⟦b:anitēs⟧ (Plaut.).
⟦b:-ās⟧, ⟦b:-ātis⟧  ⟦b:aetās⟧, F., ⟦i:age⟧; also numerous other feminines in ⟦b:-tās⟧ (⟦r262:262⟧).
⟦b:-es⟧, ⟦b:-etis⟧  ⟦b:interpres⟧, M., F., ⟦i:go-between⟧; ⟦b:seges⟧, F., ⟦i:crop⟧; ⟦b:teges⟧, F., ⟦i:mat.⟧
⟦b:-es⟧, ⟦b:-itis⟧  Masculines mostly: ⟦b:ames⟧, ⟦i:net-pole⟧; ⟦b:antistes⟧, M., F., ⟦i:overseer⟧; ⟦b:caespes⟧, ⟦i:sod⟧; ⟦b:comes⟧, M., F., ⟦i:companion⟧; ⟦b:eques⟧, ⟦i:horseman⟧; ⟦b:fōmes⟧, ⟦i:tinder⟧; ⟦b:gurges⟧, ⟦i:whirlpool⟧; ⟦b:hospes⟧, M., F., ⟦i:guest-friend⟧; ⟦b:līmes⟧, ⟦i:path⟧; ⟦b:merges⟧, F., ⟦i:sheaf⟧; ⟦b:mīles⟧, M., F., ⟦i:soldier⟧; ⟦b:palmes⟧, ⟦i:vine-sprout⟧; ⟦b:pedes⟧, ⟦i:man afoot⟧, ⟦i:infantry⟧; ⟦b:poples⟧, ⟦i:hough⟧; ⟦b:stīpes⟧, ⟦i:trunk⟧; ⟦b:termes⟧, ⟦i:bough⟧; ⟦b:trāmes⟧, ⟦i:by-path⟧; ⟦b:dīves⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧; ⟦b:sōspes⟧, ⟦i:safe⟧; ⟦b:superstes⟧, ⟦i:surviving⟧; ⟦b:caelite⟧, Ab., ⟦i:occupant of heaven⟧, no N., adjectives.
⟦b:-ēs⟧, ⟦b:-etis⟧  ⟦b:abiēs⟧, F., ⟦i:fir⟧; ⟦b:ariēs⟧, M., ⟦i:ram⟧; ⟦b:pariēs⟧, M., ⟦i:wall⟧.
⟦b:-ēs⟧, ⟦b:-ētis⟧  Feminines: ⟦b:quiēs⟧ and ⟦b:requiēs⟧, ⟦i:rest⟧, no D., Ac. often ⟦b:requiem⟧, Ab. usually ⟦b:requiē⟧ (⟦r603:603⟧); ⟦b:inquiēs⟧, ⟦i:unrest⟧, N. only.
⟦b:-os⟧, ⟦b:-otis⟧  ⟦b:compos⟧, ⟦i:master of⟧, adjective.
⟦b:-ōs⟧, ⟦b:-ōtis⟧  ⟦b:nepōs⟧, M., ⟦i:grandson⟧, ⟦i:profligate⟧; ⟦b:sacerdōs⟧, M., ⟦i:priest⟧; ⟦b:cōs⟧, F., ⟦i:whetstone⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r130:130⟧); ⟦b:dōs⟧, F., ⟦i:dowry⟧, no G. Pl. in good writers (⟦r430:430⟧); ⟦b:dōtum⟧ once (Val. Max.), and ⟦b:dōtium⟧ in the jurists.
⟦b:-ūs⟧, ⟦b:-ūtis⟧  Feminines: ⟦b:iuventūs⟧, ⟦i:youth⟧; ⟦b:salūs⟧, ⟦i:existence⟧; ⟦b:senectūs⟧, ⟦i:old age⟧; ⟦b:servitūs⟧, ⟦i:slavery⟧, all singular only; and ⟦b:virtūs⟧, ⟦i:virtue⟧, with a plural.
⟦/⟧
⟦#478⟧
⟦b:vātēs⟧, ⟦i:bard⟧, has an ⟦b:-s-⟧ stem, namely ⟦b:-ēs⟧ (⟦r236:236⟧), in the nominative, and ⟦b:vāt-⟧ in the other cases (⟦r401:401⟧); G. Pl. ⟦b:vātum⟧, but thrice ⟦b:vātium⟧ (Cic.). The only example of a neuter stem in ⟦b:-t-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-t⟧, genitive ⟦b:-tis⟧, is ⟦b:caput⟧, ⟦i:head⟧, ⟦b:capitis⟧, and its compounds ⟦b:occiput⟧, ⟦i:back of the head⟧ and ⟦b:sinciput⟧, ⟦i:jole⟧. ⟦b:lac⟧, Ne., ⟦i:milk⟧, ⟦b:lactis⟧, has in old and late Latin nominative and accusative ⟦b:lacte⟧, ⟦b:lact⟧ once in Varro (⟦r171:171, 2⟧); acc. ⟦b:lactem⟧ occurs in Petronius once and later.
⟦#479⟧
(3.) Stems in a labial mute, ⟦b:-b-⟧ or ⟦b:-p-⟧, are declined as follows:
⟦b:mūniceps⟧, ⟦i:burgess⟧, stem ⟦b:mūnicip-⟧, M., F.
Singular: N. ⟦b:mūniceps⟧, G. ⟦b:mūnicipis⟧, D. ⟦b:mūnicipī⟧, Ac. ⟦b:mūnicipem⟧, Ab. ⟦b:mūnicipe⟧. Plural: N. ⟦b:mūnicipēs⟧, G. ⟦b:mūnicipum⟧, D. ⟦b:mūnicipibus⟧, Ac. ⟦b:mūnicipēs⟧, Ab. ⟦b:mūnicipibus⟧.
⟦#480⟧
Examples of stems in ⟦b:-b-⟧ or ⟦b:-p-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-s⟧, genitive ⟦b:-bis⟧ or ⟦b:-pis⟧, are:
⟦b:-ebs⟧, ⟦b:-ibis⟧  ⟦b:caelebs⟧, ⟦i:unmarried⟧, adjective, the only stem in ⟦b:-b-⟧.
⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:-apis⟧  ⟦b:dapis⟧, G., F., ⟦i:feast⟧, N. and D. S., and G. Pl. not used (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-eps⟧, ⟦b:-ipis⟧  ⟦b:adeps⟧ or ⟦b:adips⟧, M., F., ⟦i:fat⟧, no G. Pl; ⟦b:forceps⟧, M., F., ⟦i:pincers⟧; ⟦b:mūniceps⟧, ⟦i:burgher⟧. ⟦b:particeps⟧, ⟦i:sharing⟧, and ⟦b:prīnceps⟧, ⟦i:first⟧, adjectives.
⟦b:-eps⟧, ⟦b:-upis⟧  ⟦b:auceps⟧, ⟦i:fowler⟧; ⟦b:manceps⟧, ⟦i:contractor⟧, ⟦b:mancupis⟧ or ⟦b:mancipis⟧.
⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:-ipis⟧  ⟦b:stipis⟧, G., F., ⟦i:small change⟧, no N.
⟦b:-ops⟧, ⟦b:-opis⟧  ⟦b:Ops⟧, F., old ⟦b:Opis⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦i:goddess of power⟧; ⟦b:opis⟧, G., F., ⟦i:help⟧, no N., D. once only, Pl. ⟦b:opēs⟧, ⟦i:means⟧ (⟦r418:418⟧).
⟦/⟧

title: Stems in a Continuous Consonant
text:
⟦#481⟧
(1.) Stems in ⟦b:-l-⟧ and ⟦b:-n-⟧ are declined as follows:
Examples
Stems ⟦b:cōnsul⟧, ⟦i:consul⟧,
⟦b:cōnsul-⟧, M. ⟦b:leō⟧, ⟦i:lion⟧,
⟦b:leōn-⟧, M. ⟦b:imāgō⟧, ⟦i:likeness⟧,
⟦b:imāgin-⟧, F. ⟦b:nōmen⟧, ⟦i:name⟧,
Singular
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsul⟧  ⟦b:leō⟧  ⟦b:imāgō⟧  ⟦b:nōmen⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsulis⟧  ⟦b:leōnis⟧  ⟦b:imāginis⟧  ⟦b:nōminis⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsulī⟧  ⟦b:leōnī⟧  ⟦b:imāginī⟧  ⟦b:nōminī⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsulem⟧  ⟦b:leōnem⟧  ⟦b:imāginem⟧  ⟦b:nōmen⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsule⟧  ⟦b:leōne⟧  ⟦b:imāgine⟧  ⟦b:nōmine⟧
Plural
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsulēs⟧  ⟦b:leōnēs⟧  ⟦b:imāginēs⟧  ⟦b:nōmina⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsulum⟧  ⟦b:leōnum⟧  ⟦b:imāginum⟧  ⟦b:nōminum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsulibus⟧  ⟦b:leōnibus⟧  ⟦b:imāginibus⟧  ⟦b:nōminibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsulēs⟧  ⟦b:leōnēs⟧  ⟦b:imāginēs⟧  ⟦b:nōmina⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:cōnsulibus⟧  ⟦b:leōnibus⟧  ⟦b:imāginibus⟧  ⟦b:nōminibus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:nōmin-⟧, Ne.
⟦#482⟧
Examples of stems in ⟦b:-l-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-l⟧, genitive ⟦b:-lis⟧, are:
⟦b:-āl⟧, ⟦b:-alis⟧  ⟦b:sāl⟧, M., ⟦i:salt⟧, sometimes Ne. in the singular; no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-el⟧, ⟦b:-ellis⟧  ⟦b:fel⟧ (⟦r171:171⟧, ⟦r1:1⟧), Ne., ⟦i:gall⟧; ⟦b:mel⟧, Ne., ⟦i:honey⟧; plural only ⟦b:fella⟧, ⟦b:mella⟧.
⟦b:-il⟧, ⟦b:-ilis⟧  ⟦b:mūgil⟧, M., ⟦i:mullet⟧; ⟦b:pūgil⟧, M., ⟦i:boxer⟧; ⟦b:vigil⟧, M., ⟦i:watchman⟧.
⟦b:-ōl⟧, ⟦b:-ōlis⟧  ⟦b:sōl⟧, M., ⟦i:sun⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-ul⟧, ⟦b:-ulis⟧  ⟦b:cōnsul⟧, ⟦i:consul⟧; ⟦b:praesul⟧, ⟦i:head dancer⟧; ⟦b:exsul⟧, ⟦i:exile⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#483⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-n-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-en⟧, genitive ⟦b:-inis⟧, are:
⟦b:flāmen⟧, M., ⟦i:priest⟧; ⟦b:pecten⟧, M., ⟦i:comb⟧; ⟦b:tībīcen⟧, M., ⟦i:piper⟧; ⟦b:tubicen⟧, M., ⟦i:trumpeter⟧; ⟦b:sanguen⟧, Ne., ⟦i:blood⟧. Many neuters in ⟦b:-men⟧ (⟦r224:224⟧): as, ⟦b:certāmen⟧, ⟦i:contest⟧.
⟦#484⟧
(b.) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-n-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-ō⟧, genitive ⟦b:-ōnis⟧, are:
Many masculine concretes: as, ⟦b:pugiō⟧, ⟦i:dagger⟧; words of the agent (⟦r211:211⟧): as, ⟦b:praedō⟧, ⟦i:robber⟧; and family names: as, ⟦b:Cicerō⟧. Feminine abstracts in ⟦b:-iō⟧ (⟦r227:227⟧), and many in ⟦b:-tiō⟧ or ⟦b:-siō⟧ (⟦r228:228⟧): as, ⟦b:opīniō⟧, ⟦i:notion⟧; ⟦b:cōgitātiō⟧, ⟦i:thought⟧.
⟦#485⟧
(c.) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-n-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-ō⟧, genitive ⟦b:-inis⟧, are:
Masculines: ⟦b:Apollō⟧; ⟦b:cardō⟧, ⟦i:hinge⟧; ⟦b:ōrdō⟧, ⟦i:rank⟧; ⟦b:turbō⟧, ⟦i:whirlwind⟧. ⟦b:homo⟧, M., F., ⟦i:human being⟧; ⟦b:nēmō⟧, ⟦i:nobody⟧; for G. and Ab., ⟦b:nūllī̆us⟧ and ⟦b:nūllō⟧ are generally used; ⟦b:margō⟧, M., F., ⟦i:brink⟧. Feminines: ⟦b:grandō⟧, ⟦i:hail⟧; ⟦b:harundō⟧, ⟦i:reed⟧; ⟦b:hirundō⟧, ⟦i:swallow⟧; ⟦b:hirūdō⟧, ⟦i:leech⟧; ⟦b:testūdō⟧, ⟦i:tortoise⟧; ⟦b:virgō⟧, ⟦i:maiden⟧. Many in ⟦b:-dō⟧, ⟦b:-dinis⟧ (⟦r225:225⟧), ⟦b:-gō⟧, ⟦b:-ginis⟧ (⟦r226:226⟧), and ⟦b:-tūdō⟧, ⟦b:-tūdinis⟧ (⟦r264:264⟧): as, ⟦b:cupīdō⟧, also M., ⟦i:desire⟧; ⟦b:imāgō⟧, ⟦i:likeness⟧; ⟦b:sōlitūdō⟧, ⟦i:loneliness⟧.
⟦#486⟧
⟦b:sanguī̆s⟧, M., ⟦i:blood⟧, stem ⟦b:sanguin-⟧, takes ⟦b:-s⟧ in the nominative (⟦r171:171, 4⟧). ⟦b:canis⟧, M., F., ⟦i:dog⟧, stem ⟦b:can-⟧, and ⟦b:īuvenis⟧, M., F., ⟦i:young person⟧, stem ⟦b:iuven-⟧, have the nominative formed like that of ⟦b:-i-⟧ stems. For ⟦b:senex⟧, ⟦i:old man⟧, see ⟦r500:500⟧.
⟦#487⟧
(2.) Stems in ⟦b:-r-⟧ and ⟦b:-s-⟧ are declined as follows:
Examples
Stems ⟦b:pater⟧, ⟦i:father⟧,
⟦b:patr-⟧, M. ⟦b:dolor⟧, ⟦i:pain⟧,
⟦b:dolōr-⟧, M. ⟦b:flōs⟧, ⟦i:flower⟧,
⟦b:flōr-⟧, M. ⟦b:genus⟧, ⟦i:race⟧,
Singular
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:pater⟧  ⟦b:dolor⟧  ⟦b:flōs⟧  ⟦b:genus⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:patris⟧  ⟦b:dolōris⟧  ⟦b:flōris⟧  ⟦b:generis⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:patrī⟧  ⟦b:dolōrī⟧  ⟦b:flōrī⟧  ⟦b:generī⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:patrem⟧  ⟦b:dolōrem⟧  ⟦b:flōrem⟧  ⟦b:genus⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:patre⟧  ⟦b:dolōre⟧  ⟦b:flōre⟧  ⟦b:genere⟧
Plural
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:patrēs⟧  ⟦b:dolōrēs⟧  ⟦b:flōrēs⟧  ⟦b:genera⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:patrum⟧  ⟦b:dolōrum⟧  ⟦b:flōrum⟧  ⟦b:generum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:patribus⟧  ⟦b:dolōribus⟧  ⟦b:flōribus⟧  ⟦b:generibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:patrēs⟧  ⟦b:dolōrēs⟧  ⟦b:flōrēs⟧  ⟦b:genera⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:patribus⟧  ⟦b:dolōribus⟧  ⟦b:flōribus⟧  ⟦b:generibus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:gener-⟧, Ne.
⟦#488⟧
Many stems in ⟦b:-r-⟧ ended originally in ⟦b:-s-⟧, which became ⟦b:-r-⟧ between two vowels, and in some words in the nominative also (⟦r154:154⟧): as, ⟦b:flōs⟧, M., ⟦i:flower⟧, G. ⟦b:*flōsis⟧, ⟦b:flōris⟧; ⟦b:honōs⟧, M., ⟦i:honour⟧, G. ⟦b:honōris⟧, N. ⟦b:honor⟧.
⟦#489⟧
(a.) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-r-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-r⟧, genitive ⟦b:-ris⟧, are:
⟦b:-ar⟧, ⟦b:-aris⟧  ⟦b:baccar⟧, Ne., ⟦i:a plant⟧; ⟦b:iūbar⟧, Ne., rarely M., ⟦i:bright sky⟧, no Pl.
⟦b:-ār⟧, ⟦b:-aris⟧  ⟦b:lār⟧, M., ⟦i:household god⟧; G. Pl. ⟦b:larum⟧; two or three times ⟦b:larium⟧.
⟦b:-ār⟧, ⟦b:-arris⟧  ⟦b:fār⟧ (⟦r171:171⟧, ⟦r1:1⟧), Ne., ⟦i:spelt⟧; Pl. only N. and Ac. ⟦b:farra⟧.
⟦b:-er⟧, ⟦b:-eris⟧  Masculines: ⟦b:acipēnser⟧, ⟦i:sturgeon⟧; ⟦b:agger⟧, ⟦i:mound⟧; ⟦b:ānser⟧, rarely F., ⟦i:goose⟧; ⟦b:asser⟧, ⟦i:pole⟧; ⟦b:carcer⟧, ⟦i:jail⟧; ⟦b:later⟧, ⟦i:brick⟧; ⟦b:mulier⟧, F., ⟦i:woman⟧; ⟦b:passer⟧, ⟦i:sparrow⟧; ⟦b:vōmer⟧, ⟦i:ploughshare⟧. Neuters: ⟦b:cadāver⟧, ⟦i:corpse⟧; ⟦b:tūber⟧, ⟦i:swelling⟧; ⟦b:ūber⟧, ⟦i:breast⟧; ⟦b:verberis⟧, G., ⟦i:lash⟧, no N., generally Pl.; ⟦b:acer⟧, ⟦i:maple⟧, and some other plant names: see ⟦r573:573⟧. ⟦b:pauper⟧, ⟦i:poor⟧, adjective.
⟦b:-ter⟧, ⟦b:-tris⟧  ⟦b:accipiter⟧, M., ⟦i:hawk⟧; ⟦b:frāter⟧, M., ⟦i:brother⟧; ⟦b:māter⟧, F., ⟦i:mother⟧; ⟦b:pater⟧, M., ⟦i:father⟧.
⟦b:-ēr⟧, ⟦b:-ēris⟧  ⟦b:vēr⟧, Ne.; no Pl.
⟦b:-or⟧, ⟦b:-oris⟧  ⟦b:aequor⟧, Ne., ⟦i:sea⟧; ⟦b:marmor⟧, Ne., ⟦i:marble⟧; ⟦b:arbor⟧, F., ⟦i:tree⟧.
⟦b:-or⟧, ⟦b:-ōris⟧  ⟦b:olor⟧, M., ⟦i:swan⟧; ⟦b:soror⟧, F., ⟦i:sister⟧; ⟦b:uxor⟧, F., ⟦i:wife⟧. Many masculines in ⟦b:-or⟧ for ⟦b:-ōs⟧ (⟦r237:237⟧): as, ⟦b:odor⟧, ⟦i:smell⟧; and in ⟦b:-tor⟧, ⟦b:-tōris⟧ (⟦r205:205⟧): as, ⟦b:amātor⟧, ⟦i:lover⟧. Also gender comparatives of adjectives: as, ⟦b:trīstior⟧ (⟦r346:346⟧), M., F., ⟦i:sadder⟧.
⟦b:-ur⟧, ⟦b:-oris⟧  Neuters: ⟦b:ebur⟧, ⟦i:ivory⟧; Pl. only ⟦b:ebora⟧; ⟦b:rōbur⟧, ⟦i:heart of oak⟧; Pl. ⟦b:rōbora⟧ common, ⟦b:rōborum⟧ and ⟦b:rōboribus⟧ twice each. Also ⟦b:femur⟧, ⟦i:thigh⟧, ⟦b:femoris⟧ or ⟦b:feminis⟧, and ⟦b:iecur⟧, ⟦i:liver⟧, ⟦b:iecoris⟧, ⟦b:iecineris⟧, or ⟦b:iocineris⟧.
⟦b:-ur⟧, ⟦b:-uris⟧  ⟦b:augur⟧, M., F., ⟦i:augur⟧; ⟦b:furfur⟧, M., ⟦i:bran⟧; ⟦b:turtur⟧, M., F., ⟦i:turtle-dove⟧; ⟦b:voltur⟧ or ⟦b:vultur⟧, M., ⟦i:vulture⟧. Neuters: ⟦b:fulgur⟧, ⟦i:lightning⟧; ⟦b:guttur⟧, rarely M., ⟦i:throat⟧; ⟦b:murmur⟧, ⟦i:murmur⟧; ⟦b:sulpur⟧, ⟦i:sulphur⟧. ⟦b:cicur⟧, ⟦i:tame⟧, adjective.
⟦b:-ūr⟧, ⟦b:-ūris⟧  ⟦b:fūr⟧, M., ⟦i:thief⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#490⟧
⟦b:volucris⟧, F., ⟦i:bird⟧, stem ⟦b:volucr-⟧, has its nominative formed like that of ⟦b:-i-⟧ stems.
⟦#491⟧
(b.) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-s-⟧, or ⟦b:-r-⟧ for ⟦b:-s-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-s⟧, genitive ⟦b:-ris⟧, are:
⟦b:-aes⟧, ⟦b:-aeris⟧  ⟦b:aes⟧, Ne., ⟦i:copper⟧, ⟦i:bronze⟧; in the Pl. only ⟦b:aera⟧ and ⟦b:aerum⟧ are usual.
⟦b:-ēs⟧, ⟦b:-eris⟧  ⟦b:Cerēs⟧. ⟦b:pūbēs⟧, ⟦i:mangrown⟧; ⟦b:impūbēs⟧, ⟦i:immature⟧, adjectives; for the last more commonly ⟦b:impūbis⟧, like ⟦b:brevis⟧ (⟦r630:630⟧).
⟦b:-is⟧, ⟦b:-eris⟧  ⟦b:cinis⟧, M., ⟦i:ashes⟧; ⟦b:cucumis⟧, M., ⟦i:cucumber⟧, also with ⟦b:-i-⟧ stem; ⟦b:pulvis⟧, M., ⟦i:dust⟧; ⟦b:vōmis⟧, M., ⟦i:ploughshare⟧.
⟦b:-ōs⟧, ⟦b:-oris⟧  ⟦b:arbōs⟧, F., ⟦i:tree⟧.
⟦b:-ōs⟧, ⟦b:-ōris⟧  Masculines: ⟦b:flōs⟧, ⟦i:flower⟧; ⟦b:mōs⟧, ⟦i:custom⟧; ⟦b:rōs⟧, ⟦i:dew⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧); ⟦b:lepōs⟧, ⟦i:grace⟧; ⟦b:honōs⟧ or ⟦b:honor⟧, ⟦i:honour⟧, and some old Latin words for later ⟦b:-or⟧: as, ⟦b:odōs⟧ or ⟦b:odor⟧, ⟦i:smell⟧ (⟦r489:489⟧). ⟦b:ōs⟧, Ne., ⟦i:mouth⟧, ⟦i:face⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-us⟧, ⟦b:-eris⟧  Neuters: ⟦b:acus⟧, ⟦i:husk⟧; ⟦b:foedus⟧, ⟦i:treaty⟧; ⟦b:fūnus⟧, ⟦i:funeral⟧; ⟦b:genus⟧, ⟦i:race⟧; ⟦b:glŏ̄mus⟧ (⟦r134:134⟧), ⟦i:clew⟧; ⟦b:holus⟧, ⟦i:green stuff⟧; ⟦b:latus⟧, ⟦i:side⟧; ⟦b:mūnus⟧, ⟦i:gift⟧; ⟦b:onus⟧, ⟦i:burden⟧; ⟦b:opus⟧, ⟦i:work⟧; ⟦b:pondus⟧, ⟦i:weight⟧; ⟦b:raudus⟧ or ⟦b:rūdus⟧, ⟦i:piece of copper⟧; ⟦b:scelus⟧, ⟦i:crime⟧; ⟦b:sīdus⟧, ⟦i:constellation⟧; ⟦b:ulcus⟧, ⟦i:sore⟧; ⟦b:vellus⟧, ⟦i:fleece⟧; ⟦b:vīscus⟧, ⟦i:bowel⟧, usually plural; ⟦b:volnus⟧ or ⟦b:vulnus⟧, ⟦i:wound⟧. Also ⟦b:Venus⟧, F., and ⟦b:vetus⟧, ⟦i:old⟧, adjective.
⟦b:-us⟧, ⟦b:-oris⟧  Neuters: ⟦b:corpus⟧, ⟦i:body⟧; ⟦b:decus⟧, ⟦i:grace⟧; ⟦b:dēdecus⟧, ⟦i:disgrace⟧; ⟦b:facinus⟧, ⟦i:deed⟧; ⟦b:faenus⟧, ⟦i:interest⟧; ⟦b:frīgus⟧, ⟦i:cold⟧; ⟦b:lītus⟧, ⟦i:shore⟧; ⟦b:nemus⟧, ⟦i:grove⟧; ⟦b:pectus⟧, ⟦i:breast⟧; ⟦b:pecus⟧, ⟦i:flock⟧; ⟦b:penus⟧, ⟦i:store⟧; ⟦b:pignus⟧, ⟦i:pledge⟧; ⟦b:stercus⟧, ⟦i:dung⟧; ⟦b:tempus⟧, ⟦i:time⟧; ⟦b:tergus⟧, ⟦i:back⟧. Also ⟦b:lepus⟧, M., ⟦i:hare⟧.
⟦b:-us⟧, ⟦b:-ōris⟧  Neuter comparatives of adjectives: as, ⟦b:trīstius⟧ (⟦r346:346⟧), ⟦i:sadder⟧.
⟦b:-ūs⟧, ⟦b:-ūris⟧  Neuters: ⟦b:crūs⟧, ⟦i:leg⟧; ⟦b:iūs⟧, ⟦i:right⟧, Pl. ⟦b:iūra⟧, G. Pl. twice only (Plaut.; Cato), no D. or Ab. Pl.; ⟦b:iūs⟧, ⟦i:broth⟧, ⟦b:pūs⟧, ⟦i:pus⟧, ⟦b:rūs⟧, ⟦i:country⟧, ⟦b:tūs⟧, ⟦i:frankincense⟧, Pl. only N. and Ac. ⟦b:iūra⟧, &c. ⟦b:tellūs⟧, F., ⟦i:earth⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#492⟧
⟦b:vās⟧, Ne., ⟦i:vessel⟧, ⟦i:utensil⟧, retains the ⟦b:s⟧ between two vowels: G. ⟦b:vāsis⟧, D. ⟦b:vāsī⟧, Ab. ⟦b:vāse⟧, plural N. and Ac. ⟦b:vāsa⟧; the G. ⟦b:vāsōrum⟧, and D. and Ab. ⟦b:vāsis⟧, are formed from an ⟦b:-o-⟧ stem, ⟦b:vāso-⟧ (⟦r401:401⟧). ⟦b:mēnsis⟧, M., ⟦i:month⟧, ⟦b:mēnsis⟧, has its nominative formed like that of ⟦b:-i-⟧ stems; G. Pl. ⟦b:mēnsum⟧, sometimes ⟦b:mēnsuum⟧ or ⟦b:mēnsium⟧. ⟦b:os⟧ (⟦r171:171, 1⟧) Ne., ⟦i:bone⟧, ⟦b:ossis⟧, has no G. Pl. in good writers (⟦r430:430⟧): ⟦b:ossium⟧ late.
⟦#493⟧
The two neuters ⟦b:vīrus⟧, ⟦i:gall⟧, ⟦i:poison⟧, and ⟦b:volgus⟧ or ⟦b:vulgus⟧, ⟦i:the crowd⟧, have ⟦b:-o-⟧ stems, except in the nominative and accusative (⟦r401:401⟧), and no plural: thus, N. and Ac. ⟦b:volgus⟧, G. ⟦b:volgī⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:volgō⟧. A masculine accusative ⟦b:volgum⟧ is sometimes found. The Greek neuter ⟦b:pelagus⟧, ⟦i:the deep⟧, has also G. ⟦b:pelagī⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:pelagō⟧, Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:pelagē⟧ (⟦r508:508⟧).

title: Stems in -u- or -v-
text:
⟦#494⟧
Four substantives with stems in ⟦b:-ū-⟧ or ⟦b:-v-⟧, ⟦b:grūs⟧, F., ⟦i:crane⟧, ⟦b:gruis⟧; ⟦b:sūs⟧, M., F., ⟦i:sow⟧, ⟦i:swine⟧, ⟦b:suis⟧; ⟦b:bōs⟧, M., F., ⟦i:ox⟧, ⟦i:cow⟧, ⟦b:bovis⟧; and ⟦b:nix⟧, F., ⟦i:snow⟧, ⟦b:nivis⟧, follow the consonant declension; also the genitive ⟦b:Iovis⟧, and the other oblique cases of ⟦b:Iuppiter⟧ (⟦r500:500⟧). But ⟦b:sūs⟧ has in the plural dative and ablative ⟦b:suibus⟧, ⟦b:sūbus⟧, or ⟦b:subus⟧; ⟦b:bōs⟧ has in the plural genitive ⟦b:boum⟧ or ⟦b:bovum⟧, rarely ⟦b:bovom⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧), and in the dative and ablative ⟦b:bōbus⟧, or oftener ⟦b:būbus⟧; ⟦b:nix⟧ has no genitive plural in good writers (⟦r430:430⟧): ⟦b:nivium⟧ late, once ⟦b:nivum⟧.

title: Consonant Stems: Singular Cases
text:
⟦#495⟧
(1.) The nominative singular of gender stems in a mute is formed by adding ⟦b:-s⟧ to the stem (⟦r422:422⟧): as,
⟦b:rēg-⟧, ⟦i:king⟧, N. ⟦b:rēx⟧ (⟦r164:164⟧, ⟦r1:1⟧); ⟦b:duc-⟧, ⟦i:leader⟧, N. ⟦b:dux⟧ (⟦r135:135, 1⟧); ⟦b:custōd-⟧, ⟦i:guard⟧, N. ⟦b:custōs⟧ (⟦r171:171, 5⟧); ⟦b:aetāt-⟧, ⟦i:age⟧, N. ⟦b:aetās⟧ (⟦r171:171, 5⟧); ⟦b:caelib-⟧, ⟦i:unmarried⟧, N. ⟦b:caelebs⟧ (⟦r54:54⟧); ⟦b:mūnicip-⟧, ⟦i:burgher⟧, N. ⟦b:mūniceps⟧. ⟦b:hiem-⟧, ⟦i:winter⟧, the only stem in ⟦b:-m-⟧, N. ⟦b:hiemps⟧ (⟦r167:167⟧) or ⟦b:hiems⟧, also takes ⟦b:-s⟧.
⟦#496⟧
(2.) Stems in a continuous consonant, ⟦b:-l-⟧, ⟦b:-n-⟧, ⟦b:-r-⟧, or ⟦b:-s-⟧, and neuters have no nominative suffix (⟦r422:422⟧, ⟦r423:423⟧): as,
⟦b:cōnsul-⟧, ⟦i:consul⟧, N. ⟦i:cōnsul⟧; ⟦b:flāmin-⟧, ⟦i:special priest⟧, N. ⟦b:flāmen⟧; ⟦b:agger-⟧, ⟦i:mound⟧, N. ⟦b:agger⟧; ⟦b:iūr-⟧ for ⟦b:iūs-⟧, ⟦i:right⟧, N. ⟦b:iūs⟧.
For ⟦b:cor⟧, ⟦i:heart⟧, see ⟦r476:476⟧; ⟦b:lacte⟧, ⟦b:lac⟧, ⟦i:milk⟧, ⟦r478:478⟧; ⟦b:sanguī̆s⟧, ⟦i:blood⟧, ⟦r486:486⟧; ⟦b:-s⟧ in neuter adjectives, ⟦r612:612⟧.
⟦#497⟧
(a.) Stems in ⟦b:-ōn-⟧ drop ⟦b:-n-⟧ in the nominative; stems in ⟦b:-in-⟧ for ⟦b:-on-⟧ drop ⟦b:-n-⟧, and end in ⟦b:-ō⟧: as,
⟦b:leōn-⟧, ⟦i:lion⟧, N. ⟦b:leō⟧; ⟦b:imāgin-⟧ for ⟦b:imāgon-⟧, ⟦i:likeness⟧, N. ⟦b:imāgō⟧.
⟦#498⟧
(b.) Stems of one syllable in ⟦b:-r-⟧ for ⟦b:-s-⟧ usually retain ⟦b:-s⟧ in the nominative: as, ⟦b:flōr-⟧ for ⟦b:flōs-⟧, M., ⟦i:flower⟧, N. ⟦b:flōs⟧; ⟦b:iūr-⟧ for ⟦b:iūs-⟧, Ne., ⟦i:right⟧, N. ⟦b:iūs⟧. Some of more than one syllable also retain ⟦b:-s⟧: see ⟦r491:491⟧; but in others ⟦b:-s⟧ is changed to ⟦b:-r⟧, and in masculines a preceding ⟦b:ō⟧ is shortened: as, ⟦b:odōs⟧, ⟦i:smell⟧, ⟦b:odor⟧. ⟦b:lepōs⟧, ⟦i:grace⟧, retains ⟦b:-ōs⟧.
⟦#499⟧
(c.) Four stems in ⟦b:-er-⟧ for ⟦b:-is-⟧ have the nominative singular in ⟦b:-is⟧: ⟦b:cinis⟧, ⟦i:ashes⟧, ⟦b:cineris⟧; ⟦b:cucumis⟧, ⟦i:cucumber⟧, ⟦b:cucumeris⟧ or ⟦b:cucumis⟧; ⟦b:pulvī̆s⟧, ⟦i:dust⟧, ⟦b:pulveris⟧; and ⟦b:vōmis⟧, oftener ⟦b:vōmer⟧, ⟦i:ploughshare⟧, ⟦b:vōmeris⟧.
⟦#500⟧
The following have the nominative singular formed from a different stem from that of the other cases (⟦r401:401⟧):
⟦b:iter⟧, ⟦i:journey⟧, ⟦b:itineris⟧, stems ⟦b:iter-⟧, ⟦b:itiner-⟧; ⟦b:Iuppiter⟧ (⟦r389:389⟧) ⟦b:Iovis⟧; ⟦b:supellēx⟧, ⟦i:furniture⟧, ⟦b:supellēctilis⟧ (⟦r545:545⟧); ⟦b:senex⟧, ⟦i:old man⟧, ⟦i:man of forty or more⟧, ⟦b:senis⟧, stems ⟦b:senec-⟧, ⟦b:sen-⟧. For ⟦b:sēdēs⟧, ⟦i:seat⟧, see ⟦r476:476⟧; ⟦b:vātēs⟧, ⟦i:bard⟧, ⟦r478:478⟧. ⟦b:canis⟧, ⟦i:dog⟧, N. also ⟦b:canēs⟧ (Plaut. Enn., Lucil.), ⟦b:iuvenis⟧, ⟦i:young⟧ or ⟦i:middle-aged person⟧ (⟦r486:486⟧), ⟦b:volucris⟧, ⟦i:bird⟧ (⟦r490:490⟧), and ⟦b:mēnsis⟧, ⟦i:month⟧ (⟦r492:492⟧), have their nominatives formed like those of ⟦b:-i-⟧ stems.
⟦#501⟧
An old dative in ⟦b:-ē⟧ is sometimes retained in set phrases (⟦r507:507⟧): as, ⟦b:aerē⟧, ⟦i:money⟧; ⟦b:iūrē⟧, ⟦i:right⟧. See ⟦r98:98⟧.
⟦#502⟧
Substantives have rarely an ablative in ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-ei⟧ like ⟦b:-i-⟧ stems: as, ⟦b:capitī⟧ (Catull.), ⟦i:head⟧, for ⟦b:capite⟧; ⟦b:dōtei⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦i:dowry⟧, for ⟦b:dōte⟧. Substantives used as adjectives have sometimes ⟦b:-ī⟧: as ⟦b:artificī manū⟧, ⟦i:with artist hand⟧; but often ⟦b:-e⟧: as, ⟦b:ālite lāpsū⟧, ⟦i:with winged glide⟧. For ⟦b:-ē⟧ in old Latin there is no certain evidence.
⟦#503⟧
Adjectives in the comparative degree have sometimes an ablative in ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:meliōrī⟧, better, for ⟦b:meliōre⟧. Adjectives ‘of one ending’ with consonant stems (⟦r624:624⟧) have always ⟦b:-e⟧, except ⟦b:vetus⟧, ⟦i:old⟧, which has sometimes ⟦b:veterī⟧.
⟦#504⟧
Town names and a few appellatives have a locative case in ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:Karthāginī⟧, ⟦i:at Carthage⟧; ⟦b:rūrī⟧, ⟦i:a-field⟧, ⟦i:in the country⟧.

title: Consonant Stems: Plural Cases
text:
⟦#505⟧
The nominative and accusative plural masculine and feminine have rarely ⟦b:-īs⟧, like stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧: as ⟦b:sacerdōtīs⟧, ⟦i:priests⟧; ⟦b:meliōrīs⟧, ⟦i:better⟧. For ⟦b:-ā⟧ in neuters in old Latin, see ⟦r130:130⟧, 2.
⟦#506⟧
The genitive plural of stems in ⟦b:-tāt-⟧ (⟦r262:262⟧) is sometimes ⟦b:-ium⟧, like that of ⟦b:-ī-⟧ stems: as, ⟦b:cīvitātium⟧, ⟦i:communities⟧; ⟦b:voluptātium⟧, ⟦i:pleasures⟧ (Cic.); but chiefly in or after the Augustan age. ⟦b:mēnsis⟧, ⟦i:month⟧, has ⟦b:mēnsum⟧, but often ⟦b:mēnsuum⟧, sometimes ⟦b:mēnsium⟧. ⟦b:āles⟧, ⟦i:bird⟧, has sometimes ⟦b:ālituum⟧ in hexameter verse. For the dative and ablative ⟦b:-būs⟧, see ⟦r2505:2505⟧.
⟦#507⟧
Other case forms are found in inscriptions, as follows:
N. MVNICIPES; ⟦b:-ō⟧ for ⟦b:-ōs⟧ (⟦r66:66⟧): MAIO, i.e. ⟦b:maiōs⟧ or ⟦b:maior⟧. G. ⟦b:-es⟧, as early as 218 B.C.: SALVTES; ⟦b:-us⟧, from 186 to 100 B.C.: NOMINVS; ⟦b:-u⟧ (⟦r66:66⟧): CAESARV. D. ⟦b:-ei⟧: VIRTVTEI, soon after 290 B.C.; HEREDEI, 45 B.C.; ⟦b:-ē⟧, disappeared sooner than ⟦b:-ei⟧ except in set phrases (⟦r501:501⟧), but is equally old: IVNONE; IOVRE. Ac. ⟦b:-e⟧ (⟦r61:61⟧): APICE. Ab. ⟦b:-īd⟧ (⟦r426:426⟧): CONVENTIONID, i.e. ⟦b:cōntiōne⟧; ⟦b:-ei⟧: VIRTVTEI; ⟦b:-ī⟧: HEREDI. Plural: N. ⟦b:-īs⟧: IOVDICIS. G. ⟦b:-om⟧: POVMILIONOM; ⟦b:-ium⟧: MVNICIPIVM. D. ⟦b:-ebus⟧: TEMPESTATEBVS. Ac. ⟦b:-īs⟧: MVNICIPIS.

title: Consonant Stems: Greek Nouns
text:
⟦#508⟧
Greek appellatives of the consonant declension occasionally retain Greek case endings: as, ⟦b:lampas⟧, ⟦i:torch⟧, G. ⟦b:lampados⟧, Ac. ⟦b:lampada⟧. Plural: N. ⟦b:lampades⟧, Ac. ⟦b:lampadas⟧. ⟦b:āēr⟧, ⟦i:air⟧, has usually the accusative ⟦b:āera⟧, and ⟦b:aethēr⟧, ⟦i:upper air⟧, always has ⟦b:aethera⟧. In the plural nominative and accusative, ⟦b:cētus⟧, ⟦i:swimming monster⟧, ⟦b:melos⟧, ⟦i:strain of music⟧, and ⟦b:pelagus⟧ (⟦r493:493⟧), ⟦i:the deep⟧, have ⟦b:-ē⟧: as, ⟦b:cētē⟧. Genitive ⟦b:-ōn⟧, rare: as, ⟦b:epigrammatōn⟧, ⟦i:epigrams⟧. Dative and ablative ⟦b:-matīs⟧ from words in ⟦b:-ma⟧, ⟦b:-matis⟧: as, ⟦b:poēmatīs⟧, ⟦i:poems⟧ (⟦r401:401⟧).
⟦#509⟧
Greek proper names of the consonant declension are usually declined like Latin ones in old Latin and prose. From Vergil and Propertius on, Greek case endings grow more and more frequent, especially in poetry; they are best learned for every name from the dictionary; the commonest forms are:
Genitive ⟦b:-os⟧: as, ⟦b:Pān⟧, ⟦b:Pānos⟧; ⟦b:-ūs⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-ō⟧: as, ⟦b:Mantō⟧, ⟦b:Mantūs⟧. Dative ⟦b:-i⟧, rare: as, ⟦b:Mīnōidi⟧. Accusative ⟦b:-a⟧, common with names of persons in poetry, not in prose, more common with those of places, and even in prose: as, ⟦b:Acheronta⟧; always ⟦b:Pāna⟧; ⟦b:-ō⟧, with feminines in ⟦b:-ō⟧, ⟦b:-ūs⟧: as, ⟦b:Dīdō⟧. Vocative: ⟦b:Pallās⟧, ⟦b:Pallā⟧; in old Latin the nominative is commonly used instead of the vocative. Plural: Nominative ⟦b:-es⟧: as, ⟦b:Arcades⟧. Dative ⟦b:-sin⟧, rare: as, ⟦b:Lēmniasin⟧. Accusative ⟦b:-as⟧, very common: as, ⟦b:Lelegas⟧; in prose, ⟦b:Macedonas⟧; also in words not Greek: as, ⟦b:Allobrogas⟧ (Caes.).
⟦#510⟧
Names in ⟦b:-eus⟧, like ⟦b:Orpheus⟧, are usually declined like ⟦b:-o-⟧ stems (⟦r449:449⟧). They have less frequently Greek forms: as, G. ⟦b:Orpheos⟧, D. ⟦b:Orphei⟧ or ⟦b:Orphī⟧, Ac. ⟦b:Orphea⟧. Accusative rarely ⟦b:-ēa⟧: as, ⟦b:Ī̆lonēa⟧.
⟦#511⟧
Some names in ⟦b:-ēs⟧ have the genitive in ⟦b:-is⟧ or ⟦b:-ī⟧ and the accusative in ⟦b:-em⟧ or ⟦b:-ēn⟧ (⟦r401:401⟧): as, ⟦b:Sōcratēs⟧, G. ⟦b:Sōcratis⟧ or ⟦b:Sōcratī⟧, Ac. usually ⟦b:Sōcratem⟧, also ⟦b:Sōcratēn⟧. ⟦b:Achillēs⟧ and ⟦b:Ulixēs⟧ have in the genitive ⟦b:-eī⟧, ⟦b:-e͡i⟧, or ⟦b:-ī⟧. Names in ⟦b:-clēs⟧ have rarely the accusative ⟦b:-clea⟧: as, ⟦b:Periclea⟧.
⟦#512⟧
Some names in ⟦b:-is⟧ have forms either from a stem in ⟦b:-id-⟧, or from one in ⟦b:-i-⟧: as, ⟦b:Paris⟧, G. ⟦b:Paridis⟧, D. ⟦b:Paridī⟧, Ac. ⟦b:Paridem⟧, ⟦b:Parim⟧ or ⟦b:Parin⟧, V. ⟦b:Pari⟧.

title: Stems in -i- and Mixed Stems
text:
⟦=⟧⟦i:The Third Declension.⟧
⟦=⟧Genitive singular ⟦b:-is⟧, genitive plural ⟦b:-i-um⟧.
⟦#513⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ include both substantives and adjectives, gender words and neuters.
For the gender of substantives, see ⟦r570:570⟧.
⟦#514⟧
The nominative of gender stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ ends usually in ⟦b:-s⟧ (or ⟦b:-x⟧), sometimes in ⟦b:-l⟧ or ⟦b:-r⟧; that of neuter substantives has no suffix, and ends usually in ⟦b:-e⟧, sometimes in ⟦b:-l⟧ or ⟦b:-r⟧.
⟦#515⟧
Most stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ have as many syllables in the nominative as in the genitive.
Such words are called ⟦i:Parisyllabic⟧ words, or ⟦i:Parisyllables⟧: as, nominative ⟦b:cīvis⟧, ⟦i:citizen⟧, two syllables; genitive ⟦b:cīvis⟧, ⟦i:of a citizen⟧, also two syllables.
⟦#516⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ are declined in the main like consonant stems, but have ⟦b:-im⟧ in the accusative of some substantives, and ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the ablative of adjectives, of some gender substantives, and of neuters; in the plural they have ⟦b:-ium⟧ in the genitive, ⟦b:-īs⟧ often in the accusative of gender words, and ⟦b:-ia⟧ in the nominative and accusative neuter.

title: Parisyllables
text:
⟦#517⟧
(1.) Parisyllabic gender stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ with the nominative in ⟦b:-is⟧ are declined as follows:

Stems ⟦b:tussis⟧, ⟦i:cough⟧,
⟦b:tussi-⟧, F. ⟦b:turris⟧, ⟦i:tower⟧,
⟦b:turri-⟧, F. ⟦b:amnis⟧, ⟦i:river⟧,

case endings
⟦#518⟧
(a.) Like the singular of ⟦b:tussis⟧ are declined parisyllabic names of rivers and places, like ⟦b:Tiberis⟧, ⟦b:Hispalis⟧. Also ⟦b:cucumis⟧, M., ⟦i:cucumber⟧ (but see ⟦r491:491⟧), and the defectives ⟦b:sitis⟧, F., ⟦i:thirst⟧, Ac. ⟦b:sitim⟧, Ab. ⟦b:sitī⟧, no plural; and ⟦b:vīs⟧, F., ⟦i:power⟧, Ac. ⟦b:vim⟧, Ab. ⟦b:vī⟧. Plural (⟦r401:401⟧): N. ⟦b:vīrēs⟧, G. ⟦b:vīrium⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:vīribus⟧, Ac. ⟦b:vīrīs⟧ or ⟦b:vīrēs⟧. (The D. ⟦b:vī⟧ is only found twice; a N. and Ac. Pl. ⟦b:vīs⟧ is very rare.)
⟦#519⟧
(b.) The following feminines are declined like ⟦b:turris⟧, with ⟦b:-im⟧ or ⟦b:-em⟧ in the accusative, and ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧ in the ablative:
⟦b:clāvis⟧, ⟦i:key⟧
⟦b:febris⟧, ⟦i:fever⟧
⟦b:nāvis⟧, ⟦i:vessel⟧
⟦b:puppis⟧, ⟦i:stern⟧
⟦b:sēmentis⟧, ⟦i:planting⟧
⟦b:strigilis⟧, ⟦i:skin-scraper⟧
So also in the oblique cases, ⟦b:Liger⟧, ⟦i:the Liger⟧. ⟦b:Arar⟧, ⟦i:the Arar⟧, has in the accusative ⟦b:-im⟧, in the ablative ⟦b:-e⟧ or ⟦b:-ī⟧.
⟦#520⟧
⟦b:secūris⟧, ⟦i:axe⟧, ⟦b:messis⟧, ⟦i:crop⟧, and ⟦b:restis⟧, ⟦i:rope⟧, also have ⟦b:-im⟧ or ⟦b:-em⟧ in the accusative, but only ⟦b:secūrī⟧, ⟦b:messe⟧, and ⟦b:reste⟧ in the ablative. ⟦b:canālis⟧, ⟦i:conduit⟧, has only ⟦b:-em⟧ in the accusative, and only ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the ablative.
⟦#521⟧
(c.) The following are declined like ⟦b:amnis⟧, with ⟦b:-em⟧ in the accusative, and ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧ in the ablative:
⟦b:avis⟧, ⟦i:bird⟧
⟦b:bīlis⟧, ⟦i:bile⟧
⟦b:cīvis⟧, ⟦i:citizen⟧
⟦b:classis⟧, ⟦i:fleet⟧
⟦b:fūstis⟧, ⟦i:club⟧
⟦b:ignis⟧, ⟦i:fire⟧
⟦#522⟧
(⟦i:d.⟧) Most parisyllabic stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧, with the nominative in ⟦b:-is⟧, are declined like ⟦b:hostis⟧: as,
⟦b:ēnsis⟧, M., ⟦i:glaive⟧; ⟦b:piscis⟧, M., ⟦i:fish⟧; ⟦b:aedis⟧, F., ⟦i:temple⟧, Pl. ⟦i:house⟧ (⟦r418:418⟧); ⟦b:vītis⟧, F., ⟦i:vine⟧; and a great many others. Also gender forms of adjectives in ⟦b:-i-⟧ ‘of two endings’ (⟦r630:630⟧), except the ablative singular, which ends in ⟦b:-ī⟧.
⟦#523⟧
(2.) Parisyllables in ⟦b:-i-⟧ with the nominative in ⟦b:-ēs⟧ have their other cases like those of ⟦b:hostis⟧: such are:
⟦b:caedēs⟧, ⟦i:bloodshed⟧; ⟦b:cautēs⟧, ⟦i:rock⟧; ⟦b:clādēs⟧, ⟦i:disaster⟧; ⟦b:indolēs⟧, ⟦i:native disposition⟧, no Pl.; ⟦b:lābēs⟧, ⟦i:fall⟧; ⟦b:mōlēs⟧, ⟦i:pile⟧; ⟦b:nūbēs⟧, ⟦i:cloud⟧; ⟦b:prōlēs⟧, ⟦i:offspring⟧, no Pl.; ⟦b:pūbēs⟧, ⟦i:young population⟧, no Pl.; ⟦b:rūpēs⟧, ⟦i:crag⟧; ⟦b:saepēs⟧, ⟦i:hedge⟧; ⟦b:strāgēs⟧, ⟦i:slaughter⟧; ⟦b:subolēs⟧, ⟦i:offspring⟧; ⟦b:tābēs⟧, ⟦i:wasting⟧, no Pl., feminines; and some others. Masculine: ⟦b:verrēs⟧, ⟦i:boar⟧; ⟦b:volpēs⟧ or ⟦b:vulpēs⟧, ⟦i:fox⟧.
⟦#524⟧
⟦b:famēs⟧, ⟦i:hunger⟧, has G. twice ⟦b:famī⟧ (Cato, Lucil.), Ab. always ⟦b:famē⟧ (⟦r603:603⟧), no Pl.; ⟦b:plēbēs⟧, ⟦i:commons⟧, N. also ⟦b:plēbs⟧ or ⟦b:plēps⟧, has G. ⟦b:plēbe͡i⟧ (⟦r603:603⟧), ⟦b:plēbī⟧ or ⟦b:plēbis⟧, no Pl.
⟦#525⟧
(3.) A few stems in ⟦b:-bri-⟧, ⟦b:-cri-⟧, or ⟦b:-tri-⟧, are declined as follows:
⟦b:imber⟧, ⟦i:shower⟧, stem ⟦b:imbri-⟧, M.
Singular: N. ⟦b:imber⟧, G. ⟦b:imbris⟧, D. ⟦b:imbrī⟧, Ac. ⟦b:imbrem⟧, Ab. ⟦b:imbrī⟧, oftener ⟦b:imbre⟧. Plural: N. ⟦b:imbrēs⟧, G. ⟦b:imbrium⟧, D. ⟦b:imbribus⟧, Ac. ⟦b:imbrīs⟧ or ⟦b:imbrēs⟧, Ab. ⟦b:imbribus⟧. So also ⟦b:lunter⟧ or ⟦b:linter⟧, F. (M.), ⟦i:tub⟧, ⟦i:boat⟧, ⟦b:ūter⟧, M., ⟦i:leather bag⟧, and ⟦b:venter⟧, M., ⟦i:belly⟧, but with only ⟦b:-e⟧ in the Ab.; and the masculine of adjectives in ⟦b:-bri-⟧, ⟦b:-cri-⟧, ⟦b:-tri-⟧, N. ⟦b:-er⟧ (⟦r628:628⟧); these last have in the Ab. always ⟦b:-ī⟧.
⟦#526⟧
(4.) Parisyllabic neuters in ⟦b:-i-⟧ with the nominative in ⟦b:-e⟧ are declined as follows:

⟦#527⟧
⟦b:mare⟧ has rarely the ablative ⟦b:mare⟧ in verse: in the plural only the nominative and accusative are usual; but a genitive ⟦b:marum⟧ is once quoted (Naev.), and the ablative ⟦b:maribus⟧ is once used by Caesar.
⟦#528⟧
Examples of parisyllabic neuters in ⟦b:-i-⟧, with the nominative in ⟦b:-e⟧, genitive ⟦b:-is⟧, are:
⟦b:ancīle⟧, ⟦i:sacred shield⟧; ⟦b:aplustre⟧, ⟦i:ancient⟧; ⟦b:conclāve⟧, ⟦i:suite of rooms⟧; ⟦b:īnsīgne⟧, ⟦i:ensign⟧; ⟦b:praesaepe⟧, ⟦i:stall⟧; ⟦b:rēte⟧, ⟦i:net⟧, Ab. ⟦b:rēte⟧. Also the neuter of adjectives in ⟦b:-i-⟧ ‘of two endings’ (⟦r630:630⟧), and some words in ⟦b:-īle⟧, ⟦b:-āle⟧, ⟦b:-āre⟧, originally adjectives (⟦r313:313⟧, ⟦r314:314⟧): as, ⟦b:būbīle⟧, ⟦i:ox-stall⟧; ⟦b:fōcāle⟧, ⟦i:neckcloth⟧; ⟦b:cocleāre⟧, ⟦i:spoon⟧.

title: Imparisyllables
text:
⟦#529⟧
Sometimes a plural stem in ⟦b:-i-⟧ is combined, in the singular, with a stem in a mute, in ⟦b:-l⟧, or ⟦b:-r⟧, or rarely in ⟦b:-s⟧. These mixed stems thus become imparisyllables. Gender stems of this class are like consonant stems in the singular, except the ablative of adjectives, which has usually ⟦b:-ī⟧.
⟦#530⟧
Imparisyllabic stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ are declined as follows:

⟦#531⟧
Examples of stems in ⟦b:-ci-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-x⟧, genitive ⟦b:-cis⟧, are:
⟦b:-āx⟧, ⟦b:-ācis⟧  ⟦b:fornāx⟧, F., ⟦i:furnace⟧. Many adjectives (⟦r284:284⟧): as, ⟦b:audāx⟧, ⟦i:daring⟧.
⟦b:-aex⟧, ⟦b:-aecis⟧  ⟦b:faex⟧, F., ⟦i:dregs⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-ex⟧, ⟦b:-icis⟧  ⟦b:supplex⟧, ⟦i:suppliant⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, sometimes ⟦b:-e⟧, G. Pl. ⟦b:supplicum⟧. Adjectives: ⟦b:duplex⟧, ⟦i:twofold⟧; ⟦b:multiplex⟧, ⟦i:manifold⟧; ⟦b:quadruplex⟧, ⟦i:fourfold⟧; ⟦b:septemplex⟧, ⟦i:sevenfold⟧; ⟦b:simplex⟧, ⟦i:simple⟧; ⟦b:triplex⟧, ⟦i:threefold⟧. The foregoing have Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:duplicī⟧; ⟦b:duplice⟧ once (Hor.), ⟦b:septemplice⟧ twice (Ov.; Stat.); G. Pl. ⟦b:-ium⟧, Ne. Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧.
⟦b:-īx⟧, ⟦b:-īcis⟧  ⟦b:fēlīx⟧, ⟦i:happy⟧; ⟦b:pernīx⟧, ⟦i:nimble⟧, adjectives. Also many feminines of the agent in ⟦b:-trīx⟧ (⟦r205:205⟧): as, ⟦b:victrīx⟧, ⟦i:victorious⟧; these sometimes have a Ne. Pl. N. and Ac.: as, ⟦b:victrīcia⟧; in the G. Pl. they have ⟦b:-ium⟧, or, as substantives, ⟦b:-um⟧: as, ⟦b:nūtrīcum⟧, ⟦i:nurses⟧.
⟦b:-lx⟧, ⟦b:-lcis⟧  ⟦b:calx⟧, F. (M.), ⟦i:heel⟧; ⟦b:calx⟧, M., F., ⟦i:limestone⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧); ⟦b:falx⟧, F., ⟦i:sickle⟧.
⟦b:-nx⟧, ⟦b:-ncis⟧  ⟦b:lanx⟧, F., ⟦i:platter⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧); ⟦b:deūnx⟧, M., ⟦i:eleven twelfths⟧; ⟦b:quīncunx⟧, M., ⟦i:five twelfths⟧.
⟦b:-ox⟧, ⟦b:-ocis⟧  ⟦b:praecox⟧, ⟦i:over-ripe⟧, older stem ⟦b:praecoqui-⟧: as, G. ⟦b:praecoquis⟧; rarely with ⟦b:-o-⟧ stem (⟦r401:401⟧): as, ⟦b:praecoquam⟧.
⟦b:-ōx⟧, ⟦b:-ōcis⟧  ⟦b:celōx⟧, F., ⟦i:clipper⟧. ⟦b:atrōx⟧, ⟦i:savage⟧; ⟦b:ferōx⟧, ⟦i:wild⟧; ⟦b:vēlōx⟧, ⟦i:swift⟧, adjectives.
⟦b:-rx⟧, ⟦b:-rcis⟧  ⟦b:arx⟧, F., ⟦i:citadel⟧, G. Pl. rare and late; ⟦b:merx⟧, F., ⟦i:ware⟧, N. in old Latin sometimes ⟦b:mercēs⟧ or ⟦b:mers⟧.
⟦b:-ux⟧, ⟦b:-ucis⟧  Adjectives: ⟦b:trux⟧, ⟦i:savage⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧, G. Pl. ⟦b:-ium⟧; ⟦b:redux⟧, ⟦i:returning⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧ (⟦r558:558⟧); no G. Pl. and no Ne. N. or Ac. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-aux⟧, ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:fauce⟧, F., Ab., ⟦i:throat⟧, N. ⟦b:faux⟧ once only and late, generally Pl.
⟦b:-ūx⟧, ⟦b:-ūcis⟧  ⟦b:lūx⟧, F. (⟦r581:581⟧), ⟦i:light⟧, Ab. sometimes ⟦b:-ī⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦/⟧
⟦#532⟧
(a.) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-di-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-s⟧, genitive ⟦b:-dis⟧, are:
⟦b:-ēs⟧, ⟦b:-edis⟧  Compounds of ⟦b:pēs⟧, ⟦i:foot⟧: ⟦b:compede⟧, F., Ab., ⟦i:fetter⟧, no N., G. Pl. ⟦b:compedium⟧; adjectives: as, ⟦b:ālipēs⟧, ⟦i:wing-footed⟧, ⟦b:bipēs⟧, ⟦i:two-legged⟧, ⟦b:quadrupēs⟧, ⟦i:four-footed⟧, &c., Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, Pl. G. ⟦b:-um⟧ only (⟦r563:563⟧), Ne. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧, rare and late.
⟦b:-ns⟧, ⟦b:-ndis⟧  Feminines: ⟦b:frōns⟧, ⟦i:foliage⟧; ⟦b:glāns⟧, ⟦i:acorn⟧; ⟦b:iūglāns⟧, ⟦i:walnut⟧.
⟦b:-rs⟧, ⟦b:-rdis⟧  ⟦b:concors⟧, ⟦i:like-minded⟧, adjective, and other compounds of ⟦b:cor⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r559:559⟧) Ne. Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧, G. Pl. not usual: ⟦b:discordium⟧, ⟦i:at variance⟧, and ⟦b:vēcordium⟧, ⟦i:frantic⟧, once each.
⟦b:-aus⟧, ⟦b:-audis⟧  ⟦b:fraus⟧, F., ⟦i:deceit⟧, G. Pl. ⟦b:fraudium⟧, later ⟦b:fraudum⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#533⟧
(b.) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-ti-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-s⟧ (⟦b:-x⟧), genitive ⟦b:-tis⟧, are:
⟦b:-ās⟧, ⟦b:-ātis⟧  ⟦b:Arpīnās⟧, ⟦i:of Arpinum⟧, and adjectives from other town names; ⟦b:optimātēs⟧, ⟦i:good men and true⟧, G. Pl. ⟦b:-ium⟧, less often ⟦b:-um⟧; ⟦b:penātēs⟧, ⟦i:gods of the household store⟧.
⟦b:-es⟧, ⟦b:-etis⟧  Adjectives: ⟦b:hebes⟧, ⟦i:dull⟧; ⟦b:teres⟧, ⟦i:cylindrical⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r559:559⟧), no G. Pl., Ne. Pl. ⟦b:hebetia⟧, ⟦b:teretia⟧, late and rare; ⟦b:perpes⟧, ⟦i:lasting through⟧, Ab. ⟦b:perpetī⟧, late only; ⟦b:praepes⟧, ⟦i:swift-winged⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧, G. Pl. ⟦b:-um⟧, no Ne. Pl. N. or Ac.
⟦b:-ēs⟧, ⟦b:-ētis⟧  ⟦b:locuplēs⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧, adjective, Ab. usually ⟦b:-e⟧ of a person, ⟦b:-ī⟧ often of a thing, G. Pl. ⟦b:locuplētium⟧, sometimes ⟦b:locuplētum⟧, Ne. Pl. ⟦b:locuplētia⟧ once.
⟦b:-īs⟧, ⟦b:-ītis⟧  ⟦b:līs⟧, ⟦i:contention⟧; ⟦b:dīs⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧, adjective, Ab. always ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r559:559⟧), Pl. G. ⟦b:-ium⟧, once ⟦b:-um⟧ (Sen.), Ne. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧. ⟦b:Quirīs⟧, ⟦b:Samnīs⟧.
⟦b:-ls⟧, ⟦b:-ltis⟧  ⟦b:puls⟧, ⟦i:pottage⟧, no G. Pl. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-ns⟧, ⟦b:-ntis⟧  Masculines: ⟦b:dēns⟧, ⟦i:tooth⟧: ⟦b:fōns⟧, ⟦i:fountain⟧; ⟦b:pōns⟧, ⟦i:bridge⟧; ⟦b:mōns⟧, ⟦i:mountain⟧, N. once ⟦b:montis⟧ (Enn.); factors of twelve: ⟦b:sextāns⟧, ⟦i:one sixth⟧; ⟦b:quadrāns⟧, ⟦b:triēns⟧, ⟦b:dōdrāns⟧, ⟦b:dēxtāns⟧. Feminines: ⟦b:frōns⟧, ⟦i:forehead⟧; ⟦b:gēns⟧, ⟦i:clan⟧; ⟦b:mēns⟧, ⟦i:mind⟧. Present participles: as, ⟦b:regēns⟧, ⟦i:guiding⟧. Many adjectives: as, ⟦b:ingēns⟧, ⟦i:gigantic⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r559:559⟧); ⟦b:Vēiēns⟧, ⟦i:of Vei⟧; compounds of ⟦b:mēns⟧: as, ⟦b:āmēns⟧, ⟦i:out of one’s head⟧; of ⟦b:dēns⟧: as, ⟦b:tridēns⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, as substantive usually ⟦b:-e⟧.
⟦b:-eps⟧, ⟦b:-ipitis⟧  Adjective compounds of ⟦b:caput⟧, ⟦i:head⟧: ⟦b:anceps⟧ (⟦r543:543⟧), ⟦i:two-headed⟧, once older ⟦b:ancipēs⟧ (Plaut.); ⟦b:biceps⟧, ⟦i:two-headed⟧; ⟦b:triceps⟧, ⟦i:three-headed⟧; ⟦b:praeceps⟧, ⟦i:head-first⟧, old ⟦b:praecipēs⟧ (Plaut.; Enn.), Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r559:559⟧), no G. Pl., Ne. Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧.
⟦b:-rs⟧, ⟦b:-rtis⟧  Feminines: ⟦b:ars⟧, ⟦i:art⟧; ⟦b:cohors⟧, ⟦i:cohort⟧; ⟦b:fors⟧, ⟦i:chance⟧; ⟦b:mors⟧, ⟦i:death⟧; ⟦b:pars⟧, ⟦i:part⟧; ⟦b:sors⟧, ⟦i:lot⟧, N. twice ⟦b:sortis⟧ (Plaut.; Ter.). Adjectives: ⟦b:cōnsors⟧, ⟦i:sharing⟧, ⟦b:exsors⟧, ⟦i:not sharing⟧, no G. Pl.; ⟦b:expers⟧, ⟦i:without part⟧; ⟦b:iners⟧, ⟦i:unskilled⟧, ⟦b:sollers⟧, ⟦i:all-skilled⟧, Ne. Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧.
⟦b:-x⟧, ⟦b:-ctis⟧  ⟦b:nox⟧, F., ⟦i:night⟧; Ab. also ⟦b:noctū⟧ (⟦r401:401⟧); an old adverb form is ⟦b:nox⟧, ⟦i:nights⟧.
⟦/⟧
⟦#534⟧
(a.) Stems in ⟦b:-bi-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-bs⟧ (⟦r149:149⟧), genitive ⟦b:-bis⟧, are:
⟦b:trabs⟧, F., ⟦i:beam⟧, older N. ⟦b:trabēs⟧ (Enn.); ⟦b:plēbs⟧, F., ⟦i:commons⟧, N. sometimes ⟦b:plēps⟧, for the older ⟦b:plēbēs⟧ (⟦r603:603⟧), no Pl.; ⟦b:urbs⟧, F., ⟦i:city⟧.
⟦#535⟧
(b.) Stems in ⟦b:-pi-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-ps⟧, genitive ⟦b:-pis⟧, are:
⟦b:inops⟧, ⟦i:poor⟧, adjective, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r559:559⟧), G. Pl. ⟦b:-um⟧, no Ne. Pl. N. or Ac. (⟦r430:430⟧); ⟦b:stirps⟧, F. (M.), ⟦i:trunk⟧.
⟦#536⟧
Examples of stems in ⟦b:-li-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-l⟧, genitive ⟦b:-lis⟧, are:
⟦b:-al⟧, ⟦b:-ālis⟧  Neuters, originally adjective (⟦r546:546⟧): ⟦b:animal⟧, ⟦i:animal⟧; ⟦b:bacchānal⟧, ⟦i:shrine⟧ or ⟦i:feast of Bacchus⟧; ⟦b:cervīcal⟧, ⟦i:bolster⟧; ⟦b:puteal⟧, ⟦i:well-curb⟧; ⟦b:toral⟧, ⟦i:valance⟧; ⟦b:tribūnal⟧, ⟦i:tribunal⟧; ⟦b:vectīgal⟧, ⟦i:indirect tax⟧. Only N. or Ac.: ⟦b:cubital⟧, ⟦i:elbow-cushion⟧; ⟦b:minūtal⟧, ⟦i:minced-fish⟧; ⟦b:capital⟧, ⟦b:capitālia⟧, ⟦i:death⟧, ⟦i:capital crime⟧.
⟦b:-il⟧, ⟦b:-ilis⟧  ⟦b:vigil⟧, ⟦i:wide-awake⟧, adjective, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, as substantive ⟦b:-e⟧ (⟦r561:561⟧), G. Pl. ⟦b:vigilum⟧ (⟦r563:563⟧), no Ne. Pl. N. or Ac. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦/⟧
⟦#537⟧
(a.) Examples of stems in ⟦b:-ri-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-r⟧, genitive ⟦b:-ris⟧, are:
⟦b:-ar⟧, ⟦b:-āris⟧  Neuters, originally adjective (⟦r546:546⟧): ⟦b:calcar⟧, ⟦i:spur⟧; ⟦b:columbar⟧, ⟦i:dove-cote⟧; ⟦b:exemplar⟧, ⟦i:pattern⟧; ⟦b:lacūnar⟧, ⟦i:panel-ceiling⟧; ⟦b:pulvīnar⟧, ⟦i:couch⟧; ⟦b:subligar⟧, ⟦i:tights⟧; ⟦b:torcular⟧, ⟦i:wine-press⟧.
⟦b:-ār⟧, ⟦b:-aris⟧  Adjectives: ⟦b:pār⟧, ⟦i:equal⟧; ⟦b:dispār⟧, ⟦b:impār⟧, ⟦i:unequal⟧, for Ab., see ⟦r561:561⟧; G. Pl. ⟦b:-ium⟧, Ne. Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧; ⟦b:compār⟧, ⟦i:co-mate⟧, as substantive has G. Pl. ⟦b:-um⟧.
⟦b:-er⟧, ⟦b:-eris⟧  Adjectives: ⟦b:dēgener⟧, ⟦i:degenerate⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r559:559⟧), no Ne. Pl. N. or Ac. (⟦r430:430⟧); ⟦b:ūber⟧, ⟦i:fruitful⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, late ⟦b:-e⟧, Ne. Pl. ⟦b:ūbera⟧ once only (Acc.).
⟦b:-or⟧, ⟦b:-oris⟧  Adjectives: ⟦b:memor⟧, ⟦i:remembering⟧; ⟦b:immemor⟧, ⟦i:forgetful⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r559:559⟧), G. Pl. ⟦b:memorum⟧ (⟦r636:636⟧) once only (Verg.), no Ne. Pl. N. or Ac. (⟦r430:430⟧).
⟦b:-or⟧, ⟦b:-ōris⟧  Adjective compounds of ⟦b:color⟧: as, ⟦b:concolor⟧, ⟦i:of like shade⟧, ⟦b:discolor⟧, ⟦i:of different shade⟧, both with Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ only; ⟦b:versicolor⟧, ⟦i:pied⟧, Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, rarely ⟦b:-e⟧, Ne. Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧; the G. Pl. of these words is not usual, but ⟦b:versicōlorum⟧ once.
⟦/⟧
⟦#538⟧
(b.) Stems in ⟦b:-ri-⟧, with nominative ⟦b:-s⟧ of the stem, genitive ⟦b:-ris⟧, are ⟦b:glīs⟧, F., ⟦i:dormouse⟧, ⟦b:glīris⟧; ⟦b:mās⟧, M., ⟦i:male⟧, ⟦b:maris⟧; ⟦b:mūs⟧, F., ⟦i:mouse⟧, ⟦b:mūris⟧.
⟦#539⟧
The only imparisyllabic stem in ⟦b:-si-⟧ is ⟦b:ās⟧ (⟦r171:171, 1⟧), M., ⟦i:unit, an as⟧, G. ⟦b:assis⟧, with its compounds ⟦b:bēs⟧, ⟦i:two thirds⟧, G. ⟦b:bessis⟧, and ⟦b:sēmis⟧, ⟦i:half an as⟧, ⟦i:half⟧, G. ⟦b:sēmissis⟧.

title: Stems in -i- and Mixed Stems: Singular Cases
text:
⟦#540⟧
(1.) The nominative singular of gender stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ is usually formed by adding ⟦b:-s⟧ to the stem (⟦r422:422⟧). But many gender substantives have the nominative in ⟦b:-ēs⟧ (⟦r236:236⟧, ⟦r401:401⟧): as,
⟦b:amni-⟧, ⟦i:river⟧, N. ⟦b:amnis⟧; ⟦b:aedi-⟧, ⟦i:temple⟧, N. ⟦b:aedis⟧; ⟦b:brevi-⟧, ⟦i:short⟧, N. ⟦b:brevis⟧. With N. ⟦b:-ēs⟧: ⟦b:nūbi-⟧, ⟦i:cloud⟧, N. ⟦b:nūbēs⟧; for other examples, see ⟦r523:523⟧.
⟦#541⟧
Some substantives form the nominative in both these ways: as, ⟦b:vallēs⟧ and ⟦b:vallis⟧, ⟦i:valley⟧, equally common; ⟦b:aedis⟧, ⟦i:temple⟧, later ⟦b:aedēs⟧; for ⟦b:caedēs⟧, ⟦i:slaughter⟧, ⟦b:clādēs⟧, ⟦i:disaster⟧, and ⟦b:mōlēs⟧, ⟦i:pile⟧, ⟦b:caedis⟧, &c., occur exceptionally.
⟦#542⟧
A few stems in ⟦b:-bri-⟧, ⟦b:-cri-⟧, or ⟦b:-tri-⟧, drop ⟦b:-i-⟧ in the nominative. The endings ⟦b:brs⟧, ⟦b:crs⟧, ⟦b:trs⟧, then change to ⟦b:-ber⟧, ⟦b:-cer⟧, ⟦b:-ter⟧ (111, ⟦i:b⟧): as, ⟦b:imbrī-⟧, ⟦i:shower⟧, N. ⟦b:imber⟧ (⟦r525:525⟧).
⟦#543⟧
Of gender imparisyllables, some have lost ⟦b:-i-⟧ of the stem before ⟦b:-s⟧ in the nominative; others have originally a consonant stem in the nominative (⟦r529:529-535⟧).
Thus, ⟦b:monti-⟧, ⟦i:mountain⟧, and ⟦b:sorti-⟧, ⟦i:lot⟧, have N. ⟦b:mōns⟧ and ⟦b:sors⟧ for an older ⟦b:montis⟧ and ⟦b:sortis⟧; but ⟦b:dēns⟧, ⟦i:tooth⟧, and ⟦b:regēns⟧, ⟦i:ruling⟧, have as original stems ⟦b:dent-⟧ and ⟦b:regent-⟧. Adjectives in ⟦b:-cipiti-⟧ have N. ⟦b:-ceps⟧ (⟦r533:533⟧).
⟦#544⟧
A few adjective stems in ⟦b:-li-⟧ or ⟦b:-ri-⟧ drop ⟦b:-i-⟧ in the nominative without taking ⟦b:-s⟧ (⟦r536:536⟧, ⟦r537:537⟧): as, ⟦b:vigili-⟧, ⟦i:wide-awake⟧, N. ⟦b:vigil⟧; ⟦b:pari-⟧, ⟦i:equal⟧, N. ⟦b:pār⟧; so also ⟦b:Arar⟧ and ⟦b:Liger⟧. Three substantives in ⟦b:-ri-⟧ for ⟦b:-si-⟧ likewise drop ⟦b:-i-⟧, and end in the original ⟦b:-s⟧ (⟦r538:538⟧): ⟦b:glīri-⟧ for ⟦b:glīsi-⟧, ⟦i:dormouse⟧, N. ⟦b:glīs⟧; ⟦b:mās⟧, ⟦i:male⟧; ⟦b:mūs⟧, ⟦i:mouse⟧.
⟦#545⟧
For ⟦b:carō⟧, F., ⟦i:flesh⟧, ⟦b:carnis⟧ (Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, usually ⟦b:-e⟧, no G. Pl.) see 135, 2. ⟦b:supellēx⟧, F., ⟦i:furniture⟧, ⟦b:supellēctilis⟧ (Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧, no Pl.), has the nominative formed from a different stem from that of the other cases (⟦r401:401⟧).
⟦#546⟧
(2) Neuter stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ have no nominative suffix, and end in ⟦b:-e⟧ for ⟦b:-i-⟧ of the stem (107, ⟦i:b⟧): as,
⟦b:mari-⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧, N. ⟦b:mare⟧; ⟦b:brevi-⟧, ⟦i:short⟧, N. ⟦b:breve⟧. In some words, originally neuter adjectives in ⟦b:-āle⟧ and ⟦b:-āre⟧, the ⟦b:-e⟧ is dropped and the ⟦b:ā⟧ shortened: as, ⟦b:animāle⟧, ⟦i:living thing⟧, ⟦b:animal⟧ (⟦r536:536⟧); ⟦b:exemplāre⟧ (Lucr.), ⟦i:pattern⟧, ⟦b:exemplar⟧ (⟦r537:537⟧). Some neuter adjectives end in ⟦b:-l⟧ or ⟦b:-r⟧ (⟦r536:536⟧, ⟦r537:537⟧); and some ‘of one ending’ end in ⟦b:-s⟧ (⟦r612:612⟧).
⟦#547⟧
The accusative singular of gender substantives usually has ⟦b:-em⟧, like consonant stems (⟦r424:424⟧); but a few substantives with the nominative in ⟦b:-is⟧ have ⟦b:-im⟧ only, and some have either ⟦b:-im⟧ or ⟦b:-em⟧.
⟦#548⟧
(a.) Accusatives in ⟦b:-im⟧
Are ⟦b:sitim⟧, ⟦b:tussim⟧, ⟦b:vim⟧,  ⟦i:thirst⟧, ⟦i:cough⟧, ⟦i:strength⟧
And ⟦b:būrim⟧, ⟦b:cucumim⟧.  ⟦i:ploughtail⟧, ⟦i:cucumber⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#549⟧
The accusative in ⟦b:-im⟧ is found in many adverbs (⟦r700:700⟧): as, ⟦b:partim⟧, ⟦i:in part⟧; in some adverbial expressions: as, ⟦b:adamussim⟧, ⟦b:examussim⟧, ⟦i:to a T⟧, ⟦b:adfatim⟧, ⟦i:to satiety⟧, ⟦b:ad ravim⟧, ⟦i:to hoarseness⟧; in some names of rivers and cities: as, ⟦b:Tiberim⟧, ⟦b:Hispalim⟧; and in some Greek words (⟦r565:565⟧).
⟦#550⟧
(b.) Six have the accusative commonly in ⟦b:-im⟧, sometimes in ⟦b:-em⟧:
⟦b:febrim⟧, ⟦b:-em⟧, ⟦i:fever⟧
⟦b:pelvim⟧, ⟦b:-em⟧, ⟦i:basin⟧
⟦b:puppim⟧, ⟦b:-em⟧, ⟦i:stern⟧
⟦b:restim⟧, ⟦b:-em⟧, ⟦i:rope⟧
⟦b:secūrim⟧, ⟦b:-em⟧, ⟦i:axe⟧
⟦b:turrim⟧, ⟦b:-em⟧, ⟦i:tower⟧
⟦#551⟧
Six have the accusative commonly in ⟦b:-em⟧, sometimes in ⟦b:-im⟧:
⟦b:bipennem⟧, ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦i:two-edged axe⟧
⟦b:clāvem⟧, ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦i:key⟧
⟦b:messem⟧, ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦i:crop⟧
⟦b:nāvem⟧, ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦i:ship⟧
⟦b:sēmentem⟧, ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦i:planting⟧
⟦b:strigilem⟧, ⟦b:-im⟧, ⟦i:skin-scraper⟧
⟦#552⟧
In the ablative, gender substantives have usually ⟦b:-e⟧, and neuters and adjectives have ⟦b:-ī⟧: as,
⟦b:hoste⟧, ⟦i:enemy⟧; ⟦b:marī⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧; ⟦b:ācrī⟧, ⟦i:sharp⟧, ⟦b:brevī⟧, ⟦i:short⟧, ⟦b:audācī⟧, ⟦i:daring⟧.
⟦#553⟧
(1.) Of gender substantives with the nominative in ⟦b:-is⟧, a few have only ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the ablative, and many have either ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧.
⟦#554⟧
(a.) These ablatives have only ⟦b:-ī⟧:
⟦b:secūrī⟧, ⟦b:sitī⟧, ⟦b:tussī⟧, ⟦b:vī⟧,  ⟦i:axe⟧, ⟦i:thirst⟧, ⟦i:cough⟧, ⟦i:strength⟧
⟦b:canālī⟧, ⟦b:cucumī⟧,  ⟦i:conduit⟧, ⟦i:cucumber⟧
⟦/⟧
Some names of rivers and cities have only ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:Tiberī⟧, ⟦b:Hispalī⟧. The locative also ends in ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:Neāpolī⟧, ⟦i:at Neapolis⟧.
⟦#555⟧
(b.) These ablatives of gender substantives with the nominative in ⟦b:-is⟧ have ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧:
⟦b:amne⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦i:river⟧
⟦b:ave⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦i:bird⟧
⟦b:bīle⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦i:bile⟧
⟦b:cīvī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:citizen⟧
⟦b:classe⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦i:fleet⟧
⟦b:clāvī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:key⟧
⟦b:febrī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:fever⟧
⟦b:fūstī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:club⟧
⟦b:ignī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:fire⟧
⟦b:nāvī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:ship⟧
⟦b:orbī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:circle⟧
⟦b:puppī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:stern⟧
⟦b:sēmentī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:planting⟧
⟦b:strigilī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:skin-scraper⟧
⟦b:turrī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:tower⟧
⟦#556⟧
A few other words in ⟦b:-is⟧ have occasionally an ablative in ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:anguis⟧, ⟦i:snake⟧, ⟦b:collis⟧, ⟦i:hill⟧, ⟦b:fīnis⟧, ⟦i:end⟧, ⟦b:postis⟧, ⟦i:post⟧, ⟦b:unguis⟧, ⟦i:nail⟧, &c. ⟦b:sors⟧, ⟦i:lot⟧, ⟦b:imber⟧, ⟦i:shower⟧, and ⟦b:lūx⟧, ⟦i:light⟧, have also ⟦b:-e⟧ or ⟦b:-ī⟧; ⟦b:supellēx⟧, ⟦i:furniture⟧, has ⟦b:supellēctilī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧; ⟦b:Arar⟧ has ⟦b:-e⟧ or ⟦b:-ī⟧; ⟦b:Liger⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧.
⟦#557⟧
Neuter names of towns with the nominative in ⟦b:-e⟧ have ⟦b:-e⟧ in the ablative: as, ⟦b:Praeneste⟧. ⟦b:rēte⟧, ⟦i:net⟧, has only ⟦b:rēte⟧; ⟦b:mare⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧, has rarely ⟦b:mare⟧ (⟦r527:527⟧).
⟦#558⟧
(2.) Adjectives ‘of two endings’ with stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ (⟦r630:630⟧) often have ⟦b:-e⟧ in the ablative when they are used as substantives, and sometimes in verse, when a short vowel is needed: as,
⟦b:adfīnī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:connection by marriage⟧; ⟦b:aedīle⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦i:aedile⟧; ⟦b:familiārī⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦i:friend⟧. But some, even as substantives, have ⟦b:-ī⟧: as, ⟦b:aequālī⟧, ⟦i:of the same age⟧, ⟦b:cōnsulārī⟧, ⟦i:ex-consul⟧, ⟦b:gentīlī⟧, ⟦i:tribesman⟧. Adjectives of place in ⟦b:-ēnsis⟧ (⟦r330:330⟧) usually have ⟦b:-ī⟧, but sometimes ⟦b:-e⟧: as, ⟦b:Tarquiniēnse⟧. Proper names have usually ⟦b:-e⟧: as, ⟦b:Iuvenāle⟧.
⟦#559⟧
Adjectives ‘of one ending’ with stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ (⟦r632:632⟧), have commonly ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the ablative. The following ablatives have only ⟦b:-ī⟧:
⟦b:āmentī⟧, ⟦i:frenzied⟧, ⟦b:ancipitī⟧, ⟦i:two-headed⟧, ⟦b:praecipitī⟧, ⟦i:head-first⟧, ⟦b:concolōrī⟧, ⟦i:of like hue⟧, ⟦b:concordī⟧, ⟦i:harmonious⟧, ⟦b:discordī⟧, ⟦i:at variance⟧, ⟦b:sōcordī⟧, ⟦i:imperceptive⟧, ⟦b:dēgenerī⟧, ⟦i:degenerate⟧, ⟦b:dītī⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧, ⟦b:teretī⟧, ⟦i:rounded⟧, ⟦b:ingentī⟧, ⟦i:huge⟧, ⟦b:inopī⟧, ⟦i:without means⟧, ⟦b:memorī⟧, ⟦i:remembering⟧, ⟦b:immemorī⟧, ⟦i:forgetful⟧.
⟦#560⟧
Present participles, when used as adjectives, have ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the ablative, otherwise ⟦b:-e⟧: as,
⟦b:ā sapientī virō⟧, ⟦i:by a wise man⟧; ⟦b:adulēscente⟧, ⟦i:youth⟧, substantive; ⟦b:Rōmulō rēgnante⟧, ⟦i:in the reign of Romulus⟧, ablative absolute (⟦r1362:1362⟧).
⟦#561⟧
Other adjectives ‘of one ending’ occasionally have ⟦b:-e⟧ in the ablative when used as substantives or as epithets of persons, or in verse when a short syllable is needed: as,
⟦b:cōnsortī⟧, ⟦i:sharing⟧, ⟦b:parī⟧, ⟦i:equal⟧, ⟦b:vigilī⟧, ⟦i:wide-awake⟧, ⟦b:fēlīcī⟧, ⟦i:happy⟧, as adjectives; but ⟦b:cōnsorte⟧, &c., as substantives; in prose, ⟦b:imparī⟧, ⟦b:disparī⟧, ⟦i:unequal⟧; in verse, ⟦b:impare⟧, ⟦b:dispare⟧. Proper names have ⟦b:-e⟧: as, ⟦b:Fēlīce⟧.

title: Stems in -i- and Mixed Stems: Plural Cases
text:
⟦#562⟧
In the plural, gender nominatives have ⟦b:-ēs⟧, rarely ⟦b:-īs⟧ or ⟦b:-eīs⟧, and gender accusatives have ⟦b:-īs⟧ or ⟦b:-ēs⟧ indifferently, sometimes ⟦b:-eis⟧; after about 50 A.D., ⟦b:-ēs⟧ was the prevalent ending for both cases. Neuters add ⟦b:-a⟧ to the stem, making ⟦b:-ia⟧; for ⟦b:-iā́⟧ in old Latin, cf. ⟦r2505:2505⟧.
⟦#563⟧
In the genitive plural, present participles, some substantive stems in ⟦b:-nt(i)-⟧, and some adjectives ‘of two endings’ (⟦r631:631⟧) have occasionally ⟦b:-um⟧: as,
⟦b:amantum⟧, ⟦i:lovers⟧; ⟦b:rudentum⟧, ⟦i:rigging⟧; ⟦b:agrestum⟧, ⟦i:country folk⟧; ⟦b:caelestum⟧, ⟦i:heaven’s tenantry⟧. ⟦b:apis⟧, ⟦i:bee⟧, has commonly ⟦b:-um⟧; ⟦b:caedēs⟧, ⟦i:slaughter⟧, and ⟦b:fraus⟧, ⟦i:deceit⟧, have rarely ⟦b:-um⟧. For ⟦b:-um⟧ in some adjectives ‘of one ending,’ see ⟦r636:636⟧; for ⟦b:-bū́s⟧ in the dative and ablative in old Latin, see ⟦r2505:2505⟧.
⟦#564⟧
Other case forms are found in inscriptions, as follows:
N. without ⟦b:-is⟧: VECTIGAL, i.e. ⟦b:vectīgālis⟧, adjective; ⟦b:-e⟧ for ⟦b:-is⟧ (⟦r66:66⟧, ⟦r41:41⟧): MILITARE, i.e. ⟦b:mīlitāris⟧, adjective; ⟦b:-ēs⟧ (⟦r540:540⟧): AIDILES, i.e. ⟦b:aedīlis⟧; CIVES, i.e. ⟦b:cīvis⟧. G. ⟦b:-us⟧, from 186 to 100 B.C.: PARTVS, i.e. ⟦b:partis⟧. D. ⟦b:-ei⟧: VRBEI. Ac. ⟦b:-i⟧ (⟦r61:61⟧): PARTI, i.e. ⟦b:partem⟧; ⟦b:-e⟧: AIDE, i.e. ⟦b:aedem⟧. Ab. ⟦b:-ei⟧: FONTEI; ⟦b:-e⟧: SERVILE, i.e. ⟦b:servīlī⟧. Plural: N. ⟦b:-ēs⟧: FINES; ⟦b:-eis⟧: FINEIS; ⟦b:-īs⟧: FINIS.

title: Stems in -i- and Mixed Stems: Greek Nouns
text:
⟦#565⟧
Greek stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ are usually declined like Latin ones, with the accusative in ⟦b:-im⟧, and ablative in ⟦b:-ī⟧. But the accusative sometimes has ⟦b:-n⟧: as, ⟦b:poēsin⟧, ⟦i:poetry⟧, ⟦b:Charybdin⟧; similarly ⟦b:Capyn⟧; and a vocative occurs: as, ⟦b:Charybdi⟧. The plural genitive ⟦b:Metamorphōseōn⟧, and as ablative ⟦b:Metamorphōsesin⟧, occur as titles of books.

title: Characteristics of Stems in -i-
text:
⟦#566⟧
Parisyllables with nominatives in ⟦b:-is⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧, or ⟦b:-e⟧, and a few in ⟦b:-er⟧; and imparisyllables with nominatives in ⟦b:-al⟧, and in ⟦b:-ar⟧ for ⟦b:-āre⟧, have stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧.
But ⟦b:canis⟧, ⟦b:iuvenis⟧ (⟦r486:486⟧), ⟦b:volucris⟧ (⟦r490:490⟧), ⟦b:mēnsis⟧ (⟦r492:492⟧), ⟦b:sēdēs⟧ (⟦r476:476⟧), and ⟦b:vātēs⟧ (⟦r478:478⟧), have consonant stems.
⟦#567⟧
Under ⟦b:-i-⟧ stems may also conveniently be grouped the following classes, which have usually a consonant form in the singular, and an ⟦b:-i-⟧ form in the plural:
⟦#568⟧
(a.) Imparisyllabic adjectives with the genitive in ⟦b:-is⟧, except comparatives and the dozen with consonant stems (⟦r624:624⟧), and imparisyllables with a nominative in ⟦b:-s⟧ or ⟦b:-x⟧ preceded by any consonant except ⟦b:p⟧. But ⟦b:cōniūnx⟧ (⟦r472:472⟧) and ⟦b:caelebs⟧ (⟦r480:480⟧) have consonant stems.
⟦#569⟧
(b.) The following monosyllables: ⟦b:ās⟧, ⟦i:unit⟧, ⟦i:an as⟧, ⟦b:faex⟧, ⟦i:dregs⟧, ⟦b:fraus⟧, ⟦i:deceit⟧, ⟦b:glīs⟧, ⟦i:dormouse⟧, ⟦b:līs⟧, ⟦i:strife⟧, ⟦b:lūx⟧, ⟦i:light⟧, ⟦b:mās⟧, ⟦i:male⟧, ⟦b:mūs⟧, ⟦i:mouse⟧, ⟦b:nox⟧, ⟦i:night⟧, ⟦b:stirps⟧, ⟦i:trunk⟧, ⟦b:vīs⟧, ⟦i:strength⟧. Also ⟦b:fauce⟧, ⟦i:throat⟧, and ⟦b:compede⟧, ⟦i:fetter⟧, both Ab., no N., and ⟦b:fornāx⟧, ⟦i:furnace⟧.

title: Gender of Consonant Stems and -i- Stems
text:
⟦#570⟧
The gender of many of these substantives is determined by their meaning (⟦r404:404-412⟧); that of participles used as substantives follows the gender of the substantive understood; Greek substantives follow the Greek gender. The gender of other words may be conveniently arranged for the memory according to the nominative endings as follows.

title: Masculine
text:
⟦#571⟧
Imparisyllables in ⟦b:-es⟧ or ⟦b:-ēs⟧ and substantives in ⟦b:-er⟧, ⟦b:-ō⟧, ⟦b:-or⟧, and ⟦b:-ōs⟧ are masculine: as,
⟦b:caespes⟧, ⟦i:sod⟧; ⟦b:pēs⟧, ⟦i:foot⟧; ⟦b:agger⟧, ⟦i:mound⟧; ⟦b:sermō⟧, ⟦i:speech⟧; ⟦b:pallor⟧, ⟦i:paleness⟧; ⟦b:flōs⟧, ⟦i:flower⟧.
⟦#572⟧
These imparisyllables in ⟦b:-es⟧ or ⟦b:-ēs⟧ are feminine: ⟦b:merges⟧, ⟦i:sheaf⟧, ⟦b:seges⟧, ⟦i:crop⟧, ⟦b:teges⟧, ⟦i:mat⟧; ⟦b:requiēs⟧ and ⟦b:quiēs⟧, ⟦i:rest⟧; ⟦b:compedēs⟧, plural, ⟦i:fetters⟧; ⟦b:mercēs⟧, ⟦i:reward⟧. ⟦b:aes⟧, ⟦i:copper⟧, ⟦i:bronze⟧, is neuter.
⟦#573⟧
These substantives in ⟦b:-er⟧ are neuter: ⟦b:cadāver⟧, ⟦i:corpse⟧, ⟦b:iter⟧, ⟦i:way⟧, ⟦b:tūber⟧, ⟦i:swelling⟧, ⟦i:truffle⟧, ⟦b:ūber⟧, ⟦i:udder⟧, ⟦b:verberis⟧, ⟦i:lash⟧, genitive, no nominative; also names of plants in ⟦b:-er⟧: as, ⟦b:acer⟧, ⟦i:maple⟧, ⟦b:cicer⟧, ⟦i:chickpea⟧, ⟦b:papāver⟧, ⟦i:poppy⟧, ⟦b:piper⟧, ⟦i:pepper⟧, ⟦b:siler⟧, ⟦i:osier⟧, ⟦b:siser⟧, ⟦i:skirret⟧, ⟦b:sūber⟧, ⟦i:corktree⟧. ⟦b:linter⟧, ⟦i:tub⟧, ⟦i:boat⟧, is feminine, once masculine. ⟦b:vēr⟧, ⟦i:spring⟧, is neuter.
⟦#574⟧
Substantives in ⟦b:-ō⟧, with genitive ⟦b:-inis⟧ (⟦r485:485⟧), are feminine; as, ⟦b:imāgō⟧, ⟦b:imāginis⟧, ⟦i:likeness⟧; also ⟦b:carō⟧, ⟦b:carnis⟧, ⟦i:flesh⟧, and words of action in ⟦b:-iō⟧ and ⟦b:-tiō⟧ (⟦r227:227⟧, ⟦r228:228⟧). But ⟦b:cardō⟧, ⟦i:hinge⟧, ⟦b:ōrdō⟧, ⟦i:rank⟧, and ⟦b:turbō⟧, ⟦i:whirlwind⟧, are masculine. ⟦b:margō⟧, ⟦i:brink⟧, and ⟦b:cupīdō⟧, ⟦i:desire⟧, are sometimes masculine.
⟦#575⟧
These substantives in ⟦b:-or⟧ are neuter: ⟦b:ador⟧, ⟦i:spelt⟧, ⟦b:aequor⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧, ⟦b:marmor⟧, ⟦i:marble⟧, ⟦b:cor⟧, ⟦i:heart⟧. ⟦b:arbor⟧, ⟦i:tree⟧, is feminine.
⟦#576⟧
These substantives in ⟦b:-ōs⟧ are feminine: ⟦b:cōs⟧, ⟦i:whetstone⟧, ⟦b:arbōs⟧, ⟦i:tree⟧, ⟦b:dōs⟧, ⟦i:dowry⟧. ⟦b:ōs⟧, ⟦b:ōris⟧, ⟦i:mouth⟧, ⟦i:face⟧, is neuter, also ⟦b:os⟧, ⟦b:ossis⟧, ⟦i:bone⟧.

title: Feminine
text:
⟦#577⟧
Parisyllables in ⟦b:-ēs⟧, and substantives in ⟦b:-ās⟧, ⟦b:-aus⟧, ⟦b:-is⟧, ⟦b:-s⟧ preceded by a consonant, and ⟦b:-x⟧, are feminine: as,
⟦b:nūbēs⟧, ⟦i:cloud⟧; ⟦b:aetās⟧, ⟦i:age⟧; ⟦b:laus⟧, ⟦i:praise⟧; ⟦b:nāvis⟧, ⟦i:ship⟧; ⟦b:urbs⟧, ⟦i:city⟧; ⟦b:pāx⟧, ⟦i:peace⟧.
⟦#578⟧
⟦b:ās⟧, ⟦b:assis⟧, ⟦i:penny⟧, is masculine. ⟦b:vās⟧, ⟦i:vessel⟧, ⟦i:utensil⟧, and the defectives ⟦b:fās⟧, ⟦i:right⟧, and ⟦b:nefās⟧, ⟦i:wrong⟧, are neuter.
⟦#579⟧
Substantives in ⟦b:-nis⟧ are masculine; also twenty-nine others in ⟦b:-is⟧, as follows:
⟦b:axis⟧, ⟦b:callis⟧, ⟦b:caulis⟧, ⟦b:anguis⟧,  ⟦i:axle⟧, ⟦i:path⟧, ⟦i:cabbage⟧, ⟦i:snake⟧
⟦b:fascis⟧, ⟦b:fūstis⟧, ⟦b:lapis⟧, ⟦b:sanguī̆s⟧,  ⟦i:bundle⟧, ⟦i:club⟧, ⟦i:stone⟧, ⟦i:blood⟧
⟦b:piscis⟧, ⟦b:postis⟧, ⟦b:pulvī̆s⟧, ⟦b:ēnsis⟧,  ⟦i:fish⟧, ⟦i:post⟧, ⟦i:dust⟧, ⟦i:glaive⟧
⟦b:torquis⟧, ⟦b:torris⟧, ⟦b:unguis⟧, ⟦b:mēnsis⟧,  ⟦i:twisted collar⟧, ⟦i:firebrand⟧, ⟦i:nail⟧, ⟦i:month⟧
⟦b:vectis⟧, ⟦b:vermis⟧, ⟦b:vōmis⟧, ⟦b:collis⟧,  ⟦i:lever⟧, ⟦i:worm⟧, ⟦i:ploughshare⟧, ⟦i:hill⟧
⟦b:glīs⟧, ⟦b:canālis⟧, also ⟦b:follis⟧,  ⟦i:dormouse⟧, ⟦i:conduit⟧, ⟦i:ball⟧
⟦b:cassēs⟧, ⟦b:sentēs⟧, ⟦b:veprēs⟧, ⟦b:orbis⟧,  ⟦i:nets⟧, ⟦i:brambles⟧, ⟦i:thorns⟧, plurals, ⟦i:circle⟧
⟦b:cucumis⟧, and sometimes ⟦b:corbis⟧.  ⟦i:cucumber⟧, ⟦i:basket⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:būrim⟧, ⟦i:ploughtail⟧, accusative only, is also masculine. A few of the above are sometimes feminine: as, ⟦b:amnis⟧, ⟦b:anguis⟧, ⟦b:callis⟧, ⟦b:canālis⟧, ⟦b:cinis⟧, ⟦b:fīnis⟧, ⟦b:fūnis⟧, ⟦b:torquis⟧, ⟦b:veprēs⟧, &c.
⟦#580⟧
Four in ⟦b:-s⟧ preceded by a consonant are masculine: ⟦b:dēns⟧, ⟦i:tooth⟧, ⟦b:fōns⟧, ⟦i:fountain⟧, ⟦b:pōns⟧, ⟦i:bridge⟧, ⟦b:mōns⟧, ⟦i:mountain⟧; also factors of twelve: ⟦b:sextāns⟧, ⟦i:one sixth⟧, ⟦b:quadrāns⟧, ⟦b:triēns⟧, ⟦b:dōdrāns⟧, ⟦b:dēxtāns⟧; ⟦b:rudēns⟧, ⟦i:rope⟧, once. ⟦b:adeps⟧, ⟦i:fat⟧, and ⟦b:forceps⟧, ⟦i:pincers⟧, are masculine or feminine. ⟦b:stirps⟧, ⟦i:stock⟧, is sometimes masculine.
⟦#581⟧
⟦b:calix⟧, ⟦i:cup⟧, ⟦b:fornix⟧, ⟦i:arch⟧, and ⟦b:trādux⟧, ⟦i:vinelayer⟧, are masculine; also substantives in ⟦b:-ūnx⟧ and ⟦b:-ex⟧; except ⟦b:nex⟧, ⟦i:murder⟧, and ⟦b:precī⟧, ⟦i:prayer⟧, dative, no nominative, which are feminine; also rarely ⟦b:grex⟧, ⟦i:herd⟧. ⟦b:cortex⟧, ⟦i:bark⟧, ⟦b:forfex⟧, ⟦i:scissors⟧, ⟦b:silex⟧, ⟦i:flint⟧, and ⟦b:obice⟧, ⟦i:barrier⟧, ablative, no nominative, are either masculine or feminine. ⟦b:calx⟧, ⟦i:heel⟧, and ⟦b:calx⟧, ⟦i:lime⟧, are sometimes masculine, also ⟦b:lūx⟧, ⟦i:light⟧, in the ablative in old Latin.

title: Neuter
text:
⟦#582⟧
Substantives in ⟦b:-c⟧, ⟦b:-e⟧, ⟦b:-l⟧, ⟦b:-n⟧, ⟦b:-t⟧, in ⟦b:-ar⟧, ⟦b:-ur⟧, ⟦b:-us⟧, and ⟦b:-ūs⟧, are neuter: as,
⟦b:lac⟧, ⟦i:milk⟧; ⟦b:mare⟧, ⟦i:sea⟧; ⟦b:animal⟧, ⟦i:animal⟧; ⟦b:carmen⟧, ⟦i:song⟧; ⟦b:caput⟧, ⟦i:head⟧; ⟦b:calcar⟧, ⟦i:spur⟧; ⟦b:fulgur⟧, ⟦i:lightning⟧; ⟦b:corpus⟧, ⟦i:body⟧; ⟦b:iūs⟧, ⟦i:right⟧.
⟦#583⟧
⟦b:sōl⟧, ⟦i:sun⟧, ⟦b:pecten⟧, ⟦i:comb⟧, ⟦b:liēn⟧, ⟦i:spleen⟧, ⟦b:rēnēs⟧, ⟦i:kidneys⟧, plural, and ⟦b:furfur⟧, ⟦i:bran⟧, are masculine. So usually ⟦b:sāl⟧, ⟦i:salt⟧, but sometimes neuter in the singular. ⟦b:fār⟧, ⟦i:spelt⟧, is neuter.
⟦#584⟧
⟦b:pecus⟧, ⟦i:beast⟧, is feminine; also ⟦b:tellūs⟧, ⟦i:earth⟧, and the substantives in ⟦b:-ūs⟧ which have ⟦b:-ūdis⟧ (⟦r475:475⟧) or ⟦b:-ūtis⟧ (⟦r477:477⟧) in the genitive: as, ⟦b:palūs⟧, ⟦i:marsh⟧; ⟦b:iuventūs⟧, ⟦i:youth⟧.

title: Stems in -u-
text:
⟦=⟧⟦i:The Fourth Declension.⟧
⟦=⟧Genitive singular ⟦b:-ūs⟧, genitive plural ⟦b:-u-um⟧.
⟦#585⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-u-⟧ are substantive only, and mostly masculine.
⟦#586⟧
There are only three neuters in common use, ⟦b:cornū⟧, ⟦i:horn⟧, ⟦b:genū⟧, ⟦i:knee⟧, and ⟦b:verū⟧, ⟦i:a spit⟧. But some cases of other neuters are used: as, ablative ⟦b:pecū⟧, ⟦i:flock⟧; plural nominative and accusative ⟦b:artua⟧, ⟦i:limbs⟧ (Plaut.); OSSVA, ⟦i:bones⟧ (inscr.).
⟦#587⟧
The nominative of stems in ⟦b:-u-⟧ ends, including the stem vowel, in ⟦b:-u-s⟧ in gender words, and in lengthened ⟦b:-ū⟧ of the stem in neuters.
⟦#588⟧
Most substantives in ⟦b:-u-⟧ are masculines in ⟦b:-tu-⟧ or ⟦b:-su-⟧, often defective in case (⟦r235:235⟧). The following words are feminine: ⟦b:acus⟧, ⟦i:pin⟧, ⟦i:needle⟧, ⟦b:domus⟧, ⟦i:house⟧, ⟦b:manus⟧, ⟦i:hand⟧, ⟦b:porticus⟧, ⟦i:colonnade⟧; ⟦b:tribus⟧, ⟦i:tribe⟧; and the plurals ⟦b:īdūs⟧, ⟦i:ides⟧, and ⟦b:quīnquātrūs⟧, ⟦i:feast of Minerva⟧; rarely ⟦b:penus⟧, ⟦i:store⟧, and ⟦b:specus⟧, ⟦i:cave⟧.
⟦#589⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-u-⟧ are declined as follows:
Examples
Stems ⟦b:flūctus⟧, ⟦i:wave⟧,
⟦b:flūctu-⟧, M. ⟦b:cornū⟧, ⟦i:horn⟧,

title: Stems in -u-: Singular Cases
text:
⟦#590⟧
In the genitive, the uncontracted form ⟦b:-uis⟧ sometimes occurs: as, ⟦b:anuis⟧, ⟦i:old woman⟧ (Ter.). A genitive in ⟦b:-tī⟧ is rather common: as, ⟦b:adventī⟧, ⟦i:arrival⟧; ⟦b:ōrnātī⟧, ⟦i:embellishment⟧ (Ter.); ⟦b:senātī⟧, ⟦i:senate⟧. In the dative, ⟦b:-ū⟧ is regularly found for ⟦b:-uī⟧ in neuters and often in gender words.

title: Stems in -u-: Plural Cases
text:
⟦#591⟧
In the genitive plural, a shorter form in ⟦b:-um⟧ is occasionally found: as, ⟦b:passum⟧, ⟦i:steps⟧ (Plaut., Mart.); ⟦b:currum⟧, ⟦i:chariots⟧ (Verg.); EXERCITVM. The quantity of the ⟦b:u⟧ and the origin of this ending are uncertain.
⟦#592⟧
In the dative and ablative plural, the following retain ⟦b:-u-bus⟧: ⟦b:acus⟧, ⟦i:pin⟧, ⟦i:needle⟧, ⟦b:arcus⟧, ⟦i:bow⟧, ⟦b:partus⟧, ⟦i:birth⟧, ⟦b:tribus⟧, ⟦i:tribe⟧. The following have ⟦b:-u-bus⟧ or ⟦b:-i-bus⟧ (⟦r28:28⟧): ⟦b:artūs⟧, plural, ⟦i:joints⟧, ⟦b:lacus⟧, ⟦i:lake⟧, ⟦b:portus⟧, ⟦i:haven⟧, ⟦b:specus⟧, ⟦i:cave⟧, ⟦b:genū⟧, ⟦i:knee⟧, ⟦b:verū⟧, ⟦i:a spit⟧. All other words have ⟦b:-i-bus⟧ only.
⟦#593⟧
Other case forms are found in inscriptions, as follows:
G. ⟦b:-uos⟧: SENATVOS; ⟦b:-ū⟧ (⟦r66:66⟧) SENATV; ⟦b:-uus⟧, in the imperial age (⟦r29:29, 1⟧): EXERCITVVS. D. ⟦b:-uei⟧ (⟦r29:29, 2⟧): SENATVEI. Ac. ⟦b:-u⟧ (⟦r61:61⟧): MANV. Ab. ⟦b:-uu⟧ (⟦r29:29, 1⟧): ARBITRATVV; ⟦b:-uō⟧, once, by some thought to be for ⟦b:-ūd⟧ (⟦r426:426⟧); MAGISTRATVO. Plural: N. ⟦b:-uus⟧ (⟦r29:29, 1⟧): MAGISTRATVVS.
⟦#594⟧
⟦b:domus⟧, ⟦i:house⟧, F., has stems of two forms, ⟦b:domu-⟧ and ⟦b:domo-⟧ (⟦r401:401⟧); it is declined as follows: N. ⟦b:domus⟧, G. ⟦b:domūs⟧, rarely ⟦b:domī⟧, D. ⟦b:domuī⟧ or ⟦b:domō⟧, Ac. ⟦b:domum⟧, Ab. ⟦b:domō⟧ or ⟦b:domū⟧, Locative ⟦b:domī⟧, rarely ⟦b:domuī⟧. Plural: N. ⟦b:domūs⟧, G. ⟦b:domuum⟧, later ⟦b:domōrum⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:domibus⟧, Ac. ⟦b:domōs⟧, less commonly ⟦b:domūs⟧.
⟦#595⟧
Some other substantives have an ⟦b:-u-⟧ stem in some of their cases, and an ⟦b:-o-⟧ stem in others: see ⟦b:angiportus⟧, ⟦b:arcus⟧, ⟦b:caestus⟧, ⟦b:colus⟧, ⟦b:cornū⟧, ⟦b:cornus⟧, ⟦b:cupressus⟧, ⟦b:fīcus⟧, ⟦b:fretus⟧, ⟦b:gelus⟧, ⟦b:laurus⟧, ⟦b:murtus⟧, ⟦b:penus⟧, ⟦b:pīnus⟧, ⟦b:quercus⟧, ⟦b:rīctus⟧, ⟦b:tonitrus⟧, in the dictionary.

title: Stems in -ē-
text:
⟦=⟧⟦i:The Fifth Declension.⟧
⟦=⟧Genitive singular ⟦b:-ē̆ī⟧, genitive plural ⟦b:-ē-rum⟧.
⟦#596⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-ē-⟧ are substantive only, and feminine.
⟦#597⟧
⟦b:diēs⟧, ⟦i:day⟧, is always masculine in the plural, and commonly in the singular; but the feminine is common when ⟦b:diēs⟧ denotes length of time or a set day. ⟦b:merīdiēs⟧, ⟦i:midday⟧, is masculine and singular only.
⟦#598⟧
The nominative of stems in ⟦b:-ē-⟧ ends, including the stem vowel, in ⟦b:-ē-s⟧.
⟦#599⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-ē-⟧ are of two classes:
⟦#600⟧
(1.) Stems of the first class have one or two syllables; there are four of them: ⟦b:rēs⟧, ⟦i:thing⟧, ⟦b:spēs⟧, ⟦i:hope⟧, ⟦b:diēs⟧, ⟦i:day⟧, and ⟦b:fidēs⟧, ⟦i:faith⟧.
Of this class, ⟦b:rēs⟧ and ⟦b:diēs⟧ have a plural throughout; ⟦b:spēs⟧ has only the nominative and accusative plural, and ⟦b:fidēs⟧ has no plural.
⟦#601⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-ē-⟧ of the first class are declined as follows:
Examples
Stems ⟦b:rēs⟧, ⟦i:thing⟧,
⟦b:rē-⟧, F. ⟦b:diēs⟧, ⟦i:day⟧,
⟦b:diē-⟧, M. Stem and
Singular
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:rēs⟧, ⟦i:a⟧ (or ⟦i:the⟧) ⟦i:thing⟧  ⟦b:diēs⟧  ⟦b:-es⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:rĕ̄i⟧, ⟦b:re͡i⟧, ⟦i:a thing’s⟧, ⟦i:of a thing⟧  ⟦b:diēī⟧, ⟦b:die͡i⟧  ⟦b:-ē̆ī⟧, ⟦b:-ēī⟧, ⟦b:-e͡i⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:rĕ̄i⟧, ⟦b:re͡i⟧, ⟦i:to⟧ or ⟦i:for a thing⟧  ⟦b:diēī⟧, ⟦b:die͡i⟧  ⟦b:-ē̆ī⟧, ⟦b:-ēī⟧, ⟦b:-e͡i⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:rem⟧, ⟦i:a thing⟧  ⟦b:diem⟧  ⟦b:-em⟧
