Plural
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:rēs⟧, (⟦i:the⟧) ⟦i:things⟧  ⟦b:diēs⟧  ⟦b:-ēs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:rērum⟧, ⟦i:things’⟧, ⟦i:of things⟧  ⟦b:diērum⟧  ⟦b:-ērum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:rēbus⟧, ⟦i:to⟧ or ⟦i:for things⟧  ⟦b:diēbus⟧  ⟦b:-ēbus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:rēs⟧, ⟦i:things⟧  ⟦b:diēs⟧  ⟦b:-ēs⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:rēbus⟧, ⟦i:from⟧, ⟦i:with⟧, or ⟦i:by things⟧  ⟦b:diēbus⟧  ⟦b:-ēbus⟧
⟦/⟧
case endings
⟦#602⟧
⟦b:fidēs⟧ is declined like ⟦b:rēs⟧; it has once a genitive ⟦b:fidēs⟧ (Plaut.). For ⟦b:rēī⟧, ⟦b:reī⟧, or ⟦b:re͡i⟧, and ⟦b:fidēī⟧, ⟦b:fideī⟧, or ⟦b:fide͡i⟧, see 127, 4. ⟦b:diēs⟧ has rarely a genitive ⟦b:diēs⟧ (Enn.) or ⟦b:diī⟧ (Verg.). ⟦b:spēs⟧ has only the genitive and dative ⟦b:spe͡i⟧ in verse. A genitive or dative in ⟦b:-ē⟧ is sometimes found: as, ⟦b:rē⟧, ⟦b:diē⟧, ⟦b:fidē⟧.
⟦#603⟧
A few cases of other words sometimes follow this class (⟦r401:401⟧): as, ⟦b:plēbēs⟧ (⟦r524:524⟧), ⟦i:commons⟧, G. ⟦b:plēbe͡i⟧ or ⟦b:plēbī⟧; ⟦b:famēs⟧ (⟦r524:524⟧), ⟦i:hunger⟧, Ab. always ⟦b:famē⟧; ⟦b:requiēs⟧ (⟦r477:477⟧), ⟦i:rest⟧, G. ⟦b:requiē⟧ (Sall.), Ac. ⟦b:requiem⟧, Ab. ⟦b:requiē⟧; ⟦b:tābēs⟧ (⟦r523:523⟧), ⟦i:waste⟧, Ab. ⟦b:tābē⟧, ⟦b:*contāgēs⟧, ⟦i:contact⟧, Ab. ⟦b:contāgē⟧ (Lucr.), &c.
⟦#604⟧
(2.) Stems of the second class are formed by the suffix ⟦b:-iē-⟧ or ⟦b:-tiē-⟧, and have three or more syllables.
This class, which is parallel to stems in ⟦b:-iā-⟧, has usually no genitive, dative, or plural. Many stems, especially those in ⟦b:-tiē-⟧, have also a collateral form in ⟦b:-iā-⟧, and the genitive and dative, when used at all, are commonly from a stem in ⟦b:-iā-⟧.
⟦#605⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-ē-⟧ of the second class are declined as follows:
⟦b:lūxuriēs⟧, ⟦i:extravagance⟧, stem ⟦b:lūxuriē-⟧, F.
⟦i:Nom.⟧ ⟦b:lūxuriēs⟧, ⟦i:Acc.⟧ ⟦b:lūxuriem⟧, ⟦i:Abl.⟧ ⟦b:lūxuriē⟧.
⟦#606⟧
A few examples of the genitive of these stems are found: as, ⟦b:perniciī⟧, ⟦b:perniciēs⟧, or ⟦b:perniciē⟧, ⟦i:ruin⟧ (Cic.); ⟦b:rabiēs⟧, ⟦i:fury⟧ (Lucr.); ⟦b:aciē⟧, ⟦i:edge of battle⟧ (Sall., Caes., auct. B. Afr.), ⟦b:faciē⟧, ⟦i:make⟧ (Plaut., Lucil.), ⟦b:speciē⟧, ⟦i:looks⟧ (Caes.); ⟦b:aciēī⟧ (auct. B. Afr.). And a very few of the dative: as, ⟦b:aciēī⟧ twice (Caes.); ⟦b:perniciēī⟧, ⟦b:perniciī⟧ (Nep.); ⟦b:perniciē⟧ (Liv.).
⟦#607⟧
⟦b:ēluviēs⟧, ⟦i:offscouring⟧, ⟦i:wash⟧, has the nominative of the plural, and ⟦b:glaciēs⟧, ⟦i:ice⟧, has the accusative of the plural. Five words only have the nominative and accusative plural:
⟦b:seriēs⟧, ⟦b:aciēs⟧, ⟦i:row⟧, ⟦i:edge⟧,
⟦b:speciēs⟧, ⟦b:faciēs⟧, ⟦i:look⟧, ⟦i:make⟧,
⟦b:effigiēs⟧, ⟦i:likeness⟧.

title: Inflection of the Noun: The Adjective
text:
⟦#608⟧
Adjectives are declined like substantives, and it has been shown already how their cases are formed. But they differ from substantives in having different forms in some of their cases to denote different genders; it is convenient therefore to put their complete declension together.
⟦#609⟧
Adjective stems end in ⟦b:-o-⟧ and ⟦b:-ā-⟧, in a consonant, or in ⟦b:-i-⟧.
⟦#610⟧
An accusative plural of a stem in ⟦b:-u-⟧, ⟦b:anguimanūs⟧, ⟦i:with a serpent for a hand⟧, is once used (Lucr.). There are no adjective stems in ⟦b:-ē-⟧.
⟦#611⟧
Adjectives are often conveniently said to be ‘⟦i:of three endings⟧,’ ‘⟦i:of two endings⟧,’ or ‘⟦i:of one ending⟧.’
By the ‘ending’ is meant the ending of the nominative singular: thus, ⟦b:bonus⟧, ⟦b:bona⟧, ⟦b:bonum⟧, ⟦i:good⟧, and ⟦b:ācer⟧, ⟦b:ācris⟧, ⟦b:ācre⟧, ⟦i:sharp⟧, are ‘of three endings’ (⟦r409:409⟧); ⟦b:brevis⟧, ⟦b:breve⟧, ⟦i:short⟧, is ‘of two endings’ (⟦r410:410⟧); and ⟦b:audāx⟧, ⟦i:bold⟧, is ‘of one ending’ (⟦r410:410⟧).
⟦#612⟧
Adjectives ‘of one ending’ which form a gender nominative in ⟦b:-s⟧, retain the ⟦b:-s⟧ irrationally in the nominative and accusative neuter singular: as, N. M. and F. ⟦b:audāx⟧, N. and Ac. Ne. also ⟦b:audāx⟧.

title: Stems in -o- and -ā-
text:
⟦#613⟧
Most adjectives with stems in ⟦b:-o-⟧ and ⟦b:-ā-⟧ are declined as follows:
Example
Stems M. ⟦b:bonus⟧, F. ⟦b:bona⟧, Ne. ⟦b:bonum⟧, ⟦i:good⟧
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:bonus⟧  ⟦b:bona⟧  ⟦b:bonum⟧  ⟦b:boni⟧  ⟦b:bonae⟧  ⟦b:bona⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:bonī⟧  ⟦b:bonae⟧  ⟦b:bonī⟧  ⟦b:bonōrum⟧  ⟦b:bonārum⟧  ⟦b:bonōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:bonō⟧  ⟦b:bonae⟧  ⟦b:bonō⟧  ⟦b:bonīs⟧  ⟦b:bonīs⟧  ⟦b:bonīs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:bonum⟧  ⟦b:bonam⟧  ⟦b:bonum⟧  ⟦b:bonōs⟧  ⟦b:bonās⟧  ⟦b:bona⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:bonō⟧  ⟦b:bonā⟧  ⟦b:bonō⟧  ⟦b:bonīs⟧  ⟦b:bonīs⟧  ⟦b:bonīs⟧
⟦i:Voc.⟧  ⟦b:bone⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:bono-⟧, ⟦b:bonā-⟧. Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#614⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-io-⟧ and ⟦b:-iā-⟧ have no consonant ⟦b:i⟧ in cases ending in ⟦b:-i⟧ or ⟦b:-īs⟧ (⟦r153:153, 3⟧): as ⟦b:plēbēius⟧, ⟦i:plebeian⟧, G. S. M. and Ne., and N. Pl. M. ⟦b:plēbēī⟧, D. and Ab. Pl. ⟦b:plēbēīs⟧.
⟦#615⟧
Stems in ⟦b:-ro-⟧ preceded by a long vowel retain ⟦b:-us⟧ in the nominative singular masculine and are declined like ⟦b:bonus⟧ (⟦r453:453⟧): as, ⟦b:sevērus⟧, ⟦i:stern⟧; also
⟦b:ferus⟧, ⟦b:merus⟧, ⟦i:wild⟧, ⟦i:unmixed⟧
⟦b:mōrigerus⟧, ⟦i:complaisant⟧
⟦b:praeposterus⟧, ⟦i:reversed⟧
⟦b:properus⟧, ⟦i:hasty⟧
⟦b:prōsperus⟧, ⟦i:lucky⟧
⟦b:triquetrus⟧, ⟦i:three-cornered⟧
⟦#616⟧
(1.) Some stems in ⟦b:-ro-⟧ preceded by a short vowel end in ⟦b:-r⟧ in the nominative singular masculine and have no vocative (⟦r454:454⟧); they are declined as follows:
Example
Stems M. ⟦b:līber⟧, F. ⟦b:lībera⟧, Ne. ⟦b:līberum⟧, ⟦i:free⟧,
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:līber⟧  ⟦b:lībera⟧  ⟦b:līberum⟧  ⟦b:līberī⟧  ⟦b:līberae⟧  ⟦b:lībera⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:līberī⟧  ⟦b:līberae⟧  ⟦b:līberī⟧  ⟦b:līberōrum⟧  ⟦b:līberārum⟧  ⟦b:līberōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:līberō⟧  ⟦b:līberae⟧  ⟦b:līberō⟧  ⟦b:līberīs⟧  ⟦b:līberīs⟧  ⟦b:līberīs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:līberum⟧  ⟦b:līberam⟧  ⟦b:līberum⟧  ⟦b:līberōs⟧  ⟦b:līberās⟧  ⟦b:lībera⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:līberō⟧  ⟦b:līberā⟧  ⟦b:līberō⟧  ⟦b:līberīs⟧  ⟦b:līberīs⟧  ⟦b:līberīs⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:lībero-⟧, ⟦b:līberā-⟧. Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
Such are: compounds, chiefly poetical, ending in ⟦b:-fer⟧ and ⟦b:-ger⟧, ⟦i:bearing⟧, ⟦i:carrying⟧, ⟦i:having⟧: as, ⟦b:caelifer⟧, ⟦i:heaven-upholding⟧; ⟦b:corniger⟧, ⟦i:horned⟧; also the following:
(⟦b:alter⟧, ⟦r618:618⟧), ⟦b:asper⟧, ⟦i:other⟧, ⟦i:rough⟧
⟦b:lacer⟧, ⟦b:līber⟧, ⟦i:torn⟧, ⟦i:free⟧
⟦b:gibber⟧, ⟦b:miser⟧, ⟦i:hump-backed⟧, ⟦i:forlorn⟧
⟦b:satur⟧, ⟦b:sēmifer⟧, ⟦i:full⟧, ⟦i:half-beast⟧
⟦b:tener⟧, ⟦b:Trēver⟧, ⟦i:tender⟧, ⟦i:Treveran⟧
⟦b:dexter⟧, ⟦i:right⟧, has ⟦b:dextera⟧, ⟦b:dexterum⟧, or ⟦b:dextra⟧, ⟦b:dextrum⟧, G. ⟦b:dexterī⟧, or ⟦b:dextrī⟧, &c. ⟦b:sinister⟧, ⟦i:left⟧, has usually ⟦b:sinistra⟧, &c., rarely ⟦b:sinisteram⟧ (Plaut., Ter.). ⟦b:asper⟧ has a plural accusative ⟦b:asprōs⟧ (Stat.), and ablative ⟦b:asprīs⟧ (Verg.).
⟦#617⟧
(2.) Other stems in ⟦b:-ro-⟧ have a vowel before ⟦b:r⟧ only in the nominative singular masculine ⟦b:-er⟧ (⟦r454:454⟧); they are declined as follows:
Example
Stems M. ⟦b:aeger⟧, F. ⟦b:aegra⟧, Ne. ⟦b:aegrum⟧, ⟦i:ill⟧,
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:aeger⟧  ⟦b:aegra⟧  ⟦b:aegrum⟧  ⟦b:aegrī⟧  ⟦b:aegrae⟧  ⟦b:aegra⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:aegrī⟧  ⟦b:aegrae⟧  ⟦b:aegrī⟧  ⟦b:aegrōrum⟧  ⟦b:aegrārum⟧  ⟦b:aegrōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:aegrō⟧  ⟦b:aegrae⟧  ⟦b:aegrō⟧  ⟦b:aegrīs⟧  ⟦b:aegrīs⟧  ⟦b:aegrīs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:aegrum⟧  ⟦b:aegram⟧  ⟦b:aegrum⟧  ⟦b:aegrōs⟧  ⟦b:aegrās⟧  ⟦b:aegra⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:aegrō⟧  ⟦b:aegrā⟧  ⟦b:aegrō⟧  ⟦b:aegrīs⟧  ⟦b:aegrīs⟧  ⟦b:aegrīs⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:aegro-⟧, ⟦b:aegrā-⟧. Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#618⟧
Nine adjectives or adjective pronouns have the pronoun form ⟦b:-ī̆us⟧ in the genitive singular and ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the dative singular, for masculine, feminine, and neuter alike; they are the following:
⟦b:alius⟧, ⟦i:another⟧
⟦b:sōlus⟧, ⟦i:alone⟧
⟦b:tōtus⟧, ⟦i:whole⟧
⟦b:ūnus⟧, ⟦i:one⟧
⟦b:ūllus⟧, ⟦i:any at all⟧
⟦b:nūllus⟧, ⟦i:no⟧
⟦b:alter⟧, ⟦i:the other⟧
⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦i:which of the two⟧
⟦b:neuter⟧, ⟦i:neither⟧
⟦#619⟧
Of the above words, those with the nominative in ⟦b:-us⟧ are declined like ⟦b:ūnus⟧ (⟦r638:638⟧). But ⟦b:alius⟧ has N. and Ac. Ne. ⟦b:aliud⟧ (⟦r659:659⟧); for the G., ⟦b:alterī̆us⟧ is mostly used, except in the combination ⟦b:alīus modī⟧, ⟦i:of another sort⟧; the N. M. is rarely ⟦b:alis⟧, Ne. ⟦b:alid⟧, D. rarely ⟦b:alī⟧. ⟦b:alter⟧ is declined like ⟦b:līber⟧ (⟦r616:616⟧), except in the genitive singular ⟦b:alterī̆us⟧ (⟦r127:127, 6⟧) and dative ⟦b:alterī⟧. For ⟦b:uter⟧ and its derivatives, see ⟦r693:693⟧.
⟦#620⟧
The ordinary genitive and dative of ⟦b:-o-⟧ and ⟦b:-ā-⟧ stems, from some of the above words, is sometimes found: G. and D. ⟦b:aliae⟧, ⟦b:sōlae⟧, ⟦b:alterae⟧, D. ⟦b:aliō⟧, ⟦b:alterae⟧, &c.

title: Consonant Stems: Of Two Endings
text:
⟦#621⟧
The only consonant stems of two endings are comparatives (⟦r346:346⟧); they are declined as follows:
Example
Stems M. and F. ⟦b:trīstior⟧, Ne. ⟦b:trīstius⟧, ⟦i:sadder⟧,
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:trīstior⟧  ⟦b:trīstius⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōrēs⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōra⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōris⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōris⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōrum⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōrī⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōrī⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōribus⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōribus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōrem⟧  ⟦b:trīstius⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōres⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōra⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōre⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōre⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōribus⟧  ⟦b:trīstiōribus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:trīstiōr-⟧, ⟦b:trīstius-⟧. Singular. Plural. Masc. and Fem. Neut. Masc. and Fem. Neut.
⟦#622⟧
The ablative rarely has ⟦b:-ī⟧ for ⟦b:-e⟧: as, ⟦b:meliōrī⟧ (⟦r503:503⟧); the accusative plural masculine and feminine rarely have ⟦b:-īs⟧: as, ⟦b:meliōrīs⟧ (⟦r505:505⟧).
⟦#623⟧
⟦b:plūs⟧, ⟦i:more⟧, has in the singular only Ne. N. and Ac. ⟦b:plūs⟧, G. ⟦b:plūris⟧, and Ab. ⟦b:plūre⟧. Plural: N. M. and F. ⟦b:plūrēs⟧, Ne. ⟦b:plūra⟧, G. ⟦b:plūrium⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:plūribus⟧, Ac. M. and F. ⟦b:plūrēs⟧ or ⟦b:plūrīs⟧, Ne. ⟦b:plūra⟧. ⟦b:complūrēs⟧, ⟦i:a good many⟧, plural only, has N. M. and F. ⟦b:complūrēs⟧, Ne. N. and Ac. ⟦b:complūria⟧ or ⟦b:complūra⟧, G. ⟦b:complūrium⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:complūribus⟧, Ac. M. and F. ⟦b:complūrēs⟧ or ⟦b:complūrīs⟧.

title: Consonant Stems: Of One Ending
text:
⟦#624⟧
A dozen adjectives ‘of one ending,’ mostly words applying to persons, with consonant stems throughout, have no nominative or accusative neuter plural; they are:
⟦b:caelebs⟧, ⟦b:compos⟧, ⟦i:unmarried⟧, ⟦i:master of⟧
⟦b:*dēses⟧, ⟦b:dīves⟧, ⟦i:lazy⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧
⟦b:particeps⟧, ⟦b:prīnceps⟧, ⟦i:sharing⟧, ⟦i:first⟧
⟦b:pūbēs⟧, ⟦b:impūbēs⟧, ⟦i:mangrown⟧, ⟦i:immature⟧
⟦b:sōspes⟧, ⟦b:superstes⟧, ⟦i:safe⟧, ⟦i:surviving⟧
⟦b:pauper⟧, ⟦b:cicur⟧, ⟦i:poor⟧, ⟦i:tame⟧
⟦#625⟧
When these adjectives have a neuter, it is the same as the gender forms, except in the accusative singular; they are declined as follows:
M. F. and Ne. ⟦b:dīves⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧, stem ⟦b:dīvit-⟧.
Singular: N. ⟦b:dīves⟧, G. ⟦b:dīvitis⟧, D. ⟦b:dīvitī⟧, Ac. M. and F. ⟦b:dīvitem⟧, Ne. ⟦b:dīves⟧, Ab. ⟦b:dīvite⟧. Plural: N. and Ac. M. and F. ⟦b:dīvitēs⟧, G. ⟦b:dīvitum⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:dīvitibus⟧.
⟦#626⟧
The plural ⟦b:caelitēs⟧, ⟦i:heavenly⟧, ⟦i:occupants of heaven⟧, is also declined like the plural of ⟦b:dīves⟧; the singular Ab. ⟦b:caelite⟧ occurs a couple of times. ⟦b:vetus⟧, ⟦i:old⟧, G. ⟦i:veteris⟧, is also declined like ⟦b:dīves⟧, but has a Ne. Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:vetera⟧; the Ab. S. is regularly ⟦b:vetere⟧, but ⟦b:veterī⟧ is sometimes used.

title: Stems in -i-: Of Three Endings
text:
⟦#627⟧
A dozen adjectives with stems in ⟦b:-bri-⟧, ⟦b:-cri-⟧, or ⟦b:-tri-⟧, have a distinctive form in ⟦b:-er⟧ for the masculine nominative singular; they are:
⟦b:celeber⟧, ⟦i:thronged⟧
⟦b:salūber⟧, ⟦i:healthy⟧
⟦b:ācer⟧, ⟦i:keen⟧
⟦b:alacer⟧, ⟦i:lively⟧
⟦b:volucer⟧, ⟦i:winged⟧
⟦b:campester⟧, ⟦i:of a plain⟧
⟦b:equester⟧, ⟦i:cavalry-⟧
⟦b:palūster⟧, ⟦i:of a swamp⟧
⟦b:pedester⟧, ⟦i:foot-⟧
⟦b:puter⟧, ⟦i:rotten⟧
⟦b:silvester⟧, ⟦i:woody⟧
⟦b:terrester⟧, ⟦i:land-⟧
So also ⟦b:celer⟧, swift. The names of months, ⟦b:September⟧, ⟦b:Octōber⟧, ⟦b:November⟧, ⟦b:December⟧, are also adjectives with stems in ⟦b:-bri-⟧, but are not used in the neuter. Other adjectives with stems in ⟦b:-bri-⟧, ⟦b:-cri-⟧, or ⟦b:-tri-⟧, have no distinctive form for the masculine nominative singular: as, ⟦b:muliebris⟧, ⟦b:mediocris⟧, ⟦b:inlūstris⟧.
⟦#628⟧
These adjectives are declined as follows:
Example
Stem M. ⟦b:ācer⟧, F. ⟦b:ācris⟧, Ne. ⟦b:ācre⟧, ⟦i:sharp⟧
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:ācer⟧  ⟦b:ācris⟧  ⟦b:ācre⟧  ⟦b:ācres⟧  ⟦b:ācres⟧  ⟦b:ācria⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:ācris⟧  ⟦b:ācris⟧  ⟦b:ācris⟧  ⟦b:ācrium⟧  ⟦b:ācrium⟧  ⟦b:ācrium⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:ācrī⟧  ⟦b:ācrī⟧  ⟦b:ācrī⟧  ⟦b:ācribus⟧  ⟦b:ācribus⟧  ⟦b:ācribus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:ācrem⟧  ⟦b:ācrem⟧  ⟦b:ācre⟧  ⟦b:ācrīs⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧  ⟦b:acrīs⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧  ⟦b:ācria⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:ācrī⟧  ⟦b:ācrī⟧  ⟦b:ācrī⟧  ⟦b:ācribus⟧  ⟦b:ācribus⟧  ⟦b:ācribus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:ācri-⟧. Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#629⟧
In all cases but the masculine nominative singular these adjectives are just like those in ⟦b:-i-⟧ ‘of two endings’ (⟦r630:630⟧). But the ablative always has ⟦b:-ī⟧, never ⟦b:-e⟧, and the genitive plural always has ⟦b:-ium⟧, never ⟦b:-um⟧. In ⟦b:celer⟧ the second ⟦b:e⟧ belongs to the stem: M. ⟦b:celer⟧, F. ⟦b:celeris⟧, Ne. ⟦b:celere⟧; the genitive plural, which is ⟦b:celerum⟧, is found only as a substantive. Most of these adjectives have now and then a masculine in ⟦b:-is⟧, like adjectives ‘of two endings’ (⟦r630:630⟧), and in old Latin the nominative ⟦b:-er⟧ is rarely feminine.

title: Stems in -i-: Of Two Endings
text:
⟦#630⟧
Adjectives ‘of two endings’ with stems in ⟦b:-i-⟧ are declined as follows:
Example
Stem M. and F. ⟦b:brevis⟧, Ne. ⟦b:breve⟧, ⟦i:short⟧
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:brevis⟧  ⟦b:breve⟧  ⟦b:brevēs⟧  ⟦b:brevia⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:brevis⟧  ⟦b:brevis⟧  ⟦b:brevium⟧  ⟦b:brevium⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:brevī⟧  ⟦b:brevī⟧  ⟦b:brevibus⟧  ⟦b:brevibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:brevem⟧  ⟦b:breve⟧  ⟦b:brevīs⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧  ⟦b:brevia⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:brevī⟧  ⟦b:brevī⟧  ⟦b:brevibus⟧  ⟦b:brevibus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:brevi-⟧. Singular. Plural. Masc. and Fem. Neut. Masc. and Fem. Neut.
⟦#631⟧
The ablative is sometimes ⟦b:-e⟧ when these adjectives are used substantively or in verse (⟦r558:558⟧). The genitive plural is rarely ⟦b:-um⟧ for ⟦b:-ium⟧ (⟦r563:563⟧).

title: Stems in -i-: Of One Ending
text:
⟦#632⟧
Most adjectives ‘of one ending’ have a consonant form of the stem in the singular, except usually in the ablative (⟦r633:633⟧), and an ⟦b:-i-⟧ stem in the plural; they are declined as follows:
Examples
Stems M. F. and Ne. ⟦b:audāx⟧, ⟦i:bold⟧,
⟦b:audāc(i)-⟧ M. F. Ne. ⟦b:regēns⟧, ⟦i:ruling⟧,
Singular
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:audāx⟧  ⟦b:audāx⟧  ⟦b:regēns⟧  ⟦b:regēns⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:audācis⟧  ⟦b:audācis⟧  ⟦b:regentis⟧  ⟦b:regentis⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:audācī⟧  ⟦b:audācī⟧  ⟦b:regentī⟧  ⟦b:regentī⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:audācem⟧  ⟦b:audāx⟧  ⟦b:regentem⟧  ⟦b:regēns⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:audācī⟧  ⟦b:audācī⟧  ⟦b:regente⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧  ⟦b:regente⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧
Plural
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:audācēs⟧  ⟦b:audācia⟧  ⟦b:regentēs⟧  ⟦b:regentia⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:audācium⟧  ⟦b:audācium⟧  ⟦b:regentium⟧  ⟦b:regentium⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:audācibus⟧  ⟦b:audācibus⟧  ⟦b:regentibus⟧  ⟦b:regentibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:audācīs⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧  ⟦b:audācia⟧  ⟦b:regentīs⟧, ⟦b:-ēs⟧  ⟦b:regentia⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:audācibus⟧  ⟦b:audācibus⟧  ⟦b:regentibus⟧  ⟦b:regentibus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:regent(i)-⟧ Masc. & Fem. Neut. Masc. & Fem. Neut. Masc. & Fem. Neut. Masc. & Fem. Neut.
⟦#633⟧
Present participles have ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the ablative, when they are used as adjectives, otherwise ⟦b:-e⟧ (⟦r560:560⟧). For ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧ in other words, see ⟦r559:559⟧, ⟦r561:561⟧. For ⟦b:-ium⟧ or ⟦b:-um⟧ in the genitive plural, ⟦r563:563⟧.
⟦#634⟧
Most adjectives ‘of one ending’ in ⟦b:-i-⟧ are declined as above (⟦r632:632⟧); some of them have peculiarities in some of their cases, as follows:
⟦#635⟧
(1.) ⟦b:trux⟧ (⟦r531:531⟧), ⟦i:savage⟧, has Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧, G. Pl. ⟦b:-ium⟧, no Ne. Pl. N. or Ac. ⟦b:redux⟧ (⟦r531:531⟧), ⟦i:returning⟧, has Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧ or ⟦b:-e⟧, no G. Pl. or Ne. Pl. N. or Ac. ⟦b:hebes⟧, ⟦i:dull⟧, ⟦b:teres⟧, ⟦i:cylindrical⟧ (⟦r533:533⟧), and compounds of ⟦b:caput⟧, ⟦i:head⟧, as ⟦b:anceps⟧, (⟦r533:533⟧), ⟦i:two-headed⟧, have Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, no G. Pl.; a Ne. Pl. N. or Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧ is rare. For ⟦b:locuplēs⟧, ⟦i:rich⟧, see ⟦r533:533⟧.
⟦#636⟧
(2.) The following have ⟦b:-ī⟧ in the ablative, but ⟦b:-um⟧ of consonant stems in the genitive plural, and no nominative or accusative neuter plural: ⟦b:inops⟧ (⟦r535:535⟧), ⟦i:without means⟧, ⟦b:vigil⟧ (⟦r536:536⟧), ⟦i:wide-awake⟧, ⟦b:memor⟧ (⟦r537:537⟧), ⟦i:remembering⟧, ⟦b:dēgener⟧, ⟦i:degenerate⟧, ūber (⟦r537:537⟧), ⟦i:prolific⟧, has Ab. ⟦b:-ī⟧, twice ⟦b:-e⟧, Ne. Pl. once ⟦b:-a⟧ (Acc.). Compounds of ⟦b:pēs⟧, as, ⟦b:bipēs⟧ (⟦r532:532⟧), ⟦i:two-legged⟧, have a late and rare Ne. Pl. N. and Ac. ⟦b:-ia⟧.

title: The Numeral Adjective
text:
⟦#637⟧
Of the cardinals, ⟦b:ūnus⟧, ⟦b:duo⟧, ⟦b:trēs⟧, and the hundreds except ⟦b:centum⟧ are declined. The other cardinals are not declined.
⟦#638⟧
⟦b:ūnus⟧, ⟦i:one⟧, is declined as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:ūnus⟧  ⟦b:ūna⟧  ⟦b:ūnum⟧  ⟦b:ūnī⟧  ⟦b:ūnae⟧  ⟦b:ūna⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:ūnīus⟧  ⟦b:ūnīus⟧  ⟦b:ūnīus⟧  ⟦b:ūnōrum⟧  ⟦b:ūnārum⟧  ⟦b:ūnōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:ūnī⟧  ⟦b:ūnī⟧  ⟦b:ūnī⟧  ⟦b:ūnīs⟧  ⟦b:ūnīs⟧  ⟦b:ūnīs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:ūnum⟧  ⟦b:ūnam⟧  ⟦b:ūnum⟧  ⟦b:ūnōs⟧  ⟦b:ūnās⟧  ⟦b:ūna⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:ūnō⟧  ⟦b:ūnā⟧  ⟦b:ūnō⟧  ⟦b:ūnīs⟧  ⟦b:ūnīs⟧  ⟦b:ūnīs⟧
⟦/⟧
Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
In verse, the genitive singular is often ⟦b:ūnius⟧.
⟦#639⟧
⟦b:duo⟧, ⟦i:two⟧, and ⟦b:trēs⟧, ⟦i:three⟧, are declined as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:duo⟧  ⟦b:duae⟧  ⟦b:duo⟧  ⟦b:trēs⟧  ⟦b:tria⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:duōrum⟧  ⟦b:duārum⟧  ⟦b:duōrum⟧  ⟦b:trium⟧  ⟦b:trium⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:duōbus⟧  ⟦b:duābus⟧  ⟦b:duōbus⟧  ⟦b:tribus⟧  ⟦b:tribus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:duo⟧ or ⟦b:duōs⟧  ⟦b:duās⟧  ⟦b:duo⟧  ⟦b:trēs⟧ or ⟦b:trīs⟧  ⟦b:tria⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:duōbus⟧  ⟦b:duābus⟧  ⟦b:duōbus⟧  ⟦b:tribus⟧  ⟦b:tribus⟧
⟦/⟧
Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. & Fem. Neut.
⟦#640⟧
In dramatic verse, ⟦b:du͡o⟧, &c., is common. In the genitive plural, ⟦b:duo⟧ sometimes has ⟦b:duū̆m⟧ (⟦r462:462⟧). ⟦b:ambō⟧, ⟦i:both⟧, is declined like ⟦b:duo⟧, but has ⟦b:-ō⟧ in the nominative and accusative, and only ⟦b:ambōrum⟧ and ⟦b:ambārum⟧ in the genitive plural. For the forms ⟦b:duo⟧, ⟦b:ambō⟧, see ⟦r415:415⟧; ⟦b:duōbus⟧, ⟦b:duābus⟧, ⟦r464:464⟧, ⟦r442:442⟧.
⟦#641⟧
Hundreds are declined like the plural of ⟦b:bonus⟧ (⟦r613:613⟧): as, ⟦b:ducentī⟧, ⟦b:ducentae⟧, ⟦b:ducenta⟧, ⟦i:two hundred⟧, G. ⟦b:ducentōrum⟧ or ⟦b:ducentū̆m⟧ (⟦r462:462⟧), &c.
⟦#642⟧
The adjective ⟦b:mīlle⟧, ⟦i:thousand⟧, is not declined. The substantive has in the singular only N. Ac. Ab. ⟦b:mīlle⟧, or Ab. ⟦b:mīllī⟧; plural: N. and Ac. ⟦b:mīllia⟧ (⟦b:mīlia⟧), G. ⟦b:mīllium⟧ (⟦b:mīlium⟧), D. and Ab. ⟦b:mīllibus⟧ (⟦b:mīlibus⟧).
⟦#643⟧
Ordinals, as ⟦b:prīmus⟧, ⟦i:first⟧, and distributives, as ⟦b:bīnī⟧, ⟦i:two each⟧, are declined like ⟦b:bonus⟧ (⟦r613:613⟧). But distributives seldom have a singular, and often have the genitive plural ⟦b:-ū̆m⟧ (⟦r462:462⟧): as, ⟦b:bīnū̆m⟧.

title: The Personal and Reflexive Pronoun
text:
⟦#644⟧
The pronoun of the first person, ⟦b:ego⟧, ⟦i:I⟧, of the second person, ⟦b:tū⟧, ⟦i:thou⟧, and the reflexive pronoun, ⟦b:suī⟧, ⟦b:sē⟧, ⟦i:himself⟧, ⟦i:herself⟧, ⟦i:itself⟧, ⟦i:themselves⟧, are declined as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:ego⟧  ⟦b:nōs⟧  ⟦b:tū⟧  ⟦b:vōs⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:meī⟧  ⟦b:nostrum, -trī⟧  ⟦b:tuī⟧  ⟦b:vestrū̆m, -trī⟧  ⟦b:suī⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:mihī̆, mi⟧  ⟦b:nōbīs⟧  ⟦b:tibī̆⟧  ⟦b:vōbīs⟧  ⟦b:sibī̆⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:mē⟧  ⟦b:nōs⟧  ⟦b:tē⟧  ⟦b:vōs⟧  ⟦b:sē⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:mē⟧  ⟦b:nōbīs⟧  ⟦b:tē⟧  ⟦b:vōbīs⟧  ⟦b:sē⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:ego⟧, ⟦i:I⟧ ⟦b:tu⟧, ⟦i:thou⟧ ⟦b:sui⟧, ⟦i:self⟧ Sing. Plur. Sing. Plur. Sing. & Plur.
⟦#645⟧
The nominatives ⟦b:ego⟧ and ⟦b:tū⟧, and the accusatives ⟦b:mē⟧, ⟦b:tē⟧ and ⟦b:sē⟧, have no case ending. The last vowel of ⟦b:ego⟧ is rarely long in Plautus, long or short in Lucilius. The nominative ego has a different stem from that of its other cases, and the plurals of ⟦b:ego⟧ and ⟦b:tū⟧ have a different stem from that of the singular.
⟦#646⟧
⟦b:meī⟧, ⟦b:tuī⟧, and ⟦b:suī⟧, which are often monosyllables in old verse, were originally the genitive of the neuter possessives, used substantively. An old genitive ⟦b:mīs⟧ is quoted, and ⟦b:tīs⟧ occurs rarely in Plautus.
⟦#647⟧
The relation of the ending ⟦b:-bīs⟧ in ⟦b:vōbīs⟧ to ⟦b:-bī̆⟧ in ⟦b:tibī̆⟧ may be due to analogy with ⟦b:illīs, illī⟧. ⟦b:nōbīs⟧ is formed after ⟦b:vōbīs⟧.
⟦#648⟧
In old Latin, the ablative is ⟦b:mēd, tēd, sēd⟧ (⟦r426:426⟧), which forms are also used irrationally for the accusative. But by Terence’s time the ⟦b:-d⟧ was no longer used (⟦r143:143⟧).
⟦#649⟧
Older forms for ⟦b:vestrū̆m⟧ and ⟦b:vestrī⟧ are ⟦b:vostrūm⟧ and ⟦b:vostrī⟧. The genitive plural was originally a genitive of the possessive: that in ⟦b:-ī⟧ being the neuter singular, that in ⟦b:-ū̆m⟧ the masculine or feminine plural. In old Latin, ⟦b:nostrōrum⟧, ⟦b:nostrārum⟧, ⟦b:vostrōrum⟧, ⟦b:vostrārum⟧ also occur.
⟦#650⟧
Emphasis is given (1.) by reduplication (⟦r189:189⟧): Ac. and Ab. ⟦b:mēmē⟧, ⟦b:tētē⟧, rare; ⟦b:sēsē⟧, very common. (2.) by ⟦b:-te⟧ added to the N. of ⟦b:tū⟧: ⟦b:tūte⟧. (3.) by ⟦b:-met⟧ added to any case but the genitive plural: as, ⟦b:egomet⟧; but ⟦b:tū⟧ has only ⟦b:tūtemet⟧ or ⟦b:tūtimet⟧.
⟦#651⟧
In inscriptions, the datives MIHEI, TIBEI, and SIBEI occur, so written in verse sometimes even when the last syllable is short; and MIHE, TIBE. Plural: D. and Ab. VOBEIS. Ac. ENOS in an old hymn; SEESE (⟦r29:29, 1⟧).

title: The Personal and Reflexive Possessive
text:
⟦#652⟧
The possessives of ⟦b:ego⟧, ⟦b:tū⟧, and ⟦b:suī⟧, are ⟦b:meus⟧, ⟦i:mine⟧, ⟦b:tuus⟧, ⟦i:thine⟧, and ⟦b:suus⟧, ⟦i:his, her, its, their⟧ (⟦i:own⟧), declined like ⟦b:bonus⟧ (⟦r613:613⟧), except that ⟦b:meus⟧ has ⟦b:mī⟧ in the vocative singular masculine (⟦r459:459⟧); those of ⟦b:nōs⟧ and ⟦b:vōs⟧ are ⟦b:noster⟧, ⟦i:our⟧, and ⟦b:voster⟧, later ⟦b:vester⟧, ⟦i:your⟧, declined like ⟦b:aeger⟧ (⟦r617:617⟧).
⟦#653⟧
Old forms are ⟦b:tuos⟧, ⟦b:tuom⟧, and ⟦b:suos⟧, ⟦b:suom⟧ (⟦r452:452⟧). In old verse ⟦b:me͡us⟧, ⟦b:me͡i⟧, &c., ⟦b:tu͡os⟧, ⟦b:tu͡i⟧, &c., ⟦b:su͡os⟧, ⟦b:su͡i⟧, &c., often occur. ⟦b:sōs⟧ for ⟦b:suōs⟧, ⟦b:sās⟧ for ⟦b:suās⟧, and ⟦b:sīs⟧ for ⟦b:suīs⟧, are old and rare.
⟦#654⟧
Other case forms are found in inscriptions, as follows:
MEEIS, MIEIS, monosyllable; TOVAM; SVEI, SOVOM, SOVO, SVVO, SOVEIS, SVEIS, SVIEIS.
⟦#655⟧
Emphasis is given (1.) by ⟦b:-met⟧ added to ⟦b:suō⟧, ⟦b:suā⟧, ⟦b:suōs⟧, and to ⟦b:mea⟧ and ⟦b:sua⟧, neuter plural: as, ⟦b:suōmet⟧; (2.) by ⟦b:-pte⟧, which is oftenest found with the ablative: as, ⟦b:suōpte⟧.

title: Other Pronouns
text:
⟦#656⟧
Some pronouns have a peculiar genitive singular in ⟦b:-ī̆us⟧ and dative singular in ⟦b:-ī⟧, for masculine, feminine, and neuter alike.
These are: ⟦b:iste⟧, ⟦b:ille⟧, ⟦b:ipse⟧, ⟦b:uter⟧, and their derivatives. Some other words of a pronoun character also have this form of the genitive and dative: see ⟦r618:618⟧.
⟦#657⟧
In verse, the ⟦b:-ī-⟧ of the genitive is often shortened, and always in ⟦b:utriusque⟧; but ⟦b:neutrīus⟧ is not found with short i. In dramatic verse, the genitive singular of ⟦b:iste⟧, ⟦b:ille⟧, or ⟦b:ipse⟧, is often two syllables.
⟦#658⟧
⟦b:hīc⟧, is, ⟦b:quī⟧ or ⟦b:quis⟧, and their derivatives have the genitive singular in ⟦b:-ius⟧, thus: ⟦b:huius⟧, ⟦b:eius⟧, and ⟦b:quoius⟧ or ⟦b:cuius⟧; in dramatic verse, these genitives are often one syllable. Their datives are ⟦b:huic⟧ for ⟦b:hoice⟧, ⟦b:ē̆ī⟧ or ⟦b:e͡i⟧, and ⟦b:quoi⟧ or ⟦b:cui⟧.
⟦#659⟧
Six words have a peculiar neuter nominative and accusative singular in ⟦b:-d⟧: ⟦b:id⟧, ⟦b:illud⟧, ⟦b:istud⟧, ⟦b:quid⟧, ⟦b:quod⟧, ⟦b:aliud⟧, and derivatives. In manuscripts, ⟦b:-t⟧ is sometimes found for ⟦b:-d⟧: as, ⟦b:it⟧, ⟦b:illut⟧, ⟦b:istut⟧, &c.; sometimes also in inscriptions of the empire. In ⟦b:hoc⟧ for ⟦b:*hod-ce⟧ and in ⟦b:istuc⟧ and ⟦b:illuc⟧ for ⟦b:*istud-ce⟧, ⟦b:*illud-ce⟧, the ⟦b:d⟧ has vanished (166, 1; ⟦r171:171, 1⟧).

title: The Demonstrative Pronoun
text:
⟦#660⟧
The demonstrative pronouns are ⟦b:hīc⟧, ⟦i:this⟧, ⟦i:this near me⟧; ⟦b:iste⟧, ⟦b:istic⟧, ⟦i:that⟧, ⟦i:that near you⟧; and ⟦b:ille⟧, ⟦b:illic⟧, ⟦i:yonder⟧, ⟦i:that⟧.
⟦#661⟧
The demonstrative pronoun ⟦b:hīc⟧, ⟦i:this⟧, ⟦i:this near me⟧, is declined as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:hīc⟧  ⟦b:haec⟧  ⟦b:hoc⟧  ⟦b:hī⟧  ⟦b:hae⟧  ⟦b:haec⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:huius⟧  ⟦b:huius⟧  ⟦b:huius⟧  ⟦b:hōrum⟧  ⟦b:hārum⟧  ⟦b:hōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:huic⟧  ⟦b:huic⟧  ⟦b:huic⟧  ⟦b:hīs⟧  ⟦b:hīs⟧  ⟦b:hīs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:hunc⟧  ⟦b:hanc⟧  ⟦b:hoc⟧  ⟦b:hōs⟧  ⟦b:hās⟧  ⟦b:haec⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:hōc⟧  ⟦b:hāc⟧  ⟦b:hōc⟧  ⟦b:hīs⟧  ⟦b:hīs⟧  ⟦b:hīs⟧
⟦/⟧
Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#662⟧
The stem of ⟦b:hīc⟧ is ⟦b:ho-⟧, ⟦b:hā-⟧; to most of its cases a demonstrative ⟦b:-c⟧ for ⟦b:-ce⟧ is attached. The masculine and feminine nominative singular and nominative and accusative neuter plural take an ⟦b:-i-⟧: ⟦b:hīc⟧ for ⟦b:*ho-i-ce⟧ (108, ⟦i:a⟧); ⟦b:haec⟧ for ⟦b:ha-i-ce⟧ (⟦r96:96⟧). ⟦b:hunc⟧, ⟦b:hanc⟧, are for ⟦b:*hom-ce⟧, ⟦b:*ham-ce⟧. For the quantity of the first syllable of ⟦b:huius⟧, see 153, 2; of ⟦b:hoc⟧, ⟦r171:171, 1⟧.
⟦#663⟧
Old forms with the full ending ⟦b:-ce⟧ are rare except after ⟦b:-s⟧: Plural Ne. Acc. ⟦b:haece⟧ (Enn.); G. F. ⟦b:hārumce⟧ (Cato); also G. ⟦b:hōrunc⟧, ⟦b:hārunc⟧ (Pl., T.); ⟦b:hōsce⟧, D. and Ab. ⟦b:hīsce⟧ (Pl., T.). After 100 B.C., the full form ⟦b:-ce⟧ is not found, except occasionally after ⟦b:-s⟧: ⟦b:huiusce⟧, ⟦b:hōsce⟧, ⟦b:hāsce⟧, ⟦b:hīsce⟧. Before ⟦b:-ne⟧ interrogative it is retained in the weakened form ⟦b:-ci-⟧: as, ⟦b:hīcine⟧. But ⟦b:hīcne⟧, ⟦b:hocne⟧, ⟦b:huicne⟧, &c., are found, though rarely.
⟦#664⟧
The nominative ⟦b:hic⟧ or ⟦b:hicine⟧ found in the dramatists and rarely later is probably for ⟦b:*ho-c⟧, ⟦b:*he-c⟧ (103, ⟦i:a⟧). A nominative plural feminine ⟦b:haec⟧ is found in writers of all ages. Other and rare forms are: Pl. N. M. ⟦b:hīsce⟧ (⟦r461:461⟧), D. or Ab. ⟦b:hībus⟧.
⟦#665⟧
Other case forms of ⟦b:hīc⟧ are found in inscriptions, as follows:
N. M. HEC, HIC. G. HOIVS, HVIIVS (⟦r23:23⟧), HVIVS, HOIVSCE, HOIVSQVE, HVIVSQVE. D. HOICE, HOIC, HOI, HVIC, HVI. Ac. M. HONC, HOC; F. HANCE; Ne. HOCE, HVC. Ab. M. and Ne. HOCE; F. HACE, oftener than HAC in republican inscriptions; HAACE (⟦r29:29, 1⟧). Loc. HEICE, HEIC. Plural: N. M. HEISCE, HEIS, or HEI, HISCE or HIS; HI, not before Augustus; Ne. N. and Ac. HAICE, HAECE. G. HORVNC. D. and Ab. HEISCE, HIBVS. Ac. F. HASCE.
⟦#666⟧
The demonstrative pronouns ⟦b:iste⟧, ⟦i:that⟧, ⟦i:that near you⟧, and ⟦b:ille⟧, ⟦i:yonder⟧, are declined alike, as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:ille⟧  ⟦b:illa⟧  ⟦b:illud⟧  ⟦b:illī⟧  ⟦b:illae⟧  ⟦b:illa⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:illī̆us⟧  ⟦b:illī̆us⟧  ⟦b:illī̆us⟧  ⟦b:illōrum⟧  ⟦b:illārum⟧  ⟦b:illōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:illī⟧  ⟦b:illī⟧  ⟦b:illī⟧  ⟦b:illīs⟧  ⟦b:illīs⟧  ⟦b:illīs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:illum⟧  ⟦b:illam⟧  ⟦b:illud⟧  ⟦b:illōs⟧  ⟦b:illās⟧  ⟦b:illa⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:illō⟧  ⟦b:illā⟧  ⟦b:illō⟧  ⟦b:illīs⟧  ⟦b:illīs⟧  ⟦b:illīs⟧
⟦/⟧
Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#667⟧
The first syllable of ⟦b:iste⟧ and ⟦b:ille⟧ is often short in the dramatists. Old forms of ⟦b:iste⟧ are: N. ⟦b:istus⟧, G. ⟦b:istī⟧, in ⟦b:istīmodī⟧, D. F. ⟦b:istae⟧. The initial ⟦b:i⟧ of ⟦b:iste⟧ and of ⟦b:istic⟧ (⟦r669:669⟧), is sometimes not written: as, ⟦b:sta rēs⟧ (Cic.), ⟦b:stūc perīculum⟧ (Ter.). Old forms of ⟦b:ille⟧ are: N. ⟦b:olus⟧ (⟦r81:81⟧); ⟦b:ollus⟧ or ⟦b:olle⟧, &c.: as, D. S. or N. Pl. ⟦b:ollī⟧, D. Pl. ⟦b:ollīs⟧. G. ⟦b:illī⟧, in ⟦b:illīmodī⟧, D. F. ⟦b:illae⟧. The dramatists have ⟦b:eccistam⟧, ⟦b:eccilla⟧, ⟦b:eccillud⟧, ⟦b:eccillum⟧, ⟦b:eccillam⟧, for ⟦b:ecce istam⟧, &c., and ⟦b:ellum⟧, ⟦b:ellam⟧, for ⟦b:em illum⟧, &c.
⟦#668⟧
Other case forms of ille are found in inscriptions, as follows:
D. F. ILLAE. Plural: N. M. ILLEI. G. OLORVM (⟦r81:81⟧). D. and Ab. OLLEIS, ILLEIS.
⟦#669⟧
⟦b:istic⟧ and ⟦b:illic⟧, compounded of ⟦b:iste⟧, ⟦b:ille⟧, and ⟦b:-ce⟧ or ⟦b:-c⟧, are declined alike, as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:illic⟧  ⟦b:illaec⟧  ⟦b:illuc⟧  ⟦b:illīc⟧  ⟦b:illaec⟧  ⟦b:illaec⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:illunc⟧  ⟦b:illanc⟧  ⟦b:illuc⟧  ⟦b:illōsce⟧  ⟦b:illāsce⟧  ⟦b:illaec⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:illōc⟧  ⟦b:illāc⟧  ⟦b:illōc⟧  ⟦b:illīsce⟧  ⟦b:illīsce⟧  ⟦b:illīsce⟧
⟦/⟧
Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#670⟧
Rare forms are: N. and Ac. Ne. ⟦b:istoc⟧, ⟦b:illoc⟧, G. ⟦b:illīusce⟧, D. ⟦b:illīc⟧, Ab. F. ⟦b:istāce⟧, ⟦b:illāce⟧. Plural: N. M. ⟦b:illīsce⟧ (⟦r461:461⟧), ⟦b:illīc⟧, Ac. ⟦b:illōsce⟧, ⟦b:illāsce⟧. Before ⟦b:-ne⟧ interrogative, ⟦b:-ce⟧ becomes ⟦b:-ci-⟧: N. ⟦b:illicine⟧, ⟦b:istucine⟧, Ac. ⟦b:illancine⟧, Ab. ⟦b:istōcine⟧, ⟦b:istācinē⟧. Pl. Ac. ⟦b:istōscine⟧.

title: The Determinative Pronoun
text:
⟦#671⟧
The determinative pronoun ⟦b:is⟧, ⟦i:that⟧, ⟦i:the aforesaid⟧, ⟦i:the one⟧, is declined as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:is⟧  ⟦b:ea⟧  ⟦b:id⟧  ⟦b:eī⟧, ⟦b:iī⟧, or ⟦b:ī⟧  ⟦b:eae⟧  ⟦b:ea⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:eius⟧  ⟦b:eius⟧  ⟦b:eius⟧  ⟦b:eōrum⟧  ⟦b:eārum⟧  ⟦b:eōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:ē̆ī⟧  ⟦b:ē̆ī⟧  ⟦b:ē̆ī⟧  ⟦b:eīs⟧, ⟦b:iīs⟧, or ⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:eīs⟧, ⟦b:iīs⟧, or ⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:eīs⟧, ⟦b:iīs⟧, or ⟦b:īs⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:eum⟧  ⟦b:eam⟧  ⟦b:id⟧  ⟦b:eōs⟧  ⟦b:eās⟧  ⟦b:ea⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:eō⟧  ⟦b:eā⟧  ⟦b:eō⟧  ⟦b:eīs⟧, ⟦b:iīs⟧, or ⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:eīs⟧, ⟦b:iīs⟧, or ⟦b:īs⟧  ⟦b:eīs⟧, ⟦b:iīs⟧, or ⟦b:īs⟧
⟦/⟧
Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#672⟧
⟦b:is⟧ and ⟦b:id⟧ (⟦r659:659⟧) are formed from a stem ⟦b:-i-⟧, and the other parts from a stem ⟦b:eo-⟧, ⟦b:eā-⟧. The genitive is sometimes written in Cicero and Plautus ⟦b:eiius⟧; for the quantity of the first syllable of ⟦b:eius⟧, see 153, 2; for ⟦b:ĕ̄i⟧, see 127, 3, and 127, 4.
⟦#673⟧
In old verse, the genitive singular rarely has the first syllable short. Old and rare forms are: D. F. ⟦b:eae⟧, Ac. M. ⟦b:im⟧ or ⟦b:em⟧. Pl. D, and Ab. ⟦b:ī̆bus⟧, F. ⟦b:eābus⟧ (⟦r442:442⟧). In dramatic verse, ⟦b:e͡um⟧, ⟦b:e͡am⟧, ⟦b:e͡i⟧, ⟦b:e͡o⟧, ⟦b:e͡a⟧, and ⟦b:e͡i⟧, ⟦b:e͡orum⟧, ⟦b:e͡arum⟧, ⟦b:e͡os⟧, ⟦b:e͡as⟧, ⟦b:e͡is⟧, are often found; also ⟦b:eccum⟧, ⟦b:eccam⟧, ⟦b:eccōs⟧, ⟦b:eccās⟧, ⟦b:ecca⟧, for ⟦b:ecce eum⟧, &c.
⟦#674⟧
Other case forms of ⟦b:is⟧ are found in inscriptions, as follows:
N. EIS, 124 B.C. G. EIVS, EIIVS, EIIVS or EIIVS (⟦r23:23⟧). D. EIEI, 123 B.C.; EEI, IEI; EI, 123 B.C., and common in all periods. Plural: N. EEIS, EIS, IEIS, till about 50 B.C.; EEI, EI, IEI. D. and Ab. EEIS, EIEIS, IEIS, IS; after the republic, IIS, IIS.
⟦#675⟧
A rare and old pronoun equivalent to ⟦b:is⟧ is ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦b:sam⟧, accusative singular, ⟦b:sōs⟧, accusative plural, and ⟦b:sīs⟧, dative plural.

title: The Pronoun of Identity
text:
⟦#676⟧
The pronoun of identity, ⟦b:īdem⟧, ⟦i:the same⟧, is declined as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:īdem⟧  ⟦b:eadem⟧  ⟦b:idem⟧  ⟦b:eīdem⟧ or ⟦b:īdem⟧  ⟦b:eaedem⟧  ⟦b:eadem⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:eiusdem⟧  ⟦b:eiusdem⟧  ⟦b:eiusdem⟧  ⟦b:eōrundem⟧  ⟦b:eārundem⟧  ⟦b:eōrundem⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:eīdem⟧  ⟦b:eīdem⟧  ⟦b:eīdem⟧  ⟦b:eīsdem⟧ or ⟦b:īsdem⟧  ⟦b:eīsdem⟧ or ⟦b:īsdem⟧  ⟦b:eīsdem⟧ or ⟦b:īsdem⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:eundem⟧  ⟦b:eandem⟧  ⟦b:idem⟧  ⟦b:eōsdem⟧  ⟦b:eāsdem⟧  ⟦b:eadem⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:eōdem⟧  ⟦b:eādem⟧  ⟦b:eōdem⟧  ⟦b:eīsdem⟧ or ⟦b:īsdem⟧  ⟦b:eīsdem⟧ or ⟦b:īsdem⟧  ⟦b:eīsdem⟧ or ⟦b:īsdem⟧
⟦/⟧
Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#677⟧
In manuscripts and editions, the plural nominative masculine is often written ⟦b:iīdem⟧, and the dative and ablative ⟦b:iīsdem⟧. The singular nominative masculine is rarely ⟦b:eisdem⟧ or ⟦b:isdem⟧ (Plaut., Enn.), ⟦b:eidem⟧ (Cic., Varr.), neuter ⟦b:īdem⟧ (Plaut.). In verse, ⟦b:eundem⟧, ⟦b:e͡andem⟧, ⟦b:e͡idem⟧, ⟦b:e͡odem⟧, ⟦b:e͡adem⟧, and ⟦b:e͡idem⟧, ⟦b:e͡aedem⟧, ⟦b:e͡orundem⟧, ⟦b:e͡osdem⟧, ⟦b:e͡asdem⟧, are often found.
⟦#678⟧
Other case forms of ⟦b:īdem⟧ are found in inscriptions, as follows:
N. M. EISDEM, 123 B.C., ISDEM, 59 B.C., both common till Caesar’s time; EIDEM; Ne. EIDEM, 71 B.C. D. IDEM. Plural: N. M. EISDEM, ISDEM, EIDEM, till Caesar’s time; IIDEM, once only. D. and Ab. ISDEM, very rarely IISDEM.

title: The Intensive Pronoun
text:
⟦#679⟧
The intensive pronoun ⟦b:ipse⟧, ⟦i:himself⟧, stems ⟦b:ipso-⟧, ⟦b:ipsā-⟧, is declined like ⟦b:ille⟧ (⟦r666:666⟧), but has the nominative and accusative neuter singular ⟦b:ipsum⟧.
⟦#680⟧
In dramatic verse, ⟦b:ipse⟧ has rarely the first syllable short, and often has the older form ⟦b:ipsus⟧. Plautus has these forms: N. F. ⟦b:eapse⟧, Ac. ⟦b:eumpse⟧, ⟦b:eampse⟧, Ab. ⟦b:eōpse⟧, ⟦b:eāpse⟧, equivalent to ⟦b:ipsa⟧, &c. So ⟦b:reāpse⟧ for ⟦b:rē ipsā⟧.

title: quī AND quis
text:
⟦#681⟧
The stem ⟦b:qui-⟧, or ⟦b:quo-⟧, ⟦b:quā-⟧, is used in three ways: as a relative, ⟦i:who⟧, ⟦i:which⟧; as an interrogative, ⟦i:who? which? what?⟧ as an indefinite, ⟦i:any⟧.
⟦#682⟧
(⟦i:a⟧.) The relative ⟦b:quī⟧, ⟦i:who⟧, ⟦i:which⟧, is declined as follows:
⟦i:Nom.⟧  ⟦b:quī⟧  ⟦b:quae⟧  ⟦b:quod⟧  ⟦b:quī⟧  ⟦b:quae⟧  ⟦b:quae⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:cuius⟧  ⟦b:cuius⟧  ⟦b:cuius⟧  ⟦b:quōrum⟧  ⟦b:quārum⟧  ⟦b:quōrum⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:cui⟧  ⟦b:cui⟧  ⟦b:cui⟧  ⟦b:quibus⟧  ⟦b:quibus⟧  ⟦b:quibus⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:quem⟧  ⟦b:quam⟧  ⟦b:quod⟧  ⟦b:quōs⟧  ⟦b:quās⟧  ⟦b:quae⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:quō⟧  ⟦b:quā⟧  ⟦b:quō⟧  ⟦b:quibus⟧  ⟦b:quibus⟧  ⟦b:quibus⟧
⟦/⟧
Singular. Plural. Masc. Fem. Neut. Masc. Fem. Neut.
⟦#683⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) The interrogative adjective ⟦b:quī⟧, ⟦b:quae⟧, ⟦b:quod⟧, ⟦i:which? what?⟧ is declined like the relative ⟦b:quī⟧ (⟦r682:682⟧).
⟦#684⟧
The interrogative substantive has in the nominative singular ⟦b:quis⟧, ⟦b:quid⟧, ⟦i:who? what?⟧ the rest is like ⟦b:quī⟧ (⟦r682:682⟧).
In old Latin, ⟦b:quis⟧ is both masculine and feminine, but a separate feminine form ⟦b:quae⟧ is used three or four times.
⟦#685⟧
⟦b:quis⟧ interrogative is sometimes used adjectively with appellatives: as, ⟦b:quis senātor?⟧ ⟦i:what senator?⟧ And ⟦b:quī⟧ is sometimes used substantively: as, ⟦b:quī prīmus Ameriam nūntiat?⟧ ⟦i:who is the first to bring the tidings to Ameria?⟧
⟦#686⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) The indefinite ⟦b:quis⟧ or ⟦b:quī⟧, ⟦i:one⟧, ⟦i:any⟧, has the following forms:
⟦b:quis⟧ and ⟦b:quid⟧ masculine and neuter substantives, ⟦b:quī⟧ and ⟦b:quod⟧ adjectives; feminine singular nominative and neuter plural nominative and accusative commonly ⟦b:qua⟧, also ⟦b:quae⟧. The rest is like ⟦b:quī⟧ (⟦r682:682⟧).
⟦#687⟧
⟦b:quis⟧, ⟦b:quem⟧, ⟦b:quid⟧, and ⟦b:quibus⟧ come from the stem ⟦b:qui-⟧; the other parts come from ⟦b:quo-⟧, ⟦b:quā-⟧. ⟦b:quae⟧ stands for an older ⟦b:quai⟧ (⟦r690:690⟧). For ⟦b:quid⟧ and ⟦b:quod⟧, see ⟦r659:659⟧.
⟦#688⟧
Old forms of the genitive singular are ⟦b:quoius⟧, and of the dative ⟦b:quoiei⟧, ⟦b:quoiī⟧, or ⟦b:quoi⟧, also in derivatives of ⟦b:quī⟧ or ⟦b:quis⟧. A genitive plural ⟦b:quōiūm⟧ is old and rare. The dative and ablative plural is sometimes ⟦b:quīs⟧ from ⟦b:quo-⟧, ⟦b:quā-⟧. A nominative plural interrogative and indefinite ⟦b:quēs⟧ is rare (Pacuv.).
⟦#689⟧
The ablative or locative is sometimes ⟦b:quī⟧, from the stem ⟦b:qui-⟧: as an interrogative, ⟦i:how?⟧ as a relative, ⟦i:wherewith⟧, ⟦i:whereby⟧, masculine, feminine, or neuter, in old Latin sometimes with a plural antecedent; especially referring to an indefinite person, and with ⟦b:cum⟧ attached, ⟦b:quīcum⟧; and as an indefinite, ⟦i:somehow⟧.
⟦#690⟧
Other case forms of ⟦b:quī⟧ or ⟦b:quis⟧ and their derivatives are found in inscriptions, as follows:
N. QVEI, prevalent in republican inscriptions; also QVI; once QVE. G. QVOIVS, regularly in republican inscriptions; cviivs, cviivs, cviivs (⟦r23:23⟧), once QVIVS (⟦r20:20⟧). D. QVOIEI, QVOI; once F. QVAI. Ab. QVEI. Plural: N. M. QVEI, but after 120 B.C., occasionally QVI; QVES, indefinite; F. and Ne. QVAI. G. QVOIVM.

title: Derivatives of quī and quis
text:
⟦#691⟧
The derivatives of ⟦b:quī⟧ and ⟦b:quis⟧ have commonly ⟦b:quis⟧ and ⟦b:quid⟧ as substantives, and ⟦b:quī⟧ and ⟦b:quod⟧ as adjectives. Forms requiring special mention are named below:
⟦#692⟧
⟦b:quisquis⟧, ⟦i:whoever⟧, ⟦i:whatever⟧, ⟦i:everybody who⟧, ⟦i:everything which⟧, an indefinite relative, has only these forms in common use: N. M. ⟦b:quisquis⟧, sometimes F. in old Latin, Ne. N. and Ac. ⟦b:quicquid⟧ or ⟦b:quidquid⟧, Ab. M. and Ne. as adjective ⟦b:quōquō⟧.
Rare forms are: N. M. ⟦b:quīquī⟧, Ac. ⟦b:quemquem⟧, once Ab. F. ⟦b:quāquā⟧, as adverb ⟦b:quīquī⟧, once D. ⟦b:quibusquibus⟧. A short form of the genitive occurs in ⟦b:quoiquoimodī⟧ or ⟦b:cuicuimodī⟧, ⟦i:of whatsoever sort⟧.
⟦b:aliquis⟧ or ⟦b:aliquī⟧, ⟦b:aliqua⟧, once ⟦b:aliquae⟧ (Lucr.), ⟦b:aliquid⟧ or ⟦b:aliquod⟧, ⟦i:some one⟧, ⟦i:some⟧; Ab. M. sometimes, Ne. often ⟦b:aliquī⟧ (⟦r689:689⟧). Pl. Ne. N. and Ac. only ⟦b:aliqua⟧; D. and Ab. sometimes ⟦b:aliquīs⟧ (⟦r668:668⟧).
⟦b:ecquis⟧ or ⟦b:ecquī⟧, ⟦b:ecqua⟧ or ⟦b:ecquae⟧, ⟦b:ecquid⟧ or ⟦b:ecquod⟧, ⟦i:any?⟧ Besides the nominative only these forms are found: D. eccui, Ac. ⟦b:ecquem⟧, ⟦b:ecquam⟧, ⟦b:ecquid⟧, Ab. M. and Ne. ⟦b:ecquō⟧. Pl. N. ⟦b:ecquī⟧, Ac. M. ⟦b:ecquōs⟧, F. ⟦b:ecquās⟧.
⟦b:quīcumque⟧, ⟦b:quaecumque⟧, ⟦b:quodcumque⟧, ⟦i:whoever⟧, ⟦i:whichever⟧, ⟦i:everybody who⟧, ⟦i:everything which⟧. The ⟦b:cumque⟧ is sometimes separated from ⟦b:quī⟧ by an intervening word. An older form is ⟦b:quīquomque⟧, &c.
⟦b:quīdam⟧, ⟦b:quaedam⟧, ⟦b:quiddam⟧ or ⟦b:quoddam⟧, ⟦i:a⟧, ⟦i:a certain⟧, ⟦i:some one⟧, ⟦i:so and so⟧; Ac. ⟦b:quendam⟧, ⟦b:quandam⟧. Pl. G. ⟦b:quōrundam⟧, ⟦b:quārundam⟧.
⟦b:quīlibet⟧, ⟦b:quaelibet⟧, ⟦b:quidlibet⟧ or ⟦b:quodlibet⟧, ⟦i:any you please⟧.
⟦b:quisnam⟧, rarely ⟦b:quīnam⟧, ⟦b:quaenam⟧, ⟦b:quidnam⟧ or ⟦b:quodnam⟧, ⟦i:who ever? who in the world?⟧ Sometimes ⟦b:nam quis⟧, &c.
⟦b:quispiam⟧, ⟦b:quaepiam⟧, ⟦b:quippiam⟧, ⟦b:quidpiam⟧ or ⟦b:quodpiam⟧, ⟦i:any⟧, ⟦i:any one⟧; Ab. also ⟦b:quīpiam⟧ (⟦r689:689⟧), sometimes as adverb, ⟦i:in any way⟧.
⟦b:quisquam⟧, ⟦b:quicquam⟧ or ⟦b:quidquam⟧, ⟦i:anybody at all⟧, ⟦i:anything at all⟧, generally a substantive, less frequently an adjective, ⟦i:any at all⟧. There is no distinctive feminine form, and ⟦b:quisquam⟧ and ⟦b:quemquam⟧ are rarely, and in old Latin, used as a feminine adjective. Ab. also ⟦b:quīquam⟧ (⟦r689:689⟧), sometimes as adverb, ⟦i:in any way at all⟧. No plural.
⟦b:quisque⟧, ⟦b:quaeque⟧, ⟦b:quicque⟧, ⟦b:quidque⟧ or ⟦b:quodque⟧, ⟦i:each⟧. Sometimes ⟦b:ūnus⟧ is prefixed: ⟦b:ūnusquisque⟧; both parts are declined. ⟦b:quisque⟧ and ⟦b:quemque⟧ are sometimes feminine. Ab. S. ⟦b:quīque⟧ (⟦r689:689⟧) rare, Ab. Pl. ⟦b:quīsque⟧ (⟦r688:688⟧) once (Lucr.).
⟦b:quīvīs⟧, ⟦b:quaevīs⟧, ⟦b:quidvīs⟧ or ⟦b:quodvīs⟧, ⟦i:which you will⟧; Ab. also ⟦b:quīvīs⟧ (⟦r689:689⟧).

title: uter
text:
⟦#693⟧
⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦b:utra⟧, ⟦b:utrum⟧, ⟦i:whether? which of the two?⟧ has the genitive singular ⟦b:utrīus⟧, and the dative singular ⟦b:utrī⟧.
The rest is like ⟦b:aeger⟧ (⟦r617:617⟧). ⟦b:uter⟧ is sometimes relative, ⟦i:whichsoever⟧, or indefinite, ⟦i:either of the two⟧.

title: Derivatives of uter
text:
⟦#694⟧
The derivatives of ⟦b:uter⟧ are declined like ⟦b:uter⟧; they are:
⟦b:neuter⟧, ⟦i:neither of the two⟧, genitive ⟦b:neutrīus⟧, always with ⟦b:ī⟧ (⟦r657:657⟧). When used as a grammatical term, ⟦i:neuter⟧, the genitive is always ⟦b:neutrī⟧: as, ⟦b:generis neutrī⟧, ⟦i:of neither gender⟧.
⟦b:utercumque⟧, ⟦b:utracumque⟧, ⟦b:utrumcumque⟧, ⟦i:whichever of the two⟧, ⟦i:either of the two⟧.
⟦b:uterlibet⟧, ⟦i:whichever you please⟧.
⟦b:uterque⟧, ⟦i:whichsoever⟧, ⟦i:both⟧. G. always ⟦b:utriusque⟧ (⟦r657:657⟧).
⟦b:utervīs⟧, ⟦i:whichever you wish⟧.
⟦b:alteruter⟧, F. ⟦b:altera utra⟧, Ne. ⟦b:alterutrum⟧ or ⟦b:alterum utrum⟧, ⟦i:one or the other⟧, G. ⟦b:alterīus utrīus⟧, once late ⟦b:alterutrīus⟧, D. ⟦b:alterutrī⟧, Ac. M. ⟦b:alterutrum⟧ or ⟦b:alterum utrum⟧, F. ⟦b:alterutram⟧ once (Plin.) or ⟦b:alteram utram⟧, Ab. ⟦b:alterutrō⟧ or ⟦b:alterō utrō⟧, F. ⟦b:alterā utrā⟧. No Pl., except D. ⟦b:alterutrīs⟧ once (Plin.).

title: Correlative Pronouns
text:
⟦#695⟧
Pronouns often correspond with each other in meaning and form; some of the commonest correlatives are the following:
Kind. Interrogative. Indefinite. Demonstrative,
⟦b:quis⟧, ⟦b:quī⟧, ⟦i:who?⟧  ⟦b:quis⟧, ⟦b:quī⟧, ⟦b:aliquis⟧  ⟦b:hīc⟧, ⟦b:iste⟧, ⟦b:ille⟧ ⟦b:is⟧, ⟦b:quisque⟧  quī
⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦i:which of the two?⟧  ⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦b:alteruter⟧  ⟦b:uterque⟧  ⟦b:uter⟧, ⟦b:quī⟧
⟦b:quot⟧, ⟦i:how many?⟧ (⟦r431:431⟧)  ⟦b:aliquot⟧  ⟦b:tot⟧  ⟦b:quot⟧
⟦b:quantus⟧, ⟦i:how large?⟧ (⟦r613:613⟧)  ⟦b:aliquantus⟧, ⟦b:quantusvīs⟧  ⟦b:tantus⟧  ⟦b:quantus⟧
⟦b:quālis⟧, ⟦i:of what sort?⟧ (⟦r630:630⟧)  ⟦b:quālislibet⟧  ⟦b:tālis⟧  ⟦b:quālis⟧
⟦/⟧
Determinative, &c. Relative. Simple Alternative Number Quantity Quality

title: Nouns As Adverbs
text:
⟦#696⟧
Adverbs, conjunctions, and prepositions are chiefly noun or pronoun cases which have become fixed in a specific form and with a specific meaning. Many of these words were still felt to be live cases, even in the developed period of the language; with others the consciousness of their noun character was lost.
⟦#697⟧
Three cases are used adverbially: the accusative, the ablative, and the locative.
⟦#698⟧
The rather indeterminate meaning of the accusative and the ablative is sometimes more exactly defined by a preposition. The preposition may either accompany its usual case: as, ⟦b:adamussim, admodum, īlicō⟧; or it may be loosely prefixed, with more of the nature of an adverb than of a preposition, to a case with which it is not ordinarily used: as, ⟦b:examussim, intereā⟧. Sometimes it stands after the noun: as, ⟦b:parumper⟧, ⟦i:a little while⟧. Besides the three cases named above, other forms occur, some of which are undoubtedly old case endings, though they can no longer be recognized as such: see ⟦r710:710⟧.

title: Accusative of Substantives
text:
⟦#699⟧
⟦b:domum⟧, ⟦i:homeward, home⟧; ⟦b:rūs⟧, ⟦i:afield⟧; ⟦b:forās⟧, ⟦i:out of doors⟧ ⟦b:(*forā-); vicem⟧, ⟦i:instead⟧; ⟦b:partim⟧, ⟦i:in part⟧; old ⟦b:noenum⟧ or ⟦b:noenu⟧, common ⟦b:nōn⟧, for ⟦b:ne-oenum⟧, i.e. ⟦b:ūnum⟧, ⟦i:not one, naught, not⟧; ⟦b:admodum⟧, ⟦i:to a degree, very⟧; ⟦b:adamussim, examussim⟧, ⟦i:to a T⟧; ⟦b:adfatim⟧, ⟦i:to satiety⟧; ⟦b:invicem⟧, ⟦i:in turn, each other⟧.
⟦#700⟧
Many adverbs in ⟦b:-tim⟧ and ⟦b:-sim⟧ denote manner (⟦r549:549⟧): as, ⟦b:cautim⟧, ⟦i:warily⟧, ⟦b:statim⟧, ⟦i:at once⟧, ⟦b:sēnsim⟧, ⟦i:perceptibly, gradually⟧; ⟦b:ōstiātim⟧, ⟦i:door by door⟧, ⟦b:virītim⟧, ⟦i:man by man⟧, ⟦b:fūrtim⟧, ⟦i:stealthily⟧.

title: Accusative of Adjectives and Pronouns
text:
⟦#701⟧
Neuters: all comparative adverbs in ⟦b:-ius⟧ (⟦r361:361⟧): as, ⟦b:doctius⟧, ⟦i:more learnedly⟧; so ⟦b:minus⟧, ⟦i:less⟧, ⟦b:magis⟧, ⟦i:more⟧ (⟦r363:363⟧). ⟦b:prīmum⟧, ⟦i:first⟧, ⟦b:secundum⟧, secondly, &c.; ⟦b:tum⟧, ⟦i:then⟧ (⟦b:to-⟧, ⟦i:that⟧): ⟦b:commodum⟧, ⟦i:just in time⟧; ⟦b:minimum⟧, ⟦i:at least⟧, ⟦b:potissimum⟧, ⟦i:in preference⟧, ⟦b:postrēmum⟧, ⟦i:at last⟧, ⟦b:summum⟧, ⟦i:at most⟧; ⟦b:versum⟧, ⟦i:toward⟧, ⟦b:rursum, russum, rūsum⟧, ⟦i:back⟧; ⟦b:facile⟧, ⟦i:easily⟧, ⟦b:impūne⟧, ⟦i:scotfree⟧, ⟦b:recēns⟧, ⟦i:lately⟧, ⟦b:semel⟧, ⟦i:once⟧ (⟦b:simili-⟧), ⟦b:simul⟧, ⟦i:together⟧ (⟦b:simili-⟧). Plural: ⟦b:cētera⟧, ⟦i:for the rest⟧; ⟦b:quia⟧, ⟦i:because⟧ (⟦b:qui-⟧); in old Latin ⟦b:frūstra⟧, ⟦i:in vain⟧ (⟦b:fraud-⟧).
⟦#702⟧
Feminines: ⟦b:bifāriam⟧, ⟦i:twofold⟧; ⟦b:cōram⟧, ⟦i:face to face⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧ or ⟦b:co-, *ōrā-⟧); ⟦b:tam⟧, ⟦i:so⟧ (⟦b:tā-⟧, ⟦i:that⟧); ⟦b:quam⟧, ⟦i:as, how⟧. Plural: ⟦b:aliās⟧, ⟦i:on other occasions⟧.

title: Ablative of Substantives
text:
⟦#703⟧
⟦b:domō⟧, ⟦i:from home⟧, ⟦b:rūre⟧, ⟦i:from the country⟧; ⟦b:hodiē⟧, ⟦i:to-day⟧ (⟦b:ho-⟧, ⟦b:diē-⟧), ⟦b:volgō⟧, ⟦i:publicly⟧, ⟦b:vespere⟧, ⟦i:by twilight⟧, ⟦b:noctū⟧, ⟦i:by nights⟧, ⟦i:nights⟧, ⟦b:lūce⟧, ⟦i:by light⟧, ⟦b:tempore⟧, ⟦i:in times⟧, ⟦i:betimes⟧; ⟦b:sponte⟧, ⟦i:voluntarily⟧, ⟦b:forte⟧, ⟦i:by chance⟧; ⟦b:quotannīs⟧, ⟦i:yearly⟧; ⟦b:grātiīs⟧ or ⟦b:grātīs⟧, ⟦i:for nothing⟧, ⟦b:ingrātiīs⟧ or ⟦b:ingrātīs⟧, ⟦i:against one’s will⟧; ⟦b:īlicō⟧, ⟦i:on the spot⟧ (169, 4; 170, 2), ⟦b:forīs⟧, ⟦i:out of doors⟧ (⟦b:*forā-⟧).

title: Ablative of Adjectives and Pronouns
text:
⟦#704⟧
Many adverbs in ⟦b:-ō⟧ are formed from adjectives of time: as, ⟦b:perpetuō⟧, ⟦i:to the end⟧, ⟦b:crēbrō⟧, ⟦i:frequently⟧, ⟦b:rārō⟧, ⟦i:seldom⟧, ⟦b:repentīnō⟧, ⟦i:suddenly⟧, ⟦b:sērō⟧, ⟦i:late⟧, ⟦b:prīmō⟧, ⟦i:at first⟧. Many denote manner: as, ⟦b:arcānō⟧, ⟦i:privily⟧, ⟦b:sēriō⟧, ⟦i:in earnest⟧. Some are formed from participles: as, ⟦b:auspicātō⟧, ⟦i:with auspices taken⟧; ⟦b:compositō⟧, ⟦i:by agreement⟧. A plural is rare: ⟦b:alternīs⟧, ⟦i:alternately⟧.
⟦#705⟧
Instead of ⟦b:-ō⟧, neuter ablatives commonly have ⟦b:-ē⟧: as, ⟦b:longē⟧, ⟦i:far⟧, ⟦b:doctē⟧, ⟦i:wisely⟧. So also superlatives: ⟦b:facillimē⟧, ⟦i:most easily⟧, anciently FACILVMED (⟦r362:362⟧). Consonant stems have ⟦b:-e⟧: as, ⟦b:repente⟧, ⟦i:suddenly⟧.
⟦#706⟧
From pronouns some end in ⟦b:-ī⟧ (⟦r689:689⟧): as, ⟦b:quī⟧, ⟦i:how?⟧ indefinite, ⟦b:quī⟧, ⟦i:somehow⟧; ⟦b:atquī⟧, ⟦i:but somehow⟧; ⟦b:quī-quam⟧, ⟦i:in any way at all⟧.
⟦#707⟧
Feminines: many in ⟦b:-ā⟧: ⟦b:ūnā⟧, ⟦i:together⟧; ⟦b:circā⟧, ⟦i:around⟧; ⟦b:contrā⟧, ⟦i:against⟧ (⟦b:com-⟧, ⟦r347:347⟧); ⟦b:extrā⟧, ⟦i:outside⟧ (⟦b:ex⟧, ⟦r347:347⟧); in classical Latin, ⟦b:frūstrā⟧, ⟦i:in vain⟧ (⟦b:fraud-⟧). So, especially, adverbs denoting the ‘route by which:’ ⟦b:hāc⟧, ⟦i:this way⟧; ⟦b:rēctā⟧, ⟦i:straightway⟧.

title: Locative
text:
⟦#708⟧
In ⟦b:-ī⟧, from names of towns and a few other words: ⟦b:Karthāginī⟧, ⟦i:at Carthage⟧; ⟦b:Rōmae⟧, for ⟦b:Rōmāī⟧, ⟦i:at Rome⟧; ⟦b:domī⟧, ⟦i:at home;⟧ ⟦b:illī⟧, commonly ⟦b:illī-c⟧, ⟦i:there⟧ (⟦b:illo-⟧), ⟦b:istī⟧, commonly ⟦b:istī-c⟧, ⟦i:where you are⟧, ⟦b:hī-c⟧, ⟦i:here⟧ (⟦b:ho-⟧); old ⟦b:sei⟧, common ⟦b:sī⟧, ⟦i:at that⟧, ⟦i:in that case⟧, ⟦i:so⟧, ⟦i:if⟧; ⟦b:sīc⟧, ⟦i:so⟧ (⟦b:sī⟧, ⟦b:-ce⟧).
⟦#709⟧
In ⟦b:-bī̆⟧, from some pronouns: ⟦b:ibī̆⟧, ⟦i:there⟧ (⟦b:i-⟧); ⟦b:ubī̆⟧ (for ⟦b:*quobī̆⟧, ⟦r146:146⟧), ⟦i:where⟧; ⟦b:alicubī̆⟧, ⟦i:somewhere⟧; ⟦b:sī-cubi⟧, ⟦i:if anywhere⟧, ⟦b:nē-cubi⟧, ⟦i:lest anywhere⟧.

title: Other Endings
text:
⟦#710⟧
Besides the above, other endings are also found in words of this class: as,
⟦b:-s⟧ in ⟦b:abs⟧, ⟦i:from⟧, ⟦b:ex⟧, ⟦i:out of⟧; similarly ⟦b:us-que⟧, ⟦i:in every case⟧, ⟦i:ever⟧, ⟦b:us-quam⟧, ⟦i:anywhere at all⟧. ⟦b:-tus⟧ has the meaning of an ablative: as, ⟦b:intus⟧, ⟦i:from within⟧, ⟦i:within⟧; ⟦b:antīquitus⟧, ⟦i:from old times⟧, ⟦i:anciently⟧; ⟦b:funditus⟧, ⟦i:from the bottom⟧, ⟦i:entirely⟧. ⟦b:-ō⟧ denotes the ‘place to which’ in adverbs from pronoun stems: as, ⟦b:eō⟧, ⟦i:thither⟧; ⟦b:quō⟧, ⟦i:whither⟧; ⟦b:illō⟧, or ⟦b:illūc⟧, for ⟦b:illoi-ce⟧, ⟦i:thither⟧, after ⟦b:hūc⟧; ⟦b:hōc⟧, commonly ⟦b:hūc⟧, perhaps for ⟦b:hoi-ce⟧ (⟦r99:99⟧) ⟦i:hither⟧. ⟦b:-im⟧ denotes the ‘place from which:’ as, ⟦b:istim⟧, commonly ⟦b:istinc⟧, ⟦i:from where you are⟧; ⟦b:illim⟧, commonly ⟦b:illinc⟧, ⟦i:from yonder⟧; ⟦b:hinc⟧, ⟦i:hence⟧; ⟦b:exim⟧, ⟦i:thereupon⟧; also ⟦b:-de⟧: as, ⟦b:unde⟧, ⟦i:whence⟧ (⟦b:quo-⟧, ⟦r146:146⟧), ⟦b:sī-cunde⟧, ⟦i:if from any place⟧, ⟦b:nē-cunde⟧, ⟦i:lest from anywhere⟧. ⟦b:-ter⟧: as comparative (⟦r347:347⟧): ⟦b:praeter⟧, ⟦i:further⟧, ⟦i:beyond⟧, ⟦b:inter⟧, ⟦i:between⟧; denoting manner: ⟦b:ācriter⟧, ⟦i:sharply⟧; ⟦b:amanter⟧, ⟦i:affectionately⟧; rarely from ⟦b:-o-⟧ stems: as, ⟦b:firmiter⟧, ⟦i:steadfastly⟧.

title: Correlative Adverbs
text:
⟦#711⟧
Adverbs derived from pronoun stems often correspond with each other in meaning and form; some of the commonest correlatives are the following:
Interrogative. Indefinite. Demonstrative,
⟦b:ubī̆⟧, ⟦i:where?⟧  ⟦b:alicubī̆⟧ ⟦b:usquam⟧ ⟦b:uspiam⟧ ⟦b:ubivīs⟧  ⟦b:hīc, istīc, illīc⟧ ⟦b:ibī̆, ibī̆dem⟧  ⟦b:ubī̆⟧
⟦b:quō⟧, ⟦i:whither?⟧  ⟦b:aliquō⟧ ⟦b:quōlibet⟧ ⟦b:quōvīs⟧  ⟦b:hūc, istūc, illūc⟧ ⟦b:eō, eōdem⟧  ⟦b:quō⟧
⟦b:quorsum⟧, ⟦i:whitherward?⟧  ⟦b:aliquōvorsum⟧  ⟦b:horsum, istorsum⟧  ⟦b:quorsum⟧
⟦b:unde⟧, ⟦i:whence?⟧  ⟦b:alicunde⟧ ⟦b:undelibet⟧  ⟦b:hinc, istinc, illinc⟧ ⟦b:inde, indidem⟧  ⟦b:unde⟧
⟦b:quandō⟧, ⟦i:when?⟧  ⟦b:aliquandō⟧ ⟦b:umquam⟧  ⟦b:nunc, tum, tunc⟧  ⟦b:quom⟧ or ⟦b:cum⟧
⟦b:quotiēns⟧, ⟦i:how often?⟧  ⟦b:aliquotiēns⟧  ⟦b:totiēns⟧  ⟦b:quotiēns⟧
⟦b:quā⟧, ⟦i:by what way?⟧  ⟦b:aliquā⟧ ⟦b:quāvīs⟧  ⟦b:hāc, istāc, illāc⟧ ⟦b:eā, eādem⟧  ⟦b:quā⟧
⟦b:utī⟧ or ⟦b:ut⟧, ⟦i:how⟧?  ⟦b:aliquā⟧  ⟦b:ita, sīc⟧  ⟦b:utī⟧ or ⟦b:ut⟧ (⟦r146:146⟧)
⟦b:quam⟧, ⟦i:how?⟧  ⟦b:aliquam⟧  ⟦b:tam⟧  ⟦b:quam⟧
⟦/⟧
Determinative, &c. Relative. Place Time Way Manner Degree

title: Sentences As Adverbs
text:
⟦#712⟧
Some adverbs are condensed sentences: as,
⟦b:īlicet⟧, ⟦i:you may go, straightway⟧ (⟦b:īre licet⟧); ⟦b:scīlicet⟧, ⟦i:you may know, obviously, of course⟧ (⟦b:scīre licet⟧); ⟦b:vidē̆licet⟧, ⟦i:you can see, plainly⟧ (⟦b:vidēre licet⟧); ⟦b:nūdiustertius⟧, ⟦i:now is the third day, day before yesterday⟧ (⟦b:num dius⟧, i.e. ⟦b:diēs⟧, ⟦b:tertius⟧); ⟦b:forsitan⟧, ⟦i:maybe⟧ (⟦b:fors sit an⟧); ⟦b:mīrum quantum⟧, ⟦i:strange how much, astonishingly⟧; ⟦b:nesciō quō pactō⟧, ⟦b:nesciō quōmodo⟧, ⟦i:somehow or other, unfortunately⟧.
⟦#713⟧
The verb is inflected by attaching person endings to the several stems.

title: Inflection of the Verb: The Stem
text:
⟦#714⟧
The stem contains the meaning of the verb, and also denotes the mode (mood) and the time (tense) of the action as viewed by the speaker.
⟦#715⟧
There are three Moods, ⟦i:Indicative⟧, ⟦i:Subjunctive⟧, and ⟦i:Imperative⟧.
⟦#716⟧
There are six Tenses in the indicative, three of the present system, ⟦i:Present⟧, ⟦i:Imperfect⟧, and ⟦i:Future⟧; and three of the perfect system, ⟦i:Perfect⟧, ⟦i:Pluperfect⟧, and ⟦i:Future Perfect⟧. The subjunctive lacks the futures; the imperative has only the present.
⟦#717⟧
The meanings of the moods and tenses are best learnt from reading. No satisfactory translation can be given in the paradigms, especially of the subjunctive, which requires a variety of translations for its various uses.
⟦#718⟧
The verb has two principal stems: I. The Present stem, which is the base of the present system; II. The Perfect stem, which is the base of the perfect active system.
⟦#719⟧
The perfect system has no passive; its place is supplied by the perfect participle with a form of ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧, or less frequently of ⟦b:fuī⟧, ⟦i:am become⟧.
⟦#720⟧
Many verbs have only the present system: as, ⟦b:maereō⟧, ⟦i:mourn⟧; some have only the perfect system: as, ⟦b:meminī⟧, ⟦i:remember⟧. Some verbs have a present and perfect system made up of two separate roots or stems: as, present indicative ⟦b:ferō⟧, ⟦i:carry⟧, perfect indicative ⟦b:tulī⟧, and perfect participle ⟦b:lātus⟧; present ⟦b:possum⟧, ⟦i:can⟧, perfect ⟦b:potuī⟧.

title: The Person Ending
text:
⟦#721⟧
The person ending limits the meaning of the stem by pointing out the person of the subject. There are three Persons, the ⟦i:First⟧, used of the speaker, the ⟦i:Second⟧, of what is spoken to, and the ⟦i:Third⟧, of what is spoken of. The person ending furthermore indicates number and voice.
⟦#722⟧
There are two Numbers: the ⟦i:Singular⟧, used of one, and the ⟦i:Plural⟧, used of more than one.
⟦#723⟧
There are two Voices: the ⟦i:Active⟧, indicating that the subject acts, and the ⟦i:Passive⟧, indicating that the subject acts on himself, or more commonly is acted on by another.
⟦#724⟧
Only transitive verbs have all persons of the passive. Intransitive verbs have in the passive only the third person singular, used impersonally; the participle in this construction is neuter.
⟦#725⟧
Some verbs have only the passive person endings, but with a reflexive or an active meaning; such are called ⟦i:Deponents⟧: see ⟦r798:798⟧.
⟦#726⟧
The person endings are as follows:
⟦i:First person.⟧  ⟦b:-m⟧  ⟦b:-mus⟧  ⟦i:not used⟧  ⟦i:not used⟧  ⟦b:-r⟧  ⟦b:-mur⟧  ⟦i:not used⟧  ⟦i:not used⟧
⟦i:Second person.⟧  ⟦b:-s⟧  ⟦b:-tis⟧  ⟦i:none⟧, ⟦b:-tō⟧  ⟦b:-te⟧, ⟦b:-tōte⟧  ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:-re⟧  [⟦b:-minī⟧]  ⟦b:-re⟧, ⟦b:-tor⟧  [⟦b:-minī⟧]
⟦i:Third person.⟧  ⟦b:-t⟧  ⟦b:-nt⟧  ⟦b:-tō⟧  ⟦b:-ntō⟧  ⟦b:-tur⟧  ⟦b:-ntur⟧  ⟦b:-tor⟧  ⟦b:-ntor⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦i:Voice.⟧ Active. Passive. ⟦i:Mood.⟧ Ind. & Sub. Imperative. Ind. & Sub. Imperative. ⟦i:Number.⟧ Sing. Plur. Sing. Plur. Sing. Plur. Sing. Plur.
⟦#727⟧
In the perfect indicative active, the second person singular ends in ⟦b:-tī⟧, and the third person plural in ⟦b:-runt⟧ for an older ⟦b:-ront⟧, or in ⟦b:-re⟧. ⟦b:-re⟧ is most used in poetry and history, and by Cato and Sallust; ⟦b:-runt⟧ by Cicero, and almost always by Caesar.
⟦#728⟧
In the indicative ⟦b:-m⟧ is not used in the present (except in ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧, and ⟦b:inquam⟧, ⟦i:quoth I⟧), in the perfect or future perfect, or in the future in ⟦b:-bō⟧. ⟦b:-s⟧ is not used in ⟦b:es⟧ for ⟦b:ess⟧, ⟦i:thou art⟧, and in ⟦b:ēs⟧, ⟦i:eatest⟧ (⟦r171:171, 1⟧).
⟦#729⟧
In inscriptions, ⟦b:-d⟧ sometimes stands for ⟦b:-t⟧ (⟦r149:149, 2⟧) in the third person singular, and sometimes ⟦b:-t⟧ is not used: as, FECID, ⟦i:made⟧, for ⟦i:fēcit⟧; DEDE, ⟦i:gave⟧, for ⟦b:dedēt⟧ or ⟦b:dedit⟧. And other forms of the third person plural of the indicative active are sometimes used: as, Pisaurian DEDROT, DEDRO (with syncope, ⟦r111:111⟧) for ⟦b:dederunt⟧, ⟦i:gave⟧; EMERV, ⟦i:bought⟧, for ⟦b:ēmērunt⟧; once DEDERI, probably for ⟦b:dedēre⟧ (⟦r856:856⟧).
⟦#730⟧
In the passive second person singular, Terence has always, Plautus commonly ⟦b:-re⟧; later it is unusual in the present indicative, except in deponents; but in other tenses ⟦b:-re⟧ is preferred, especially in the future ⟦b:-bere⟧, by Cicero, ⟦b:-ris⟧ by Livy and Tacitus. The second person plural passive is wanting; its place is supplied by a single participial form in ⟦b:-minī⟧, which is used without reference to gender, for gender words and neuters alike (⟦r297:297⟧).
⟦#731⟧
Deponents have rarely ⟦b:-mino⟧, in the imperative singular: as, second person, ⟦b:prōgredimino⟧, ⟦i:step forward thou⟧ (Plaut.); in laws, as third person: FRVIMINO, ⟦i:let him enjoy⟧; or ⟦b:-tō⟧ and ⟦b:-ntō⟧ for ⟦b:-tor⟧ and ⟦b:-ntor⟧: as, ⟦b:ūtitō⟧, ⟦i:let him use⟧; ⟦b:ūtuntō⟧, ⟦i:let them use⟧. In a real passive, ⟦b:-ntō⟧ is rare: as, CENSENTO, ⟦i:let them be rated⟧.

title: Nouns of the Verb
text:
⟦#732⟧
The verb is accompanied by some nouns, which are conveniently, though not quite accurately, reckoned parts of the verb; they are:
Three Infinitives, ⟦i:Present Active⟧ and ⟦i:Passive⟧, and ⟦i:Perfect Active⟧, sometimes called the ⟦i:Infinitive Mood⟧. For the future active and passive and the perfect passive, compound forms are used.
The ⟦i:Gerund⟧ and the ⟦i:Gerundive⟧.
Two ⟦i:Supines⟧.
Three Participles, ⟦i:Present⟧ and ⟦i:Future Active⟧, and ⟦i:Perfect Passive⟧.

title: Principal Parts
text:
⟦#733⟧
The several verb stems can readily be found, when once the principal parts are known; these are given in the dictionary.
⟦#734⟧
The Principal Parts of a verb are the ⟦i:Present Indicative Active⟧, ⟦i:Present Infinitive Active⟧, ⟦i:Perfect Indicative Active⟧, and ⟦i:Perfect Participle⟧: as,
⟦b:regō⟧, ⟦i:rule⟧  ⟦b:regere⟧  ⟦b:rēxī⟧  ⟦b:rēctus⟧
⟦b:laudō⟧, ⟦i:praise⟧  ⟦b:laudāre⟧  ⟦b:laudāvī⟧  ⟦b:laudātus⟧
⟦b:moneō⟧, ⟦i:advise⟧  ⟦b:monēre⟧  ⟦b:monuī⟧  ⟦b:monitus⟧
⟦b:audiō⟧, ⟦i:hear⟧  ⟦b:audīre⟧  ⟦b:audīvī⟧  ⟦b:auditus⟧
⟦/⟧
Pres. Indic. Pres. Infin. Perf. Indic. Perf. Part.
⟦#735⟧
The Principal Parts of deponents are the ⟦i:Present Indicative⟧, ⟦i:Present Infinitive⟧, and ⟦i:Perfect Participle⟧: as,
⟦b:queror⟧, ⟦i:complain⟧  ⟦b:querī⟧  ⟦b:questus⟧
⟦b:mīror⟧, ⟦i:wonder⟧  ⟦b:mīrārī⟧  ⟦b:mīrātus⟧
⟦b:vereor⟧, ⟦i:fear⟧  ⟦b:verērī⟧  ⟦b:veritus⟧
⟦b:partior⟧, ⟦i:share⟧  ⟦b:partīrī⟧  ⟦b:partītus⟧
⟦/⟧
Pres. Indic. Pres. Infin. Perf. Part.

title: Designation of the Verb
text:
⟦#736⟧
A verb is usually named by the present indicative active first person singular: as, ⟦b:regō⟧; ⟦b:laudō⟧, ⟦b:moneō⟧, ⟦b:audiō⟧; or by the present infinitive active: as, ⟦b:regere⟧; ⟦b:laudāre⟧, ⟦b:monēre⟧, ⟦b:audīre⟧. Deponents are named by the corresponding passive forms: as, ⟦b:queror⟧; ⟦b:mīror⟧, ⟦b:vereor⟧, ⟦b:partior⟧; or ⟦b:querī⟧; ⟦b:mīrārī⟧, ⟦b:verērī⟧, ⟦b:partīrī⟧.
⟦#737⟧
For convenience, verbs with ⟦b:-ere⟧ in the present infinitive active are called ⟦i:Verbs in⟧ ⟦b:-ere⟧; those with ⟦b:-āre⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, or ⟦b:-īre⟧, ⟦i:Verbs in⟧ ⟦b:-āre⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, or ⟦b:-īre⟧, respectively. In like manner deponents are designated as ⟦i:Verbs in⟧ ⟦b:-ī⟧; or ⟦i:Verbs in⟧ ⟦b:-ārī⟧, ⟦b:-ērī⟧, or ⟦b:-īrī⟧, respectively.

title: Theme of the Verb
text:
⟦#738⟧
The several stems of the verb come from a form called the ⟦i:Theme⟧. In primitives, the theme is a root; in denominatives, the theme is a noun stem.
Thus, ⟦b:⟦i:reg-⟧⟧ in ⟦b:reg-ō⟧ is a root; while ⟦b:vesti-⟧ in ⟦b:vesti-ō⟧, ⟦i:dress⟧, is a noun stem. The noun stem is sometimes modified in form. Oftentimes the noun stem is only presumed: as, ⟦b:audi-⟧ in ⟦b:audi-ō⟧.
⟦#739⟧
Some verbs have a denominative theme in the present system, and a primitive theme in the perfect system, others have the reverse.
⟦#740⟧
Most verbs with an infinitive of more than two syllables in ⟦b:-āre⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, or ⟦b:-īre⟧, or, if deponent, in ⟦b:-ārī⟧, ⟦b:-ērī⟧, or ⟦b:-īrī⟧, are denominative; most other verbs are primitive.
Thus, ⟦b:laudāre⟧, ⟦b:monēre⟧, ⟦b:audīre⟧; ⟦b:mīrārī⟧, ⟦b:verērī⟧, ⟦b:partīrī⟧, are denominative; while ⟦b:esse⟧, ⟦b:dare⟧, (⟦b:dē⟧)⟦b:lēre⟧, ⟦b:regere⟧, ⟦b:querī⟧, are primitive. A few verbs, however, which have the appearance of denominatives, are thought to be primitive in their origin.

title: Arrangement of the Verb
text:
⟦#741⟧
Verbs are divided into two classes, according to the form of the present system: I. Root verbs, and verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, mostly primitive; II. Verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, or ⟦b:-īre⟧, mostly denominative.
⟦#742⟧
Verbs are sometimes arranged without regard to difference of kind, in the alphabetical order of the vowel before -s of the second person singular of the present indicative active, ⟦b:ā⟧, ⟦b:ē⟧, ⟦b:i⟧, ⟦b:ī⟧: thus, ⟦b:laudās⟧, ⟦b:monēs⟧, ⟦b:regis⟧, ⟦b:audīs⟧, sometimes called the ⟦i:first⟧, ⟦i:second⟧, ⟦i:third⟧, and ⟦i:fourth conjugation⟧ respectively.

title: Primitive Verbs
text:
⟦#743⟧
A few of the oldest and commonest verbs of everyday life have a bare root as stem in the present indicative or in parts of it; and some of them have other peculiarities; such are called ⟦i:Root Verbs⟧, or by some, ⟦i:irregular⟧ (⟦r744:744-781⟧). Most primitives are verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, like ⟦b:regō⟧ (⟦r782:782⟧).

title: Root Verbs: With a Prevalent Bare Root
text:
⟦=⟧⟦i:Irregular Verbs.⟧
⟦#744⟧
Primitives with the bare root as present indicative stem in almost all their forms are ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧, ⟦b:dō⟧, ⟦i:give⟧, ⟦i:put⟧, and compounds; and with the root doubled, ⟦b:bibō⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧, ⟦b:serō⟧, ⟦i:sow⟧, and ⟦b:sistō⟧, ⟦i:set⟧.

title: sum, am (es-, s-)
text:
⟦#745⟧
⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧, is used only in the present system (⟦r720:720⟧). The perfect system is supplied by forms of ⟦b:fuī⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:fu-⟧⟧).

⟦#746⟧
For the first person ⟦b:sum⟧, Varro mentions ⟦b:esum⟧ as an archaic form. This ⟦b:e⟧ was probably prefixed by analogy with the other forms; for the ⟦b:-m⟧, and for ⟦b:es⟧, see ⟦r728:728⟧. For ⟦b:sim⟧, &c., and ⟦b:siem⟧, &c., see ⟦r841:841⟧. In the imperfect ⟦b:eram⟧, &c., and the future ⟦b:erō⟧, &c., ⟦b:s⟧ has become ⟦b:r⟧ (⟦r154:154⟧).
⟦#747⟧
The indicative and imperative ⟦b:es⟧ is for older ⟦b:ess⟧ (⟦r171:171, 1⟧), and is regularly used long by Plautus and Terence. The ⟦b:e⟧ of ⟦b:es⟧ and ⟦b:est⟧ is not pronounced after a vowel or ⟦b:-m⟧, and is often omitted in writing: as ⟦b:experrēcta es⟧, pronounced ⟦b:experrēctas⟧; ⟦b:epistula est⟧, pronounced ⟦b:epistulast⟧; ⟦b:cōnsilium est⟧, pronounced ⟦b:cōnsiliumst⟧. In the dramatists, ⟦b:-s⟧ preceded by a vowel, which is usually short, unites with a following ⟦b:es⟧ or ⟦b:est⟧: thus, ⟦b:tū servos es⟧ becomes ⟦b:tū servos⟧; ⟦b:similis est⟧, ⟦b:similist⟧; ⟦b:virtūs est⟧, ⟦b:virtūst⟧; ⟦b:rēs est⟧, ⟦b:rēst⟧.
⟦#748⟧
Old forms are: SONT (inscr. about 120 B.C.); with suffix ⟦b:-scō⟧ (⟦r834:834⟧), ⟦b:escit⟧ (for ⟦b:*esscit⟧), ⟦i:gets to be⟧, ⟦i:will be⟧, ⟦b:escunt⟧; present subjunctive, ⟦b:siem⟧, ⟦b:siēs⟧, ⟦b:siet⟧, and ⟦b:sient⟧ (⟦r841:841⟧), common in inscriptions down to 100 B.C., and in old verse; also in compounds; imperative ⟦b:estōd⟧ rare.
⟦#749⟧
The present participle is used only as an adjective. It has two forms: ⟦b:sontem⟧ (accusative, no nominative), which has entirely lost its original meaning of ⟦i:being⟧, ⟦i:actual⟧, ⟦i:the real man⟧, and has only the secondary meaning of ⟦i:guilty⟧, and ⟦b:īnsōns⟧, ⟦i:innocent⟧; and ⟦b:-sēns⟧ in ⟦b:absēns⟧, ⟦i:away⟧, ⟦b:praesēns⟧, ⟦i:at hand⟧, ⟦b:dī cōnsentēs⟧, ⟦i:gods collective⟧; also once INSENTIBVS. ⟦b:sum⟧ has no gerund or gerundive.
⟦#750⟧
A subjunctive present ⟦b:fuam⟧, ⟦b:fuās⟧, ⟦b:fuat⟧, and ⟦b:fuant⟧ occurs in old Latin; and an imperfect ⟦b:forem⟧, ⟦b:forēs⟧, ⟦b:foret⟧, and ⟦b:forent⟧, in all periods. The present infinitive ⟦b:fore⟧, ⟦i:to get to be⟧, ⟦i:become⟧, has a future meaning. Old forms in the perfect system are FVVEIT (⟦r29:29, 1⟧), FVET; ⟦b:fūit⟧, ⟦b:fūimus⟧, ⟦b:fūerim⟧, ⟦b:fūerit⟧, ⟦b:fūerint⟧, ⟦b:fūisset⟧ (Plaut., Enn.). ⟦b:fuī⟧ has no perfect participle or supine.
⟦#751⟧
⟦=⟧⟦b:possum⟧, ⟦i:can⟧.
⟦=⟧Principal parts: ⟦b:possum⟧, ⟦b:posse⟧; (⟦b:potuī⟧, see ⟦r875:875⟧.)
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:possum, potes, potest⟧  ⟦b:possumus, potestis, possunt⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:poteram, poterās, poterat⟧  ⟦b:poterāmus, poterātis, poterant⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:poterō, poteris, poterit⟧  ⟦b:poterimus, poteritis, poterunt⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:possim, possīs, possit⟧  ⟦b:possīmus, possītis, possint⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:possem, possēs, posset⟧  ⟦b:possēmus, possētis, possent⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:posse⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
INDICATIVE MOOD. SUBJUNCTIVE MOOD. INFINITIVE. PARTICIPLE.
⟦#752⟧
⟦b:possum⟧ is formed from ⟦b:pote⟧, ⟦i:able⟧, and ⟦b:sum⟧, juxtaposed (166, 2; ⟦r396:396⟧). The separate forms ⟦b:potis sum⟧, &c., or ⟦b:pote sum⟧, &c., are also used, and sometimes even ⟦b:potis⟧ or ⟦b:pote⟧ alone takes the place of a verb; in either case ⟦b:potis⟧ and ⟦b:pote⟧ are indeclinable, and are applied to gender words and neuters both.
⟦#753⟧
⟦b:t⟧ is retained before a vowel, except in ⟦b:possem⟧, &c., for ⟦b:potessem⟧, &c., and in ⟦b:posse⟧; ⟦b:t⟧ before ⟦b:s⟧ changes to ⟦b:s⟧ (⟦r166:166, 2⟧). Old forms are: ⟦b:possiem⟧, &c., (⟦r748:748⟧), ⟦b:potessem⟧, ⟦b:potisset⟧, ⟦b:potesse⟧. Rare forms are POTESTO (inscr. 58 B.C.), and passives, as ⟦b:potestur⟧, &c., with a passive infinitive (⟦r1484:1484⟧). ⟦b:possum⟧ has no participles; the perfect system, ⟦b:potuī⟧, &c., is like ⟦b:fuī⟧, &c. (⟦r745:745⟧).

title: dō, give, put (dā-, da-)
text:
⟦#754⟧
There are two verbs ⟦b:dō⟧, one meaning ⟦i:give⟧, and one meaning ⟦i:put⟧. The ⟦b:dō⟧ meaning ⟦i:put⟧ is oftenest used in compounds; the simple verb has been crowded out by ⟦b:pōnō⟧. The present system of ⟦b:dō⟧ is as follows:
⟦=⟧Principal parts: ⟦b:dō⟧, ⟦b:dare⟧, ⟦b:dedī⟧, ⟦b:datus⟧.
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:dō⟧, ⟦b:dās⟧, ⟦b:dat⟧  ⟦b:damus⟧, ⟦b:datis⟧, ⟦b:dant⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:dabam⟧, ⟦b:dabās⟧, ⟦b:dabat⟧  ⟦b:dabāmus⟧, ⟦b:dabātis⟧, ⟦b:dabant⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:dabō⟧, ⟦b:dabis⟧, ⟦b:dabit⟧  ⟦b:dabimus⟧, ⟦b:dabitis⟧, ⟦b:dabunt⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:dem⟧, ⟦b:dēs⟧, ⟦b:det⟧  ⟦b:dēmus⟧, ⟦b:dētis⟧, ⟦b:dent⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:darem⟧, ⟦b:darēs⟧, ⟦b:daret⟧  ⟦b:darēmus⟧, ⟦b:darētis⟧, ⟦b:darent⟧
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:dā⟧ or ⟦b:datō⟧, ⟦b:datō⟧  ⟦b:date⟧ or ⟦b:datōte⟧, ⟦b:dantō⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:dare⟧  ⟦b:dāns⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:dandī⟧, &c.
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:daris⟧ or ⟦b:-re⟧, ⟦b:datur⟧  ⟦b:damur⟧, ⟦b:daminī⟧, ⟦b:dantur⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:dabar⟧, ⟦b:dabāre⟧ or ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:dabātur⟧  ⟦b:dabāmur⟧, ⟦b:dabāminī⟧, ⟦b:dabantur⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:dabor⟧, ⟦b:dabere⟧ or ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:dabitur⟧  ⟦b:dabimur⟧, ⟦b:dabiminī⟧, ⟦b:dabuntur⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:dēre⟧ or ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:dētur⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:dēminī⟧, ⟦b:dentur⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:darer⟧, ⟦b:darēre⟧ or ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:darētur⟧  ⟦b:darēmur⟧, ⟦b:darēminī⟧, ⟦b:darentur⟧
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:dare⟧ or ⟦b:dator⟧, ⟦b:dator⟧  ⟦b:daminī⟧, ⟦b:dantor⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:darī⟧  ⟦b:dandus⟧
⟦/⟧

⟦#755⟧
In the present system ⟦b:a⟧ is short throughout in the first syllable, except in ⟦b:dās⟧ and ⟦b:dā⟧. For ⟦b:dedī⟧, ⟦b:datus⟧, and supines ⟦b:datum⟧, ⟦b:datū⟧, see ⟦r859:859⟧ and ⟦r900:900⟧.
⟦#756⟧
Old forms: ⟦b:danunt⟧ of uncertain origin (⟦r833:833⟧) for ⟦b:dant⟧. From another form of the root come ⟦b:duis⟧, ⟦b:duit⟧; ⟦b:interduō⟧, ⟦b:concrēduō⟧, perfect ⟦b:concrēduī⟧; subjunctive ⟦b:duim⟧, ⟦b:duīs⟧ (⟦b:duās⟧), ⟦b:duit⟧ and ⟦b:duint⟧ (⟦r841:841⟧), and compounds, used especially in law language, and in praying and cursing; ⟦b:crēduam⟧, ⟦b:crēduās⟧ or ⟦b:crēduīs⟧, ⟦b:crēduat⟧ or ⟦b:crēduit⟧.
⟦#757⟧
Real compounds of ⟦b:dō⟧ have a present system like ⟦b:regō⟧ (⟦r782:782⟧); in the perfect and the perfect participle, ⟦b:e⟧ and ⟦b:a⟧ become ⟦b:i⟧: as, ⟦b:abdō⟧, ⟦i:put away⟧, ⟦b:abdere⟧, ⟦b:abdidī⟧, ⟦b:abditus⟧; ⟦b:crēdō⟧, ⟦i:put trust in⟧. ⟦b:perdō⟧, ⟦i:fordo⟧, ⟦i:destroy⟧, and ⟦b:vēndō⟧, ⟦i:put for sale⟧, have gerundives ⟦b:perdendus⟧, ⟦b:vēndundus⟧, and perfect participles ⟦b:perditus⟧, ⟦b:vēnditus⟧; the rest of the passive is supplied by forms of pereō and ⟦b:vēneō⟧. ⟦b:reddō⟧, ⟦i:give back⟧, has future ⟦b:reddibō⟧ 3 times (Plaut.). In the apparent compounds with ⟦b:circum⟧, ⟦b:pessum⟧, ⟦b:satis⟧, and ⟦b:vēnum⟧, ⟦b:dō⟧ remains without change, as in ⟦r754:754⟧.

title: bibō, serō, and sistō
text:
⟦#758⟧
⟦b:bibō⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧, ⟦b:serō⟧, ⟦i:sow⟧ (for ⟦b:*si-sō⟧, ⟦r154:154⟧), and ⟦b:sistō⟧, ⟦i:set⟧, form their present stem by reduplication of the root (⟦r189:189⟧). The vowel before the person endings is the root vowel, which becomes variable, like a formative vowel (⟦r824:824⟧). These verbs have the present system like ⟦b:regō⟧ (⟦r782:782⟧).

title: inquam, eō, and queō
text:
⟦#759⟧
⟦b:inquam⟧, ⟦b:eō⟧, and ⟦b:queō⟧ have the bare root as present stem, in almost all their parts; in a few parts only the root is extended by a formative vowel (⟦r829:829⟧).

title: inquam, say I, quoth I
text:
⟦#760⟧
⟦b:inquam⟧, ⟦i:say I⟧, is chiefly used in quoting a person’s direct words; and, from its meaning, is naturally very defective. The only parts in common use are the following:
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:inquam⟧, ⟦b:inquis⟧, ⟦b:inquit⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:inquiunt⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:inquiēs⟧, ⟦b:inquiet⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
INDICATIVE MOOD.
⟦#761⟧
Rare forms are: subjunctive ⟦b:inquiat⟧ (Cornif.), indicative imperfect ⟦b:inquiēbat⟧ (Cic.), used twice each; indicative present ⟦b:inquimus⟧ (Hor.), perfect ⟦b:inquiī⟧ (Catull.), ⟦b:inquīstī⟧ (Cic.), once each; imperative ⟦b:inque⟧, 4 times (Plaut. 2, Ter. 2), ⟦b:inquitō⟧, 3 times (Plaut.). For ⟦b:inquam⟧, see ⟦r728:728⟧.
⟦#762⟧
⟦=⟧Principal parts: ⟦b:eō⟧, ⟦b:īre⟧, ⟦b:iī⟧, ⟦b:itum⟧.
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:eō⟧, ⟦b:īs⟧, ⟦b:it⟧  ⟦b:īmus⟧, ⟦b:ītis⟧, ⟦b:eunt⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:ībam⟧, ⟦b:ībās⟧, ⟦b:ībat⟧  ⟦b:ībāmus⟧, ⟦b:ībātis⟧, ⟦b:ībant⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:ībō⟧, ⟦b:ībis⟧, ⟦b:ībit⟧  ⟦b:ībimus⟧, ⟦b:ībitis⟧, ⟦b:ībunt⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:iī⟧, ⟦b:īstī⟧, ⟦b:iīt⟧ or ⟦b:īt⟧  ⟦b:iimus⟧, ⟦b:īstis⟧, ⟦b:iērunt⟧ or ⟦b:-re⟧
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:ieram⟧, ⟦b:ierās⟧, ⟦b:ierat⟧  ⟦b:ierāmus⟧, ⟦b:ierātis⟧, ⟦b:ierant⟧
⟦i:F. P.⟧  ⟦b:ierō⟧, ⟦b:ieris⟧, ⟦b:ierit⟧  ⟦b:ierimus⟧, ⟦b:ieritis⟧, ⟦b:ierint⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:eam⟧, ⟦b:eās⟧, ⟦b:eat⟧  ⟦b:eāmus⟧, ⟦b:eātis⟧, ⟦b:eant⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:īrem⟧, ⟦b:īrēs⟧, ⟦b:īret⟧  ⟦b:īrēmus⟧, ⟦b:īrētis⟧, ⟦b:īrent⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:ierim⟧, ⟦b:ierīs⟧, ⟦b:ierit⟧  ⟦b:ierīmus⟧, ⟦b:ierītis⟧, ⟦b:ierint⟧
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:īssem⟧, ⟦b:īssēs⟧, ⟦b:īsset⟧  ⟦b:īssēmus⟧, ⟦b:īssētis⟧, ⟦b:īssent⟧
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:ī⟧ or ⟦b:ītō⟧, ⟦b:ītō⟧  ⟦b:īte⟧ or ⟦b:ītōte⟧, ⟦b:euntō⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:īre⟧  ⟦b:iēns⟧, ⟦i:Gen.⟧ ⟦b:euntis⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:īsse⟧  ⟦b:itum⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:itūrus esse⟧  ⟦b:itūrus⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:eundī⟧
⟦i:Dat.⟧  ⟦b:eundō⟧
⟦i:Acc.⟧  ⟦b:eundum⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦i:Abl.⟧  ⟦b:eundō⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
INDICATIVE MOOD. SUBJUNCTIVE MOOD. IMPERATIVE MOOD. INFINITIVE. PARTICIPLE. GERUND. SUPINE.

title: eō, go (ī- for ei-, i-)
text:
⟦#763⟧
The passive is only used impersonally, and has a neuter gerundive ⟦b:eundum⟧ and participle ⟦b:itum⟧; but transitive compounds, as ⟦b:adeō⟧, ⟦i:go up to⟧, have a complete passive: as, ⟦b:adeor⟧, ⟦b:adīris⟧, &c. ⟦b:ambiō⟧, ⟦i:go round⟧, ⟦i:canvass⟧, follows denominatives in ⟦b:-īre⟧ (⟦r796:796⟧), but has once or twice the imperfect ⟦b:ambībat⟧, ⟦b:ambībant⟧, ⟦b:ambībātur⟧ (Liv., Tac., Plin. ⟦i:Ep.⟧), and once the future ⟦b:ambībunt⟧ (Plin.); future perfect ⟦b:ambīssit⟧, ⟦b:ambīssint⟧, once each (prol. Plaut.).
⟦#764⟧
The ⟦b:ī⟧ is weakened from ⟦b:ei⟧ (⟦r98:98⟧): as, ⟦b:eis⟧, ⟦b:eit⟧, ⟦b:eite⟧, ⟦b:abeis⟧, ⟦b:abei⟧ (Plaut.); EITVR, ABEI, ADEITVR (inscr. 130 B.C.), VENEIRE (49 B.C.), PRAETEREIS. Before ⟦b:o⟧, ⟦b:u⟧, or ⟦b:a⟧, the root becomes ⟦b:e⟧. For ⟦b:u⟧ in ⟦b:euntis⟧, see ⟦r902:902⟧.
⟦#765⟧
Old forms are: ⟦b:īerō⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:īī⟧, ⟦b:īerant⟧ (Ter.), once each (⟦r126:126⟧); in an inscription of 186 B.C., ADIESET, ADIESENT, ADIESE, and of 146 B.C., REDIEIT (29, 2; ⟦r132:132⟧); INTERIEISTI. A future in ⟦b:-iet⟧, as ⟦b:trānsiet⟧ (Sen.), is late and rare.
⟦#766⟧
A double ⟦b:i⟧ is found in ⟦b:iissēs⟧ and ⟦b:iisset⟧ once each (⟦i:Ciris⟧, Nepos), also sometimes in compounds of these forms: as ⟦b:rediissēs⟧, ⟦b:interiisset⟧. Compounds sometimes have it also in the perfect infinitive and in the second person singular of the perfect indicative: as, ⟦b:abiisse⟧, ⟦b:abiistī⟧; also in ⟦b:rediistis⟧ once (Stat.). In the first person of the perfect indicative a single long ⟦b:ī⟧ is found rarely in late writers in the singular: as, ⟦b:adī⟧ (Val. Fl.).
⟦#767⟧
A few examples are found of a perfect system with ⟦b:v⟧, as ⟦b:īvī⟧, &c. This form is confined almost exclusively to poetry and late prose.
(⟦i:a⟧) Examples of simple forms with ⟦b:v⟧ are: ⟦b:īvisse⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:īvit⟧ (Cato), ⟦b:īvī⟧ (Varro), ⟦b:īverat⟧ (Catull.). (⟦i:b⟧) Compound forms: ⟦b:exīvī⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:obīvit⟧ (Verg.), ⟦b:subīvit⟧ (Stat.); ⟦b:trānsīvisse⟧ (Claud. ap. Tac.), ⟦b:inīvimus⟧, ⟦b:trānsīvī⟧, ⟦b:trānsīvimus⟧ (Curt.), ⟦b:trānsīvit⟧, ⟦b:trānsīverant⟧ (Sen.), ⟦b:exīvit⟧ (Gell.). Apparent compounds (⟦r396:396⟧): ⟦b:īntrō īvit⟧ (C. Gracch., Piso, Gell.).

title: queō, can
text:
⟦#768⟧
⟦b:queō⟧, ⟦i:can⟧, and ⟦b:nequeō⟧, ⟦i:can’t⟧, have the perfect ⟦b:quīvī⟧, the rest like ⟦b:eō⟧ (⟦r762:762⟧); but they have no imperative, gerundive, or future participle, and the present participle is rare. ⟦b:queō⟧ is commonly used with a negative, and some parts only so. Passive forms are rare, and only used with a passive infinitive (⟦r1484:1484⟧).

title: edō, eat (ed-, ēd-)
text:
⟦#769⟧
⟦b:edō⟧, ⟦i:eat⟧, has a present system with a formative vowel like ⟦b:regō⟧ throughout (⟦r782:782⟧); but in some parts of the present, and of the imperfect subjunctive, parallel root forms are usually found, with ⟦b:d⟧ of the root changed to ⟦b:s⟧, and the vowel lengthened (⟦r135:135⟧), as may be seen in the following:
⟦=⟧Principal parts: ⟦b:edō⟧, ⟦b:ēsse⟧, ⟦b:ēdī⟧, ⟦b:ēsus⟧.
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:edō⟧, ⟦b:ēs⟧ or ⟦b:edis⟧, ⟦b:ēst⟧ or ⟦b:edit⟧  ⟦b:edimus⟧, ⟦b:ēstis⟧ or ⟦b:editis⟧, ⟦b:edunt⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:edim⟧, ⟦b:edīs⟧, ⟦b:edit⟧ or ⟦b:edam⟧, ⟦b:edās⟧, ⟦b:edat⟧  ⟦b:edīmus⟧, ⟦b:edītis⟧, ⟦b:edint⟧ or ⟦b:edāmus⟧, ⟦b:edātis⟧, ⟦b:edant⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:ēssem⟧, ⟦b:ēssēs⟧, ⟦b:ēsset⟧ or ⟦b:ederem⟧, ⟦b:ederēs⟧, ⟦b:ederet⟧  ⟦b:ēssēmus⟧, ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:ēssent⟧ or ⟦b:ederēmus⟧, ⟦b:ederētis⟧, ⟦b:ederent⟧
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:ēs⟧ or ⟦b:ede⟧, ⟦b:ēstō⟧ or ⟦b:editō⟧  ⟦b:ēste⟧ or ⟦b:edite⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:ēsse⟧  ⟦b:edēns⟧
⟦/⟧
INDICATIVE MOOD. SUBJUNCTIVE MOOD. IMPERATIVE MOOD. INFINITIVE. PARTICIPLE.
⟦#770⟧
For ⟦b:ēs⟧, see ⟦r728:728⟧; for ⟦b:edim⟧, &c., ⟦r841:841⟧. In the passive, the indicative present ⟦b:ēstur⟧ is used, and imperfect subjunctive ⟦b:ēssētur⟧. The perfect participle ⟦b:ēsus⟧ is for an older ⟦b:ēssus⟧ (⟦r170:170, 7⟧). Supines ⟦b:ēssum⟧, ⟦b:ēssū⟧ (Plaut.).
⟦#771⟧
⟦b:comedō⟧, ⟦i:eat up⟧, has also the following root forms: ⟦b:comēs⟧, ⟦b:comēst⟧, ⟦b:comēstis⟧; ⟦b:comēstō⟧; ⟦b:comēsse⟧; ⟦b:comēssēs⟧, ⟦b:comēsset⟧, ⟦b:comēssēmus⟧. The present subjunctive has also ⟦b:comedim⟧, ⟦b:comedīs⟧, ⟦b:comedint⟧. The participle perfect is ⟦b:comēssus⟧, ⟦b:comēsus⟧, or ⟦b:comēstus⟧, future ⟦b:comēssūrus⟧. ⟦b:exedō⟧, ⟦i:eat out⟧, has ⟦b:exēst⟧ and ⟦b:exēsse⟧; subjunctive ⟦b:exedint⟧. ⟦b:adedō⟧, ⟦i:eat at⟧, has ⟦b:adēst⟧.
⟦#772⟧

title: volō, will, wish, want, am willing (vol-, vel-)
text:
⟦#774⟧
⟦b:volo⟧ for ⟦b:volō⟧ is rare (⟦r2443:2443⟧). ⟦b:volt⟧ and ⟦b:voltis⟧ became ⟦b:vult⟧ and ⟦b:vultis⟧ about the time of Augustus (⟦r141:141⟧). For ⟦b:volumus⟧, see ⟦r142:142⟧; ⟦b:velim⟧, &c., ⟦r841:841⟧; ⟦b:vellem⟧, &c., ⟦b:velle⟧, 166, 8. ⟦b:sīs⟧, ⟦i:an thou wilt⟧, is common for ⟦b:sī vīs⟧ (Plaut., Ter., Cic., Liv.). ⟦b:sultis⟧, ⟦i:an ‘t please you⟧, is used by Plautus for ⟦b:sī voltis⟧.
⟦#775⟧
⟦b:nōlō⟧, ⟦i:won’t⟧, is formed from ⟦b:ne-⟧, ⟦i:not⟧, and ⟦b:volō⟧, juxtaposed, and ⟦b:mālō⟧, ⟦i:like better⟧, abbreviated from ⟦b:māvolō⟧ for ⟦b:*magsvolo⟧ (⟦r779:779⟧, 170, 2).

⟦b:nevīs⟧ and ⟦b:nevolt⟧, from ⟦b:ne-⟧, ⟦i:not⟧, are found in Plautus. ⟦b:nōlō⟧ has usually no participles, but oblique cases of ⟦b:nōlēns⟧ are used a few times by post-Augustan writers (Cels., Luc., Quintil., Ta., Juv., Mart., Plin.). title: Verbs in -iō, -ere
text:
⟦#784⟧
Verbs in ⟦b:-iō⟧, ⟦b:-ere⟧, as ⟦b:capiō⟧, ⟦b:capere⟧, ⟦i:take⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:cap-⟧⟧), drop an ⟦b:i⟧ in some forms of the present and imperfect. The present system is as follows:
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:capiō⟧, ⟦b:capis⟧, ⟦b:capit⟧  ⟦b:capimus⟧, ⟦b:capitis⟧, ⟦b:capiunt⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:capiēbam⟧, ⟦b:capiēbās⟧, ⟦b:capiēbat⟧  ⟦b:capiēbāmus⟧, ⟦b:capiēbātis⟧, ⟦b:capiēbant⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:capiam⟧, ⟦b:capiēs⟧, ⟦b:capiet⟧  ⟦b:capiēmus⟧, ⟦b:capiētis⟧, ⟦b:capient⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:capiam⟧, ⟦b:capiās⟧, ⟦b:capiat⟧  ⟦b:capiāmus⟧, ⟦b:capiātis⟧, ⟦b:capiant⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:caperem⟧, ⟦b:caperēs⟧, ⟦b:caperet⟧  ⟦b:caperēmus⟧, ⟦b:caperētis⟧, ⟦b:caperent⟧
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:cape⟧ or ⟦b:capitō⟧, ⟦b:capitō⟧  ⟦b:capite⟧ or ⟦b:capitōte⟧, ⟦b:capiuntō⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:capere⟧  ⟦b:capiēns⟧
⟦i:Gen.⟧  ⟦b:capiendī⟧, &c.
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:capior⟧, ⟦b:caperis⟧ or ⟦b:-re⟧, ⟦b:capitur⟧  ⟦b:capimur⟧, ⟦b:capiminī⟧, ⟦b:capiuntur⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:capiēbar⟧, ⟦b:capiēbāre⟧ or ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:capiēbātur⟧  ⟦b:capiēbāmur⟧, ⟦b:capiēbāminī⟧, ⟦b:capiēbantur⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:capiar⟧, ⟦b:capiēre⟧ or ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:capiētur⟧  ⟦b:capiēmur⟧, ⟦b:capiēminī⟧, ⟦b:capientur⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:capiar⟧, ⟦b:capiāre⟧ or ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:capiātur⟧  ⟦b:capiāmur⟧, ⟦b:capiāminī⟧, ⟦b:capiantur⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:caperer⟧, ⟦b:caperēre⟧ or ⟦b:-ris⟧, ⟦b:caperētur⟧  ⟦b:caperēmur⟧, ⟦b:caperēminī⟧, ⟦b:caperentur⟧
⟦.⟧  ⟦b:capere⟧ or ⟦b:capitor⟧, ⟦b:capitor⟧  ⟦b:capiminī⟧, ⟦b:capiuntor⟧

⟦#785⟧
There are a dozen verbs in ⟦b:-īō⟧, ⟦b:-ere⟧, like ⟦b:capiō⟧, and three deponents in ⟦b:-ior⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, all formed from consonant roots with a short vowel: see ⟦r836:836⟧. ⟦b:aiō⟧, ⟦i:say⟧, and ⟦b:fīō⟧, ⟦i:grow⟧, ⟦i:become⟧, have certain peculiarities arising from the blending of the root with the suffix.
⟦=⟧(1.) ⟦b:aiō⟧, ⟦i:say⟧, ⟦i:say ay⟧, ⟦i:avouch⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:ag-⟧⟧).
⟦#786⟧
⟦b:aiō⟧, ⟦i:say⟧, is defective, and has only these parts in common use:
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Ind. Pres.⟧  ⟦b:aiō⟧, ⟦b:ais⟧, ⟦b:ait⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:aiunt⟧
⟦i:Ind. Imp.⟧  ⟦b:aiēbam⟧, ⟦b:aiēbās⟧, ⟦b:aiēbat⟧  ⟦b:aiēbāmus⟧, ⟦b:aiēbātis⟧, ⟦b:aiēbant⟧
⟦i:Subj. Pres.⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:aiās⟧, ⟦b:aiāt⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#787⟧
For ⟦b:aiō⟧, sometimes written ⟦b:aiiō⟧ (⟦r23:23⟧), see 153, 2. Old forms are: present ⟦b:ais⟧, ⟦b:aīs⟧, ⟦b:a͡is⟧, or with ⟦b:-n⟧ interrogative ⟦b:āin⟧, ⟦b:a͡in⟧; ⟦b:aīt⟧, ⟦b:ait⟧, or ⟦b:a͡it⟧; imperfect ⟦b:a͡ibam⟧, ⟦b:a͡ibās⟧, ⟦b:a͡ibat⟧, and ⟦b:a͡ibant⟧; imperative once only, ⟦b:aī⟧ (Naev.). A participle ⟦b:aientibus⟧, ⟦i:affirmative⟧, occurs once (Cic.).
⟦=⟧(2.) ⟦b:fīō⟧, ⟦i:become⟧, ⟦i:am made⟧.
⟦#788⟧
⟦b:fīō⟧, ⟦i:become⟧, and ⟦b:factus sum⟧ supplement each other: in the present system, the passive of ⟦b:faciō⟧, ⟦i:make⟧, except the gerundive, ⟦b:faciendus⟧, is not used, ⟦b:fīō⟧, &c., taking its place; in the perfect system, only ⟦b:factus sum⟧, &c., is used.
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Ind. Pres.⟧  ⟦b:fīō⟧, ⟦b:fīs⟧, ⟦b:fit⟧  ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:——⟧, ⟦b:fīunt⟧
⟦i:Ind. Imp.⟧  ⟦b:fīēbam⟧, ⟦b:fīēbās⟧, ⟦b:fīēbat⟧  ⟦b:fīēbāmus⟧, ⟦b:fīēbātis⟧, ⟦b:fīēbant⟧
⟦i:Ind. Fut.⟧  ⟦b:fīam⟧, ⟦b:fīēs⟧, ⟦b:fīet⟧  ⟦b:fīēmus⟧, ⟦b:fīētis⟧, ⟦b:fīent⟧
⟦i:Subj. Pres.⟧  ⟦b:fīam⟧, ⟦b:fīās⟧, ⟦b:fīat⟧  ⟦b:fīāmus⟧, ⟦b:fīātis⟧, ⟦b:fīant⟧
⟦i:Subj. Imp.⟧  ⟦b:fierem⟧, ⟦b:fierēs⟧, ⟦b:fieret⟧  ⟦b:fierēmus⟧, ⟦b:fierētis⟧, ⟦b:fierent⟧
⟦i:Imper.⟧  ⟦b:fī⟧  ⟦b:fīte⟧
⟦i:Infin. Pres.⟧  ⟦b:fierī⟧  ⟦i:Part. Pres.⟧ ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#789⟧
In ⟦b:fīō⟧, &c., ⟦b:ī⟧ represents an older ⟦b:ei⟧, seen in FEIENT (inscr. 45 B.C.). The infinitive ⟦b:fierī⟧ for ⟦b:fierei⟧ owes its passive ending to analogy; the active form ⟦b:fiere⟧ occurs twice (Enn., Laev.). The vowel before ⟦b:-er-⟧ in ⟦b:fierem⟧, &c., and ⟦b:fierī⟧, is sometimes long in the dramatists, where a cretic (- ⏑ -) is required, but otherwise always short.
⟦#790⟧
⟦b:-fīō⟧ is used in apparent compounds (⟦r394:394⟧): as, ⟦b:patē̆fit⟧. In real compounds commonly ⟦b:-ficior⟧: as, ⟦b:cōnficior⟧; but sometimes ⟦b:-fīō⟧: as, ⟦b:cōnfit⟧, ⟦b:cōnfīunt⟧, ⟦b:cōnfīat⟧, ⟦b:cōnfieret⟧, ⟦b:cōnfierent⟧, ⟦b:cōnfī̆erī⟧; ⟦b:dēfit⟧, ⟦b:dēfīet⟧, ⟦b:dēfīat⟧, ⟦b:dēfierī⟧; ⟦b:effit⟧, ⟦b:effīant⟧, ⟦b:ecfīerī⟧; ⟦b:īnfit⟧; ⟦b:interfīat⟧, ⟦b:interfīerī⟧; ⟦b:superfit⟧, ⟦b:superfīat⟧.
⟦#791⟧
Some verbs in ⟦b:-iō⟧, ⟦b:-ere⟧ (or ⟦b:-ior⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧), have occasionally the form of verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧ (or ⟦b:-īrī⟧), in some parts of the present system, oftenest before an ⟦b:r⟧, and particularly in the passive infinitive: as,
⟦b:fodīrī⟧, 3 times (Cato, Col. 2), ⟦b:circumfodīrī⟧ (Col.), ⟦b:ecfodīrī⟧ (Plaut.); ⟦b:adgredīrī⟧ (⟦b:adgredīrier⟧), 4 times (Plaut.), ⟦b:prōgredīrī⟧ (Plaut.); ⟦b:morīrī⟧ 6 times (Plaut. 4, Pomp., Ov.), ⟦b:ēmorīrī⟧ twice (Plaut., Ter.); ⟦b:orīrī⟧, always; ⟦b:parīre⟧, twice (Plaut., Enn.); usually ⟦b:potīrī⟧ (⟦b:potīrier⟧). Also ⟦b:cupīret⟧ (Lucr.); ⟦b:adgredīre⟧, ⟦b:adgredībor⟧, ⟦b:adgredīmur⟧ (Plaut.); ⟦b:morīmur⟧ (Enn.); ⟦b:orīris⟧ (Varr., Sen.), ⟦b:adorītur⟧ (Lucil., Lucr.), ⟦b:orīrētur⟧ (Cic., Nep., Sall., Liv.), ⟦b:adorīrētur⟧ (Liv., Suet.); ⟦b:parībis⟧ (Pomp.), PARIRET (inscr.); ⟦b:potīris⟧ (Manil.), ⟦b:potītur⟧ (Lucil., Ov.), &c., &c.

title: The Deponent Verb
text:
⟦#798⟧
Deponents, that is, verbs with passive person endings and a reflexive or an active meaning (⟦r725:725⟧), have these active noun forms: participles, the future infinitive, the gerund, and the supines.
