⟦#799⟧
Three deponents in ⟦b:-ior⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧, ⟦b:gradior⟧, ⟦i:walk⟧, ⟦b:morior⟧, ⟦i:die⟧, and ⟦b:patior⟧, ⟦i:suffer⟧, and their compounds, have a present system like the passive of ⟦b:capiō⟧ (⟦r784:784⟧). But ⟦b:adgredior⟧ and ⟦b:prōgredior⟧ and ⟦b:morior⟧ and ⟦b:ēmorior⟧ have sometimes the forms of verbs in ⟦b:-īrī⟧; for these, and for ⟦b:orior⟧, ⟦i:arise⟧, ⟦b:orīrī⟧, ⟦b:ortus⟧, and ⟦b:potior⟧, ⟦i:become master of⟧, ⟦b:potīrī⟧, ⟦b:potītus⟧, see ⟦r791:791⟧. By far the largest number of deponents are verbs in ⟦b:-ārī⟧, like ⟦b:mīror⟧, ⟦b:mīrārī⟧ (⟦r368:368⟧).
⟦#800⟧
Some verbs waver between active and passive person endings: as, ⟦b:adsentiō⟧, ⟦i:agree⟧, ⟦b:adsentīre⟧, and ⟦b:adsentior⟧, ⟦b:adsentīrī⟧; ⟦b:populō⟧, ⟦i:ravage⟧, ⟦b:populāre⟧, and ⟦b:populor⟧, ⟦b:populārī⟧: see ⟦r1481:1481⟧.
⟦#801⟧
A few verbs are deponent in the present system only: as, ⟦b:dēvortor⟧, ⟦i:turn in⟧, perfect ⟦b:dēvortī⟧; ⟦b:revortor⟧, ⟦i:turn back⟧, perfect ⟦b:revortī⟧, but with active perfect participle ⟦b:revorsus⟧. Four are deponent in the perfect system only: ⟦b:fīdō⟧, ⟦i:trust⟧, ⟦b:fīdere⟧, ⟦b:fīsus⟧, and the compounds, ⟦b:cōnfīdō⟧, ⟦b:diffīdō⟧; and ⟦b:audeō⟧, ⟦i:dare⟧, ⟦b:audēre⟧, ⟦b:ausus⟧, ⟦b:gaudeō⟧, ⟦i:feel glad⟧, ⟦b:gaudēre⟧, ⟦b:gāvīsus⟧, and ⟦b:soleō⟧, ⟦i:am used⟧, ⟦b:solēre⟧, ⟦b:solitus⟧. Most impersonals in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ have both an active and a deponent form in the perfect system: see ⟦r815:815⟧, ⟦r816:816⟧.

title: Periphrastic Forms
text:
⟦#802⟧
(1.) The future active participle with a form of ⟦b:sum⟧ is used to denote an intended or future action: as,
⟦=⟧⟦b:rēctūrus sum⟧, ⟦i:I am going to rule⟧, ⟦i:intend to rule⟧.
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus sum⟧, ⟦b:es⟧, ⟦b:est⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī sumus⟧, ⟦b:estis⟧, ⟦b:sunt⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus eram⟧, ⟦b:erās⟧, ⟦b:erat⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī erāmus⟧, ⟦b:erātis⟧, ⟦b:erant⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus erō⟧, ⟦b:eris⟧, ⟦b:erit⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī erimus⟧, ⟦b:eritis⟧, ⟦b:erunt⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus fuī⟧, ⟦b:fuistī⟧, ⟦b:fuit⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī fuimus⟧, ⟦b:fuistis⟧, ⟦b:fuērunt⟧
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus fueram⟧, ⟦b:fuerās⟧, ⟦b:fuerat⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī fuerāmus⟧, ⟦b:fuerātis⟧, ⟦b:fuerant⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus sim⟧, ⟦b:sīs⟧, ⟦b:sit⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī sīmus⟧, ⟦b:sītis⟧, ⟦b:sint⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus essem⟧, ⟦b:essēs⟧, ⟦b:esset⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī essēmus⟧, ⟦b:essētis⟧, ⟦b:essent⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus fuerim⟧, ⟦b:fuerīs⟧, ⟦b:fuerit⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī fuerīmus⟧, ⟦b:fuerītis⟧, ⟦b:fuerint⟧
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus fuissem⟧, ⟦b:fuissēs⟧, ⟦b:fuisset⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrī fuissēmus⟧, ⟦b:fuissētis⟧, ⟦b:fuissent⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus esse⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:rēctūrus fuisse⟧
⟦/⟧
INDICATIVE MOOD. SUBJUNCTIVE MOOD. INFINITIVE.
⟦#803⟧
A future perfect is hardly ever used: as, ⟦b:fuerit victūrus⟧ (Sen.). In the imperfect subjunctive, ⟦b:forem⟧, ⟦b:forēs⟧, ⟦b:foret⟧, and ⟦b:forent⟧ are sometimes used (Nep., Sall., Liv., Vell.).
⟦#804⟧
(2.) The gerundive with a form of ⟦b:sum⟧ is used to denote action which requires to be done: as,
⟦=⟧⟦b:regendus sum⟧, ⟦i:I am to be ruled⟧, ⟦i:must be ruled⟧.
⟦.⟧  Singular.  Plural.
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:regendus sum⟧, ⟦b:es⟧, ⟦b:est⟧  ⟦b:regendī sumus⟧, ⟦b:estis⟧, ⟦b:sunt⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:regendus eram⟧, ⟦b:erās⟧, ⟦b:erat⟧  ⟦b:regendī erāmus⟧, ⟦b:erātis⟧, ⟦b:erant⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:regendus erō⟧, ⟦b:eris⟧, ⟦b:erit⟧  ⟦b:regendī erimus⟧, ⟦b:eritis⟧, ⟦b:erunt⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:regendus fuī⟧, ⟦b:fuistī⟧, ⟦b:fuit⟧  ⟦b:regendī fuimus⟧, ⟦b:fuistis⟧, ⟦b:fuērunt⟧
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:regendus fueram⟧, ⟦b:fuerās⟧, ⟦b:fuerat⟧  ⟦b:regendī fuerāmus⟧, ⟦b:fuerātis⟧, ⟦b:fuerant⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:regendus sim⟧, ⟦b:sīs⟧, ⟦b:sit⟧  ⟦b:regendī sīmus⟧, ⟦b:sītis⟧, ⟦b:sint⟧
⟦i:Imp.⟧  ⟦b:regendus essem⟧, ⟦b:essēs⟧, ⟦b:esset⟧  ⟦b:regendī essēmus⟧, ⟦b:essētis⟧, ⟦b:essent⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:regendus fuerim⟧, ⟦b:fuerīs⟧, ⟦b:fuerit⟧  ⟦b:regendī fuerīmus⟧, ⟦b:fuerītis⟧, ⟦b:fuerint⟧
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:regendus fuissem⟧, ⟦b:fuissēs⟧, ⟦b:fuisset⟧  ⟦b:regendī fuissēmus⟧, ⟦b:fuissētis⟧, ⟦b:fuissent⟧
⟦i:Pres.⟧  ⟦b:regendus esse⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:regendus fuisse⟧
⟦/⟧
INDICATIVE MOOD. SUBJUNCTIVE MOOD. INFINITIVE.

title: Defective Verbs
text:
⟦#805⟧
(1.) Some verbs have only a few forms: as,
⟦b:inquam⟧, ⟦i:quoth I⟧ (⟦r760:760⟧); ⟦b:aiō⟧, ⟦i:avouch⟧ (⟦r786:786⟧). See also ⟦b:apage⟧, ⟦i:avaunt⟧, ⟦i:get thee behind me⟧, ⟦b:cedo⟧, ⟦i:give⟧, ⟦i:tell⟧, ⟦b:fārī⟧, ⟦i:to lift up one’s voice⟧, ⟦b:havē̆⟧ or ⟦b:avē̆⟧ and ⟦b:salvē⟧, ⟦i:all hail⟧, ⟦b:ovat⟧, ⟦i:triumphs⟧, and ⟦b:quaesō⟧, ⟦i:prithee⟧, in the dictionary.
⟦#806⟧
(2.) Many verbs have only the present system; such are:
⟦#807⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧ (⟦r745:745⟧); ⟦b:ferō⟧, ⟦i:carry⟧ (⟦r780:780⟧); ⟦b:fīō⟧, ⟦i:grow⟧, ⟦i:become⟧ (⟦r788:788⟧).
⟦#808⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) Some verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧: ⟦b:angō⟧, ⟦i:throttle⟧, ⟦b:bītō⟧, ⟦i:go⟧, ⟦b:clangō⟧, ⟦i:sound⟧, ⟦b:claudō⟧ or ⟦b:claudeō⟧, ⟦i:hobble⟧, ⟦b:fatīscō⟧, ⟦i:gape⟧, ⟦b:glīscō⟧, ⟦i:wax⟧, ⟦b:glūbō⟧, ⟦i:peel⟧, ⟦b:hīscō⟧, ⟦i:gape⟧, ⟦b:temnō⟧, ⟦i:scorn⟧, ⟦b:vādō⟧, ⟦i:go⟧, ⟦b:vergō⟧, ⟦i:slope⟧. Also many inceptives (⟦r834:834⟧): as, ⟦b:dītēscō⟧, ⟦i:get rich⟧, ⟦b:dulcēscō⟧, ⟦i:get sweet⟧, &c., &c.
⟦#809⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) Some verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧: ⟦b:albeō⟧, ⟦i:am white⟧, ⟦b:aveō⟧, ⟦i:long⟧, ⟦b:calveō⟧, ⟦i:am bald⟧, ⟦b:cāneō⟧, ⟦i:am gray⟧, ⟦b:clueō⟧, ⟦i:am called⟧, ⟦i:hight⟧, ⟦b:flāveō⟧, ⟦i:am yellow⟧, ⟦b:hebeō⟧, ⟦i:am blunt⟧, ⟦b:immineō⟧, ⟦i:threaten⟧, ⟦b:lacteō⟧, ⟦i:suck⟧, ⟦b:līveō⟧, ⟦i:look dark⟧, ⟦b:maereō⟧, ⟦i:mourn⟧, ⟦b:polleō⟧, ⟦i:am strong⟧, ⟦b:renīdeō⟧, ⟦i:am radiant⟧, ⟦b:squāleō⟧, ⟦i:am scaly⟧, ⟦b:ūmeō⟧, ⟦i:am wet⟧.
⟦#810⟧
(⟦i:d.⟧) Some verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧: ⟦b:balbūtiō⟧, ⟦i:sputter⟧, ⟦b:feriō⟧, ⟦i:strike⟧, ⟦b:ganniō⟧, ⟦i:yelp⟧, ⟦b:ineptiō⟧, ⟦i:am a fool⟧, ⟦b:superbiō⟧, ⟦i:am stuck up⟧, ⟦b:tussiō⟧, ⟦i:cough⟧. Also most desideratives (⟦r375:375⟧).
⟦#811⟧
Many verbs are not attended by a perfect participle, and lack in consequence the perfect passive system, or, if deponent, the perfect active system.
⟦#812⟧
(3.) Some verbs have only the perfect system: so particularly ⟦b:coepī⟧, ⟦i:have begun⟧, ⟦i:began⟧ (⟦r120:120⟧); and with a present meaning, ⟦b:ōdī⟧, ⟦i:have come to hate⟧, ⟦i:hate⟧; and ⟦b:meminī⟧, ⟦i:have called to mind⟧, ⟦i:remember⟧. The following is a synopsis of these three verbs:
⟦.⟧  Active.  Passive.  Active.  Active.
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:coepī⟧  ⟦b:coeptus sum⟧  ⟦b:ōdī⟧  ⟦b:meminī⟧
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:coeperam⟧  ⟦b:coeptus eram⟧  ⟦b:ōderam⟧  ⟦b:memineram⟧
⟦i:F. P.⟧  ⟦b:coeperō⟧  ⟦b:coeptus erō⟧  ⟦b:ōderō⟧  ⟦b:meminerō⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:coeperim⟧  ⟦b:coeptus sim⟧  ⟦b:ōderim⟧  ⟦b:meminerim⟧
⟦i:Plup.⟧  ⟦b:coepissem⟧  ⟦b:coeptus essem⟧  ⟦b:ōdissem⟧  ⟦b:meminissem⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:mementō⟧, ⟦b:mementōte⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦b:coepisse⟧  ⟦b:coeptus esse⟧  ⟦b:ōdisse⟧  ⟦b:meminisse⟧
⟦i:Perf.⟧  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:coeptus⟧  ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦i:Fut.⟧  ⟦b:coeptūrus⟧  ⟦.⟧  ⟦b:ōsūrus⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
INDICATIVE MOOD. SUBJUNCTIVE MOOD. IMPERATIVE MOOD. INFINITIVE. PARTICIPLES.
⟦#813⟧
A few forms of the present system of ⟦b:coepī⟧ occur in old writers: as, ⟦b:coepiō⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:coepiam⟧ (Caec., Cato), ⟦b:coepiat⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:coeperet⟧ (Ter.), and ⟦b:coepere⟧ (Plaut.); perfect once ⟦b:coēpit⟧ (Lucr.). ⟦b:ōsus sum⟧ or ⟦b:fuī⟧ (Plaut., C. Gracch., Gell.), ⟦b:exōsus sum⟧ (Verg., Sen., Curt., Gell.), and ⟦b:perōsus sum⟧ (Suet., Col., Quint.), are sometimes used as deponents. ⟦b:meminī⟧ is the only verb which has a perfect imperative active. ⟦b:ōdī⟧ and ⟦b:meminī⟧ have no passive.
⟦#814⟧
⟦b:coeptūrus⟧ is rather rare and late (Liv. 2, Plin., Suet.), once as future infinitive (Quint.); and ⟦b:ōsūrus⟧ is very rare (Cic., Gell.). ⟦b:exōsus⟧ and ⟦b:perōsus⟧, as active participles, ⟦i:hating bitterly⟧, are not uncommon in writers of the empire; the simple ⟦b:ōsus⟧ is not used as a participle.
⟦#815⟧
(4.) Impersonal verbs have usually only the third person singular, and the infinitive present and perfect: as,
(⟦i:a.⟧) ⟦b:pluit⟧, ⟦i:it rains⟧, ⟦b:tonat⟧, ⟦i:it thunders⟧, and other verbs denoting the operations of nature. (⟦i:b.⟧) Also a few verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ denoting feeling: as, ⟦b:miseret⟧ (or ⟦b:miserētur⟧, ⟦b:miserēscit⟧), ⟦i:it distresses⟧, ⟦b:miseritum est⟧; ⟦b:paenitet⟧, ⟦i:it repents⟧, ⟦b:paenituit⟧; ⟦b:piget⟧, ⟦i:it grieves⟧, ⟦b:piguit⟧ or ⟦b:pigitum est⟧; ⟦b:pudet⟧, ⟦i:it shames⟧, ⟦b:puduit⟧ or ⟦b:puditum est⟧; ⟦b:taedet⟧, ⟦i:it is a bore⟧, ⟦b:taesum est⟧.
⟦#816⟧
Some other verbs, less correctly called impersonal, with an infinitive or a sentence as subject, are likewise defective: as,
⟦b:lubet⟧ or ⟦b:libet⟧, ⟦i:it suits⟧, ⟦b:lubitum⟧ or ⟦b:libitum est⟧, ⟦b:lubuit⟧ or ⟦b:libuit⟧; ⟦b:licet⟧, ⟦i:it is allowed⟧, ⟦b:licuit⟧ or ⟦b:licitum est⟧; ⟦b:oportet⟧, ⟦i:it is proper⟧, ⟦b:oportuit⟧; ⟦b:rē fert⟧ or ⟦b:rēfert⟧, ⟦i:it concerns⟧, ⟦b:rē ferre⟧ or ⟦b:rēferre⟧, ⟦b:rē tulit⟧ or ⟦b:rētulit⟧. For the impersonal use of the third person singular passive, as ⟦b:pugnātur⟧, ⟦i:there is fighting⟧, ⟦b:pugnandum est⟧, ⟦i:there must be fighting⟧, see ⟦r724:724⟧.
⟦#817⟧
Of the impersonals in ⟦b:-ēre⟧, some have other forms besides the third person singular and the infinitives: as,
⟦b:paenitēns⟧, ⟦i:repenting⟧, ⟦b:paenitendus⟧, ⟦i:to be regretted⟧, late; ⟦b:pigendus⟧, ⟦i:irksome⟧; ⟦b:pudēns⟧, ⟦i:modest⟧, ⟦b:pudendus⟧, ⟦i:shameful⟧, ⟦b:puditūrum⟧, ⟦i:going to shame⟧; ⟦b:lubēns⟧ or ⟦b:libēns⟧, ⟦i:with willing mind⟧, ⟦i:gladly⟧, very common indeed; imperative LICETO, ⟦i:be it allowed⟧ (inscrr. 133-111 B.C.), ⟦b:licēns⟧, ⟦i:unrestrained⟧, ⟦b:licitus⟧, ⟦i:allowable⟧; gerunds ⟦b:pudendum⟧, ⟦b:pudendō⟧, ⟦b:pigendum⟧.

title: Redundant Verbs
text:
⟦#818⟧
(1.) Some verbs have more than one form of the present stem: thus,
⟦#819⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) Verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have rarely forms of verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ in the present system: as, ⟦b:abnueō⟧, ⟦i:nod no⟧, ⟦b:abnuēbunt⟧ (Enn.), for ⟦b:abnuō⟧, ⟦b:abnuent⟧; ⟦b:congruēre⟧, ⟦i:to agree⟧ (Ter.), for ⟦b:congruere⟧. For verbs in ⟦b:-iō⟧, ⟦b:-ere⟧ (or ⟦b:-ior⟧, ⟦b:-ī⟧), with forms of verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧ (or ⟦b:-īrī⟧), see ⟦r791:791⟧. Once ⟦b:pīnsībant⟧ (Enn.).
⟦#820⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) Some verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ have occasionally a present stem like verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧: as, ⟦b:lavis⟧, ⟦i:washest⟧, ⟦b:lavit⟧, &c., for ⟦b:lavās⟧, ⟦b:lavat⟧, &c.; ⟦b:sonit⟧, ⟦i:sounds⟧, ⟦b:sonunt⟧, for ⟦b:sonat⟧, ⟦b:sonant⟧. Others have occasionally a present stem like verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧: as, ⟦i:dēnseō⟧, ⟦i:thicken⟧, ⟦i:dēnsērī⟧, for ⟦i:dēnsō⟧, ⟦b:dēnsārī⟧.
⟦#821⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) Some verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ have occasionally a present stem like verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧: as, ⟦b:fervit⟧, ⟦i:boils⟧, ⟦b:fervont⟧, for ⟦b:fervet⟧, ⟦b:fervent⟧. See also ⟦b:fulgeō⟧, ⟦b:oleō⟧, ⟦b:scateō⟧, ⟦b:strīdeō⟧, ⟦b:tergeō⟧, ⟦b:tueor⟧ in the dictionary. ⟦b:cieō⟧, ⟦i:set a going⟧, sometimes has a present stem in ⟦b:-īre⟧, particularly in compounds: as, ⟦b:cīmus⟧, ⟦b:ciunt⟧, for ⟦b:ciēmus⟧, ⟦b:cient⟧.
⟦#822⟧
(⟦i:d.⟧) Some verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧ have occasionally a present stem like verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧: as, ⟦b:ēvenunt⟧, ⟦i:turn out⟧, for ⟦b:ēveniunt⟧; ⟦b:ēvenat⟧, ⟦b:ēvenant⟧, for ⟦b:ēveniat⟧, ⟦b:ēveniant⟧, and ⟦b:advenat⟧, ⟦b:pervenat⟧, for ⟦b:adveniat⟧, ⟦b:perveniat⟧ (Plaut.).
⟦#823⟧
(2.) Some verbs have more than one form of the perfect stem: as,
⟦b:eō⟧, ⟦i:go⟧, old ⟦b:īī⟧ (⟦r765:765⟧), common ⟦b:iī⟧, rarely ⟦b:īvī⟧ (⟦r767:767⟧); ⟦b:pluit⟧, ⟦i:it rains⟧, ⟦b:pluit⟧, sometimes ⟦b:plūvit⟧. See also ⟦b:pangō⟧, ⟦b:parcō⟧, ⟦b:clepō⟧, ⟦b:vollō⟧ or ⟦b:vellō⟧, ⟦b:intellegō⟧, ⟦b:pōnō⟧, ⟦b:nectō⟧, and ⟦b:adnectō⟧, ⟦b:saliō⟧ and ⟦b:īnsiliō⟧, ⟦b:applicō⟧, ⟦b:explicō⟧ and ⟦b:implicō⟧, ⟦b:dīmicō⟧ and ⟦b:necō⟧ in the dictionary. Some compound verbs have a form of the perfect which is different from that of the simple verb: as, ⟦b:canō⟧, ⟦i:make music⟧, ⟦b:cecinī⟧, ⟦b:concinuī⟧, ⟦b:occinuī⟧; ⟦b:pungō⟧, ⟦i:punch⟧, ⟦b:pupugī⟧, ⟦b:compunxī⟧, ⟦b:expunxī⟧; ⟦b:legō⟧, ⟦i:pick up⟧, ⟦b:lēgī⟧, ⟦b:dīlēxī⟧, ⟦b:intellēxī⟧, ⟦b:neglēxī⟧; ⟦b:emō⟧, ⟦i:take⟧, ⟦i:buy⟧, ⟦b:ēmī⟧ (⟦b:adēmī⟧, ⟦b:exēmī⟧), ⟦b:cōmpsī⟧, ⟦b:dēmpsī⟧, ⟦b:prōmpsī⟧, ⟦b:sūmpsī⟧.

title: Variable Vowel
text:
⟦#824⟧
The final vowel of a tense stem is said to be ⟦i:variable⟧ when it is ⟦b:-o-⟧ in some of the forms, and ⟦b:-u-⟧, ⟦b:-e-⟧, or ⟦b:-i-⟧ in others.
⟦#825⟧
The sign for the variable vowel is ⟦b:-o|e-⟧: thus, ⟦b:rego|e-⟧, which may be read ‘⟦b:rego-⟧ or ⟦b:rege-⟧,’ represents ⟦b:rego-⟧ or ⟦b:regu-⟧, ⟦b:rege-⟧ or ⟦b:regi-⟧, as seen in ⟦b:rego-r⟧ or ⟦b:regu-nt⟧, ⟦b:rege-re⟧ or ⟦b:regi-t⟧.
⟦#826⟧
The variable vowel occurs in the present of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, except in the subjunctive, in the future in ⟦b:-bō⟧ or ⟦b:-bor⟧, and in the future perfect, as may be seen in the paradigms. It is usually short; but in the active, ⟦b:o⟧ is long: as, ⟦b:regō⟧, ⟦b:laudābō⟧, ⟦b:laudāverō⟧; and poets rarely lengthen ⟦b:i⟧ in the second and third person singular of the present. For the future perfect, see ⟦r882:882⟧.
⟦#827⟧
In old Latin, the stem vowel of the third person plural of the present was ⟦b:o⟧: as, COSENTIONT; ⟦b:o⟧ was long retained after ⟦b:v⟧, ⟦b:u⟧, or ⟦b:qu⟧ (107, ⟦i:c⟧): as, ⟦b:vīvont⟧, ⟦b:ruont⟧, ⟦b:sequontur⟧; or, if ⟦b:o⟧ was not retained, ⟦b:qu⟧ became ⟦b:c⟧: as, ⟦b:secuntur⟧.

title: The Present System: Root Verbs
text:
⟦#828⟧
A root without addition is used as the present stem, in the present tense or parts of the present tense, in root verbs (⟦r744:744-781⟧): as,
⟦b:es-t⟧, ⟦i:is⟧; ⟦b:da-t⟧, ⟦i:gives⟧; ⟦b:inqui-t⟧, ⟦i:quoth he⟧; ⟦b:i-t⟧, ⟦i:goes⟧; ⟦b:nequi-t⟧, ⟦i:can’t⟧; ⟦b:ēs-t⟧, ⟦i:eats⟧; ⟦b:vol-t⟧, ⟦i:will⟧; ⟦b:fer-t⟧, ⟦i:carries⟧. With reduplicated root (⟦r189:189⟧): ⟦b:bibi-t⟧, ⟦i:drinks⟧; ⟦b:seri-t⟧, ⟦i:sows⟧; ⟦b:sisti-t⟧, ⟦i:sets⟧.

title: The Present System: Verbs in -ere
text:
⟦#829⟧
(1.) The present stem of many verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ is formed by adding a variable vowel ⟦b:-o|e-⟧, which appears in the first person singular active as ⟦b:-ō⟧, to a root ending in a consonant or in two consonants: as,
⟦b:rego|e-⟧  ⟦b:regō⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:reg-⟧⟧
⟦b:verto|e-⟧  ⟦b:vertō⟧, ⟦i:turn⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:vert-⟧⟧
⟦/⟧
Present Stem. Verb. From Theme.
Other examples are: ⟦b:tegō⟧, ⟦i:cover⟧, ⟦b:petō⟧, ⟦i:make for⟧; ⟦b:mergō⟧, ⟦i:dip⟧, ⟦b:serpō⟧, ⟦i:creep⟧; ⟦b:pendō⟧, ⟦i:weigh⟧; ⟦b:dīcō⟧, ⟦i:say⟧, ⟦b:fīdō⟧, ⟦i:trust⟧, ⟦b:scrībō⟧, ⟦i:write⟧, with long ⟦b:ī⟧ for ⟦b:ei⟧ (⟦r98:98⟧); ⟦b:dūcō⟧, ⟦i:lead⟧, with long ⟦b:ū⟧ for ⟦b:eu⟧, ⟦b:ou⟧ (⟦r100:100⟧); ⟦b:lūdō⟧, ⟦i:play⟧, with long ⟦b:ū⟧ for ⟦b:oi⟧, ⟦b:oe⟧ (⟦r99:99⟧); ⟦b:laedō⟧, ⟦i:hit⟧, ⟦b:claudō⟧, ⟦i:shut⟧; ⟦b:rādō⟧, ⟦i:scrape⟧, ⟦b:cēdō⟧, ⟦i:move along⟧, ⟦b:fīgō⟧, ⟦i:fix⟧, ⟦b:rōdō⟧, ⟦i:gnaw⟧, ⟦b:glūbō⟧, ⟦i:peel⟧. ⟦b:*furō⟧, ⟦i:rave⟧; ⟦b:agō⟧, ⟦i:drive⟧, ⟦b:alō⟧, ⟦i:nurture⟧. ⟦b:gignō⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧, (⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:gn-⟧⟧), has reduplication, and ⟦b:sīdō⟧, ⟦i:settle⟧, ⟦i:light⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:sed-⟧⟧, ⟦b:⟦i:sd-⟧⟧), is also the result of an ancient reduplication (⟦r189:189⟧).
⟦#830⟧
In some present stems an original consonant has been modified: as, ⟦b:gerō⟧, ⟦i:carry⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:ges-⟧⟧), ⟦b:ūrō⟧, ⟦i:burn⟧ (⟦r154:154⟧); ⟦b:trahō⟧, ⟦i:draw⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:tra⟧⟧⟦b:gh-⟧), ⟦b:vehō⟧, ⟦i:cart⟧ (⟦r152:152⟧); or has disappeared: as, ⟦b:fluō⟧, ⟦i:flow⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:flū⟧⟧⟦b:gu-⟧).
⟦#831⟧
Some roots in a mute have a nasal before the mute in the present stem: as, ⟦b:frangō⟧, ⟦i:break⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:frag-⟧⟧). Other examples are: ⟦b:iungō⟧, ⟦i:join⟧, ⟦b:linquō⟧, ⟦i:leave⟧, ⟦b:pangō⟧, ⟦i:fix⟧, ⟦b:pingō⟧, ⟦i:paint⟧; ⟦b:findō⟧, ⟦i:cleave⟧, ⟦b:fundō⟧, ⟦i:pour⟧; ⟦b:-cumbō⟧, ⟦i:lie⟧, ⟦b:lambō⟧, ⟦i:lick⟧, ⟦b:rumpō⟧, ⟦i:break⟧ (⟦r164:164, 3⟧). The nasal sometimes runs over into the perfect or perfect participle, or both.
⟦#832⟧
(2.) The present stem of many verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ is formed by adding a suffix ending in a variable vowel ⟦b:-o|e-⟧, which appears in the first person singular active as ⟦b:-ō⟧, to a root: thus, ⟦b:-nō⟧, ⟦b:-scō⟧, ⟦b:-tō⟧, ⟦b:-iō⟧: as,
⟦b:lino|e-⟧  ⟦b:linō⟧, ⟦i:besmear⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:li-⟧⟧
⟦b:crēsco|e-⟧  ⟦b:crēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:crē-⟧⟧
⟦b:pecto|e-⟧  ⟦b:pectō⟧, ⟦i:comb⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:pec-⟧⟧
⟦b:capio|e-⟧  ⟦b:capiō⟧, ⟦i:take⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:cap-⟧⟧
⟦/⟧
Present Stem. Verb. From Theme.
⟦#833⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) ⟦b:-nō⟧ is added to roots in a vowel, or in a continuous sound, ⟦b:-m-⟧, ⟦b:-r-⟧, or ⟦b:-l-⟧.
So regularly ⟦b:linō⟧, ⟦i:besmear⟧, ⟦b:sinō⟧, ⟦i:let⟧; ⟦b:temnō⟧, ⟦i:scorn⟧, ⟦b:cernō⟧, ⟦i:sift⟧, ⟦b:spernō⟧, ⟦i:spurn⟧, only. The third persons plural ⟦b:danunt⟧ (Naev., Plaut.) for ⟦b:dant⟧, ⟦b:prōdīnunt⟧, ⟦b:redīnunt⟧ (Enn.) for ⟦b:prōdeunt⟧, ⟦b:redeunt⟧ hardly belong here; their formation is obscure. In a few verbs, ⟦b:-n⟧ is assimilated (⟦r166:166, 6⟧): as, ⟦b:tollō⟧, ⟦i:lift⟧. Sometimes the doubled ⟦b:l⟧ runs into the perfect (⟦r855:855⟧): as, ⟦b:vellī⟧, ⟦b:fefellī⟧. ⟦b:minuō⟧, ⟦i:lessen⟧, and ⟦b:sternuō⟧, ⟦i:sneeze⟧, have a longer suffix ⟦b:-nuo|e-⟧.
⟦#834⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) ⟦b:-scō⟧, usually meaning ‘⟦i:begin to⟧,’ forms presents called ⟦i:Inceptives⟧ or ⟦i:Inchoatives⟧.
⟦b:-scō⟧ is attached: first, to roots: as, ⟦b:nāscor⟧, ⟦i:am born⟧, ⟦b:nōscō⟧, ⟦i:learn⟧, ⟦b:pāscō⟧, ⟦i:feed⟧, ⟦b:scīscō⟧, ⟦i:resolve⟧; consonant roots have ⟦b:ī⟧, less commonly ⟦b:ē⟧, before the suffix: as, ⟦b:tremīscō⟧ or ⟦b:tremēscō⟧, ⟦i:fall a-trembling⟧, ⟦b:nancīscor⟧, ⟦i:get⟧ (⟦r831:831⟧); but ⟦b:discō⟧, ⟦i:learn⟧ (⟦r170:170, 1⟧), and ⟦b:poscō⟧, ⟦i:demand⟧ (⟦r170:170⟧, ⟦r10:10⟧), are shortened; see ⟦r168:168⟧. Secondly, to a form of the present stem of denominative verbs, especially of those in ⟦b:-ēre⟧: as, ⟦b:clārēscō⟧, ⟦i:brighten⟧; the stem is often assumed only, as in ⟦b:inveterāscō⟧, ⟦i:grow old⟧, ⟦b:mātūrēscō⟧, ⟦i:get ripe⟧. Many inceptives are used only in composition: as, ⟦b:extimēscō⟧, ⟦i:get scared⟧, ⟦b:obdormīscō⟧, ⟦i:drop asleep⟧.
⟦#835⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) ⟦b:-tō⟧ occurs in the following presents from guttural roots: ⟦b:flectō⟧, ⟦i:turn⟧, ⟦b:nectō⟧, ⟦i:string⟧, ⟦b:pectō⟧, ⟦i:comb⟧, ⟦b:plector⟧, ⟦i:am struck⟧, ⟦b:amplector⟧, ⟦i:hug⟧, ⟦b:complector⟧, ⟦i:clasp⟧. From a lingual root ⟦b:⟦i:vid-⟧⟧, comes ⟦b:vīsō⟧, ⟦i:go to see⟧, ⟦i:call on⟧ (⟦r153:153⟧). From vowel roots: ⟦b:bētō⟧ or ⟦b:bītō⟧, ⟦i:go⟧, and ⟦b:metō⟧, ⟦i:mow⟧.
⟦#836⟧
(⟦i:d.⟧) ⟦b:-iō⟧ is usually added to consonant roots with a short vowel; the following have presents formed by this suffix:
⟦b:capiō⟧, ⟦i:take⟧, ⟦b:cupiō⟧, ⟦i:want⟧, ⟦b:faciō⟧, ⟦i:make⟧, ⟦b:fodiō⟧, ⟦i:dig⟧, ⟦b:fugiō⟧, ⟦i:run away⟧, ⟦b:iaciō⟧, ⟦i:throw⟧, ⟦b:pariō⟧, ⟦i:bring forth⟧, ⟦b:quatiō⟧, ⟦i:shake⟧, ⟦b:rapiō⟧, ⟦i:seize⟧, ⟦b:sapiō⟧, ⟦i:have sense⟧, and their compounds; the compounds of ⟦b:*laciō⟧, ⟦i:lure⟧, and ⟦b:speciō⟧ or ⟦b:spiciō⟧, ⟦i:spy⟧, and the deponents ⟦b:gradior⟧, ⟦i:step⟧, ⟦b:morior⟧, ⟦i:die⟧, and ⟦b:patior⟧, ⟦i:suffer⟧, and their compounds. For occasional forms like those of verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧ (or ⟦b:-īrī⟧), see ⟦r791:791⟧. For ⟦b:aiō⟧, see ⟦r786:786⟧; for ⟦b:fīō⟧, ⟦r788:788⟧.
⟦#837⟧
A few present stems are formed by adding a variable vowel ⟦b:-o|e-⟧, for an older ⟦b:-io|e-⟧, to a vowel root: as,
⟦b:ruō⟧, ⟦i:tumble down⟧, ⟦b:rui-s⟧, ⟦b:rui-t⟧, ⟦b:rui-mus⟧, ⟦b:rui-tis⟧, ⟦b:ruu-nt⟧ (⟦r114:114⟧). Vowel roots in ⟦b:-ā-⟧, ⟦b:-ē-⟧, or ⟦b:-ī-⟧ have a present stem like that of denominatives: as, ⟦b:stō⟧, ⟦i:stand⟧, ⟦b:stā-s⟧, ⟦b:sta-t⟧, ⟦b:stā-mus⟧, ⟦b:stā-tis⟧, ⟦b:sta-nt⟧; ⟦b:fleō⟧, ⟦i:weep⟧, ⟦b:flē-s⟧, ⟦b:fle-t⟧, ⟦b:flē-mus⟧, ⟦b:flē-tis⟧, ⟦b:fle-nt⟧; ⟦b:neō⟧, ⟦i:spin⟧, has once ⟦b:neu-nt⟧ for ⟦b:ne-nt⟧ (Tib.); ⟦b:sciō⟧, ⟦i:know⟧, ⟦b:scī-s⟧, ⟦b:sci-t⟧, ⟦b:scī-mus⟧, ⟦b:scī-tis⟧, ⟦b:sciu-nt⟧.
⟦#838⟧
Most present stems formed by adding the suffix ⟦b:-iō⟧ to a root ending in ⟦b:-l-⟧, ⟦b:-r-⟧, or ⟦b:-n-⟧, and all formed by adding ⟦b:-iō⟧ to a long syllable, have the form of denominatives in ⟦b:-īre⟧ in the present system: as, ⟦b:saliō⟧, ⟦i:leap⟧, ⟦b:salīre⟧, ⟦b:aperiō⟧, ⟦i:open⟧, ⟦b:aperīre⟧, ⟦b:veniō⟧, ⟦i:come⟧, ⟦b:venīre⟧; ⟦b:farciō⟧, ⟦i:cram⟧, ⟦b:farcīre⟧.

title: Denominatives
text:
⟦#839⟧
The present stem of denominatives is formed by attaching a variable vowel ⟦b:-o|e-⟧, for an older ⟦b:-io|e-⟧, to a theme consisting of a noun stem: as,
⟦b:cēnao|e-⟧  ⟦b:cēnō⟧, ⟦i:dine⟧  ⟦b:cēnā-⟧
⟦b:flōreo|e-⟧  ⟦b:flōreō⟧, ⟦i:blossom⟧  ⟦b:flōre-⟧
⟦b:vestio|e-⟧  ⟦b:vestiō⟧, ⟦i:dress⟧  ⟦b:vesti-⟧
⟦b:acuo|e-⟧  ⟦b:acuō⟧, ⟦i:point⟧  ⟦b:acu-⟧
⟦/⟧
Uncontracted Present Stem. Verb. From Theme.
The noun stem ending is often slightly modified in forming the theme: thus, ⟦b:laud-⟧ becomes ⟦b:laudā-⟧ in ⟦b:laudō⟧ for ⟦b:*laudā-ō⟧, and ⟦b:flōr-⟧ becomes ⟦b:flōre-⟧ in ⟦b:flōre-ō⟧.
⟦#840⟧
In many of the forms, the final vowel of the theme is contracted with the variable vowel: as,
⟦b:plantō⟧, ⟦b:plantās⟧ (⟦r118:118⟧, ⟦r3:3⟧) for ⟦b:*plantāi̭ō⟧, ⟦b:*plantāi̭es⟧ (⟦r153:153, 2⟧); ⟦b:monēs⟧ for ⟦b:*monēi̭es⟧ (⟦r118:118, 1⟧), ⟦b:audīs⟧ for ⟦b:*audīi̭es⟧ (⟦r118:118, 3⟧). The long ⟦b:ā⟧, ⟦b:ē⟧, or ⟦b:ī⟧, is regularly shortened in some of the forms: as, ⟦b:scit⟧, ⟦b:arat⟧, ⟦b:habet⟧, for Plautine ⟦b:scīt⟧, ⟦b:arāt⟧, ⟦b:habēt⟧. In a few forms no contraction occurs: as, ⟦b:moneō⟧, ⟦b:audiō⟧, ⟦b:audiu-nt⟧, ⟦b:audie-ntis⟧, &c., ⟦b:audie-ndus⟧, &c. (⟦r114:114⟧). Denominatives from stems in ⟦b:-u-⟧, as ⟦b:acuō⟧, are not contracted, and so have the forms of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ (⟦r367:367⟧).

title: Present Subjunctive
text:
⟦#841⟧
The suffix of the present subjunctive of ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧, is ⟦b:-ī-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-i-⟧ before ⟦b:-m⟧, ⟦b:-t⟧, and ⟦b:-nt⟧: ⟦b:si-m⟧, ⟦b:sī-s⟧, ⟦b:si-t⟧, ⟦b:sī-mus⟧, ⟦b:sī-tis⟧, ⟦b:si-nt⟧ (35, 2, 3). So also in the singular and in the third person plural, ⟦b:dui-m⟧, &c. (⟦r756:756⟧), and ⟦b:edi-m⟧, &c. (⟦r769:769⟧), and in all the persons, ⟦b:veli-m⟧, &c. (⟦b:nōli-m⟧, &c., ⟦b:māli-m⟧, &c.). An old suffix is ⟦b:-iē-⟧ (⟦b:-ie-⟧), in ⟦b:sie-m⟧, ⟦b:siē-s⟧, ⟦b:sie-t⟧, and ⟦b:sie-nt⟧.
⟦#842⟧
(1.) The present subjunctive stem of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, and ⟦b:-īre⟧, ends in ⟦b:-ā-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-a-⟧ in some of the persons; this suffix replaces the variable vowel of the indicative: as,
⟦b:rega-m⟧, ⟦b:regā-s⟧, ⟦b:rega-t⟧, ⟦b:regā-mus⟧, ⟦b:regā-tis⟧, ⟦b:rega-nt⟧; ⟦b:capia-m⟧, ⟦b:capiā-s⟧, &c.; ⟦b:monea-m⟧, ⟦b:moneā-s⟧, &c.; ⟦b:audia-m⟧, ⟦b:audiā-s⟧, &c. ⟦b:ea-m⟧, ⟦b:quea-m⟧, ⟦b:fera-m⟧, and the old ⟦b:fua-m⟧ (⟦r750:750⟧), also have the formative subjunctive vowel.
⟦#843⟧
(2.) The present subjunctive stem of verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ ends in ⟦b:-ē-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-e-⟧ in some of the persons: as,
⟦b:laude-m⟧, ⟦b:laudē-s⟧, ⟦b:laude-t⟧, ⟦b:laudē-mus⟧, ⟦b:laudē-tis⟧, ⟦b:laude-nt⟧. ⟦b:dō⟧, ⟦i:give⟧, also has ⟦b:de-m⟧, ⟦b:dē-s⟧, &c.

title: Imperative
text:
⟦#844⟧
Root verbs have a root as imperative stem (⟦r745:745-780⟧): as, ⟦b:es⟧, &c., ⟦b:fer⟧, &c. But the imperative of ⟦b:nōlō⟧ has a stem in ⟦b:-ī-⟧, like verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧: thus, ⟦b:nōlī⟧, ⟦b:nōlī-tō⟧, ⟦b:nōlī-te⟧, ⟦b:nōlī-tōte⟧.
⟦#845⟧
The imperative stem of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, and of verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, and ⟦b:-īre⟧, is the same as that of the indicative: as,
⟦b:rege⟧, ⟦b:regi-tō⟧, ⟦b:regu-ntō⟧, ⟦b:rege-re⟧; ⟦b:cape⟧, ⟦b:capi-tō⟧, ⟦b:capiu-ntō⟧; ⟦b:fī⟧; ⟦b:laudā⟧, &c.; ⟦b:monē⟧, &c.; ⟦b:audī⟧, &c.
⟦#846⟧
The second person singular imperative active of ⟦b:dīcō⟧, ⟦b:dūcō⟧, and ⟦b:faciō⟧, is usually ⟦b:dīc⟧, ⟦b:dūc⟧, and ⟦b:fac⟧, respectively, though the full forms, ⟦b:dīce⟧, &c., are also used, and are commoner in old Latin. Compounds of ⟦b:dūcō⟧ may have the short form: as, ⟦b:ēdūc⟧. ⟦b:ingerō⟧ has once ⟦b:inger⟧ (Catull.). ⟦b:sciō⟧ has regularly the singular ⟦b:scī-tō⟧, plural ⟦b:scī-tōte⟧, rarely ⟦b:scī-te⟧.

title: Imperfect Indicative
text:
⟦#847⟧
The imperfect indicative stem ends in ⟦b:-bā-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-ba-⟧ in some of the persons: as,
⟦b:daba-m⟧, ⟦b:dabā-s⟧, ⟦b:daba-t⟧, ⟦b:dabā-mus⟧, ⟦b:dabā-tis⟧, ⟦b:daba-nt⟧; ⟦b:ība-m⟧; ⟦b:quība-m⟧. In verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ and ⟦b:-ēre⟧, the suffix is preceded by a form ending in ⟦b:-ē-⟧: as, ⟦b:regēba-m⟧; ⟦b:monēba-m⟧; so also ⟦b:volēba-m⟧ (⟦b:nōlēba-m⟧, ⟦b:mālēba-m⟧), and ⟦b:ferēba-m⟧; in verbs in ⟦b:-iō⟧, ⟦b:-ere⟧, and in ⟦b:-iō⟧, ⟦b:-īre⟧, by a form ending in ⟦b:-iē-⟧: as, ⟦b:capiēba-m⟧; ⟦b:audiēba-m⟧; in verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧, by one ending in ⟦b:-ā-⟧: as, ⟦b:laudāba-m⟧. In verse, verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧ sometimes have ⟦b:-ī-⟧ before the suffix (Plaut., Ter., Catull., Lucr., Verg., &c.): as, ⟦b:audība-t⟧. ⟦b:āiō⟧, ⟦i:say⟧, has sometimes ⟦b:a͡iba-m⟧, &c. (⟦r787:787⟧).
⟦#848⟧
The suffix of the imperfect indicative of ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧, is ⟦b:-ā-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-a-⟧ before ⟦b:-m⟧, ⟦b:-t⟧, and ⟦b:-nt⟧ (35, 2, 3)the ⟦b:s⟧ becomes ⟦b:r⟧ between the vowels (⟦r154:154⟧): ⟦b:era-m⟧, ⟦b:erā-s⟧, ⟦b:era-t⟧, ⟦b:erā-mus⟧, ⟦b:erā-tis⟧, ⟦b:era-nt⟧.

title: Imperfect Subjunctive
text:
⟦#849⟧
The imperfect subjunctive stem ends in ⟦b:-rē-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-re-⟧ in some of the persons: as,
⟦b:dare-m⟧, ⟦b:darē-s⟧, ⟦b:dare-t⟧, ⟦b:darē-mus⟧, ⟦b:darē-tis⟧, ⟦b:dare-nt⟧; ⟦b:īre-m⟧, ⟦b:fore-m⟧, ⟦b:ferre-m⟧. In verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, the ⟦b:-rē-⟧ is preceded by a form ending in ⟦b:-e-⟧: as, ⟦b:regere-m⟧, ⟦b:capere-m⟧; in verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, and ⟦b:-īre⟧, by one ending in ⟦b:-ā-⟧, ⟦b:-ē-⟧, or ⟦b:-ī-⟧, respectively: as, ⟦b:laudāre-m⟧, ⟦b:monēre-m⟧, ⟦b:audīre-m⟧.
⟦#850⟧
The suffix of the imperfect subjunctive of ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧, is ⟦b:-sē-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-se-⟧ in some of the persons; ⟦b:esse-m⟧, ⟦b:essē-s⟧, ⟦b:esse-t⟧, ⟦b:essē-mus⟧, ⟦b:essē-tis⟧, ⟦b:esse-nt⟧; so also ⟦b:ēssē-s⟧, &c. (⟦r769:769⟧). ⟦b:volō⟧, ⟦i:wish⟧, ⟦b:nōlō⟧, ⟦i:won’t⟧, and ⟦b:mālō⟧, ⟦i:prefer⟧, have ⟦b:velle-m⟧, ⟦b:nōlle-m⟧, and ⟦b:mālle-m⟧ respectively (166, 8).

title: Future
text:
⟦#851⟧
The future stem of ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧, is ⟦b:ero|e-⟧: ⟦b:erō⟧, ⟦b:eri-s⟧, ⟦b:eri-t⟧, ⟦b:eri-mus⟧, ⟦b:eri-tis⟧, ⟦b:eru-nt⟧. ⟦b:dō⟧ has ⟦b:dabō⟧, ⟦b:eō⟧ has ⟦b:ībō⟧, and ⟦b:queō⟧ has ⟦b:quībō⟧.
⟦#852⟧
(1.) The future stem of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ and ⟦b:-īre⟧ ends in ⟦b:-a-⟧ in the first person singular, otherwise in ⟦b:-ē-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-e-⟧ in some of the persons: as,
⟦b:rega-m⟧, ⟦b:regē-s⟧, ⟦b:rege-t⟧, ⟦b:regē-mus⟧, ⟦b:regē-tis⟧, ⟦b:rege-nt⟧; ⟦b:capia-m⟧, ⟦b:capiē-s⟧, &c.; ⟦b:audia-m⟧, ⟦b:audiē-s⟧, &c. The first person singular is not a future form, but the subjunctive present, used with a future meaning (⟦r842:842⟧); forms in ⟦b:-em⟧ occur in manuscripts of Plautus: as, ⟦b:faciem⟧, ⟦b:sinem⟧. Verbs in ⟦b:-īre⟧ sometimes have ⟦b:-bo|e-⟧, chiefly in the dramatists: as, ⟦b:scībō⟧, ⟦b:opperībo-r⟧ (Plaut., Ter.), ⟦b:lēnību-nt⟧ (Prop.); rarely verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ (⟦r819:819⟧): as, ⟦b:exsūgēbō⟧ (Plaut.). For ⟦b:reddibō⟧, instead of the usual ⟦b:reddam⟧, see ⟦r757:757⟧.
⟦#853⟧
(2.) The future stem of verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ and ⟦b:-ēre⟧ ends in ⟦i:-bo|e-⟧, which is preceded by a form ending in long ⟦b:-ā-⟧ or ⟦b:-ē-⟧ respectively: as,
⟦b:laudābō⟧, ⟦b:laudābi-s⟧, ⟦b:laudābi-t⟧, ⟦b:laudābi-mus⟧, ⟦b:laudābi-tis⟧, ⟦b:laudābu-nt⟧. ⟦b:monēbō⟧, ⟦b:monēbi-s⟧, &c.

title: Perfect Indicative Stem
text:
⟦#854⟧
There are two kinds of perfect stems: (A.) Some verbs have as perfect stem a root, generally with some modification, but without a suffix (⟦r858:858-866⟧). (B.) Some perfects are formed with a suffix, ⟦b:-s-⟧, or ⟦b:-v-⟧ or ⟦b:-u-⟧ (⟦r867:867-875⟧).
⟦#855⟧
Some perfects of primitives are formed not from a root, but from the present stem without the formative vowel, treated as a root: as, ⟦b:prehendī⟧, ⟦i:seized⟧, from ⟦b:prehend-⟧ (⟦r866:866⟧); ⟦b:poposcī⟧, ⟦i:asked⟧, ⟦b:fefellī⟧, ⟦i:deceived⟧ (⟦r858:858⟧); ⟦b:iūnxī⟧, ⟦i:joined⟧ (⟦r867:867⟧).
⟦#856⟧
The first person of the perfect ends in ⟦b:-ī⟧, sometimes written ⟦b:ei⟧ (⟦r29:29, 2⟧). ⟦b:-t⟧, ⟦b:-stī⟧, sometimes written ⟦b:-stei⟧ (⟦r29:29, 2⟧), ⟦b:-stis⟧, and ⟦b:-mus⟧ are preceded by short ⟦b:i⟧; ⟦b:-re⟧ is always, and ⟦b:-runt⟧ is usually, preceded by long ⟦b:ē⟧: as,
⟦b:rēxī⟧, ⟦b:rēxi-stī⟧, ⟦b:rēxi-t⟧, ⟦b:rēxi-mus⟧, ⟦b:rēxi-stis⟧, ⟦b:rēxē-runt⟧ (⟦b:rēxe-runt⟧), or ⟦b:rēxē-re⟧.
⟦#857⟧
Sometimes ⟦b:-t⟧ is preceded by long ⟦b:ī⟧: as, ⟦b:iīt⟧, ⟦b:petiīt⟧, REDIEIT (⟦r29:29, 2⟧). ⟦b:-runt⟧ is sometimes preceded by short ⟦b:e⟧ (Plaut., Ter., Lucr., Hor., Ov., Verg., Phaedr.). This is the original form; ⟦b:-ē-⟧ is by analogy to ⟦b:-ēre⟧.

title: The Perfect System: Perfect Stem Without a Suffix
text:
⟦#858⟧
(1.) Some verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ form their perfect stem by prefixing to the root its initial consonant with the following vowel, which, if ⟦b:a⟧, is usually represented by ⟦b:e⟧; this is called the ⟦i:Reduplicated Perfect⟧, and the first syllable is called the ⟦i:Reduplication⟧: as,
⟦b:pu-pug-⟧  ⟦b:pungō⟧, ⟦i:punch⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:pug-⟧⟧
⟦b:pe-pig-⟧  ⟦b:pangō⟧, ⟦i:fix⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:pag-⟧⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect Stem. Verb. From Theme.
Other examples are: ⟦b:cadō⟧, ⟦i:fall⟧, ⟦b:cecidī⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:cad-⟧⟧, 104, ⟦i:c⟧); ⟦b:pariō⟧, ⟦i:bring forth⟧, ⟦b:peperī⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:par-⟧⟧, 104, ⟦i:c⟧); ⟦b:pellō⟧, ⟦i:push⟧, ⟦b:pepulī⟧ (⟦b:⟦i:pol-⟧⟧, 105, ⟦i:h⟧); ⟦b:poscō⟧, ⟦i:demand⟧, ⟦b:poposcī⟧ (⟦r855:855⟧); ⟦b:fallō⟧, ⟦i:deceive⟧, ⟦b:fefellī⟧ (⟦r855:855⟧, 104, ⟦i:c⟧); see also ⟦r923:923-932⟧. ⟦b:caedō⟧, ⟦i:cut⟧, has ⟦b:cecīdī⟧ (108, ⟦i:a⟧); and a few old forms are quoted from verbs having an ⟦b:o⟧ or an ⟦b:u⟧ in the root with ⟦b:e⟧ in the reduplication: as, ⟦b:memordī⟧, ⟦b:pepugī⟧.
⟦#859⟧
Four verbs with vowel roots also have a reduplicated perfect stem: ⟦b:dō⟧, ⟦i:give⟧, ⟦i:put⟧, ⟦b:dare⟧, ⟦b:dedī⟧; ⟦b:bibō⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧, ⟦b:bibere⟧, ⟦b:bibī⟧; ⟦b:stō⟧, ⟦i:stand⟧, ⟦b:stāre⟧, ⟦b:stetī⟧, and ⟦b:sistō⟧, ⟦i:set⟧, ⟦b:sistere⟧, ⟦b:-stitī⟧, rarely ⟦b:stitī⟧. Also four verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧: ⟦b:mordeō⟧, ⟦i:bite⟧, ⟦b:momordī⟧, ⟦b:pendeō⟧, ⟦i:hang⟧, ⟦b:pependī⟧, ⟦b:spondeō⟧, ⟦i:promise⟧, ⟦b:spopondī⟧, ⟦b:tondeō⟧, ⟦i:clip⟧, ⟦b:-totondī⟧. In the root syllable of ⟦b:spopondī⟧, ⟦i:promised⟧, ⟦b:stetī⟧, ⟦i:stood⟧, ⟦b:stitī⟧, ⟦i:set⟧, and the old ⟦b:scicidī⟧, ⟦i:clove⟧, an ⟦b:s⟧ is dropped (⟦r173:173, 2⟧).
⟦#860⟧
In compounds the reduplication is commonly dropped: as,
⟦b:cecidī⟧, ⟦i:fell⟧, compound ⟦b:concidī⟧, ⟦i:tumbled down⟧. Compounds of ⟦b:cucurrī⟧, ⟦i:ran⟧, sometimes retain the reduplication: as, ⟦b:prōcucurrī⟧. Compounds of ⟦b:bibī⟧, ⟦i:drank⟧, ⟦b:didicī⟧, ⟦i:learned⟧, ⟦b:poposcī⟧, ⟦i:asked⟧, ⟦b:stitī⟧, ⟦i:set⟧, ⟦b:stetī⟧, ⟦i:stood⟧, and ⟦b:dedī⟧, ⟦i:gave⟧, ⟦i:put⟧, retain it, the last two weakening ⟦b:e⟧ to ⟦b:i⟧: as, ⟦b:restitī⟧, ⟦i:staid back⟧. ⟦b:abscondidī⟧, ⟦i:hid away⟧, usually becomes ⟦b:abscondī⟧; in apparent compounds, ⟦b:e⟧ is usually retained: as, ⟦b:circum stetī⟧, ⟦i:stood round⟧, ⟦b:vēnum dedī⟧, ⟦i:put for sale⟧. The reduplication is also lost in the simple verbs ⟦b:tulī⟧, ⟦i:carried⟧, old ⟦b:tetulī⟧, and in ⟦b:scindō⟧, ⟦i:split⟧, ⟦b:scidī⟧, which last is rare as a simple verb.
⟦#861⟧
Some compounds with ⟦b:re-⟧ drop only the vowel of the reduplication (111, ⟦i:a⟧): as, ⟦b:reccidī⟧, ⟦i:fell back⟧; ⟦b:rettulī⟧, ⟦i:brought back⟧ (see also ⟦r781:781⟧); ⟦b:repperī⟧, ⟦i:found⟧; ⟦b:rettudī⟧, ⟦i:beat back⟧. Some perfects occur only in composition: as, percellō, ⟦i:knock down⟧, ⟦b:perculī⟧; ⟦b:cōntundō⟧, ⟦i:smash to pieces⟧, ⟦b:contudī⟧; ⟦b:diffindō⟧, ⟦i:split apart⟧, ⟦b:diffidī⟧; but ⟦b:fidī⟧ also occurs a couple of times as a simple verb.
⟦#862⟧
(2.) Some verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have a perfect stem consisting of a consonant root with a long vowel (⟦r135:135, 1⟧): as,
⟦b:ēd-⟧  ⟦b:edō⟧, ⟦i:eat⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:ed-⟧⟧
⟦b:lēg-⟧  ⟦b:legō⟧, ⟦i:pick up⟧, ⟦i:read⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:leg-⟧⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect Stem. Verb. From Theme.
Other examples are: ⟦b:fodiō⟧, ⟦i:dig⟧, ⟦b:fōdī⟧; ⟦b:fundō⟧, ⟦i:pour⟧, ⟦b:fūdī⟧; ⟦b:linquō⟧, ⟦i:leave⟧, ⟦b:līquī⟧; see ⟦r936:936-946⟧. Three verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ also have this form, ⟦b:sedeō⟧, ⟦i:sit⟧, ⟦b:sēdī⟧, ⟦b:strīdeō⟧, ⟦i:grate⟧, ⟦b:strīdī⟧, ⟦b:videō⟧, ⟦i:see⟧, ⟦b:vīdī⟧; and one in ⟦b:-īre⟧, ⟦b:veniō⟧, ⟦i:come⟧, ⟦b:vēnī⟧.
⟦#863⟧
The following verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ with ⟦b:a⟧ in the present stem, have long ⟦b:ē⟧ in the perfect stem (⟦r145:145⟧):
⟦b:agō⟧, ⟦i:do⟧, ⟦b:ēgī⟧, ⟦b:frangō⟧, ⟦i:break⟧, ⟦b:frēgī⟧, ⟦b:pangō⟧, ⟦i:fix⟧, rarely ⟦b:pēgī⟧, but always ⟦b:compēgī⟧, ⟦b:impēgī⟧, ⟦b:oppēgī⟧; ⟦b:capiō⟧, ⟦i:take⟧, ⟦b:cēpī⟧, ⟦b:faciō⟧, ⟦i:make⟧, ⟦b:fēcī⟧, ⟦b:iaciō⟧, ⟦i:throw⟧, ⟦b:iēcī⟧. So also the old ⟦b:co-ēpī⟧, ⟦i:began⟧, common ⟦b:coepī⟧.
⟦#864⟧
Two verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ and some in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ have a perfect stem consisting of a root which ends in ⟦b:-v-⟧ and has a long vowel: ⟦b:iuvō⟧, ⟦i:help⟧, ⟦b:iuvāre⟧, ⟦b:iūvī⟧, ⟦b:lavō⟧, ⟦i:wash⟧, ⟦b:lavāre⟧ or ⟦b:lavere⟧, ⟦b:lāvī⟧; ⟦b:caveō⟧, ⟦i:look out⟧, ⟦b:cavēre⟧, ⟦b:cāvī⟧; see ⟦r996:996⟧.
⟦#865⟧
Verbs in ⟦b:-uō⟧, ⟦b:-uere⟧, both primitives and denominatives, have usually a perfect stem in short ⟦b:u⟧ of the theme (⟦r124:124⟧): as, ⟦b:luō⟧, ⟦i:pay⟧, ⟦b:luī⟧; ⟦b:acuō⟧, ⟦i:sharpen⟧, ⟦b:acuī⟧: see ⟦r947:947⟧, ⟦r948:948⟧. Forms with long ⟦b:ū⟧ are old and rare (⟦r126:126⟧): as, ⟦b:fūī⟧, ⟦b:adnūī⟧, ⟦b:cōnstitūī⟧, ⟦b:īnstitūī⟧. ⟦b:fluō⟧, ⟦i:flow⟧, and ⟦b:struō⟧, ⟦i:pile⟧, have ⟦b:flūxī⟧ and ⟦b:strūxi⟧ (⟦r830:830⟧).
⟦#866⟧
(3.) Some verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ from roots ending in two consonants have a perfect stem consisting of the root: as,
⟦b:mand-⟧  ⟦b:mandō⟧, ⟦i:chew⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:mand-⟧⟧
⟦b:pand-⟧  ⟦b:pandō⟧, ⟦i:open⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:pand-⟧⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect Stem. Verb. From Theme.
Other examples are: ⟦b:vortō⟧ or ⟦b:vertō⟧, ⟦i:turn⟧, ⟦b:vortī⟧ or ⟦b:vertī⟧; ⟦b:scandō⟧, ⟦i:climb⟧, ⟦b:-scendī⟧; ⟦b:prehendō⟧, ⟦i:seize⟧, ⟦b:prehendī⟧ (⟦r855:855⟧); ⟦b:vollō⟧ or ⟦b:vellō⟧, ⟦i:pluck⟧, ⟦b:vollī⟧ or ⟦b:vellī⟧; see ⟦r949:949-951⟧. Similarly ⟦b:ferveō⟧, ⟦i:boil⟧, ⟦b:fervere⟧ or ⟦b:fervēre⟧, has ⟦b:fervī⟧ or ⟦b:ferbuī⟧ (⟦r823:823⟧), and ⟦b:prandeō⟧, ⟦i:lunch⟧, ⟦b:prandēre⟧, has ⟦b:prandī⟧.

title: The Perfect System: Perfect Stem in -s-
text:
⟦#867⟧
Many verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ form their perfect stem by adding the suffix ⟦b:-s-⟧ to a root, which generally ends in a mute: as,
⟦b:carp-s-⟧  ⟦b:carpō⟧, ⟦i:pluck⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:carp-⟧⟧
⟦b:scalp-s-⟧  ⟦b:scalpō⟧, ⟦i:dig⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:scalp-⟧⟧
⟦b:ges-s-⟧  ⟦b:gerō⟧, ⟦i:bear⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:ges-⟧⟧
⟦b:dīx-⟧  ⟦b:dīcō⟧, ⟦i:say⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:dīc-⟧⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect Stem. Verb. From Theme.
Other examples are: ⟦b:dūcō⟧, ⟦i:lead⟧, ⟦b:dūxī⟧ (⟦r100:100⟧); ⟦b:fingō⟧, ⟦i:mould⟧, ⟦b:fīnxī⟧ (⟦r855:855⟧); ⟦b:lūdō⟧, ⟦i:play⟧, ⟦b:lūsī⟧ (⟦r166:166, 2⟧); ⟦b:scrībō⟧, ⟦i:write⟧, ⟦b:scrīpsī⟧ (⟦r164:164, 1⟧); ⟦b:struō⟧, ⟦i:pile⟧, ⟦b:strūxī⟧ (⟦r164:164, 1⟧); ⟦b:vīvō⟧, ⟦i:live⟧, ⟦b:vīxī⟧ (⟦r98:98⟧). Some verbs with a short vowel in the present, have a long vowel in the perfect: as, ⟦b:regō⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧, ⟦b:rēxī⟧ (⟦r135:135⟧); ⟦b:intellegō⟧, ⟦i:understand⟧, ⟦b:intellēxī⟧ (⟦r823:823⟧); ⟦b:tegō⟧, ⟦i:cover⟧, ⟦b:tēxī⟧; ⟦b:iungō⟧, ⟦i:join⟧, ⟦b:iūnxī⟧ (⟦r855:855⟧). And some verbs with a long vowel in the present, have a short vowel in the perfect: as, ⟦b:ūrō⟧, ⟦i:burn⟧, ⟦b:ussī⟧ (⟦r830:830⟧). See ⟦r952:952⟧-961.
⟦#868⟧
Some verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ also have a perfect in ⟦b:-s-⟧: as ⟦b:algeō⟧, ⟦i:am cold⟧, ⟦b:alsī⟧ (⟦r170:170, 3⟧); ⟦b:haereō⟧, ⟦i:stick⟧, ⟦b:haesī⟧ (⟦r166:166, 2⟧): see ⟦r999:999⟧, ⟦r1000:1000⟧. Also some in ⟦b:-īre⟧: as, ⟦b:sarciō⟧, ⟦i:patch⟧, ⟦b:sarsī⟧ (⟦r170:170, 3⟧): see ⟦r1014:1014⟧, ⟦r1015:1015⟧.

title: Perfect Stem in -v- or -u-
text:
⟦#869⟧
(1.) Some verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, with vowel roots, and almost all verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ or ⟦b:-īre⟧, form their perfect stem by adding the suffix ⟦b:-v-⟧ to a theme ending in a long vowel: as,
⟦b:crē-v-⟧  ⟦b:crēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:crē-⟧⟧
⟦b:laudā-v-⟧  ⟦b:laudō⟧, ⟦i:praise⟧  ⟦b:laudā-⟧
⟦b:audī-v-⟧  ⟦b:audiō⟧, ⟦i:hear⟧  ⟦b:audī-⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect Stem. Verb. From Theme.
For other verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ with a perfect stem in ⟦b:-v-⟧, and particularly ⟦b:terō⟧, ⟦b:cernō⟧, ⟦b:spernō⟧, and ⟦b:sternō⟧, see ⟦r962:962-970⟧.
⟦#870⟧
A few verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have a perfect stem in ⟦b:-v-⟧ attached to a presumed theme in long ⟦b:ī⟧: as, ⟦b:cupiō⟧, ⟦i:want⟧, ⟦b:cupīvī⟧; ⟦b:petō⟧, ⟦i:aim at⟧, ⟦b:petīvī⟧; ⟦b:quaerō⟧, ⟦i:inquire⟧, ⟦b:quaesīvī⟧; ⟦b:arcēssō⟧, ⟦i:fetch⟧, ⟦b:arcēssīvī⟧; see ⟦r966:966-970⟧.
⟦#871⟧
A few verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧ also have a perfect stem in ⟦b:-v-⟧: as, ⟦b:fleō⟧, ⟦i:weep⟧, ⟦b:flēre⟧, ⟦b:flēvī⟧; see ⟦r1001:1001-1003⟧. And three verbs in ⟦b:-ēscere⟧ have a perfect stem in ⟦b:-v-⟧ attached to a presumed theme in long ⟦b:ē⟧: ⟦b:-olēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow⟧, ⟦b:-olēvī⟧; ⟦b:quiēscō⟧, ⟦i:get quiet⟧, ⟦b:quiēvī⟧; ⟦b:suēscō⟧, ⟦i:get used⟧, ⟦b:suēvī⟧.
⟦#872⟧
One verb in ⟦b:-āscere⟧ has a perfect stem in ⟦b:-v-⟧ attached to a presumed theme in long ⟦b:ā⟧: ⟦b:advesperāscit⟧, ⟦i:it gets dusk⟧, ⟦b:advesperāvit⟧.
⟦#873⟧
(2.) Many verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ form their perfect stem by adding the suffix ⟦b:-u-⟧ to a consonant root: as,
⟦b:al-u-⟧  ⟦b:alō⟧, ⟦i:nurture⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:al-⟧⟧
⟦b:gen-u-⟧  ⟦b:gignō⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧  ⟦b:⟦i:gen-⟧⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect Stem. Verb. From Theme.
Other examples are: ⟦b:colō⟧, ⟦i:cultivate⟧, ⟦b:coluī⟧; ⟦b:cōnsulō⟧, ⟦i:consult⟧, ⟦b:cōnsuluī⟧; ⟦b:-cumbō⟧, ⟦i:lie⟧, ⟦b:-cubuī⟧; ⟦b:fremō⟧, ⟦i:roar⟧, ⟦b:fremuī⟧; ⟦b:ēliciō⟧, ⟦i:draw out⟧, ⟦b:ēlicuī⟧; ⟦b:molō⟧, ⟦i:grind⟧, ⟦b:moluī⟧; ⟦b:rapiō⟧, ⟦i:snatch⟧, ⟦b:rapuī⟧; ⟦b:serō⟧, ⟦i:string⟧, ⟦b:-seruī⟧; ⟦b:stertō⟧, ⟦i:snore⟧, ⟦b:-stertuī⟧; ⟦b:strepō⟧, ⟦i:make a racket⟧, ⟦b:strepuī⟧; ⟦b:texō⟧, ⟦i:weave⟧, ⟦b:texuī⟧; ⟦b:volō⟧, ⟦i:will⟧, ⟦b:voluī⟧; ⟦b:compescō⟧, ⟦i:check⟧, ⟦b:compescuī⟧ (⟦r855:855⟧); see ⟦r971:971-976⟧.
⟦#874⟧
Some verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ also have a perfect stem in ⟦b:-u-⟧: as, ⟦b:crepō⟧, ⟦i:rattle⟧, ⟦b:crepāre⟧, ⟦b:crepuī⟧ (⟦r993:993⟧); and many in ⟦b:-ēre⟧: as, ⟦b:moneō⟧, ⟦i:warn⟧, ⟦b:monēre⟧, ⟦b:monuī⟧: see ⟦r1004:1004-1006⟧; also four in ⟦b:-īre⟧: as, ⟦b:saliō⟧, ⟦i:leap⟧, ⟦b:salīre⟧, ⟦b:saluī⟧ (⟦r1019:1019⟧).
⟦#875⟧
The perfect ⟦b:potuī⟧ to the present ⟦b:possum⟧ (⟦r751:751⟧) is from a lost present ⟦b:*poteō⟧, ⟦b:*potēre⟧ (⟦r922:922⟧). ⟦b:pōnere⟧ (for ⟦b:*po-sinere⟧, ⟦r112:112⟧; 170, 2) forms an old perfect ⟦b:posīvī⟧ (⟦r964:964⟧), later ⟦b:posuī⟧, as if ⟦b:pos-⟧ were the stem.

title: Perfect Subjunctive
text:
⟦#876⟧
The perfect subjunctive stem ends in ⟦b:-erī-⟧, for which ⟦b:-eri-⟧ is sometimes used (35, 2, 3): as,
⟦b:rēxeri-m⟧, ⟦b:rēxerī-s⟧, ⟦b:rēxeri-t⟧, ⟦b:rēxerī-mus⟧, ⟦b:rēxerī-tis⟧, ⟦b:rēxeri-nt⟧.
⟦#877⟧
In the perfect subjunctive, long ⟦b:ī⟧ is found before the person endings ⟦b:-s⟧, ⟦b:-mus⟧, and ⟦b:-tis⟧, some 25 times, as follows: ⟦b:-īs⟧, 18 times (Plaut. 3, Pac., Enn., Ter., Hor., Tib., Sen., inscr., once each, Ov. 8), ⟦b:-īmus⟧, 4 times (Plaut. 3, Ter. 1), ⟦b:-ītis⟧, 3 times (Plaut. 2, Enn. 1).
⟦#878⟧
In the perfect subjunctive, short ⟦b:i⟧ is found, as in the future perfect, some 9 times, thus: ⟦b:-is⟧, 8 times (Plaut. in anapests 3, Verg. 2, Hor. 3), ⟦b:-imus⟧ once (Verg.). But before ⟦b:-tis⟧, short ⟦b:i⟧ is not found.

title: Perfect Imperative
text:
⟦#879⟧
One verb only, ⟦b:meminī⟧, ⟦i:remember⟧, has a perfect imperative; in this imperative, the person endings are not preceded by a vowel, thus: ⟦b:memen-tō⟧, ⟦b:memen-tōte⟧.

title: Pluperfect Indicative
text:
⟦#880⟧
The pluperfect indicative stem ends in ⟦b:-erā-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-era-⟧ in some of the persons: as,
⟦b:rēxera-m⟧, ⟦b:rēxerā-s⟧, ⟦b:rēxera-t⟧, ⟦b:rēxerā-mus⟧, ⟦b:rēxerā-tis⟧, ⟦b:rēxera-nt⟧.

title: Pluperfect Subjunctive
text:
⟦#881⟧
The pluperfect subjunctive stem ends in ⟦b:-issē-⟧, which becomes ⟦b:-isse-⟧ in some of the persons: as,
⟦b:rēxisse-m⟧, ⟦b:rēxissē-s⟧, ⟦b:rēxisse-t⟧, ⟦b:rēxissē-mus⟧, ⟦b:rēxissē-tis⟧, ⟦b:rēxisse-nt⟧.

title: Future Perfect
text:
⟦#882⟧
The future perfect stem ends in ⟦b:-erō-⟧ and ⟦b:-eri-⟧: as,
⟦b:rēxerō⟧, ⟦b:rēxeri-s⟧, ⟦b:rēxeri-t⟧, ⟦b:rēxeri-mus⟧, ⟦b:rēxeri-tis⟧, ⟦b:rēxeri-nt⟧.
⟦#883⟧
In the future perfect, short ⟦b:i⟧ is found before the person endings ⟦b:-s⟧, ⟦b:-mus⟧, and ⟦b:-tis⟧, some 40 times, as follows: ⟦b:-is⟧, 29 times (Plaut. 2, Cic. 1, Catull. 1, Verg. 7, Hor. 12, Ov. 4, Germ. 1, Juv. 1); ⟦b:-imus⟧, 3 times (Plaut., Ter., Lucr.); ⟦b:-itis⟧, 8 times (Enn. 1, Plaut. 5, Ov. 2).
⟦#884⟧
In the future perfect, long ⟦b:ī⟧ is found, as in the perfect subjunctive, some 33 times, thus: ⟦b:-īs⟧, 28 times (Plaut. 3, Hor. 5, Ov. 15, Prop., Stat., Mart., Priap., inscr., once each), ⟦b:-īmus⟧, once (Catull.), ⟦b:-ītis⟧, 4 times (Ov. 3, Priap. 1).

title: Short or Old Forms
text:
⟦#885⟧
(1.) Some shorter forms in the perfect system are principally found in old Latin.
⟦#886⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) Shorter forms in the perfect indicative, the pluperfect subjunctive, and the infinitive, most of them from perfects in ⟦b:-s-⟧ (⟦r867:867⟧), occur chiefly in verse: thus,
Perfect indicative, second person singular, common: as, ⟦b:dīxtī⟧ (Plaut., Ter., Cic.); plural, rare: as, ⟦b:accestis⟧ (Verg.). Pluperfect subjunctive singular, not very common: as, ⟦b:exstīnxem⟧ (Verg.), ⟦b:intellēxēs⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:vīxet⟧ (Verg.); plural, once only, ⟦b:ērēpsēmus⟧ (Hor.). Infinitive, ⟦b:dīxe⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:cōnsūmpse⟧ (Lucr.).
⟦#887⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) A perfect subjunctive stem in ⟦b:-sī-⟧ or in ⟦b:-ssī-⟧, and a future perfect indicative stem in ⟦b:-so|e-⟧ or in ⟦b:-sso|e-⟧, occur chiefly in old laws and prayers, and in dramatic verse: as,
Perfect subjunctive: ⟦b:faxim⟧, ⟦b:faxīs⟧, FAXSEIS (inscr. 145 B.C.), ⟦b:faxit⟧, ⟦b:faxīmus⟧, ⟦b:faxītis⟧, ⟦b:faxint⟧; ⟦b:ausim⟧, ⟦b:ausīs⟧, ⟦b:ausit⟧; ⟦b:locāssim⟧, ⟦b:amāssīs⟧, ⟦b:servāssit⟧, ⟦b:amāssint⟧, ⟦b:prohibēssīs⟧, ⟦b:prohibēssit⟧, ⟦b:cohibēssit⟧, ⟦b:licēssit⟧.
Future perfect indicative: ⟦b:faxō⟧, ⟦b:faxis⟧, ⟦b:faxit⟧, ⟦b:faxitis⟧, ⟦b:capsō⟧, ⟦b:recepsō⟧, ⟦b:iussō⟧, ⟦b:occīsit⟧, ⟦b:capsimus⟧; ⟦b:levāssō⟧, ⟦b:invītāssitis⟧, ⟦b:mulcāssitis⟧, ⟦b:exoculāssitis⟧, ⟦b:prohibēssis⟧, ⟦b:prohibēssint⟧. Denominatives in ⟦b:-āre⟧ have also, in old Latin, a future perfect infinitive: as, ⟦b:impetrāssere⟧.
⟦#888⟧
Passive inflections, as future perfect ⟦b:faxitur⟧, ⟦b:turbāssitur⟧, deponent MERCASSITVR (inscr. 111 B.C.), are very rare; and, indeed, with the exception of ⟦b:faxō⟧ and ⟦b:ausim⟧, even the active forms had become antiquated by 150 B.C. Denominatives in ⟦b:-īre⟧ never have the above formations. But ⟦b:ambiō⟧, ⟦i:canvass⟧, is thought to have a future perfect ⟦b:ambīssit⟧ twice (Plaut. prol.).
⟦#889⟧
(2.) Shortened forms from perfect stems formed by the suffix ⟦b:-v-⟧ (⟦r869:869⟧) are very common in all periods.
⟦#890⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) In tenses formed from perfect stems in ⟦b:-āv-⟧, ⟦b:-ēv-⟧, and ⟦b:-ōv-⟧, ⟦b:v⟧ is often dropped before ⟦b:-is-⟧, ⟦b:-ēr-⟧, or ⟦b:-er-⟧, and the vowels thus brought together are contracted (⟦r153:153, 1⟧): as,
⟦b:laudāvistī⟧, ⟦b:laudāstī⟧; ⟦b:laudāvistis⟧, ⟦b:laudāstis⟧; ⟦b:laudāvērunt⟧, ⟦b:laudārunt⟧ (but the form in ⟦b:-re⟧, as ⟦b:laudāvēre⟧, is never contracted); ⟦b:laudāverim⟧, ⟦b:laudārim⟧, &c.; ⟦b:laudāveram⟧, ⟦b:laudāram⟧, &c.; ⟦b:laudāvissem⟧, ⟦b:laudāssem⟧, &c.; ⟦b:laudāverō⟧, ⟦b:laudārō⟧, &c.; ⟦b:laudāvisse⟧, ⟦b:laudāsse⟧.
⟦b:-plēvistī⟧, ⟦b:-plēstī⟧; ⟦b:-plēvistis⟧, ⟦b:-plēstis⟧; ⟦b:-plēvērunt⟧, ⟦b:-plērunt⟧; ⟦b:plēverim⟧, ⟦b:-plērim⟧, &c.; ⟦b:-plēveram⟧, ⟦b:-plēram⟧, &c.; ⟦b:-plēvissem⟧, ⟦b:-plēssem⟧, &c.; ⟦b:-plēverō⟧, ⟦b:-plērō⟧, &c.; ⟦b:-plēvisse⟧, ⟦b:-plēsse⟧.
⟦b:nōvistī⟧, ⟦b:nōstī⟧; ⟦b:nōvistis⟧, ⟦b:nōstis⟧; ⟦b:nōvērunt⟧, ⟦b:nōrunt⟧; ⟦b:nōverim⟧, ⟦b:nōrim⟧, &c.; ⟦b:nōveram⟧, ⟦b:nōram⟧, &c.; ⟦b:nōvissem⟧, ⟦b:nōssem⟧, &c.; ⟦b:nōverō⟧ always retains the ⟦b:v⟧, but ⟦b:cōgnōrō⟧, &c.; ⟦b:nōvisse⟧, ⟦b:nōsse⟧.
⟦#891⟧
The verbs in which ⟦b:v⟧ belongs to the root (⟦r864:864⟧), are not thus shortened, except ⟦b:moveō⟧, mostly in compounds. From ⟦b:iuvō⟧, ⟦b:iuerint⟧ (Catull.), ⟦b:adiuerō⟧ (Enn.), once each, and twice ⟦b:adiuerit⟧ (Plaut., Ter.) are unnecessary emendations.
⟦#892⟧
Contractions in the perfect before ⟦b:-t⟧ and ⟦b:-mus⟧ are rare: as, ⟦b:inrītāt⟧, ⟦b:disturbāt⟧; ⟦b:suēmus⟧ or ⟦b:su͡emus⟧ (Lucr.), ⟦b:nōmus⟧ (Enn.), ⟦b:cōnsu͡emus⟧ (Prop.).
⟦#893⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) In tenses formed from perfect stems in ⟦b:-īv-⟧, ⟦b:v⟧ is often dropped before ⟦b:-is-⟧, ⟦b:-ēr-⟧, or ⟦b:-er-⟧; but contraction is common only in the forms which have ⟦b:-is-⟧: as,
⟦b:audīvistī⟧, ⟦b:audīstī⟧; ⟦b:audīvistis⟧, ⟦b:audīstis⟧; ⟦b:audīvērunt⟧, ⟦b:audiērunt⟧; ⟦b:audīverim⟧, ⟦b:audierim⟧, &c.; ⟦b:audīveram⟧, ⟦b:audieram⟧, &c.; ⟦b:audīvissem⟧, ⟦b:audīssem⟧, &c.; ⟦b:audīverō⟧, ⟦b:audierō⟧, &c.; ⟦b:audīvisse⟧, ⟦b:audīsse⟧. Sometimes ⟦b:audiī⟧, ⟦b:audiit⟧, ⟦b:audīt⟧. Intermediate between the long and the short forms are ⟦b:audīerās⟧ and ⟦b:audīerit⟧, once each (Ter.). In the perfect subjunctive, ⟦b:sinō⟧ has ⟦b:sīverīs⟧ (Plaut., Cato), ⟦b:sīrīs⟧ (Plaut., Cato, Liv.), ⟦b:sīreis⟧ (Pac.), or ⟦b:seirīs⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:sīrit⟧ (Plaut., Liv.), ⟦b:sīrītis⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:sīverint⟧ (Plaut., Curt.), ⟦b:sierint⟧ (Cic., Curt.), or ⟦b:sīrint⟧ (Plaut.). ⟦b:dēsinō⟧ is thought to have ⟦b:dēsīmus⟧ in the perfect indicative a couple of times (Sen., Plin. ⟦i:Ep.⟧).

title: Infinitive
text:
⟦#894⟧
The active infinitive has the ending ⟦b:-re⟧ in the present, and ⟦b:-isse⟧ in the perfect: as,
⟦b:dare⟧; ⟦b:regere⟧, ⟦b:capere⟧; ⟦b:laudāre⟧, ⟦b:monēre⟧, ⟦b:audīre⟧. ⟦b:rēxisse⟧; ⟦b:laudāvisse⟧ or ⟦b:laudāsse⟧, ⟦b:monuisse⟧, ⟦b:audīvisse⟧ or ⟦b:audīsse⟧.
⟦#895⟧
For ⟦b:-rē⟧ in old Latin, see 134, 2. The infinitive of ⟦b:fīō⟧, ⟦i:become⟧, ends in ⟦b:-rī⟧, ⟦b:fī̆erī⟧, with a passive ending (⟦r789:789⟧); twice ⟦b:fīere⟧ (Enn. Laev.). An older form for ⟦b:-re⟧ is ⟦b:-se⟧, found in ⟦b:esse⟧, ⟦i:to be⟧, ⟦b:ēsse⟧, ⟦i:to eat⟧, and their compounds. For ⟦b:velle⟧, ⟦i:to wish⟧ (⟦b:mālle⟧, ⟦b:nōlle⟧), see 166, 8. In the perfect, ⟦b:eō⟧, ⟦i:go⟧, sometimes has ⟦b:-iisse⟧ in compounds (⟦r766:766⟧), and in poetry, ⟦b:petō⟧, ⟦i:go to⟧, has rarely ⟦b:petiisse⟧.
⟦#896⟧
The present infinitive passive of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ has the ending ⟦b:-ī⟧; that of other verbs has ⟦b:-rī⟧: as,
⟦b:regī⟧, ⟦b:capī⟧; ⟦b:laudārī⟧, ⟦b:monērī⟧, ⟦b:audīrī⟧. ⟦b:ferō⟧, ⟦i:carry⟧, has ⟦b:ferrī⟧. The length of the ⟦b:ī⟧ is sometimes indicated by the spelling ⟦b:ei⟧ (⟦r29:29, 2⟧): as, DAREI.
⟦#897⟧
A longer form in ⟦b:-ier⟧ for ⟦b:-ī⟧, and ⟦b:-rier⟧ for ⟦b:-rī⟧, is common in old laws and dramatic verse, and occurs sometimes in other poetry: as, FIGIER, ⟦i:to be posted⟧, GNOSCIER, ⟦i:to be read⟧ (inscr. 186 B.C.); ⟦b:dīcier⟧, ⟦i:to be said⟧, ⟦b:cūrārier⟧, ⟦i:to be looked after⟧ (Plaut.); ⟦b:dominārier⟧, ⟦i:to be lord paramount⟧ (Verg.).
⟦#898⟧
The place of the perfect passive, future active, and future passive infinitive is supplied by a circumlocution, as seen in the paradigms. For the future perfect ⟦b:-āssere⟧, see ⟦r887:887⟧.

title: Gerundive and Gerund
text:
⟦#899⟧
The gerundive stem is formed by adding ⟦b:-ndo-⟧, nominative ⟦b:-ndus⟧, ⟦b:-nda⟧, ⟦b:-ndum⟧, to the present stem: as,
⟦b:dandus⟧, stem ⟦b:dando-⟧; ⟦b:regendus⟧, ⟦b:capiendus⟧; ⟦b:laudandus⟧, ⟦b:monendus⟧, ⟦b:audiendus⟧. Verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ and ⟦b:-īre⟧ often have ⟦b:-undus⟧, when not preceded by ⟦b:u⟧ or ⟦b:v⟧, especially in formal style: as, ⟦b:capiundus⟧; ⟦b:eō⟧, ⟦i:go⟧, always has ⟦b:eundum⟧, and ⟦b:orior⟧, ⟦i:rise⟧, ⟦b:oriundus⟧. For the adjective use, see ⟦r288:288⟧. The gerund is like the oblique cases of the neuter singular. For ⟦b:-bundus⟧, see ⟦r289:289⟧; ⟦b:-cundus⟧, ⟦r290:290⟧.

title: Supine
text:
⟦#900⟧
The supine stem is formed by the suffix ⟦b:-tu-⟧, which is often changed to ⟦b:-su-⟧ (⟦r912:912⟧).
This suffix is attached to a root or to a form of the present stem after the manner of the perfect participle (⟦r906:906⟧): as, ⟦b:nūntiātum⟧, ⟦i:to report⟧, ⟦b:nūntiātū⟧, ⟦i:in reporting⟧, stem ⟦b:nūntiātu-⟧. Many of the commonest verbs have no supine: as, ⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦b:eō⟧, ⟦b:ferō⟧; ⟦b:regō⟧, ⟦b:emō⟧, ⟦b:tegō⟧; ⟦b:amō⟧, ⟦b:dēleō⟧, ⟦b:doceō⟧, &c., &c.

title: Present Participle
text:
⟦#901⟧
The present participle stem is formed by adding ⟦b:-nt-⟧ or ⟦b:-nti-⟧, nominative ⟦b:-ns⟧, to the present stem: as,
⟦b:dāns⟧, ⟦i:giving⟧, stems ⟦b:dant-⟧, ⟦b:danti-⟧; ⟦b:regēns⟧, ⟦b:capiēns⟧; ⟦b:laudāns⟧, ⟦b:monēns⟧, ⟦b:audiēns⟧.
⟦#902⟧
The adjective ⟦b:sontem⟧ (accusative, no nominative), which was originally the participle of ⟦b:sum⟧, has ⟦b:o⟧ before the suffix, and ⟦b:absēns⟧ and ⟦b:praesēns⟧ have ⟦b:e⟧; the participle of ⟦b:eō⟧ has ⟦b:ē⟧ in the nominative singular, otherwise ⟦b:u⟧, ⟦b:iēns⟧, ⟦b:euntis⟧, &c. ⟦b:n⟧ rarely drops before ⟦b:-s⟧ (⟦r63:63⟧): as, LIBES (inscr.), ⟦b:exsultās⟧ (Enn.), ⟦b:animās⟧ (Lucr.).
⟦#903⟧
Some adjectives which were originally present participles have no verb: as, ⟦b:clēmēns⟧, ⟦i:merciful⟧, ⟦b:ēlegāns⟧, ⟦i:choice⟧, ⟦b:ēvidēns⟧, ⟦i:clear⟧, ⟦b:frequēns⟧, ⟦i:thick⟧, ⟦b:petulāns⟧, ⟦i:wanton⟧, ⟦b:recēns⟧, ⟦i:fresh⟧, ⟦b:repēns⟧, ⟦i:sudden⟧, &c., &c. For ⟦b:potēns⟧, ⟦i:powerful⟧, see ⟦r922:922⟧.

title: Future Participle
text:
⟦#904⟧
The future participle suffix is ⟦b:-tūro-⟧, nominative ⟦b:-tūrus⟧, ⟦b:-tūra⟧, ⟦b:-tūrum⟧, which is often changed to ⟦b:-sūro-⟧, nominative ⟦b:-sūrus⟧, ⟦b:-sūra⟧, ⟦b:-sūrum⟧ (⟦r912:912⟧).
This suffix is added to a theme after the manner of the perfect participle (⟦r906:906⟧): as, ⟦b:rēctūrus⟧, ⟦i:going to guide⟧; ⟦b:laudātūrus⟧, ⟦i:going to praise⟧.
⟦#905⟧
Some future participles have a different formation from that of the perfect participle: as, ⟦b:mortuus⟧, ⟦i:dead⟧, ⟦b:moritūrus⟧; see also in the dictionary ⟦b:arguō⟧, ⟦b:fruor⟧, ⟦b:orior⟧, ⟦b:ruō⟧, ⟦b:secō⟧. And some verbs have two forms of the future participle: as, ⟦b:āgnōscō⟧, ⟦b:īgnōscō⟧, ⟦b:hauriō⟧, ⟦b:iuvō⟧, ⟦b:pariō⟧. Some verbs which have no perfect participle have a future participle: as, ⟦b:acquiēscō⟧, ⟦b:appāreō⟧, ⟦b:ardeō⟧, ⟦b:caleō⟧, ⟦b:careō⟧, ⟦b:doleō⟧, ⟦b:ēsuriō⟧, ⟦b:fugiō⟧, ⟦b:haereō⟧, ⟦b:incidō⟧, ⟦b:iaceō⟧, ⟦b:-nuō⟧, ⟦b:parcō⟧, ⟦b:rauciō⟧, ⟦b:recidō⟧, ⟦b:sonō⟧, ⟦b:stō⟧, ⟦b:valeō⟧.

title: Perfect Participle
text:
⟦#906⟧
The perfect participle suffix is ⟦b:-to-⟧, nominative ⟦b:-tus⟧, ⟦b:-ta⟧, ⟦b:-tum⟧, which is often changed to ⟦b:-so-⟧, nominative ⟦b:-sus⟧, ⟦b:-sa⟧, ⟦b:-sum⟧ (⟦r912:912⟧).
⟦#907⟧
The perfect participle was originally active as well as passive, and some participles have retained the active meaning: as,
⟦b:adultus⟧, ⟦i:grown up⟧; ⟦b:ēmersus⟧, ⟦i:rising out from⟧; ⟦b:exōsus⟧, ⟦b:perōsus⟧, ⟦i:hating bitterly⟧; ⟦b:placitus⟧, ⟦i:engaging⟧; ⟦b:iūrātus⟧, ⟦i:sworn⟧, ⟦b:coniūrātus⟧, ⟦i:conspiring⟧; ⟦b:prānsus⟧, ⟦i:having lunched⟧, ⟦b:cēnātus⟧, ⟦i:having dined⟧, ⟦b:pōtus⟧, ⟦i:drunk⟧, &c. The perfect participles of deponents are usually active, but sometimes passive: as, ⟦b:meditātus⟧, ⟦i:having studied⟧, or ⟦i:studied⟧. Many verbs are not accompanied by a perfect participle (⟦r811:811⟧), particularly verbs in ⟦b:-ēre⟧, with a parallel adjective in ⟦b:-idus⟧ (⟦r287:287⟧). Intransitive verbs have usually only the neuter. A perfect active participle ⟦b:meminēns⟧ is said to have been used twice (Plaut., Laev.).
⟦#908⟧
The perfect participle is formed in one of two separate ways:
⟦#909⟧
(1.) From a theme consisting of a root; in this way the participles of most verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ and ⟦b:-ēre⟧ are formed: as,
⟦b:gestus⟧, ⟦i:carried⟧, ⟦b:aptus⟧, ⟦i:fit⟧, ⟦b:solūtus⟧, ⟦i:loosed⟧ (⟦r142:142⟧), ⟦b:iūnctus⟧, ⟦i:joined⟧ (⟦r831:831⟧), ⟦b:sparsus⟧, ⟦i:sprinkled⟧ (⟦r170:170, 3⟧); ⟦b:doctus⟧, ⟦i:taught⟧.
⟦#910⟧
In some consonant root participles of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧, ⟦b:-āre⟧, or ⟦b:-ēre⟧, which have the suffix ⟦b:-u-⟧ in the perfect stem (⟦r873:873⟧), the ⟦b:-to-⟧ is preceded by a short ⟦b:i⟧: as, ⟦b:genitus⟧, ⟦i:born⟧ (⟦r971:971-976⟧); ⟦b:domitus⟧, ⟦i:tamed⟧ (⟦r993:993⟧); ⟦b:monitus⟧, ⟦i:warned⟧ (⟦r1003:1003⟧, ⟦r1004:1004⟧, ⟦r1009:1009⟧). In old Latin, ⟦b:e⟧ occurs: as, MERETA (⟦r41:41⟧); ⟦b:e⟧ is retained in ⟦b:vegetus⟧, ⟦i:sprightly⟧. One participle has ⟦b:-tuo-⟧: ⟦b:mortuus⟧, ⟦i:dead⟧.
⟦#911⟧
Some verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧ have participles from consonant roots: as, ⟦b:frictus⟧, ⟦i:rubbed⟧, ⟦b:fricō⟧, ⟦b:fricāre⟧; see ⟦r993:993⟧. Also some in ⟦b:-īre⟧: as, ⟦b:fartus⟧, ⟦i:stuffed⟧ (⟦r170:170, 3⟧), ⟦b:farciō⟧, ⟦b:farcīre⟧; ⟦b:fultus⟧, ⟦i:propped⟧, ⟦b:fulciō⟧, ⟦b:fulcīre⟧; see ⟦r1011:1011-1015⟧, and ⟦r1017:1017⟧, ⟦r1019:1019⟧, ⟦r1020:1020⟧.
⟦#912⟧
Roots in ⟦b:-d-⟧ and ⟦b:-t-⟧ change ⟦b:-to-⟧ to ⟦b:-so-⟧, before which the dentals change to ⟦b:s⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧). After long vowels, nasals, and liquids the double ⟦b:ss⟧ is simplified to ⟦b:s⟧: as, ⟦b:fossus⟧, ⟦i:dug⟧, but ⟦b:dīvīsus⟧, ⟦i:divided⟧; ⟦b:vorsus⟧ or ⟦b:versus⟧, ⟦i:turned⟧. The suffix ⟦b:-so-⟧ is also found with some roots in ⟦b:-l-⟧, ⟦b:-m-⟧, or ⟦b:-r-⟧ and a few others: as, ⟦b:pulsus⟧ (⟦r159:159⟧).
⟦#913⟧
(2.) From a theme in long ⟦b:ā⟧ or in long ⟦b:ī⟧; in this way participles are regularly formed from denominatives in ⟦b:-āre⟧ or ⟦b:-īre⟧ respectively: as,
⟦b:laudātus⟧, ⟦i:praised⟧; ⟦b:audītus⟧, ⟦i:heard⟧.
⟦#914⟧
A few perfect participles of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ are formed from a presumed theme in long ⟦b:ī⟧, or long ⟦b:ē⟧, or from one in long ⟦b:ū⟧: as, ⟦b:petītus⟧, ⟦i:aimed at⟧; ⟦b:exolētus⟧, ⟦i:grown out⟧; see ⟦r967:967-970⟧; ⟦b:tribūtus⟧, ⟦i:assigned⟧; see ⟦r947:947⟧, ⟦r948:948⟧.
⟦#915⟧
(1.) Many perfect participles formed from consonant roots have a short root vowel (⟦r135:135, 1⟧): as,
⟦b:adspectus⟧, ⟦i:beheld⟧; ⟦b:captus⟧, ⟦i:taken⟧; ⟦b:coctus⟧, ⟦i:cooked⟧; ⟦b:commentus⟧, ⟦i:devising⟧; ⟦b:cultus⟧, ⟦i:tilled⟧; ⟦b:dictus⟧, ⟦i:said⟧, verb ⟦b:dīcō⟧; ⟦b:ductus⟧, ⟦i:led⟧, ⟦b:dūcō⟧; ⟦b:factus⟧, ⟦i:made⟧; ⟦b:fossus⟧, ⟦i:dug⟧; ⟦b:gestus⟧, ⟦i:carried⟧; ⟦b:inlectus⟧, ⟦i:allured⟧; ⟦b:questus⟧, ⟦i:complaining⟧; ⟦b:raptus⟧, ⟦i:seized⟧; ⟦b:tersus⟧, ⟦i:neat⟧; ⟦b:textus⟧, ⟦i:woven⟧; ⟦b:vorsus⟧, ⟦i:turned⟧.
⟦#916⟧
(2.) Some perfect participles formed from consonant roots have a long root vowel, sometimes even when the vowel of the parallel present stem is short (135, 1; 122, ⟦i:f⟧): as,
⟦b:fīxus⟧, ⟦i:fastened⟧, verb ⟦b:fīgō⟧; ⟦b:-flīctus⟧, ⟦i:dashed⟧, ⟦b:-flīgō⟧; ⟦b:pāstus⟧, ⟦i:fed⟧, ⟦b:pāscō⟧; ⟦b:pollūctus⟧, ⟦i:offered up⟧, ⟦b:pollūceō⟧; ⟦b:scrīptus⟧, ⟦i:written⟧, ⟦i:scrībō⟧; ⟦b:-cāsus⟧, ⟦i:fallen⟧, ⟦b:cadō⟧. Also ⟦b:āctus⟧, ⟦i:driven⟧, ⟦b:agō⟧; ⟦b:vīsus⟧, ⟦i:seen⟧, ⟦b:videō⟧; ⟦b:frūctus⟧, ⟦i:enjoying⟧, ⟦b:fruor⟧; ⟦b:lēctus⟧, ⟦i:culled⟧, ⟦b:legō⟧; ⟦b:pīctus⟧, ⟦i:painted⟧, ⟦b:pingō⟧; ⟦b:rēctus⟧, ⟦i:ruled⟧, ⟦b:regō⟧; ⟦b:ēsus⟧, ⟦i:eaten⟧, ⟦b:edō⟧; ⟦b:strūctus⟧, ⟦i:piled⟧, ⟦b:struō⟧; ⟦b:tēctus⟧, ⟦i:covered⟧, ⟦b:tegō⟧; ⟦b:ūnctus⟧, ⟦i:anointed⟧, ⟦b:unguō⟧; ⟦b:frāctus⟧, ⟦i:broken⟧, ⟦b:frangō⟧; ⟦b:pāctus⟧, ⟦i:fixed⟧, ⟦b:pangō⟧. Furthermore, ⟦b:iūnctus⟧, ⟦i:joined⟧, ⟦b:iungō⟧; ⟦b:sānctus⟧, ⟦i:hallowed⟧, ⟦b:sanciō⟧ (⟦r831:831⟧); also, ⟦b:fūnctus⟧, ⟦i:having performed⟧, ⟦b:fungor⟧.
⟦#917⟧
(1.) Most perfect participles formed from vowel roots have a long root vowel: as,
⟦b:lātus⟧, ⟦i:borne⟧ (⟦r169:169⟧, ⟦r1:1⟧); ⟦b:nātus⟧, ⟦i:born⟧; ⟦b:-plētus⟧, ⟦i:filled⟧; ⟦b:trītus⟧, ⟦i:worn⟧; ⟦b:nōtus⟧, ⟦i:known⟧; ⟦b:sūtus⟧, ⟦i:sewed⟧. So also an isolated ⟦b:rūtus⟧, in the law phrase ⟦b:rūta caesa⟧, or ⟦b:rūta et caesa⟧, ⟦i:diggings and cuttings⟧, i.e. ⟦i:minerals and timber⟧.
⟦#918⟧
(2.) Ten perfect participles formed from vowel roots have a short root vowel; they are:
⟦b:citus⟧, ⟦b:datus⟧, ⟦i:hurried⟧, ⟦i:given⟧
⟦b:itum⟧, ⟦b:ratus⟧, ⟦i:gone⟧, ⟦i:thinking⟧
⟦b:-rutus⟧, ⟦b:satus⟧, ⟦i:fallen⟧, ⟦i:planted⟧
⟦b:situs⟧, ⟦b:status⟧, ⟦i:lying⟧, ⟦i:set⟧
⟦b:litus⟧, ⟦b:quitus⟧, ⟦i:besmeared⟧, ⟦i:been able⟧
⟦#919⟧
As ⟦b:citus⟧, so always ⟦b:percitus⟧ and ⟦b:incitus⟧ (once ⟦b:incītus⟧, doubtful); usually ⟦b:concitus⟧, rarely ⟦b:concītus⟧; ⟦b:excitus⟧ and ⟦b:excītus⟧ equally common; always ⟦b:accītus⟧. ⟦b:ambītus⟧ always has long ⟦b:ī⟧ (⟦r763:763⟧). ⟦b:āgnitus⟧, ⟦i:recognized⟧, ⟦b:cōgnitus⟧, ⟦i:known⟧, and the adjectives ⟦b:inclutus⟧ or ⟦b:inclitus⟧, ⟦i:of high renown⟧, and ⟦b:putus⟧, ⟦i:clean⟧, have a short root vowel. For ⟦b:dēfrūtum⟧, ⟦b:dēfrutum⟧, see ⟦r134:134⟧, 1.

title: List of Verbs Arranged According to the Principal Parts
text:
⟦#920⟧
I. The principal parts of root verbs and of verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ are formed in a variety of ways and are best learned separately for every verb (⟦r922:922-986⟧).
⟦#921⟧
II. The principal parts of verbs in ⟦b:-āre⟧, ⟦b:-ēre⟧, and ⟦b:-īre⟧, are usually formed as follows:
⟦b:laudō⟧, ⟦i:praise⟧  ⟦b:laudāre⟧  ⟦b:laudāvī⟧  ⟦b:laudātus⟧
⟦b:moneō⟧, ⟦i:advise⟧  ⟦b:monēre⟧  ⟦b:monuī⟧  ⟦b:monitus⟧
⟦b:audiō⟧, ⟦i:hear⟧  ⟦b:audīre⟧  ⟦b:audīvī⟧  ⟦b:audītus⟧
⟦/⟧
For other formations, see ⟦r989:989-1022⟧.

title: Primitive Verbs: Root Verbs
text:
⟦#922⟧
Root verbs have their principal parts as follows:
⟦b:sum⟧, ⟦i:am⟧  ⟦b:esse⟧  ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:——⟧, ⟦i:become⟧, ⟦i:get⟧, ⟦i:am⟧  ⟦b:fore⟧  ⟦b:fuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
For ⟦b:fuam⟧, &c., ⟦b:forem⟧, &c., ⟦b:fore⟧, see ⟦r750:750⟧. ⟦b:fuī⟧, &c., serves as the perfect system of ⟦b:sum⟧.
⟦b:pos-sum⟧, ⟦i:can⟧  ⟦b:pos-se⟧  ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:——⟧, ⟦i:can⟧  ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:potuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦b:potuī⟧, &c., serves as the perfect system of ⟦b:possum⟧. Of the present system of ⟦b:potuī⟧, only ⟦b:potēns⟧, ⟦i:powerful⟧, is used, and only as an adjective.
⟦b:dō⟧, ⟦i:give⟧, ⟦i:put⟧  ⟦b:dare⟧  ⟦b:dedī⟧  ⟦b:datus⟧
⟦/⟧
For compounds, see ⟦r757:757⟧.
⟦b:bibō⟧, ⟦i:drink⟧  ⟦b:bibere⟧  ⟦b:bibī⟧  ⟦b:pōtus⟧
⟦/⟧
So the compounds, with the reduplication preserved in the perfect system (⟦r860:860⟧).
⟦b:serō⟧, ⟦i:sow⟧  ⟦b:serere⟧  ⟦b:sēvī⟧  ⟦b:satus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds have ⟦b:i⟧ for ⟦b:a⟧ in the perfect participle: as, ⟦b:cōn-situs⟧.
⟦b:sistō⟧, ⟦i:set⟧  ⟦b:sistere⟧  ⟦b:-stitī⟧, rarely ⟦b:stitī⟧  ⟦b:status⟧
⟦b:inquam⟧, ⟦i:quoth I⟧  ⟦b:——⟧  ⟦b:inquiī⟧ once  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:eō⟧, ⟦i:go⟧  ⟦b:īre⟧  ⟦b:iī⟧, very rarely ⟦b:īvī⟧  ⟦b:itum⟧, ⟦b:-itus⟧
⟦b:queō⟧, ⟦i:can⟧  ⟦b:quīre⟧  ⟦b:quīvī⟧  ⟦b:quitus⟧
⟦b:ne-queō⟧, ⟦i:can’t⟧  ⟦b:ne-quīre⟧  ⟦b:ne-quīvī⟧  ⟦b:ne-quitus⟧
⟦b:edō⟧, ⟦i:eat⟧  ⟦b:ēsse⟧  ⟦b:ēdī⟧  ⟦b:ēsus⟧
⟦b:volō⟧, ⟦i:will⟧, ⟦i:wish⟧, ⟦i:want⟧  ⟦b:velle⟧  ⟦b:voluī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:nōlō⟧, ⟦i:won’t⟧  ⟦b:nōlle⟧  ⟦b:nōluī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:mālō⟧, ⟦i:like better⟧  ⟦b:mālle⟧  ⟦b:māluī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:ferō⟧, ⟦i:carry⟧  ⟦b:ferre⟧  (⟦b:tulī⟧)  (⟦b:lātus⟧)
⟦/⟧
For ⟦b:tulī⟧, old ⟦b:tetulī⟧, and ⟦b:lātus⟧, see ⟦r780:780⟧; for the perfect of ⟦b:re-ferō⟧, ⟦r861:861⟧.

title: Primitive Verbs: Perfect Stem Without a Suffix
text:
⟦#923⟧
(1 ⟦i:a⟧.) The following verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have a reduplicated perfect stem (⟦r858:858⟧), and the perfect participle, when used, in ⟦b:-tus⟧:
⟦#924⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r829:829⟧).
⟦b:canō⟧, ⟦i:make music⟧  ⟦b:canere⟧  ⟦b:cecinī⟧  (⟦b:cantātus⟧)
⟦/⟧
For ⟦b:con-cinō⟧, ⟦b:oc-cinō⟧, and ⟦b:prae-cinō⟧, see ⟦r971:971⟧ and ⟦r823:823⟧.

⟦b:pluit⟧, ⟦i:it rains⟧  ⟦b:pluere⟧  ⟦b:pluit⟧, ⟦b:plūvit⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:ruō⟧, ⟦i:tumble down⟧  ⟦b:ruere⟧  ⟦b:ruī⟧  ⟦b:-rutus⟧
⟦b:so-lvō⟧, ⟦i:loose⟧  ⟦b:so-lvere⟧  ⟦b:so-lvī⟧  ⟦b:so-lūtus⟧
⟦b:spuō⟧, ⟦i:spit⟧  ⟦b:spuere⟧  ⟦b:-spuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:statuō⟧, ⟦i:set⟧  ⟦b:statuere⟧  ⟦b:statuī⟧  ⟦b:statūtus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds have ⟦b:i⟧ for ⟦b:a⟧ throughout: as, ⟦b:cōn-stituō⟧, ⟦b:cōn-stituere⟧, &c.
⟦b:volvō⟧, ⟦i:roll⟧  ⟦b:volvere⟧  ⟦b:volvī⟧  ⟦b:volūtus⟧
⟦b:suō⟧, ⟦i:sew⟧  ⟦b:suere⟧  ⟦b:-suī⟧  ⟦b:sūtus⟧
⟦b:tribuō⟧, ⟦i:assign⟧  ⟦b:tribuere⟧  ⟦b:tribuī⟧  ⟦b:tribūtus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#948⟧
Two verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ with the present stem in ⟦b:-nuo|e-⟧ (⟦r833:833⟧), have the perfect stem in ⟦b:-nu-⟧ (⟦r865:865⟧), and the perfect participle, when used, in ⟦b:-tus⟧:
⟦b:minuō⟧, ⟦i:lessen⟧  ⟦b:minuere⟧  ⟦b:minuī⟧  ⟦b:minūtus⟧
⟦b:sternuō⟧, ⟦i:sneeze⟧  ⟦b:sternuere⟧  ⟦b:sternuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#949⟧
(3.) The following verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have a perfect stem consisting of a root ending in two consonants (⟦r866:866⟧), and the perfect participle in ⟦b:-sus⟧ (⟦r912:912⟧):
⟦#950⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r829:829⟧); most have a nasal (⟦r831:831⟧).
⟦b:-cendō⟧, ⟦i:light⟧  ⟦b:-cendere⟧  ⟦b:-cendī⟧  ⟦b:-cēnsus⟧
⟦b:-fendō⟧, ⟦i:hit⟧  ⟦b:-fendere⟧  ⟦b:-fendī⟧  ⟦b:-fēnsus⟧
⟦b:mandō⟧, ⟦i:chew⟧  ⟦b:mandere⟧  ⟦b:mandī⟧ once  ⟦b:mānsus⟧
⟦b:pandō⟧, ⟦i:open⟧  ⟦b:pandere⟧  ⟦b:pandī⟧  ⟦b:passus⟧, ⟦b:pānsus⟧
⟦/⟧
For ⟦b:dis-pennite⟧ (Plaut.), see 166, 4. ⟦b:dis-pandō⟧, ⟦b:dis-pendō⟧, has perfect participle ⟦b:dis-pessus⟧ (Plaut., Lucr.), ⟦b:dis-pānsus⟧ (Lucr., Plin., Suet.).
⟦b:pre-hendō⟧, ⟦i:seize⟧  ⟦b:pre-hendere⟧  ⟦b:pre-hendī⟧  ⟦b:pre-hēnsus⟧
⟦/⟧
Rarely ⟦b:prae-hendō⟧; but very often ⟦b:prēndō⟧, ⟦b:prēndere⟧, ⟦b:prēndī⟧, ⟦b:prēnsus⟧.
⟦b:scandō⟧, ⟦i:climb⟧  ⟦b:scandere⟧  ⟦b:-scendī⟧  ⟦b:-scēnsus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds have ⟦b:e⟧ for ⟦b:a⟧ throughout: as, ⟦b:dē-scendō⟧, ⟦b:dē-scendere⟧, &c.
⟦b:vorrō⟧, ⟦b:verrō⟧, ⟦i:sweep⟧  ⟦b:vorrere⟧, ⟦b:verrere⟧  ⟦b:-vorrī⟧, ⟦b:-verrī⟧  ⟦b:vorsus⟧, ⟦b:versus⟧
⟦b:vortō⟧, ⟦b:vertō⟧, ⟦i:turn⟧  ⟦b:vortere⟧, ⟦b:vertere⟧  ⟦b:vortī⟧, ⟦b:vertī⟧  ⟦b:vorsus⟧, ⟦b:versus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#951⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-lo|e-⟧ (⟦r833:833⟧).
⟦b:vollō⟧, ⟦b:vellō⟧, ⟦i:tear⟧  ⟦b:vollere⟧, ⟦b:vellere⟧  ⟦b:vollī⟧, ⟦b:vellī⟧  ⟦b:volsus⟧, ⟦b:vulsus⟧
⟦/⟧
Late perfect ⟦b:vulsī⟧ (Sen., Luc.); ⟦b:-vulsī⟧ (Laber., Col., Sen., Luc.).

title: Primitive Verbs: Perfect Stem in -s-
text:
⟦#952⟧
(1 ⟦i:a⟧.) The following verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have the perfect stem in ⟦b:-s-⟧ (⟦r867:867⟧), and the perfect participle, when used, in ⟦b:-tus⟧:
⟦#953⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r829:829⟧).
⟦b:carpō⟧, ⟦i:nibble⟧, ⟦i:pluck⟧  ⟦b:carpere⟧  ⟦b:carpsī⟧  ⟦b:carptus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds have ⟦b:e⟧ for ⟦b:a⟧: as, ⟦b:dē-cerpō⟧, ⟦b:dē-cerpere⟧, ⟦b:dē-cerpsī⟧, ⟦b:dē-cerptus⟧.
⟦b:com-būrō⟧, ⟦i:burn up⟧  ⟦b:com-būrere⟧  ⟦b:com-bussī⟧  ⟦b:com-būstus⟧
⟦b:cōmō⟧, ⟦i:put up⟧  ⟦b:cōmere⟧  ⟦b:cōmpsī⟧  ⟦b:cōmptus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compound of ⟦b:com-⟧ and ⟦b:emō⟧ (⟦r937:937⟧, ⟦r823:823⟧). See also ⟦b:dēmō⟧, ⟦b:prōmō⟧, ⟦b:sūmō⟧.
⟦b:coquō⟧, ⟦i:cook⟧  ⟦b:coquere⟧  ⟦b:coxī⟧  ⟦b:coctus⟧
⟦b:dēmō⟧, ⟦i:take away⟧  ⟦b:dēmere⟧  ⟦b:dēmpsī⟧  ⟦b:dēmptus⟧
⟦b:dīcō⟧, ⟦i:say⟧  ⟦b:dīcere⟧  ⟦b:dīxī⟧  ⟦b:dictus⟧
⟦/⟧
For ⟦b:dīc⟧, see ⟦r846:846⟧.
⟦b:dī-ligō⟧, ⟦i:esteem⟧  ⟦b:dī-ligere⟧  ⟦b:dī-lēxī⟧  ⟦b:dī-lēctus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compound of ⟦b:dis-⟧ and ⟦b:legō⟧ (⟦r937:937⟧, ⟦r823:823⟧). See also ⟦b:intel-legō⟧ and ⟦b:neg-legō⟧.
⟦b:dūcō⟧ ⟦i:lead⟧  ⟦b:dūcere⟧  ⟦b:dūxī⟧  ⟦b:ductus⟧
⟦/⟧
For ⟦b:dūc⟧, ⟦b:ē-dūc⟧, see ⟦r846:846⟧.
⟦b:-flīgō⟧, ⟦i:smash⟧  ⟦b:-flīgere⟧  ⟦b:-flīxī⟧  ⟦b:-flīctus⟧
⟦/⟧
Of the simple verb, ⟦b:flīgit⟧ occurs (L. Andr.), ⟦b:flīgēbant⟧ (Lucr.), and ⟦b:flīgī⟧ (L. Andr., Acc.).
⟦b:gerō⟧, ⟦i:carry⟧  ⟦b:gerere⟧  ⟦b:gessī⟧  ⟦b:gestus⟧
⟦b:intel-legō⟧, ⟦i:understand⟧  ⟦b:intel-legere⟧  ⟦b:intel-lēxī⟧  ⟦b:intel-lēctus⟧
⟦b:neg-legō⟧, ⟦i:disregard⟧  ⟦b:neg-legere⟧  ⟦b:neg-lēxī⟧  ⟦b:neg-lēctus⟧
⟦/⟧
In the perfect system very rarely ⟦b:intel-lēgī⟧ and ⟦b:neg-lēgī⟧ (⟦r862:862⟧, ⟦r823:823⟧).
⟦b:nūbō⟧, ⟦i:veil⟧, ⟦i:marry⟧ (⟦i:a man⟧)  ⟦b:nūbere⟧  ⟦b:nūpsī⟧  ⟦b:nūpta⟧
⟦b:prōmō⟧, ⟦i:take out⟧  ⟦b:prōmere⟧  ⟦b:prōmpsī⟧  ⟦b:prōmptus⟧
⟦b:regō⟧, ⟦i:guide⟧, ⟦i:rule⟧  ⟦b:regere⟧  ⟦b:rēxī⟧  ⟦b:rēctus⟧
⟦/⟧
In the present system, ⟦b:con-rigō⟧ and ⟦b:ē-rigō⟧; commonly ⟦b:por-rigō⟧, sometimes ⟦b:porgō⟧; rarely ⟦b:sur-rigō⟧, commonly ⟦b:surgō⟧; always ⟦b:pergō⟧.
⟦b:rēpō⟧, ⟦i:creep⟧  ⟦b:rēpere⟧  ⟦b:rēpsi⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:scalpō⟧, ⟦i:dig⟧  ⟦b:scalpere⟧  ⟦b:scalpsī⟧  ⟦b:scalptus⟧
⟦b:scrībō⟧, ⟦i:write⟧  ⟦b:scrībere⟧  ⟦b:scrīpsī⟧  ⟦b:scrīptus⟧
⟦b:sculpō⟧, ⟦i:carve⟧  ⟦b:sculpere⟧  ⟦b:sculpsī⟧  ⟦b:sculptus⟧
⟦b:struō⟧, ⟦i:build up⟧  ⟦b:struere⟧  ⟦b:strūxī⟧  ⟦b:strūctus⟧
⟦b:sūgō⟧, ⟦i:suck⟧  ⟦b:sūgere⟧  ⟦b:sūxī⟧  ⟦b:suctus⟧
⟦b:sūmō⟧, ⟦i:take up⟧  ⟦b:sūmere⟧  ⟦b:sūmpsī⟧  ⟦b:sūmptus⟧
⟦b:tegō⟧, ⟦i:cover⟧  ⟦b:tegere⟧  ⟦b:tēxī⟧  ⟦b:tēctus⟧
⟦b:trahō⟧, ⟦i:drag⟧  ⟦b:trahere⟧  ⟦b:trāxī⟧  ⟦b:tractus⟧
⟦b:ūrō⟧, ⟦i:burn⟧  ⟦b:ūrere⟧  ⟦b:ussī⟧  ⟦b:ustus⟧
⟦b:vehō⟧, ⟦i:cart⟧  ⟦b:vehere⟧  ⟦b:vēxī⟧  ⟦b:vectus⟧
⟦b:vīvō⟧, ⟦i:live⟧  ⟦b:vīvere⟧  ⟦b:vīxī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#954⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) With the present stem in a nasalized root followed by ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r831:831⟧).
⟦b:cingō⟧, ⟦i:gird⟧  ⟦b:cingere⟧  ⟦b:cīnxī⟧  ⟦b:cīnctus⟧
⟦b:com-pungō⟧, ⟦i:prick over⟧  ⟦b:com-pungere⟧  ⟦b:com-pūnxī⟧  ⟦b:com-pūnctus⟧
⟦/⟧
A compound of ⟦b:pungō⟧ (⟦r925:925⟧, ⟦r823:823⟧).
⟦b:ē-mungō⟧, ⟦i:clean out⟧  ⟦b:ē-mungere⟧  ⟦b:ē-mūnxī⟧  ⟦b:ē-mūnctus⟧
⟦b:ex-pungō⟧, ⟦i:prick out⟧  ⟦b:ex-pungere⟧  ⟦b:ex-pūnxī⟧  ⟦b:ex-pūnctus⟧
⟦/⟧
A compound of ⟦b:pungō⟧ (⟦r925:925⟧, ⟦r823:823⟧).
⟦b:fingō⟧, ⟦i:mould⟧  ⟦b:fingere⟧  ⟦b:fīnxī⟧  ⟦b:fīctus⟧
⟦b:iungō⟧, ⟦i:join⟧  ⟦b:iungere⟧  ⟦b:iūnxī⟧  ⟦b:iūnctus⟧
⟦b:pingō⟧, ⟦i:paint⟧  ⟦b:pingere⟧  ⟦b:pīnxī⟧  ⟦b:pīctus⟧
⟦b:plangō⟧, ⟦i:beat⟧  ⟦b:plangere⟧  ⟦b:plānxī⟧  ⟦b:plānctus⟧
⟦b:stinguō⟧, ⟦i:poke⟧, ⟦i:poke out⟧  ⟦b:stinguere⟧  ⟦b:-stīnxī⟧  ⟦b:-stīnctus⟧
⟦b:stringō⟧, ⟦i:peel⟧, ⟦i:graze⟧  ⟦b:stringere⟧  ⟦b:strīnxī⟧  ⟦b:strīctus⟧
⟦b:tingō⟧, ⟦i:wet⟧  ⟦b:tingere⟧  ⟦b:tīnxī⟧  ⟦b:tīnctus⟧
⟦b:unguō⟧, ⟦i:anoint⟧  ⟦b:unguere⟧  ⟦b:ūnxī⟧  ⟦b:ūnctus⟧
⟦/⟧
Sometimes ⟦b:ungō⟧, ⟦b:ungere⟧, &c., in the present system.
⟦#955⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-no|e-⟧ (⟦r833:833⟧).
⟦b:temnō⟧, ⟦i:scorn⟧  ⟦b:temnere⟧  (⟦b:con-tempsī⟧)  (⟦b:con-temptus⟧)
⟦/⟧
⟦#956⟧
(⟦i:d.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-io|e-⟧ (⟦r836:836⟧).
⟦b:ad-liciō⟧, ⟦i:lure⟧  ⟦b:ad-licere⟧  ⟦b:ad-lexī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:in-liciō⟧, ⟦i:inveigle⟧  ⟦b:in-licere⟧  ⟦b:in-lexī⟧  ⟦b:in-lectus⟧
⟦b:pel-liciō⟧, ⟦i:lead astray⟧  ⟦b:pel-licere⟧  ⟦b:pel-lexī⟧  ⟦b:pel-lectus⟧
⟦b:-spiciō⟧, ⟦i:spy⟧  ⟦b:-spicere⟧  ⟦b:-spēxī⟧  ⟦b:-spectus⟧
⟦/⟧
Forms of the simple verb are old and rare: as, ⟦b:specitur⟧, ⟦b:spicit⟧, ⟦b:spece⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:specimus⟧ (Varr.), ⟦b:spiciunt⟧ (Cato), ⟦b:spēxit⟧ (Naev., Enn.).
⟦#957⟧
(1 ⟦i:b⟧.) The following verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have the perfect stem in ⟦b:-s-⟧ (⟦r867:867⟧), and the perfect participle, when used, in ⟦b:-sus⟧ (⟦r912:912⟧):
⟦#958⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r829:829⟧).
⟦b:cēdō⟧, ⟦i:move along⟧  ⟦b:cēdere⟧  ⟦b:cessī⟧  ⟦b:cessus⟧
⟦b:claudō⟧, ⟦i:shut⟧  ⟦b:claudere⟧  ⟦b:clausī⟧  ⟦b:clausus⟧
⟦/⟧
Sometimes ⟦b:clūdō⟧, ⟦b:clūdere⟧, ⟦b:clūsī⟧, ⟦b:clūsus⟧. Compounds have ⟦b:ū⟧ for ⟦b:au⟧ throughout.
⟦b:dī-vidō⟧, ⟦i:separate⟧  ⟦b:dī-videre⟧  ⟦b:dī-vīsī⟧  ⟦b:dī-vīsus⟧
⟦b:fīgō⟧, ⟦i:pin⟧  ⟦b:fīgere⟧  ⟦b:fīxī⟧  ⟦b:fīxus⟧, twice ⟦b:fīctus⟧
⟦b:fluō⟧, ⟦i:flow⟧  ⟦b:fluere⟧  ⟦b:flūxī⟧  ⟦b:fluxus⟧ adjective
⟦b:laedō⟧, ⟦i:hurt⟧  ⟦b:laedere⟧  ⟦b:laesī⟧  ⟦b:laesus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds have ⟦b:ī⟧ for ⟦b:ae⟧ throughout: as, ⟦b:in-līdō⟧, ⟦b:in-līdere⟧, &c.
⟦b:lūdō⟧, ⟦i:play⟧  ⟦b:lūdere⟧  ⟦b:lūsī⟧  ⟦b:lūsus⟧
⟦b:mittō⟧, ⟦i:send⟧  ⟦b:mittere⟧  ⟦b:mīsī⟧  ⟦b:missus⟧
⟦b:mergō⟧, ⟦i:dip⟧, ⟦i:duck⟧  ⟦b:mergere⟧  ⟦b:mersī⟧  ⟦b:mersus⟧
⟦b:plaudō⟧, ⟦i:clap⟧  ⟦b:plaudere⟧  ⟦b:plausī⟧  ⟦b:plausus⟧
⟦/⟧
Also ⟦b:ap-plaudō⟧, ⟦b:ap-plaudere⟧, &c. Other compounds have usually ⟦b:ō⟧ for ⟦b:au⟧ throughout: as, ⟦b:ex-plōdō⟧, &c.; but ⟦b:ex-plaudō⟧ (Lucr.).
⟦b:premō⟧, ⟦i:squeeze⟧  ⟦b:premere⟧  ⟦b:pressī⟧  ⟦b:pressus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds have ⟦b:i⟧ for ⟦b:e⟧ in the present system: as, ⟦b:com-primō⟧, &c.
⟦b:rādō⟧, ⟦i:scrape⟧  ⟦b:rādere⟧  ⟦b:rāsī⟧  ⟦b:rāsus⟧
⟦b:rōdō⟧, ⟦i:gnaw⟧  ⟦b:rōdere⟧  ⟦b:rōsī⟧  ⟦b:rōsus⟧
⟦b:spargō⟧, ⟦i:scatter⟧  ⟦b:spargere⟧  ⟦b:sparsī⟧  ⟦b:sparsus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds usually have ⟦b:e⟧ for ⟦b:a⟧ throughout: as, ⟦b:cōn-spergō⟧, &c.
⟦b:trūdō⟧, ⟦i:shove⟧  ⟦b:trūdere⟧  ⟦b:trūsī⟧  ⟦b:trūsus⟧
⟦b:vādō⟧, ⟦i:go⟧  ⟦b:vādere⟧  ⟦b:-vāsī⟧  ⟦b:-vāsus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#959⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-sco|e-⟧ (⟦r834:834⟧).
⟦b:algēscō⟧, ⟦i:get cold⟧  ⟦b:algēscere⟧  ⟦b:alsī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:ardēscō⟧, ⟦i:flame out⟧  ⟦b:ardēscere⟧  ⟦b:arsī⟧ (⟦b:ex-arsī⟧)  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:lūcēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow light⟧  ⟦b:lūcēscere⟧  ⟦b:-lūxī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
Sometimes in the present system ⟦b:lūcīscō⟧, ⟦b:lūcīscere⟧, &c.
⟦b:frīgēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow cold⟧  ⟦b:frīgēscere⟧  ⟦b:-frīxī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:vīvēscō⟧, ⟦i:get alive⟧  ⟦b:vīvēscere⟧  (⟦b:re-vīxī⟧)  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
In composition, also ⟦b:re-vīvīscō⟧, ⟦b:re-vīvīscere⟧.
⟦#960⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-to|e-⟧ (⟦r835:835⟧).
⟦b:flectō⟧, ⟦i:turn⟧  ⟦b:flectere⟧  ⟦b:flexī⟧  ⟦b:flexus⟧
⟦b:nectō⟧, ⟦i:bind together⟧  ⟦b:nectere⟧  ⟦b:nexī⟧, ⟦b:nexuī⟧  ⟦b:nexus⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect system rare: ⟦b:nexit⟧ (Lucil., Acc.); ⟦b:nexuit⟧, ⟦b:ad-nexuerant⟧ (Sall.).
⟦b:pectō⟧, ⟦i:comb⟧  ⟦b:pectere⟧  ⟦b:pexī⟧ once  ⟦b:pexus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#961⟧
(⟦i:d.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-io|e-⟧ (⟦r836:836⟧).
⟦b:quatiō⟧, ⟦i:shake⟧  ⟦b:quatere⟧  ⟦b:-cussī⟧  ⟦b:quassus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds drop the ⟦b:a⟧ (111, ⟦i:a⟧): as, ⟦b:in-cutiō⟧, ⟦b:in-cutere⟧, ⟦b:in-cussī⟧, ⟦b:in-cussus⟧.

title: Primitive Verbs: Perfect Stem in -v-
text:
⟦#962⟧
(2 ⟦i:a⟧.) The following verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have the perfect stem in ⟦b:-v-⟧, preceded by a long vowel of the root (⟦r869:869⟧), and the perfect participle, when used, in ⟦b:-tus⟧:
⟦#963⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r829:829⟧).
⟦b:terō⟧, ⟦i:rub⟧  ⟦b:terere⟧  ⟦b:trīvī⟧  ⟦b:trītus⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect infinitive once in pentameter verse (⟦r823:823⟧) ⟦b:at-teruisse⟧ (Tib.).
⟦#964⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-no|e-⟧ (⟦r833:833⟧).
⟦b:cernō⟧, ⟦i:sift⟧, ⟦i:separate⟧, ⟦i:see⟧  ⟦b:cernere⟧  ⟦b:crēvī⟧, ⟦i:decided⟧  ⟦b:certus⟧, ⟦b:-crētus⟧
⟦b:linō⟧, ⟦i:besmear⟧  ⟦b:linere⟧  ⟦b:lēvī⟧, rarely ⟦b:līvī⟧  ⟦b:litus⟧
⟦/⟧
In the present system some forms in ⟦b:-īre⟧ are used by late writers.
⟦b:sinō⟧, ⟦i:leave⟧, ⟦i:let⟧  ⟦b:sinere⟧  ⟦b:sīvī⟧  ⟦b:situs⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect system forms of ⟦b:sinō⟧ and ⟦b:dē-sinō⟧ in ⟦b:-v-⟧ are: ⟦b:sīvī⟧ (Plaut., Ter., Cic.); ⟦b:dē-sīvit⟧ (Sen.), ⟦b:sīvistis⟧ (Cic.), once each; ⟦b:sīverīs⟧ (Plaut., Cato), ⟦b:dē-sīverit⟧ (Cato, Gell.), ⟦b:sīverint⟧ (Plaut., Curt.), ⟦b:sīvisset⟧ (Cic., Liv.). Much oftener without ⟦b:-v-⟧: as, ⟦b:dē-siī⟧ (Sen.), ⟦b:sīstī⟧ (Plaut., Cic.); ⟦b:dē-sīstī⟧ often, ⟦b:siit⟧ once (Ter.), ⟦b:dē-siit⟧ (Varr., Sen., &c.), ⟦b:dē-sīt⟧ (Mart., &c.), ⟦b:dē-siimus⟧ (Lent.), ⟦b:dē-sīmus⟧ (⟦r893:893⟧), ⟦b:sīstis⟧; ⟦b:dē-siērunt⟧ (Cic., Liv.); ⟦b:dē-sierat⟧, ⟦b:dē-sierit⟧ (Cic.); ⟦b:dē-sīssem⟧, &c., ⟦b:sīsset⟧, ⟦b:sīssent⟧, ⟦b:dē-sīsse⟧. For ⟦b:sīrīs⟧, &c., see ⟦r893:893⟧; for ⟦b:pōnō⟧, ⟦r972:972⟧.
⟦b:spernō⟧, ⟦i:spurn⟧  ⟦b:spernere⟧  ⟦b:sprēvī⟧  ⟦b:sprētus⟧
⟦b:sternō⟧, ⟦i:strew⟧  ⟦b:sternere⟧  ⟦b:strāvī⟧  ⟦b:strātus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#965⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-sco|e-⟧ (⟦r834:834⟧).
⟦b:crēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow⟧  ⟦b:crēscere⟧  ⟦b:crēvī⟧  ⟦b:crētus⟧
⟦b:nōscō⟧, ⟦i:get to know⟧  ⟦b:nōscere⟧  ⟦b:nōvī⟧  ⟦b:nōtus⟧ adjective
⟦/⟧
Compounds: ⟦b:ī-gnōscō⟧, ⟦b:ī-gnōvī⟧, ⟦b:ī-gnōtum⟧; ⟦b:ā-gnōscō⟧, ⟦b:ā-gnōvī⟧, ⟦b:ā-gnitus⟧; ⟦b:cō-gnōscō⟧, ⟦b:cō-gnōvī⟧, ⟦b:cō-gnitus⟧; ⟦b:dī-nōscō⟧, ⟦b:dī-nōvī⟧, rarely ⟦b:dī-gnōscō⟧, ⟦b:dī-gnōvī⟧, ⟦b:——⟧; ⟦b:inter-nōscō⟧, ⟦b:inter-nōvī⟧, ⟦b:——⟧. Old passive infinitive GNOSCIER (inscr. 186 B.C.).
⟦b:pāscō⟧, ⟦i:feed⟧  ⟦b:pāscere⟧  ⟦b:pāvī⟧  ⟦b:pāstus⟧
⟦b:scīscō⟧, ⟦i:enact⟧  ⟦b:scīscere⟧  ⟦b:scīvī⟧  ⟦b:scītus⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#966⟧
(2 ⟦i:b⟧.) The following verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have the perfect stem in ⟦b:-v-⟧, preceded by the long vowel of a presumed denominative stem (⟦r870:870⟧), and the perfect participle, when used, in ⟦b:-tus⟧:
⟦#967⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r829:829⟧).
⟦b:petō⟧, ⟦i:aim at⟧  ⟦b:petere⟧  ⟦b:petīvī⟧  ⟦b:petītus⟧
⟦/⟧
In the perfect, sometimes ⟦b:petiī⟧ (Cic., Ov., Liv., Val. Fl., Plin. ⟦i:Ep.⟧), PETIEI (inscr.), ⟦b:petī⟧ late (Sen., Stat.); ⟦b:petiit⟧ (Cic., Hor., Tac., Suet.), ⟦b:petīt⟧ (Verg., Ov., Phaedr., Sen., Luc., Suet.), ⟦b:petiisse⟧ (Verg., Hor., Ov., Val. Fl., Stat.).
⟦b:quaerō⟧, ⟦i:inquire⟧  ⟦b:quaerere⟧  ⟦b:quaesīvī⟧  ⟦b:quaesītus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds sometimes retain ⟦b:ae⟧ in old Latin, but usually have ⟦b:ī⟧ for ⟦b:ae⟧ throughout: as, ⟦b:con-quīrō⟧, ⟦b:con-quīrere⟧, &c.
⟦#968⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-sco|e-⟧ (⟦r834:834⟧).
⟦b:ab-olēscō⟧, ⟦i:vanish away⟧  ⟦b:ab-olēscere⟧  ⟦b:ab-olēvī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:ad-olēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow up⟧  ⟦b:ad-olēscere⟧  ⟦b:ad-olēvī⟧  ⟦b:ad-ultus⟧
⟦b:con-cupīscō⟧, ⟦i:hanker for⟧  ⟦b:con-cupīscere⟧  ⟦b:con-cupīvī⟧  ⟦b:con-cupītus⟧
⟦b:-dormīscō⟧, ⟦i:fall asleep⟧  ⟦b:-dormīscere⟧  ⟦b:-dormīvī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:ex-olēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow out⟧  ⟦b:ex-olēscere⟧  ⟦b:ex-olēvī⟧  ⟦b:ex-olētus⟧
⟦b:in-veterāscō⟧, ⟦i:get set⟧  ⟦b:in-veterāscere⟧  ⟦b:in-veterāvī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:obs-olēscō⟧, ⟦i:get worn out⟧  ⟦b:obs-olēscere⟧  ⟦b:obs-olēvī⟧  ⟦b:obs-olētus⟧ adj.
⟦b:quiēscō⟧, ⟦i:get still⟧  ⟦b:quiēscere⟧  ⟦b:quiēvī⟧  ⟦b:quiētus⟧ adjective
⟦b:re-sipīscō⟧, ⟦i:come to⟧  ⟦b:re-sipīscere⟧  ⟦b:re-sipīvī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:suēscō⟧, ⟦i:get used⟧  ⟦b:suēscere⟧  ⟦b:suēvī⟧  ⟦b:suētus⟧
⟦b:vesperāscit⟧, ⟦i:gets dusk⟧  ⟦b:vesperāscere⟧  ⟦b:vesperāvit⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#969⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-io|e-⟧ (⟦r836:836⟧).
⟦b:cupiō⟧, ⟦i:want⟧  ⟦b:cupere⟧  ⟦b:cupīvī⟧  ⟦b:cupītus⟧
⟦/⟧
Once with a form in ⟦b:-īre⟧ (⟦r791:791⟧), ⟦b:cupīret⟧ (Lucr.).
⟦b:sapiō⟧, ⟦i:have a smack⟧  ⟦b:sapere⟧  ⟦b:sapīvī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds have ⟦b:i⟧ for ⟦b:a⟧: as, ⟦b:re-sipiō⟧, &c.
⟦#970⟧
(⟦i:d.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-sso|e-⟧ (⟦r375:375⟧).
⟦b:ar-cēssō⟧, ⟦i:send for⟧  ⟦b:ar-cēssere⟧  ⟦b:ar-cēssīvī⟧  ⟦b:ar-cēssītus⟧
⟦/⟧
Sometimes ⟦b:ac-cersō⟧, &c.; infinitive rarely ⟦b:ar-cēssīrī⟧ or ⟦b:ac-cersīrī⟧.
⟦b:capēssō⟧, ⟦i:undertake⟧  ⟦b:capēssere⟧  ⟦b:capēssīvī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:facēssō⟧, ⟦i:do⟧, ⟦i:make off⟧  ⟦b:facēssere⟧  ⟦b:facēssīvī⟧  ⟦b:facēssītus⟧
⟦/⟧
Perfect system rare: ⟦b:facēssierīs⟧ or ⟦b:facēsserīs⟧ (Cic.), ⟦b:facēssīsset⟧ (Tac.).
⟦b:in-cēssō⟧, ⟦i:attack⟧  ⟦b:in-cēssere⟧  ⟦b:in-cēssīvī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:lacēssō⟧, ⟦i:provoke⟧  ⟦b:lacēssere⟧  ⟦b:lacēssīvī⟧  ⟦b:lacēssītus⟧
⟦/⟧

title: Primitive Verbs: Perfect Stem in -u-
text:
⟦#971⟧
(3.) The following verbs in ⟦b:-ere⟧ have the perfect stem in ⟦b:-u-⟧ (⟦r873:873⟧), and the perfect participle, when used, in ⟦b:-tus⟧; in some participles ⟦b:-tus⟧ is preceded by a short ⟦b:i⟧, thus, ⟦b:-itus⟧ (⟦r910:910⟧):
⟦#972⟧
(⟦i:a.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r829:829⟧).
⟦b:alō⟧, ⟦i:bring up⟧  ⟦b:alere⟧  ⟦b:aluī⟧  ⟦b:altus⟧, rarely ⟦b:alitus⟧
⟦b:colō⟧, ⟦i:till⟧, ⟦i:stay round⟧, ⟦i:court⟧  ⟦b:colere⟧  ⟦b:coluī⟧  ⟦b:cultus⟧
⟦b:con-cinō⟧, ⟦i:chime with⟧  ⟦b:con-cinere⟧  ⟦b:con-cinuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
A compound of ⟦b:canō⟧ (⟦r924:924⟧, ⟦r823:823⟧). See also ⟦b:oc-cinō⟧ and ⟦b:prae-cinō⟧.
⟦b:cōn-sulō⟧, ⟦i:consult⟧  ⟦b:cōn-sulere⟧  ⟦b:cōn-suluī⟧  ⟦b:cōn-sultus⟧
⟦b:depsō⟧, ⟦i:knead⟧  ⟦b:depsere⟧  ⟦b:depsuī⟧  ⟦b:depstus⟧
⟦b:fremō⟧, ⟦i:growl⟧  ⟦b:fremere⟧  ⟦b:fremuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:gemō⟧, ⟦i:groan⟧  ⟦b:gemere⟧  ⟦b:gemuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:molō⟧, ⟦i:grind⟧  ⟦b:molere⟧  ⟦b:moluī⟧  ⟦b:molitus⟧
⟦b:oc-cinō⟧, ⟦i:sing ominously⟧  ⟦b:oc-cinere⟧  ⟦b:oc-cinuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
Once with reduplication, ⟦b:oc-cecinerit⟧ (Liv.).
⟦b:oc-culō⟧, ⟦i:hide⟧  ⟦b:oc-culere⟧  ⟦b:oc-culuī⟧  ⟦b:oc-cultus⟧
⟦b:pīsō⟧, ⟦b:pīnsō⟧, ⟦i:bray⟧  ⟦b:pīsere⟧, ⟦b:pīnsere⟧  ⟦b:pīnsuī⟧, ⟦b:pīsīvī⟧  ⟦b:pistus⟧
⟦/⟧
Once (⟦r818:818⟧, ⟦r847:847⟧) ⟦b:pīnsībant⟧ (Enn.). Perfect once ⟦b:pīnsuī⟧ (Pomp.), once (⟦r823:823⟧, ⟦r893:893⟧) ⟦b:pīsiērunt⟧ (Varr.). Perfect participle often ⟦b:pīnsītus⟧ (Col.), once ⟦b:pīnsus⟧ (Vitr.).
⟦b:pōnō⟧, ⟦i:place⟧  ⟦b:pōnere⟧  ⟦b:po-suī⟧  ⟦b:po-situs⟧
⟦/⟧
A compound of ⟦b:po-⟧ and ⟦b:sinō⟧ (⟦r964:964⟧). Perfect in old Latin ⟦b:po-sīvī⟧ (⟦r893:893⟧); ⟦b:po-suī⟧ is first used by Ennius (⟦r875:875⟧). Perfect participle in verse sometimes, ⟦b:po-stus⟧, ⟦b:-po-stus⟧; inf. ⟦b:inposīsse⟧ (Plaut.).
⟦b:prae-cinō⟧, ⟦i:play before⟧  ⟦b:prae-cinere⟧  ⟦b:prae-cinuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:serō⟧, ⟦i:string⟧  ⟦b:serere⟧  ⟦b:-seruī⟧  ⟦b:sertus⟧
⟦b:stertō⟧, ⟦i:snore⟧  ⟦b:stertere⟧  (⟦b:dē-stertuī⟧)  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:strepō⟧, ⟦i:make a racket⟧  ⟦b:strepere⟧  ⟦b:strepuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:texō⟧, ⟦i:weave⟧  ⟦b:texere⟧  ⟦b:texuī⟧  ⟦b:textus⟧
⟦b:tremō⟧, ⟦i:quake⟧  ⟦b:tremere⟧  ⟦b:tremuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:vomō⟧, ⟦i:throw up⟧  ⟦b:vomere⟧  ⟦b:vomuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
⟦#973⟧
(⟦i:b.⟧) With reduplication and ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ in the present stem (⟦r829:829⟧).
⟦b:gignō⟧, ⟦i:beget⟧  ⟦b:gignere⟧  ⟦b:genuī⟧  ⟦b:genitus⟧
⟦/⟧
Present sometimes also without reduplication, ⟦b:genit⟧, &c. (Varr., Lucr.).
⟦#974⟧
(⟦i:c.⟧) With the present stem in a nasalized root followed by ⟦b:-o|e-⟧ (⟦r831:831⟧).
⟦b:ac-cumbō⟧, ⟦i:lie by⟧  ⟦b:ac-cumbere⟧  ⟦b:ac-cubuī⟧  ⟦b:ac-cubitus⟧
⟦/⟧
So also ⟦b:in-cumbō⟧; ⟦b:dis-cumbō⟧ has ⟦b:dis-cubuī⟧, ⟦b:dis-cubitum⟧. Compounds with ⟦b:dē⟧, ⟦b:ob⟧, ⟦b:prō⟧, ⟦b:re-⟧, and ⟦b:sub⟧, have ⟦b:-cubuī⟧, ⟦b:——⟧.
⟦#975⟧
(⟦i:d.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-io|e-⟧ (⟦r836:836⟧).
⟦b:ē-liciō⟧, ⟦i:coax out⟧  ⟦b:ē-licere⟧  ⟦b:ē-licuī⟧  ⟦b:ē-licitus⟧
⟦b:rapiō⟧, ⟦i:seize⟧  ⟦b:rapere⟧  ⟦b:rapuī⟧  ⟦b:raptus⟧
⟦/⟧
Compounds have ⟦b:i⟧ for ⟦b:a⟧ in the present and perfect systems, and ⟦b:e⟧ in the perfect participle: as, ⟦b:ē-ripiō⟧, ⟦b:ē-ripere⟧, ⟦b:ē-ripuī⟧, ⟦b:ē-reptus⟧. Old Latin has ⟦b:u⟧ in ⟦b:dē-rupier⟧ and in ⟦b:sub-rupiō⟧, ⟦b:sub-rupere⟧, ⟦b:sub-rupuī⟧, ⟦b:sub-ruptus⟧; shortened forms are: ⟦b:surpuit⟧, ⟦b:surpuerit⟧ (Plaut.), ⟦b:surpit⟧ (Plaut. prol.), ⟦b:surpere⟧ (Lucr.), ⟦b:surpite⟧, ⟦b:surpuerat⟧ (Hor.). For ⟦b:sub-repsit⟧ (Plaut.), see ⟦r887:887⟧.
⟦#976⟧
(⟦i:e.⟧) With the present stem in ⟦b:-sco|e-⟧ (⟦r835:835⟧); for ⟦b:com-pēscuī⟧, see 855.
⟦b:acēscō⟧, ⟦i:get sour⟧  ⟦b:acēscere⟧  ⟦b:-acuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:alēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow up⟧  ⟦b:alēscere⟧  (⟦b:co-aluī⟧)  (⟦b:co-alitus⟧)
⟦b:ārēscō⟧, ⟦i:dry up⟧  ⟦b:ārēscere⟧  ⟦b:-āruī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:calēscō⟧, ⟦i:get warm⟧  ⟦b:calēscere⟧  ⟦b:-caluī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:candēscō⟧, ⟦i:get white⟧  ⟦b:candēscere⟧  ⟦b:-canduī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:cānēscō⟧, ⟦i:get grey⟧  ⟦b:cānēscere⟧  ⟦b:cānuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:clārēscō⟧, ⟦i:get bright⟧  ⟦b:clārēscere⟧  ⟦b:clāruī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:com-pescō⟧, ⟦i:check⟧  ⟦b:com-pescere⟧  ⟦b:com-pescuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:con-ticēscō⟧, ⟦i:get all still⟧  ⟦b:con-ticēscere⟧  ⟦b:con-ticuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦/⟧
Also in the present system, ⟦b:con-ticīscō⟧, ⟦b:con-ticīscere⟧, &c.
⟦b:crēbrēscō⟧, ⟦i:get common⟧  ⟦b:crēbrēscere⟧  ⟦b:-crēbruī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:crūdēscō⟧, ⟦i:wax bad⟧  ⟦b:crūdēscere⟧  (⟦b:re-crūduī⟧)  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:-dolēscō⟧, ⟦i:get pained⟧  ⟦b:-dolēscere⟧  ⟦b:-doluī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:dūrēscō⟧, ⟦i:get hard⟧  ⟦b:dūrēscere⟧  ⟦b:dūruī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧

⟦b:fervēscō⟧, ⟦i:boil up⟧  ⟦b:fervēscere⟧  ⟦b:-ferbuī⟧, ⟦b:-fervī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:flōrēscō⟧, ⟦i:blossom out⟧  ⟦b:flōrēscere⟧  ⟦b:-flōruī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:horrēscō⟧, ⟦i:bristle up⟧  ⟦b:horrēscere⟧  ⟦b:-horruī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:languēscō⟧, ⟦i:get weak⟧  ⟦b:languēscere⟧  ⟦b:languī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:latēscō⟧, ⟦i:hide away⟧  ⟦b:latēscere⟧  ⟦b:-lituī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:liquēscō⟧, ⟦i:melt⟧  ⟦b:liquēscere⟧  (⟦b:dē-licuī⟧)  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:madēscō⟧, ⟦i:get moist⟧  ⟦b:madēscere⟧  ⟦b:maduī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:marcēscō⟧, ⟦i:pine away⟧  ⟦b:marcēscere⟧  (⟦b:ē-marcuī⟧)  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:mātūrēscō⟧, ⟦i:ripen⟧  ⟦b:mātūrēscere⟧  ⟦b:mātūruī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:nigrēscō⟧, ⟦i:get black⟧  ⟦b:nigrēscere⟧  ⟦b:nigruī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:nōtēscō⟧, ⟦i:get known⟧  ⟦b:nōtēscere⟧  ⟦b:nōtuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:ob-mūtēscō⟧, ⟦i:get still⟧  ⟦b:ob-mūtēscere⟧  ⟦b:ob-mūtuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:ob-surdēscō⟧, ⟦i:get deaf⟧  ⟦b:ob-surdēscere⟧  ⟦b:ob-surduī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:oc-callēscō⟧, ⟦i:get hard⟧  ⟦b:oc-callēscere⟧  ⟦b:oc-calluī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:pallēscō⟧, ⟦i:grow pale⟧  ⟦b:pallēscere⟧  ⟦b:palluī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
⟦b:pūtēscō⟧, ⟦i:get soaked⟧  ⟦b:pūtēscere⟧  ⟦b:pūtuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧

⟦b:tābēscō⟧, ⟦i:waste away⟧  ⟦b:tābēscere⟧  ⟦b:tābuī⟧  ⟦b:——⟧
